The purpose of making a distinction between a word and its meaning becomes apparent in the next chapter, with regard to sabda-sakti-bhu dhvani (implied sense arisen by the power of a word) and artha-sakti-bhu dhvani (implied sense arisen by the power of a meaning) (3.11). In sabda-sakti-bhu dhvani, the word is more important than its meaning because the word cannot be replaced, even with a synonym, without affecting the implied sense.

*eṇhiṁ sama-samaṇatthaṁ ja-uṇāiṁ siṇāṇam adisadu*  
*(Śaurasenī Prakrit)*

*ārye gṛha-karaṇīyaṁ sarvaṁ nirvāhitam eva*

**O noble elder lady, I have finished all the household duties. Now please allow me to take bath in the Yamuna so I can assuage my fatigue.**

**Перевод:**

**Here the following idea is suggested by the literal meaning, “On the pretext of taking bath in the Yamuna, I, without any anxiety, will be able to see Krsna playing on the shore of the Yamuna. I will relax there in that way.”**

Visvanatha Cakravarti explains: atra sloke padasya vyanjana-vrtter abhavad atra niscintaham ity-adi-vyangyartho vacyarthasyaiva bhavati, na tu padasyety arthah, “In this verse, since there is no suggestiveness of a single word; it is the suggestiveness of the literal meaning \[of the whole statement\] that gives rise to the suggestion described in the elaboration” (Subodhini). Thus from here onward the term tatparya artha (the meaning of the sentence) is replaced by vacya artha (literal meaning).

### 2.39

*nānārthānāṁ ca bhedakāḥ saṁyogādyāḥ (15bc)*

**Перевод:**

**The terms such as concomitance are determining factors of words that have various meanings.**

**Перевод:**

**Concomitance, disjunction, and so on are helpful determining factors in delimiting a word that has various meanings.**

### 2.40

*tathā hi,*

**Перевод:**

**The determining factors are:**

*saṁyogaś ca viyogaś ca virodha-sahacāritā*  
*sānnidhyam anya-śabdasya deśaḥ sāmarthyam aucitī*  
*liṅgam arthaḥ prakaraṇaṁ kālo vyaktir imā diśaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Concomitance; disjunction; hostility; accompaniment; juxtaposition of another word; the place; power; congruity; characteristic; meaning; context; time; and grammatical gender—these show the way.” (adapted from Vakya-padiya 2.315-316)**

### 2.41

*krameṇodāharaṇāni yathā, “sa-kaustubho bhāti vidhuḥ, śete vidhur akaustubhaḥ” saṁyoga-viyogau. “rāmārjunau tathā karṇārjunau saha niyudhyataḥ” virodhaḥ. “rādhā-mādhavayoḥ krīḍā madhumādhavayor dine” saha-cāritā. “kṛṣṇasya muni-varyasya” anyaśabdasya sānnidhyam. “vraje ’sau parameśvaraḥ” deśaḥ. asau śrī-nando vraje rājety arthaḥ. “madhunā kokilo mattaḥ, pramattā madhunā vadhūḥ” sāmarthyam aucitī ca. “utpadya hṛdaye tasyāḥ pīḍako makara-dhvajaḥ” liṅgam. kāmatve pīḍakatvam eva liṅgam. “sthāṇuḥ kṛṣṇa-guṇāmodī” arthaḥ. “devo jānāti me manaḥ” atra prakaraṇa-vaśād yuṣmadi. “citra-bhānur vibhātīti dine ’rko niśi pāvakaḥ” kālaḥ. “śāstre bhāgavataṁ bhāgavataḥ syād bhagavajjane” vyaktiḥ. eṣv abhidhā-lakṣaṇayor anavasaratvāt saṁyogāder eva vyañjakatā.*

**Перевод:**

**Examples are in order:**

**♦   samyoga (concomitance): sa-kaustubho bhati vidhuh, “Krsna looks beautiful with the Kaustubha jewel.”**

**♦   viyoga (disjunction): sete vidhur akaustubhah, “Krsna lies down without the Kaustubha jewel.”**

**♦   virodha (hostility): ramarjunau tatha karnarjunau saha niyudhyatah, “Parasurama and Kartavyryarjuna fight with each other, as do Karna and Arjuna.”**

**♦   saha-carita (accompaniment): radha-madhavayoh krida madhu-madhavayor dine, “The pastimes of Radha and Madhava occur in the days of Caitra and Vaisakha.”**

**♦   anya-sabdasyasannidhyam (juxtaposition of another word): krsnasya muni-varyasya, “of Krsna, the best of munis.”**

**♦   desa (place): vraje ’sau paramesvarah, “In Vraja, he is god.” This means: “In Vraja, Nanda is king.”**

**♦   samarthya (power): madhuna kokilo mattah, “The cuckoo is maddened by spring (madhu).”**

**♦   auciti (congruity): pramatta madhuna vadhuh, “The girl is drunk due to liquor (madhu).”**

**♦   linga (characteristic): utpadya hrdaye tasyah pidako makara- dhvajah, “Arising in her heart, Cupid torments her.” Here the characteristic is the torment through lust.**

**♦   artha (meaning): sthanuh krsna-gunamodi, “Siva delights in Krsna’s qualities.”**

**♦   prakarana (context): devo janati me manah, “The lord knows my mind.” Because of the context, the word deva (lord, king) has the sense of yusmad (you).**

**♦   kala (time): “Citra-bhanu is giving light.” If this is said during the day, citra-bhanu means the sun; if it is said at night it denotes fire.**

**♦   vyakti (grammatical gender): The word bhagavatam (neuter) denotes the scripture, whereas a bhagavata (masculine) is a devotee of the Lord.**

**In these examples, since there is no occasion for either abhidha or laksana to apply, it is only a factor, such as concomitance, that is suggestive \[of the appropriate meaning\].**

**Комментарий:**

Both Mammata and Visvanatha Kaviraja say the above factors are in the scope of Denotation (abhidha). This section (2.39-42) is meant to form the basis for Denotation-based Suggestiveness (abhidha-mula vyanjana): When the possible literal meanings of a word are narrowed down to one by the above factors, any additional meaning is only in the scope of Suggestiveness. The “suggestiveness” of the above factors is not in the scope of the function called Suggestiveness; Bhartrhari only says they are the causes of the remembrance of the specific meaning. Kavi Karnapura reasons that they are not in the scope of Denotation because by definition Denotation gives the meaning of a word merely by hearing or reading the word (2.16). He paraphrased Visvanatha Kaviraja’s definition of Denotation, but Mammata’s approach is more comprehensive: He says Denotation is simply the function that governs a literally expressive word, and then he defines it: saksat sanketitam yo ’rtham abhidhatte sa vacakah, “A literally expressive word is a word that denotes the directly assigned meaning” (Kavya-prakasa 2.7).

In truth, the literal meaning obtained by the above factors is in the scope of the function called tatparya (the drift). Commenting on Ruyyaka’s Alankara-sarvasva, Jayaratha writes: samanyanam parasparanvitatvena visesarthavabodhana-saktis tatparyam, “Tatparya is the power that makes one perceive the particular meaning, when the words are mutually syntactically connected in a general way.”

Nagesa Bhatta expounds: tatparya-niyamakam ca loke prakaranadikameva. atobhojana-prakarane “saindhavamanaya” ity ukte saindhava-padena lavana-pratyayah, yuddhavasare ’va-- pratyayah. veda-vakye caisvarya-tatparyad artha-bodhah, “In worldly usage, the context and the other factors govern the tatparya. For instance, when it is said during a meal “Bring the saindhava,” the word saindhava means salt. But when the context is war, the word saindhava means a horse. In Vedic usage, the understanding of the meaning occurs from the purport intended by the Lord.” (Parama-laghu-manjusa, tatparya-vicara)

Since Mammata, like Kavi Karnapura and Visvanatha Kaviraja, disregards tatparya by using the term vacya to signify the meaning of a sentence, to simplify things Mammata disregards the notion of tatparya in this matter as well.

The Drift, the actual sense of the sentence, is distinct from the Mimamsakas’ well-known tatparya, the purport of the sentence. In philosophy, sometimes the Mimamsakas’ tatparya signifies vivaksa (the speaker’s intention), and sometimes it is an implied sense. Mammata’s tatparya only corresponds to vivaksa. Kavi Karnapura completely ignored Mammata’s tatparya because quite often there is no difference between the Drift and vivaksa and because Mammata himself discarded the Drift, yet a subtlety in poetical theory was lost by overlooking Mammata’s tatparya.

In essence, the Drift is the same as Bhartrhari’s vakya-sphota (the flash of insight that gives the overall sense of the sentence). The constituent elements of a sentence in Nyaya—yogyata (congruity), akanksa (expectancy) and asatti (proximity) (1.9) (2.31)— are in the scope of the Drift and are used to arrive at the actual meaning of each word. The concept of yogyata is the same as the above factor called auciti (congruity): Baladeva Vidyabhusana (Sahitya-kaumudi 2.36) and Pandita-raja Jagannatha explain auciti as yogyata. In truth, all the above factors are subcategories of yogyata (auciti).

### 2.42

*yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**For example:**

*adyāloki ghana-prabhaḥ sakhi mayā kaścid vihāra-krame*  
*lolat-keśara-mālikā-vilulita-grīvo hariḥ kānane*  
*yaḥ sadyastana-kumbhi-kumbha-nikara-kṣode nakha-bhraṁśibhir*  
*muktaughair dhavalī-karoti yamunā-tīre nikuñja-sthalīḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

adya—today; aloki—was seen; ghana-prabhah—whose effulgence was dense (or whose bodily complexion was like that of a cloud); sakhi—O friend; maya—by me; kascit—a certain; vihara-krame— in the course of going (or in the course of sporting); lolat—which is swinging to and fro; kesara—of hairs on the shoulder (or of naga-kesara flowers); malika—by a multitude (or by a garland); vilulita—is caressed; grivah—whose neck; harih—a lion (or Krsna); kanane—in the forest; yah—who; sadyahtana—instantaneously; kumbhi-kumbha—of frontal lobes of the elephants (or of breasts which resemble the frontal lobes of elephants); nikara—the multitude; ksode—at the time of tearing open; nakha—because of the nails; bhramsibhih—which fall; mukta—of pearls; oghaih— with the multitudes; dhavali-karoti—makes white; yamuna-kire— on the shore of the Yamuna; nikunja-sihadh—the forest bowers.

**Перевод:**

**\[First interpretation:\]**

**Sakhi, today while taking a walk in the forest I saw a lion. His effulgence was dense. His mane was swinging to and fro. He was whitening the pleasure groves on the Yamuna’s shore with the pearls that instantly fell as he tore open the elephants’s lobes with his nails.**

**\[Second interpretation:\]**

**Sakhi, today in the course of sporting \[with my friends\] in the forest I saw Krsna. His bodily complexion was like that of a cloud. His neck was caressed by a garland of kesara flowers that was swinging to and fro. He was whitening the pleasure groves on the Yamuna’s shore with the pearls that instantly fell \[from the broken pearl necklaces\] as He tore away at the gopis’ breasts.**

*atrānekārtha-śabdānām aneka-saṁsargasya vyañjakatā.*

**Перевод:**

**In this verse, the concomitance of many things suggests the appropriate meaning of the words that have many meanings.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti explains: atra visesam-bhutanam ghana- vihara-kesara-padadmam anekartha-sambandhena visesyasya nanartha-hari-padasyapy artha-dvaya-matra-bodhakatvam, na tv indradi-bodhakatvam iti jneyam, “Here the noun hari, which has many meanings, only expresses two meanings (lion; Krsna) and no other meaning such as Indra. This is due to a connection with modifiers, such as ghana (dense; cloud), vihara (leisurely walking; sporting), kesara (mane; kesara flower), which also have more than one meaning” (Subodhini).

In this verse, hari means “lion” and “Krsna.” Kavi Karnapura points out that this is so by the factor called samyoga (concomitance): A lion has ghana-prabha (a dense effulgence) and kesara (a mane), and similarly Krsna has ghana-prabha (a complexion like that of a cloud) and kesara (naga-kesara flowers).

If the context were that the speaker is talking to her friend in the midst of elders, then the second interpretation of the verse would not be meant to be literally expressed. The verse would thus illustrate that the meaning of hari as lion is governed by abhidha whereas its meaning as Krsna is governed by vyanjana. This is Denotation-based Suggestiveness. At any rate, the verse features an implied simile between Krsna and a lion.

The above illustrates the difference between slesa and dhvani. In slesa (literal double meaning), both meanings are vacya (literal), whereas in dhvani (implied double meaning), one of the meanings is implied (vyangya) because it cannot be literally applicable in the context.

### 2.43

*evam anukaraṇa-śabdānāṁ ca vyaṅgyaṁ prati vākyārtha eva vyañjakaḥ. yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**Similarly, even the meaning of a sentence which also relates to imitative words (onomatopoeia) can suggest an implied sense. For example:**

*āsāṁ rāsa-vilāsa-lāsya-laharīm āsvādya vādya-cchalāt*  
*tā dhik tā dhig iti prabhāṣya murajaḥ svar-nartakīr nindati*  
*te nā nā ga ri mā dha mā iti muhuḥ pāṭha-svaroccāraṇāt*  
*tāsāṁ hanta jugupsate bhagavatī vāṇī ca gāna-kramān*

**Пословный перевод:**

asam—of these girls (the gopis); rasa-vilasa—in the rasa-lila; lasya—of dancing; laharim—the waves; asvadya—relishing; vadya-chalat—on the pretext of being a musical instrument; ta dhik ta dhik—the beat ta dhik ta dhik (or the words “Fie on them. Fie on them” (tah dhik tah dhik)); iti—thus; prabhasya—speaking; murajah—the muraja drum (the drum played in the rasa-lila); svar-nartakih—the dancers of heaven (the Apsaras); nindati— rebukes; te na na ga ri ma dha ma—the phrase te na na (which indicates the particular raga being sung) and the notes ga ri ma dha ma (or the words te nana-agarima-adhamah (“they are lower on account of their many kinds of inferiority”)); iti—thus; muhuh— repeatedly; patha-svara-uccaranat—because of articulating the phrase and the notes; tasam—of those girls (the gopis); hanta— ah!; jugupsate—rebukes; bhagavati—the goddess; vani— Sarasvati (languagepersonified); ca—and; gana-kraman—the styles of singing \[of the Gandharvas\].

**Перевод:**

**Relishing the waves of the gopis’ dancing in the Rasa, the muraja drum, on the plea of being a musical instrument, resounds with the beat ta dhik ta dhik, thus rebuking the dancers of heaven (tah dhik tah dhik means “Fie on them, fie on them”). And the goddess of speech, SarasvatT, by repeating the gopis’ phrase (te na na) and their notes (ga ri ma dha ma) rebukes the singing styles of the Gandharvas (te nanagarimadhamah means “They are lower on account of their many kinds of inferiority”).**

*atra te nā nā iti pāṭhaḥ. ga ri mā dha mā iti gāndhāra-ṛṣabhamadhyama-dhaivata-punar-madhyamā iti tāna-viśeṣa-svarāḥ, tābhyāṁ te nānā-vidho yo ’garimā tenādhamā ity artho vyajyate.*

**Перевод:**

**Here, te na na is the phrase, and ga ri ma dha ma, that is gandhara, rsabha, madhyama, dhaivata, and again madhyama, are the notes of a certain euphonic series. By articulating this phrase and these notes, the suggested sense is: “They are lower because of their inferiority (agarima = nicatva), which is of many kinds.”**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: In this text Kavi Karnapura describes how poets somehow or other perceive a resemblance between a meaningless inarticulate sound made by an instrument such as a drum and an articulate sound, and make poetry by attributing a meaning even to such a meaningless sound. Here the superimposed meaning of the sentence of imitative words, ta dhik, is “Fie on the dancers of heaven.” That suggests an implied meaning: the gopis ’superexcellence. The beautiful girls of Vraja (tasam = vraja- sundarinam) repeat by heart the phrase te na na, which indicates the melody (raga), and sing ga ri ma dha ma, the syllables that represent the notes named gandhara and so on. Sarasvati, however, using these same syllables, makes a coalescence of the vowel a (na na ga ri ma = nana + agarima) and thus rebukes the singing styles of the Gandharvas. Kavi Karnapura describes the meaning created by Sarasvati with the sentence beginning tabhyam (“on account of those two, they are lower because of their inferiority, which is of many kinds”). In that sentence, tabhyam (on account of those two) means patha-svaroccaranabhyam (by articulating this phrase and these notes); te (they) denotes the Gandharvas; and agariman means the opposite of gariman: nlcatvam (inferiority). The sense suggested, as a double meaning, is that, compared to the beautiful girls of Vraja, the Gandharvas are lower due to their inferiority in the art of singing. (Subodhinl)

### 2.44

*athārthānāṁ vyañjakatvasya hetavaḥ (15cd)*

**Перевод:**

**Now the causes of the suggestiveness of a meaning will be explained.**

*arthānāṁ sāmānyatvena prāg-uktānāṁ vācyādīnāṁ vyañjakatve viśeṣa-hetava ucyante.*

**Перевод:**

**The three kinds of meanings—literal, figurative and suggestive—were previously described in a general way. Now the specific causes of their becoming suggestive will be mentioned.**

**Комментарий:**

In Suggestiveness founded on Denotation, an implied sense is based either on the word (sabdl vyanjana) or on the meaning (arthi vyanjana). The difference between the two is that the implied sense is said to be based on the word when it would be altered by using a synonym of that word. Rupa Gosvami mentions this twofold classification: vyangya evatra sa sabdartha-bhavo dvidha (Ujjvala-nilamani 7.5). From now on, Kavi Karnapura begins to expound arthi vyanjana. In the next chapter, sabdl vyanjana and arthi vyanjana are referred to as sabda-sakti-mula dhvani (implied sense based on the word) and artha-sakti-mula dhvani (implied sense based on the meaning) respectively (3.11).

### 2.45

*boddhavya-vaktṛ-prakṛti-kāku-prakaraṇaiḥ saha*  
*deśa-kālādayaś cārthe vaiśiṣṭyād vyaṅgya-bodhakāḥ (16)*

**Пословный перевод:**

boddhavya—the person whom the speaker is informing; vaktr— the speaker; prakrti—the nature; kaku—the intonation of the voice; prakaranaih—the context; saha—along with; desa-kala-adayah— the place, the time, and so on; ca—and; arthe—in the meaning; vaisistyat—due to the specialty (the excellence); vyangya- bodhakah—make one aware of an implied sense.

**Перевод:**

**These factors (specialties) make one aware of an implied sense because of an excellence in the meaning: (1) boddhavya (the person who is addressed), (2) vaktr (the speaker), (3) prakrti (the nature, a special characteristic of the boddhavya or of the speaker), (4) kaku (a modulation of the tone of voice), (5) prakarana (the context), (6) desa (the place), (7) kala (the time), and so on.**

### 2.46

*atra “yātāsi svayam eva” ity-ādau tad-ānayārthaṁ na gatāsi, api tūpabhogārtham iti boddhavya-vaiśiṣṭyam. yāṁ pratīyam uktiḥ sā boddhavyā yogyā, ayogyā ced bhavati tadā dhvany-artho na saṅgacchate. vaktṛ-vaiśiṣṭyaṁ prakṛti-vaiśiṣṭyaṁ prakaraṇavaiśiṣṭyaṁ cātraiva. vaktrī śrī-rādhā, sā ca sarva-śreṣṭhatva-rūpavaiśiṣṭyavatī. prakṛtiś ca tasyāḥ sakhīṁ prati snehāt śrī-kṛṣṇāṅgasaṅga-prāpaṇaṁ vyājena karotīti yat, sakhyāś ca prakṛtir nijapriya-sakhī-dūtyārthaṁ gatāyāḥ kṛṣṇena saha sambhogaḥ katham api na sambhaved iti tathaiva jñeyā. atas tasyā vaiśiṣṭyāt tathāvidha-prakaraṇaṁ ca tatra mantavyam, tena tad-vaiśiṣṭyāc ca dvitīya-dhvani-pallavaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Verse 1.19 is an example of the specialty of the boddhavya which makes a suggestion possible: “You personally went to find My jewelled necklace. You have returned from the forest after a long time. I know your body is tender and you suffered much pain for My sake. Your breaths are drawn out, your chest was scratched by thorns, and your mouth is dry. Why are you feeling embarrassed? It is not proper for girls to go so far away by themselves in the secluded part of the forest.” (1.19)**

**In this verse, the boddhavya is a gopi. The specialty that is the boddhavya suggests the following meaning of the speaker: “You did not go to retrieve that necklace, you went to take pleasure.”**

**When the person to whom a statement is directed is the proper person to be addressed, that person is called a boddhavya. Conversely, if the person who is addressed is not suitable, then the suggested meaning would not make sense.**

**In that verse, there is also the specialty which is the speaker (vaktr-vaisistya), the specialty of the nature (prakrti-vaisistya), and the specialty which is the context (in this case the background story) (prakarana-vaisistya). The speaker is Sri Radha, and She has the excellence (vaisistya) of being the best of all. Her nature is that, by using a pretext out of affection, She makes a sakhi unite with Krsna. The nature of Radha’s friend is that although she went for the sake of serving her dear friend as a messenger, she thought that enjoying with Krsna would not happen at all. Because of the excellence of Sri Radha’s nature, another similar background story should be understood in that verse. Therefore, owing to the excellence of the context, there is a second offshoot of an implied meaning.**

### 2.47

*kāku-vaiśiṣṭyaṁ yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**The specialty of kaku (modulation of the voice) makes a suggestion possible:**

*a-i jāhi jāhi vivinaṁ riktaṁ ghettūṇa kusuma-bhāaṇaṁ su-muhi*  
*paccāamissasi tumaṁ na kealaṁ bhāaṇeṇa puṇṇeṇa*  
*(Śaurasenī Prakrit)*

*ayi yāhi yāhi vipinaṁ riktaṁ gṛhītvā kusuma-bhājanaṁ su-mukhi*  
*pratyāgamiṣyasi tvaṁ na kevalaṁ bhājanena pūrṇena*  
*(Sanskrit rendering)*

**Пословный перевод:**

ayi—O girl; yahi—you should go; yahi—you should go; vipinam— to the forest; riktam—empty; grhltva—having taken; kusuma- bhajanam—a flower basket; su-mukhi—O you whose face is beautiful; pratyagamisyasi—will return; tvam—you; na—not; kevalam—only; bhajanena—with a recipient; purnena—full.

**Перевод:**

**Go, girl. Go to the secluded forest and bring a basket for collecting flowers. You will not return with only a full basket.**

*atra na kevalaṁ kusuma-bhājanenaiva pūrṇenāgamiṣyasi, api tu pūrṇena manorathenāpi, iti nañ-kāku-dyotyam.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the suggestion arises due to a different intonation on the negative particle (na) (“you will not return with only a full basket!”). The sense is: “You will not come back with just a full basket of flowers; you will come back with your desires fulfilled too.”**

### 2.48

*deśa-vaiśiṣṭyaṁ yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**The specialty of a place makes a suggestion possible:**

*ja-uṇā-sīara-sisirā kamala-vaṇī-paaṇa-dhūa-kisala-aggā*  
*jaha vallī-dhara-pallī dhaṇṇā pekkhanti taṁ desaṁ*  
*(Śaurasenī Prakrit)*

*yamunā-śīkara-śiśirā kamala-vanī-pavana-dhūta-kisalayāgrā*  
*yatra vallī-gṛha-pallī dhanyāḥ prekṣante taṁ deśam*  
*(Sanskrit rendering)*

**Пословный перевод:**

yamuna—of the Yamuna; slkara—caused by the spray; sisira— there is coolness; kamala—of lotuses; vani—in groves; pavana— by the breeze; dhuta—is moved to and fro; kisalaya—of a shoot; agra—the front part; yatra—where; valli—fashioned with creepers; grha—of cottages (i.e. arbors); palli—there is an abundance; dhanyah—fortunate people; preksante—see; tam—that; desam— place.

**Перевод:**

**There is a place where the Yamuna’s mist gives a chill; many arbors shaped by creepers can be found; and the breeze makes the lotuses in the groves move to and fro. Fortunate people are able to see that place.**

*atra deśa-vaiśiṣṭya-ślāghayā kṛṣṇena saha tatra māṁ ramayeti sakhīṁ prati kācit sva-manorathaṁ prakāśayati.*

**Перевод:**

**Here a girl reveals her secret longing to a sakhi. Her suggestion is made possible by her praise of the excellence of that place. She implies: “You should arrange that I enjoy with Krsna there.”**

### 2.49

*kāla-vaiśiṣṭyaṁ yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**The specialty of the time makes a suggestion possible:**

*eṇhiṁ jala-hara-samaye ramaṇijjā ra-aṇa-valahītta*

*(Śaurasenī Prakrit)*

*idānīṁ jala-dhara-samaye ramaṇīyā ratna-valabhyaḥ*  
*nipatad-vāri-dhārā-gabhīratara-mukhara-garbha-kuharāḥ*  
*(Sanskrit rendering)*

**Пословный перевод:**

idanim—now; jala-dhara—of the clouds; samaye—at this time; ramaniyah—are very charming; ratna—endowed with jewels; valabhyah—the pinnacles of houses; nipatat—falling; vari-dhara— because of the shower; gabhiratara—very loud; mukhara—\[let through\] noise; garbha—inside; kuharah—\[in which pinnacles\] the openings.

**Перевод:**

**Now that the clouds have come, the jeweled pinnacles of houses are very charming. Since it is raining heavily, very loud noise can be heard through the high windows.**

### 2.50

*ādi-śabdāt prasiddhi-vaiśiṣṭyaṁ yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**Because of the word adi (2.45), there is the specialty that is prasiddhi (a well-known fact). This verse illustrates the specialty of prasiddhi that makes a suggestion possible:**

*kara-kisalaya-līlāmbuja-nimīlanonmīlanāti-kutukinyā*  
*dakṣiṇam akṣi murāreḥ pidhīyate mucyate ca sindhu-jayā*

**Пословный перевод:**

kara-kisalaya—in her fingers (“shoots of the hand”); lila-ambuja— the play lotus; nimilana—to close; unmilana—and open; ati- kutukinya—by she who is very eager; daksinam—right; aksi—eye; mura-areh—of Murari; pidhiyate—is closed; mucyate—is opened; ca—and; sindhu-jaya—by Laksmi (“born from the ocean”).

**Перевод:**

**Eager to close and open the play lotus in her hand, Laksmi closes and opens Murari’s right eye.**

*atra murārer dakṣiṇam akṣi prasiddhi-vaiśiṣṭyāt sūryātmakam iti vyajyate.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the implied sense is that Murari’s right eye has the nature of the sun. This implied meaning arises because of the specialty of that well-known fact.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti explains: “When Laksmi closes the Lord’s right eye, meaning the sun, then her play lotus closes because it perceives the Lord’s left eye, which represents the moon. And when she opens His right eye, then her play lotus blossoms.” (Subodhini)

The well-known fact is based on the scriptures. The Mundaka Upanisad states: caksusi candra-suryau, “The moon and the sun are His eyes” (2.1.4). The Brhad-aranyaka Upanisad says: tadyat tat satyam asau sa adityah, ya esa etasmin mandale purusah, yas cayam daksine ’ksan purusah, “That which is Satya is the well- known sun, who is the person in the sun as well as the being in the right eye” (5.5.2).

Kavi Karnapura’s example is an adaptation of a verse by Mammata, reiterated ahead (10.136). In Mammata’s verse, not only is the prasiddhi-vaisistya implied, it also gives rise to an implied sense.

*ity alankara-kaustubhe sabdartha-vrtti-traya-nirupano nama dvitiyah kiranah.*

**Перевод:**

**Thus ends the second ray in Alankara-kaustubha, entitled: “a disquisition on words, meanings, and the three rhetorical functions.”**

## Third Ray - First-rate Poetry

### 3.1

*atha dhvani-nirṇayaḥ. atha “dhvanir asavaḥ” iti kāvya-prāṇatvena nirūpitasya dhvaner bhedam ākhyātuṁ dhvani-śabdasya vyutpattim āha—*

**Перевод:**

**To describe the varieties of dhvani, which was mentioned as the life of poetry (1.7), he states the derivation:**

*śabdārthādibhir anyaiś ca dhvanyate ’sāv iti dhvaniḥ (1)*

**Перевод:**

**Dhvani is what is implied by a sound, by a meaning, and so on (padamsa, and the style of compounding), and by other things (onomatopoeia).**

*dhvananaṁ dhvaniḥ, dhvanyate ’neneti dhvaniḥ, dhvanyate ’sminn iti dhvanir iti bhāva-karaṇādhikaraṇa-sādhano ’pi dhvanir bhavati. tan-nirāsārthaṁ dhvanyate ’sāv iti karma-sādhana eveti pratijānīte.*

**Перевод:**

**The derivation is in the passive voice. And that is for the purpose of excluding these other derivations: (1) In the passive impersonal voice: Implying, (2) In the instrumental voice: That by means of which implying is done, and (3) In the locative: That in which there is an implication.**

**Комментарий:**

Kavi Karnapura had already frowned upon the derivation in the instrumental voice (1.14). The word dhvani is also used in the term

dhvani-kavya (first-rate poetry) (lit. the poetry called dhvani). According to Visvanatha Kaviraja, the derivation is in the locative: vacyad adhika-camatkarini vyangyarthe dhvanyate ’sminn iti vyutpattya dhvanir namottamam kavyam (Sahitya-darpana 4.1).

### 3.2

*tad eva kim ity āha,*

**Перевод:**

**What is implied? Therefore he mentions the particulars:**

*raso bhāvas tad-ābhāso vastv alaṅkāra eva ca*  
*bhāvānām udayaḥ śāntiḥ sandhiḥ śabalatā tathā*  
*sarvaṁ dhvanis taj-janitve kāvyaṁ ca dhvanir ucyate (2)*

**Перевод:**

**These are the types of dhvanis:**

**♦ rasa-dhvani (aesthetic delight),**  
**♦ bhava-dhvani (implied sthayi-bhava or implied vyabhicari),**  
**♦ rasabhasa-dhvani (semblance of a rasa),**  
**♦ bhavabhasa-dhvani (semblance of a bhava),**  
**♦ vastu-dhvani (implied idea),**  
**♦   alankara-dhvani (implied ornament),**  
**♦   bhavodaya-dhvani (rise of a vyabhicari),**  
**♦   bhava-santi-dhvani (disappearance of a vyabhicari),**  
**♦   bhava-sandhi-dhvani (combination of vyabhicaris),**  
**♦   bhava-sabalya-dhvani (mix of**

**Since it generates an implied sense, poetry as well is called dhvani.**

*rasākhya-dhvaner anye dhvanayas tu prāṇāḥ, rasākhyas tu dhvanir ātmety adoṣaḥ. rasādayaḥ paścād varṇyante.*

**Перевод:**

**The dhvanis other than rasa are the life of poetry, but the dhvani called rasa is the soul of poetry (1.7). There is no incongruity that way. The rasadis will be described later.**

**Комментарий:**

All types of dhvanis except vastu-dhvani and alankara-dhvani are collectively called rasadi-dhvani. This chapter treats of vastu- dhvani and alankara-dhvani. The rasa-adis (rasa and so on) are discussed in chapter five. A rasa is technically called rasa-dhvani because a rasa is implied.

The term vastu-dhvani is a synonym of vyangya artha (implied meaning): vastu-bhuto ’rthah (3.19). An alankara-dhvani is a vastu-dhvani that implicitly fits in a category of literary ornament. A rasadi-dhvani is a fancy type of vastu-dhvani.

The compound tat-jani in the sutra is a yasmat sah bahuvrihi: Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura says it is derived as “the poetry from which there is the origination of a first-rate implied sense.”

### 3.3

*samprati asu-bhūtānāṁ dhvanīnāṁ bhedā darśyante,*

**Перевод:**

**Now the varieties of dhvanis that are the life of poetry will be expounded:**

*ubhayor abhidhā-mūla-lakṣaṇā-mūlayos tayoḥ*  
*avivakṣita-vācyo ’ntyas tatra vācyaṁ dvidhā bhavet (3)*

*tayor dhvanyor antyo lakṣaṇā-mūlo dhvanir avivakṣita-vācyaḥ syāt. tatrāvivakṣita-vācye dhvanau vācyaṁ dvi-vidhā bhavatīty arthaḥ. kiṁ tad dvaidham ity āha.*

**Перевод:**

**There are two broad varieties of dhvanis: abhidha-mula-dhvani (implied sense based on Denotation) and laksana-mula-dhvani (implied sense based on Indication). At first, the latter will be detailed: In laksana-mula-dhvani, the literal meaning is not meant to be expressed, and is classed in two categories.**

### 3.4

*arthāntaropasaṅkrāntam atyantaṁ vā tiraskṛtam (4ab)*

**Перевод:**

**Either it changes into another meaning or it becomes obliterated.**

*evaṁ vācyam, ajahat-svārthatayā aparārthenopasaṅkrāntaṁ bhavati, anyaj jahat-svārthatayā sva-viparītenārthenākrāntaṁ bhavatīti dvaidham.*

**Перевод:**

**In laksana-mula-dhvani, the literal meaning is classed either as arthantara-sankramita-vacya (it slightly changes to another sense) or as atyanta-tiraskrta-vacya (it becomes completely obliterated).**

**The category called arthantara-sankramita-vacya corresponds to ajahat-svartha laksana (figurative usage where the meaning of the word is not lost), and atyanta-tiraskrta-vacya corresponds to jahat-svartha laksana (figurative usage where the word loses its meaning).**

### 3.5

*krameṇodāharaṇāni*

**Перевод:**

**Examples are shown in order.**  
**\[This illustrates arthantara-sankramita:\]**

*phalam api phalaṁ mākandānāṁ sitā api tāḥ sitā*  
*amṛtam amṛtaṁ drākṣā drākṣā madhūni madhūny api*  
*saha tulayituṁ tenaiteṣāṁ na kiñcana yujyate*  
*subala yad ayaṁ sāraṅgākṣyā bhavaty adharo ’dharaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

phalam—fruit; api—even; phalam—fruit; makandanam—of the mango tree; sitah—candies; api—even; tah—those well-known; sitah—candies; amrtam—nectar; amrtam—nectar; draksa— grapes; draksa—grapes; madhuni—honey; madhuni—honey; api—even; saha—with; tulayitum— to equal; tena—(with) the lips; etesam—among these; na kincana—nothing; yujyate—is able; subala—O Subala; yat—because; ayam—these (lips); saranga— are like an antelope’s; aksyah—of the girl whose eyes; bhavati— are; adharah—lips; adharah—which lessen (i.e. belittle).

**Перевод:**

**O Subala, mangos are mangos, candy is candy, nectar is nectar, grapes are grapes, and honey is honey. But they do not compare to that doe-eyed girl’s nether lip. Her lips are lips.**

*atra dvitīya-phalādi-śabdā nindādy-artha-saṅkrāntāḥ. tathā hi— phalaṁ nānāvasthaṁ pāka eva kadācin madhuraṁ bhavati, tena tan nindyam eva. sitāḥ pāka-paunaḥ-punyenaiva nirmalā bhavanti, na tv ārambha eva. amṛtaṁ devair api pīyate. drākṣā pūrva-vad eva. madhūni saraghocchiṣṭāni. adharas tu adhara eva, sarvāṇy etāny adharayatīty adharaḥ. “saha tulayituṁ tenaiteṣāṁ na kiñcana yujyate” iti viśeṣa-vacanād upameya-dvitīya-pade stutyartha eva vyaṅgyaḥ, na tūpamāna-dvitīya-pada-vad dheyāṁśatā.*

**Перевод:**

**In this verse, the meaning of the repeated words “mangoes” and so on is transformed into the sense of “criticism” and so on. For example, fruit, which has many stages, is only sometimes sweet when it is ripe. In this way fruits are unreliable and thus contemptible. Sugar candy becomes pure only by repeatedly cooking it; it is not pure in its raw state. Nectar is drunk by the gods (and the gods are inferior to Radha and Krsna). The case of the grapes follows the example of fruits in general. Honey is contemptible because it is spit out by bees. But the lips are lips (there is no criticism of the second adhara); the lips belittle all of these.**

**Because of the special statement “They do not compare with those lips”, the idea that Her lips are praised is suggested in the second word adhara, whereas the other repeated words in the verse have the sense of rejection.**

### 3.6

*yathā vā,*

**Перевод:**

**Another example of arthantara-sankramita:**

*premṇā vidrutam eka-vad yad ubhayos tan mānasaṁ mānasaṁ*  
*sarvāsv eva daśāsu yan nava-navaṁ tat sauhṛdaṁ sauhṛdam*  
*yat kṛṣṇasya vinoda-bhūr ahar ahas tad yauvanaṁ yauvanaṁ*  
*tad-viccheda-vidhau na yat-paricayas taj jīvanaṁ jīvanam*

**Пословный перевод:**

premna—due to love; vidrutam—being melted; eka-vat—(appears) as if one; yat—which (heart); ubhayoh—of the two (lovers); tat— that; manasam—heart; manasam—real heart; sarvasu—at every; eva—indeed; dasasu—stage; yat—which (love); nava-navam—is ever fresh; tat—that; sauhrdam—friendship (i.e. love); sauhrdam— real love; yat—which (youth); krsnasya—Krsna’s; vinoda—of happiness; bhuh—the abode; ahah ahah—every day; tat—that yauvanam—youth; yauvanam—real youth; tat—from Krsna; viccheda—of separation; vidhau—on the occasion; na—not; yat— of which (life); paricayah—existence; tat—that; jlvanam—life; jlvanam—is real life.

**Перевод:**

**\[Agitated because Krsna went to Mathura, Radha speaks to a confidante:\]**

**The hearts of two lovers which melt as if they were one, out of love, are hearts. The love between two persons which is ever fresh in every situation is love. If Krsna takes pleasure every day of one’s youth, that is youth. When on the occasion of separation from Krsna a person ceases to live, that life was a life.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: The idea is “that heart is a real heart.”’ There is no desire to express the literal meaning in the second word heart. The suggestion, which arises from laksana-vrtti, is that such a heart is praiseworthy (Subodhini). The implied sense is a vastu- dhvani (implied idea).

### 3.7

*sva-viparītārthenākrāntaṁ yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**This illustrates atyanta-tiraskrta**  
**(the literal meaning is obliterated):**

*saubhāgyam etad adhikaṁ mama nātha kṛṣṇa*  
*prāṇair mamātani sukhaṁ praṇayena kīrtiḥ*  
*dṛṣṭaś cirād asi kṛpāpi taveyam uccair*  
*na smaryate na bhavatātma-gṛhasya mārgaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

saubhagyam—good fortune; etat—this; adhikam—great; mama— my; natha—O master (of my life airs); krsna—O Krsna; pranaih— by the life airs; mama—my; atani—was increased; sukham— happiness; pranayena—because of your love for me; kirtih—fame; drstah—have been seen; cirad—after a long time; asi—you; krpa—mercy; api—also; tava—your; iyam—this; uccair—great; na smaryate—not remembered; na—not; bhavata—by you; atma- grhasya—of my house; margah—the path.

**Перевод:**

**\[A gopi is angry at Krsna for showing up late at the rendezvous:\]**

**Krsna, my love! Your arrival is my great good fortune! My vitality has increased my happiness, and my prestige has expanded because of Your love for me. I can see You now after so long because of Your great mercy. It’s not that You forgot the way to my house.**

*atra saubhāgyam ity asaubhāgyam, sukham iti duḥkham, kīrtir akīrtiḥ, kṛpākṛpā, ātma-gṛhasyeti para-gṛhasyeti, svaviparītenākrāntam.*

**Перевод:**

**In this verse, good fortune means misfortune, happiness means misery, fame means infamy, mercy means cruelty, and “my house” means “another’s house”. In this way, the literal meaning is obliterated by the opposite meaning.**

**Комментарий:**

Here the figurative usage is called viparita-laksana (irony) (the opposite sense). Nevertheless, the sense of “It’s not that You forgot the way to my house” as “You didn’t forget Your way to the other girl’s domicile” is obtained by Mammata’s tatparya (the Purport), because it is simply a rewording. It can be classed as the paryayokta ornament (circumlocution) (8.202).

### 3.8

*dhvanir yas tv abhidhā-mūlas tatra vācyaṁ vivakṣitam (4cd)*

**Пословный перевод:**

dhvanih—implied meaning; yah—which; tu—but; abhidha- mulah—which has its roots in Denotation; tatra—in that; vacyam— the literal meaning; vivaksitam—is desired to be expressed.

**Перевод:**

**When the implied sense arises from Denotation, however, the literal meaning is intended to be expressed.**

### 3.9

*tathāpi vyaṅgya-niṣṭhaṁ syāt*  
*sa ca dvai-vidhyam ṛcchati*  
*ko ’pi lakṣya-krama-vyaṅgyo*  
*’lakṣya-vyaṅgya-kramo ’paraḥ (5)*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatha api — still; vyangya—in a suggested meaning; nistham— which culminates; syat—is; sah—that \[ abhidha-mula-dhvani \]; ca— and; dvai-vidhyam—the state of being twofold; rcchati—attains; kah api—one of them; laksya—that is perceivable; krama—has a sequence of appearance; vyangyah—is one in which the suggested meaning; alaksya—is not perceivable; vyangya—of the suggested meaning; kramah—is one where the sequence of appearance; aparah—the other one.

**Перевод:**

**An implied sense based on Denotation has two broad categories: (1) laksya-krama-vyangya (vastu-dhvani and alankara-dhvani) and (2) alaksya-krama-vyangya (rasadi-dhvani).**

*abhidhā-mūla-dhvanau tu vivakṣitam api vācyaṁ vyaṅgya-niṣṭham. sa ca dhvanir lakṣya-krama-vyaṅgyo ’lakṣya-vyaṅgya-kramaś ceti dvi-vidhaḥ. lakṣyaṁ krama-prāptaṁ vyaṅgyaṁ yatra sa tathā, alakṣyo vyaṅgyasya kramo yatra sa tathā. kramas tu vibhāvādibhir vyajyamāna eva rasaḥ, na tu vibhāvādaya iti. lāghavāc chatapatrapatra-śatī-yugapad-vedhābhimāna-vad yatra kramo na lakṣyate, sa tāvad akramaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**In abhidha-mula-dhvani, the literal meaning, which is meant to be expressed, leads to an implied meaning. And that dhvani has two varieties. Laksya-krama-vyangya is so called because the implied sense has a perceivable sequence. (The rise of the implied sense in the mind is noticed.)**

**Alaksya-krama-vyangya, however, is so called because the sequence of the rise of the implied sense is not perceivable. In this one, the “sequence” refers to the rasa implied by the vibhavas, an anubhava, and a vyabhicari. The sequence does not refer to the vibhavas and so on themselves. It is said that the sequence is not perceived by the analogy that piercing one hundred lotus petals at once with a needle is not perceived to be sequential, because of quickness.**

### 3.10

*raso bhāvas tad-ābhāso bhāva-śānty-ādir akramaḥ (6)*

**Перевод:**

**The dhvani called alaksya-krama-vyangya has these varieties: rasa-dhvani, bhava-dhvani, rasabhasa-dhvani, bhavabhasa- dhvani, bhava-santi-dhvani, and so on.**

*rasādis tv akramo ’lakṣya-krama-vyaṅgya ity arthaḥ. ādi-śabdād bhāvodaya-bhāva-śābalya-bhāva-sandhayaḥ. ayam alakṣyakrama-vyaṅgyo rasa-nirūpaṇe darśayiṣyate.*

**Перевод:**

**Thus the rasadi-dhvanis are alaksya-krama-vyangya. In the sutra, the etceteras are bhavodaya, bhava-sabalya, and bhava- sandhi.**

**This type of abhidha-mula-dhvani, called alaksya-krama- vyangya, will be illustrated ahead in the chapter on rasa.**

### 3.11

*yatrānudhvaninā vyaṅgyaṁ*  
*lakṣyate krama-pūrvakam*  
*sa tu lakṣya-krama-vyaṅgyaḥ*  
*śabdārthobhaya-śakti-bhūḥ (7)*

**Пословный перевод:**

yatra—where; anudhvanina—as an anudhvani; vyafgyam—what is suggested; laksyate—is perceived; krama-purvakam—by means of a sequence; sah—that; tu—but; laksya-krama-vyafgyah—where the suggested meaning has a sequence of rising that is perceived; sabda—of the word; artha—of the meaning; ubhaya—or of both the word and its meaning; sakti—from the potency; bhuh—arises.

**Перевод:**

**In laksya-krama-vyangya (vastu-dhvani and alankara-dhvani), the implied meaning arises as an anudhvani by means of a sequence. That implied sense originates either from sabda- sakti, from artha-sakti, or from ubhaya-sakti.**

*anudhvanir anuraṇanaṁ, dhvaner eva dīrgha-dīrgha-bhāvaḥ, pratidhvanir iva vā. sa tu lakṣya-krama-vyaṅgyaḥ śabda-śaktibhūḥ, artha-śakti-bhūḥ, śabdārthobhaya-śakti-bhūś ceti tridhā.*

**Перевод:**

**Anudhvani means anuranana, which means either “prolongation of sound” or “echo”. There are three kinds of laksya-krama- vyangya, since the dhvani is either sabda-sakti-bhu (it arises by the power of the word), artha-sakti-bhu (it arises by the power of the meaning), or ubhaya-sakti-bhu (it arises by both the power of a word and the power of a meaning).**

**Комментарий:**

The difference between the power of the word and the power of the meaning is like the difference between sabda-slesa and artha-slesa (7.73). If the suggestive word could be replaced with a synonym without affecting the implied sense, then the dhvani is said to arise from artha-sakti.

In the elaboration, Kavi Karnapura hints that the word dhvani used in poetics originates from the word anudhvani in general language. Patanjali used the word dhvani in the sense of “prolongation of sound” (Mahabhasya 1.1.70).

### 3.12

*ādyo dvidhaivālaṅkāra-vastunor dyotanād bhavet (8)*

**Пословный перевод:**

adyah—the first one; dvidha—twofold; eva—only; alankara- vastunoh—an alankara (literary ornament) or a vastu (“the idea suggested”); dyotanat—on account of suggesting; bhavet—is.

**Перевод:**

**The first variety, sabda-sakti-bhu dhvani, has only two varieties: alankara-dhvani and vastu-dhvani.**

*ādyaḥ śabda-śakti-bhūr dvidhaiva bhavet. eva-kāras tu arthaśakti-bhava-vat śabda-śakti-bhavo ’pi dvādaśadheti, para-mataṁ vyāvartayati, athavālaṅkārasyaiva, vastuna eva, nānyataraviśiṣṭasyaivety arthaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**The word eva (only) is used to reject the opinion of others that sabda-sakti-bhu has twelve kinds like artha-sakti-bhu. Or else the word eva may be connected with the words alankara and vastu separately, meaning “because of suggesting only an alankara or only a vastu,” that is to say “neither an alankara nor a vastu characterized by something else.”**

### 3.13

*atrālaṅkāra-dyotakaḥ śabda-śakti-bhūr yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**This illustrates a sabda-sakti-bhu alankara-dhvani (ornament implied by the force of the words):**

*āśā-mātre vilasad-udayaḥ padminī-cakra-bandhuḥ*  
*siddhābhogaḥ satatam aniśāmoda-maitrī-kaṣāyaḥ*  
*rādhāśleṣādiṣu niravadhi-vyāpṛtaḥ śoṇa-pādo*  
*rociḥ-pūrair haratu bhajatāṁ śītatāṁ kṛṣṇa-candraḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

asa-matre—when there is a mere desire (or, in any direction (i.e. at any time, for those who worship Him)), (or, \[the moon rises\] merely in one direction); vilasat—splendidly; udayah— whose arising; padmini—of beautiful women (or lotuses); cakra—of multitudes; bandhuh—who is the friend; siddha—is accomplished; abhogah—whose enjoyment, or fullness; satatam— always; anisa—is continuous, or anisa: at times other than night; amoda—and bliss; maitri—friendship; kasayah—whose sweetness; radha-slesa—embracing Radha; adisu—in activities such as, (or, radha-aslesa-adisu: toward Radha, Aslesa, and other constellations); niravadhi—always; vyaprtah—engaged; sona— are reddish (indicating softness); padah—whose feet (or rays); rocih—of beauty (or radiance); puraih—with its flood; haratu— may he take away; bhajatam—for those who worship; sitatam— dullness (or coolness); krsna-candrah—the Krsna moon.

**Перевод:**

**May the Krsna moon, by its flood of effulgence, take away the coldness of those who worship Him. (The Krsna moon gives warmth, whereas the normal moon gives coolness.) He is the friend ofpadmims. (The Krsna moon is the friend of beautiful women whereas the moon is not the friend of daytime lotuses.) He is always taking pleasure (abhoga). (But the usual moon is full, abhoga, only once a month.) His bliss, friendship and sweetness are perpetual. (But the moon’s only occur at night.) The Krsna moon is always embracing Radha. (But the moon is only in conjunction with the constellations such as Radha and Aslesa once every twenty-seven days.) Krsna has soft reddish feet (pada). (But the moon’s rays, pada, are white.) He splendidly appears whenever His devotees desire Him (asa). (But the full moon only rises in one direction (asa).)**

*atra śabda-śakty-udbhutaś candra iti prasiddha-candrād vyatiriktair akhilair eva guṇair vyatirekālaṅkāro dhvanitaḥ. yady apy asau dhvanitvenālaṅkārya eva, tathāpi brāhmaṇa-śramaṇanyāyenālaṅkāra eva. evam anye ’pi.*

**Перевод:**

**The vyatireka ornament (contrast with similitude) is implied by the force of the word candra (in “the Krsna moon”) since all the qualities mentioned are different than the famous moon’s.**

**Even though it is an alankarya, as a dhvani, the dhvani is still called an alankara in accordance with the logic called brahmana- sramana (a renunciant is called a Brahmana although officially he is no longer a Brahmana). This should be understood in other instances of alankara-dhvani also.**

**Комментарий:**

The word sramana is a synonym of avadhuta. A sramana is a naked sage (Bhagavatam [11.6.47](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/6.47)). It seems contradictory to call a sramana “a Brahmana”. But by considering that he was previously a Brahmana, the designation makes sense. According to the Narada- parivrajaka Upanisad (5.1), avadhuta is the sixth and final stage of Sannyasa, after kuticaka, bahudaka, hamsa, paramahamsa and turiyatita.

A dhvani is alankarya (what has to be embellished) in the sense that it should be the focal point of the literary embellishment. Thus, although it is an alankarya-dhvani, it is called alankara-dhvani because of the convention, though by definition an alankara is something that adorns the body. The body of poetry is the sounds and the expressed meanings.

The dhvani is classed as sabda-sakti-bhu because many words cannot be changed, since they are paronomastic. Although artha- sakti occurs in the verse, it is not as prominent as sabda-sakti, therefore the dhvani is not classed as ubhaya-sakti-bhu.

### 3.14

**Перевод:**

**\[This illustrates a sabda-sakti-bhu vastu-dhvani:\]**

*dadhatī sa-madhupa-rāgaṁ*  
*parimalam ekānta-sukumārā*  
*guṇa-kalitā lalite mama*  
*bhūṣita-kaṇṭhā tvam eva vana-mālā*

**Пословный перевод:**

dadhati—possessing; sa-madhupa—for the bees (or, \[for Me\] who am drinking the nectar \[of your lips\]); ragam—\[the fragrance\] which is accompanied by affection, (or, \[romanticbliss\] accompanied by love); parimalam—the fragrance (or erotic bliss); ekanta—totally; su-kumara—very fresh (or very soft); guna—with a thread (or with qualities); kalita—endowed; lalite—O Lalita; mama—My; bhusita- kantha—by whom the neck is ornamented; tvam—you; eva—only; vana-mala—are a garland of forest flowers.

**Перевод:**

**Lalita, My garland of forest flowers has a thread and is extremely fresh and soft. It possesses a fragrance that attracts the bees. Only you are that garland ornamenting My neck.**

**\[Implied meaning:\]**

**Lalita, only you are the garland of forest flowers decorating My neck. You have many qualities and your body is very soft. You possess erotic bliss endowed with love for Me who am the drinker of the nectar of your lips.**

*atra śabda-śaktyā kaver vana-mālā-lalitayoḥ sādharmyaṁ nirūpya prayāse vyuparate sati vastu-bhūtaḥ kaścid arthaḥ sphurati. sa ca tvam eva vana-mālā, nānyeti, tvāṁ praty eva me samādaraḥ, na tu tasyām, tena tvad-āliṅganam eva me preya iti vastu.*

**Перевод:**

**When the poet’s endeavor has stopped after describing the similarities between the garland and Lalita by sabda-sakti, a certain meaning, an idea, comes out: “You alone, not any other girl, are My garland.” The implied vastu is: “I only care for you, not for Her. Therefore I only want your embrace.”**

### 3.15

*artha-śakty-udbhavo ’rthas tu vyañjakaḥ svayam-udbhavī*  
*kaveḥ prauḍhokti-niṣpanno vaktus tat-kalpitasya ca (9)*

**Пословный перевод:**

artha—of the meaning; sakti—from the power; udbhavah—arising; arthah—the meaning; tu—but; vyanjakah—suggestive; svayam— by itself; udbhavi—arising; kaveh—of the poet; praudha—bold; ukti—words; nispannah—effected by; vaktuh—of the speaker; kalpitasya —who is invented by him (the poet); ca—and.

**Перевод:**

**The suggestive sense that arises from the power of the meaning (artha-sakti) has three varieties: (1) svatah-sambhavi (naturally possible in day-to-day life), (2) kavi-praudhokti-nispanna (created by the poet’s bold words), and (3) kavi-nibaddha-vaktr- praudhokti-nispanna (created by the bold words of a speaker invented by the poet).**

*artha-śakty-udbhavo yo dhvaniḥ, sa tridhā bhavati—svataḥsambhavī, kavi-prauḍhokti-niṣpanna-śarīraḥ, tan-nibaddhavaktṛ-prauḍhokti-niṣpanna-śarīraś ceti. tatra svataḥ-sambhavī na kevalaṁ kavi-bhaṇita-mātra-niṣpannaḥ, vyavahāre ’pi samucitatvena sambhāvyamānaḥ. anyau kavinā tan-nibaddhavaktrā ca pratibhāna-mātreṇa vyavahārāsiddhāv api nirmitau.*

**Перевод:**

**The implied sense that arises from the power of the meaning has three varieties. The first one is called svatah-sambhavi because the same implied sense could suitably occur in real life, thus it is not merely invented by the poet. In the two other varieties, the dhvani is merely invented by the poet and so it would not suitably occur in day-to-day life. In these two, the suggestive meaning’s body (words and their meanings) is created by the poet and by a speaker invented by the poet respectively.**

**Комментарий:**

In the methodology of artha-sakti-bhu dhvani, the literal meaning of the text is classed in one of the above three categories. The literal sense suggests a meaning, and that implied sense suggests another meaning, for a total of twelve categories. All the types of dhvanis also apply to second-rate poetry. Sometimes the first suggestive meaning is not implied.

### 3.16

*vastutvālaṅkṛtatvābhyāṁ te dvai-vidhyena ṣaṭ smṛtāḥ (10)*

*te trayo bhedā vastu-rūpatayālaṅkāra-rūpatayā ca ṣaṭ prakārāḥ syuḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

vastutva-alankrtatvabhyam—because of being a vastu or being an alankara; te—those \[three varieties\]; dvai-vidhyena—on account of being twofold; sat—six; smrtah—are considered.

**Перевод:**

**Those three varieties become six because the implied sense is either a vastu or an alankara.**

### 3.17

*vastunā vastv-alaṅkārāv alaṅkāreṇa teṣu cet*  
*vyajyete ’py alaṅkāra-vastunī dvādaśāpi tat (11)*

*teṣu ṣaḍ-vidheṣu ced yadi vastunā vastu cālaṅkāraś ca vyajyate, alaṅkāreṇa alaṅkāro vastu ca vyajyate, tat—tadā dvādaśāpi bhavantīty arthaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

vastuna—by an idea; vastu-alankarau—a vastu and an alankara; alankarena—by a literary ornament; tesu—among those \[six types of artha-sakti-bhu dhvanis\]; cet—if; vyajyete—are implied; api—also; alankara-vastuni—an alankara and a vastu; dvadasa— twelve; api—even; tat—then.

**Перевод:**

**If the vastu-dhvani or the alankara-dhvam is suggestive, then the artha-sakti-bhu dhvani has twelve varieties, since the vastu-dhvani or the alankara-dhvani suggests either a vastu or an alankara.**

### 3.18

*krameṇodāharaṇāni,*

**Перевод:**

**Examples are shown in order. \[This is a svatah-sambhavi vastu- dhvani that suggests another vastu-dhvani,\]**

*ga-ula-mahinda-ṇandaṇa suṇṇa-ghare ettha mā pavisa*  
*ujja sahīe sāmī gomī dūraṁ gao goṭṭham*  
*(Śaurasenī Prakrit)*

*gokula-mahendra-nandana śūnya-gṛhe ’tra mā praviśa*  
*adya sakhyāḥ svāmī gomān dūraṁ gato goṣṭham*  
*(Sanskrit rendering)*

**Пословный перевод:**

gokula—of Gokula; maha-indra—of the king; nandana—O son; sunya-grhe—empty house; atra—in this; ma—do not; pravisa— enter; adya—today; sakhyah—of my friend; svami—the husband; goman—who possesses many cows; duram—far; gatah—has gone; gostham—to the pasturing grounds.

**Перевод:**

**Prince of Gokula, don’t enter this house. Today my friend’s husband, who has many cows, has gone far away to the pasturing grounds.**

*atra svāmī, na tu priyaḥ. gomī bahvīnāṁ gavāṁ patiḥ, tena śīghraṁ nāyāsyati. dūram, na tu nedīyaḥ, ataś ciraṁ vyāpyāsyā gṛhaṁ śūnyaṁ bhāvi. tenātra niḥśaṅkam eva praviśya vilasyatām iti vastu.*

**Перевод:**

**The word svami (husband, lit. master) signifies that he is not loved. Goman means he has many cows: Thus he will not return quickly. Duram (far away) signifies that he is not around. Therefore this sakhi’s home will be empty for a long time (this is the first vastu). Because of that, the lover can fearlessly go to that house and take pleasure (this is the second vastu).**

**Комментарий:**

Artha-sakti occurs here because most of the suggestive words could be replaced with synonyms without affecting the implied sense.

The speaker is indirectly inciting Krsna to go to her friend’s house, by means of viparita-laksana (opposite meaning), and so the first sentence is classed in laksana-mula atyanta-tiraskrta-vacya dhvani (implied sense based on Indication where the literal sense “Don’t enter” is completely obliterated). The second sentence of the verse illustrates the topic at hand.

### 3.19

**Перевод:**

**\[A svatah-sambhavi vastu-dhvani occasions an alankara-dhvani, \]**

*śrūyate parimale mala-śabdo*  
*mekhalādiṣu khalādy-abhiyogaḥ*  
*candanādi-rasa eva hi paṅko*  
*nīvi-keśa-rasanādiṣu bandhaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

sruyate—is heard; parimale—\[in the word\] parimala (fragrance, or erotic bliss); mala-sabdah—the word mala (dirt, impurity); mekhala—in the word mekhala (belt); adisu—and so on; khala— of the word khala (wicked man); adi—etc.; abhiyogah—the usage; candana—\[such as\] sandalwood paste; adi—etc.; rase—in reference to ointments; eva—only; hi—but; pankah—\[the word\] panka (mud); nivi—petticoat; kesa—hair; rasana—rope; adisu—in \[...\] and so on; bandhah— \[the word\] bandha (bondage).

**Перевод:**

**In Vraja, the word mala is only heard in the word parimala, and the usage of the term khala is only heard in connection with the word mekhala. Similarly, the word panka is only used in reference to ointments such as sandalwood paste, and the word bandha is only heard in reference to items such as a petticoat, a girdle, hair, and so on.**

*atra kaver aprayāsa-racana-balād vraja-loke malādy-abhāvo vastu-bhūto ’rthaḥ svataḥ-sambhavī, tena svabhāvokty-alaṅkāra iti dvedhā.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the meaning, the idea “There is no impurity (mala) and so on in Vraja”, is svatah sambhavi insofar as the poet didn’t have to make much of an effort to compose. The svabhavokti ornament (the nature) is implied by that idea. Thus two kinds of svatah-sambhavi have been shown so far.**

**Комментарий:**

Kunkuma-panka and candana-panka are types of ointments. A nivi-bandha is a petticoat but it also refers to the ends of that cloth tied into a knot in front of the body. A kesa-bandha is a hair-band, and a rasana-bandha (rasana-bandha) is a knot made with the ends of a girdle.

### 3.20

**Перевод:**

**\[The first half of this verse illustrates a svatah-sambhavi alankara-dhvani that suggests a vastu, and the second half illustrates a svatah-sambhavi alankara-dhvani that suggests another alankara,\]**

*gañjanān na hi bibheṣi gurūṇāṁ*  
*khañjanākṣi yamunām adhunāgāḥ*  
*añjanābha iha kuñjara ekaḥ*  
*kañja-nāla-dala-bhañjana-kārī*

**Пословный перевод:**

ganjanat—the chastisement; na—not; hi—certainly; bibhesi—you fear; gurunam—of the superiors; khanjana-aksi—O you whose eyes move back and forth like the tail of a wagtail bird; yamunam—to the Yamuna; adhuna—right now; agah—you have gone; anjana— \[is like the color of\] eyeliner; abhah—whose bodily complexion; iha—in this place; kunjarah—elephant; ekah—one; kanja-nala—of lotuses; dala—petals; bhanjana-kari—whose habit is to damage.

**Перевод:**

**Wagtail-eyed girl, you don’t fear your elders’ chastisement. Now you have come to the Yamuna. In this place is an elephant which has the color of eyeliner and whose habit is to damage lotus petals.**

*atra sakhīṁ prati sakhī vadati. kañjanākṣīti sambodhanamaryādayā sakhī-rūpo vaktā. adhuneti akāle ’pi yad agās tena snātuṁ nāgāḥ, kṛṣṇa-saṅgāyaivāgā iti kāvya-liṅgālaṅkāras tena tvaṁ gurūṇāṁ gañjanān na bibheṣīti guru-gañjane tava bhayaṁ nāsti, yathā kṛṣṇāṅga-saṅga-virahe iti vastu dhvanyate. evaṁ kuñjara iti kṛṣṇa-nāmāpahnavenāpahnuty-alaṅkāreṇa kṛṣṇakuñjarayoḥ sādṛśya-vyañjanād upamālaṅkāraś ceti, svataḥsambhavinaḥ śloka-trayeṇa cātur-vidhyam.*

**Перевод:**

**One sakhi speaks to another. We can infer that the speaker is a female friend because the word kanjanaksi is a customary vocative. The word adhuna (now) suggests this: “That you have gone at an unusual time means you didn’t go for bathing; you went to meet Krsna.” The kavya-linga ornament (explanatory reason) thus takes place. Next, “You don’t fear your elders’ chastisement,” which means “In separation from the touch of Krsna’s body, you have no fear of their rebuke.” That is the vastu suggested by the kavya-linga.**

**The apahnuti ornament (concealment) occurs since Krsna’s name is concealed: Only the word kunjara (elephant) is used. A simile is implied by that on account of the suggestion of similarity between Krsna and an elephant. Thus the four kinds of svatah-sambhavi have been explained with these three verses.**

**Комментарий:**

Other poetical theorists would say that the concealment is not apahnuti but the first variety of the atisayokti ornament (introsusception) (8.114). Moreover, the simile inherently involved in another ornament, such as an atisayokti, is a second-rate implied sense.

Further, the compound kanja-nala-dala-bhanjana-kari means: “It has the habit of damaging petals on the stalks of lotuses.” In this way Krsna is compared to an elephant since He damages the lotus­petal-like lips of the gopis when He kisses them. That the girls end up with bruised lips is a reason the girls fear the elders.

### 3.21

*kavi-prauḍhokteś catur-vidhyaṁ yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**The following verses are examples of the four kinds of the artha-sakti-bhu dhvani which is kavi-praudhokti (created by the poet’s bold words).**

**\[In the first half of the verse, a kavi-praudhokti vastu-dhvani suggests another vastu, and in the second half a kavi-praudhokti alankara-dhvani suggests another alankara.\]**

*spandate yadi padādi tadāsāṁ*  
*syandate madhurimāmṛta-dhārā*  
*saṅgataḥ pavana-jād vratatīnām*  
*aṅgato madhu-kaṇā iva bhūmau*

**Пословный перевод:**

spandate—moves; yadi—if; pada-adi—a limb such as a foot; tada—then; asam—of these \[gopis\]; syandate—rains down; madhurima—of sweetness; amrta-dhara—a nectarean shower; sangatah—because of the contact; pavana-jat—which manifests because of the wind; vratatinam—of the vines; angatah—from a part; madhu-kanah—drops of nectar; iva—just as; bhumau—on the ground.

**Перевод:**

**If the gopis move their feet, a gush of ambrosia in the form of sweetness rains like drops of nectar from creepers fall on the ground because of the contact occasioned by the wind.**

*atra kavi-prauḍhoktir eva, na pūrva-vat svataḥ-sambhavī sa cārthaḥ. yāsāṁ padādi-spandana-mātreṇāpy evaṁ mādhuryarasa-pratipattir ity aho āsāṁ lokottarateti vastu-bhūto ’rthaḥ. sa ca tāsāṁ rāsādi-nṛtya-vidhau vā kīdṛśa iti vastu vyanaktīti vastunā vastu. uttarārdhe vratatīnāṁ pavana-jāt saṅgāt madhu-kaṇā iveti tāsām api vratatibhir upamety upamālaṅkāreṇa svabhāvoktyalaṅkāro dhvanita iti dvedhā.*

**Перевод:**

**The verse only involves the bold words of the poet: The meaning is not svatah-sambhavi as before.**

**Since by the mere movements of their feet the gopis create such madhurya-rasa, the meaning, an idea, is that these gopis are out of this world. “So how much impressive must that sweetness be while they dance in Rasa-lfla!” In this way a vastu gives rise to another vastu.**

**A simile takes place in the second half of the verse: “like drops of nectar from creepers fall on the ground because of the contact occasioned by the wind.” Thus the gopis are compared to creepers. And this simile occasions the svabhavokti ornament (the nature). Thus two kinds of kavi-praudhokti have been shown so far.**

### 3.22

**Перевод:**

**\[Here a kavi-praudhokti vastu-dhvani suggests an alankara,\]**

*gokule kulaja-bāla-vadhūnāṁ*  
*śyāma-dhāmani manoratha-bhājām*  
*nojjagāma na jagāma virāmaṁ*  
*sauhṛdaṁ hṛdaya eva jughūrṇe*

**Пословный перевод:**

gokule—in Gokula; kula-ja—born in respectable families; bala— young; vadhunam—of the girls; syama—is dark blue; dhamani— toward Him whose bodily complexion; manoratha—ardent desires; bhajam—of those who possess; na ujjagama—didn’t arise; na jagama—didn’t attain; viramam—cessation; sauhrdam—love; hrdaye—in the heart; eva—only; jughurne—bounced around.

**Перевод:**

**In Gokula, the love of the well-mannered girls for that bluish fellow did not surge, nor did it cease. Rather, it kept bouncing in their hearts.**

*atra kavi-prauḍhoktiḥ. nojjagāmeti lajjādhikyaṁ vastu, na jagāma virāmam iti hṛdaya-kṣobhātiśayo ghūrṇatvenotprekṣita iti utprekṣālaṅkāraś ca.*

**Перевод:**

**This is kavi-praudhokti (because love does not literally bounce). The words “Love did not surge” suggest the idea that the gopis had an increase of bashfulness.**

**Moreover, that their love did not cease implies an extreme agitation of the heart (this is a vastu-dhvani), an agitation imagined to be moving around wildly. This is an implied utpreksa ornament (fanciful assumption).**

### 3.23

**Перевод:**

**\[A kavi-praudhokti alankara-dhvani occasions a vastu,\]**

*stumaḥ kiṁ tvām ambhodhara-subhaga śambhor adhi-śiraḥ*  
*padāmbhojasyāmbho yad akṛta padaṁ bhos tava tataḥ*  
*umāyai dattvārdhaṁ vapur aparam ardhaṁ ca bhavate*  
*guṇebhyo nirmuktaḥ sa param abhavad brahma parama*

**Пословный перевод:**

stumah—we praise; kim—whether; tvam—You; ambhah- dhara—like a cloud (“water bearer”); subhaga—O You who are beautiful; sambhuh—of Sambhu; adhi-sirah—on the head; pada ambhojasya—of His lotus feet; ambhah—the water (Ganga); yat—because; akrta—was made (aorist tense); padam—an abode; bhoh—(vocative term); tava—Your; tatah—therefore; umayai— unto Uma; dattva—having given; ardham—half; vapuh—his body; aparam—the other; ardham—half; ca—and; bhavate—unto You; gunebhyah—from the three modes of material nature; nirmuktah— freed; sah—he (Siva); param—supreme; abhavat—became; brahma—Brahman; parama—O supreme person.

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, You are splendid like a raincloud. The Ganges, the water that washed Your lotus feet, made her abode on Sambhu’s head. And he became thoroughly freed from the modes of material nature and merged in Brahman by offering one half of his body to Uma and the other half to You. Therefore, O Supreme Lord, shall we not praise You?**

*atra kavi-prauḍhoktiḥ. tatra śambhor adhi-śiro yad yasmāt tava padāmbhaḥ padam akṛta, tena tvam anya eva ko ’pi sarvoparivartamānaḥ stava-viṣayo nety atiśayokty-alaṅkāraḥ. tena umāyai dattvārdhaṁ vapur aparam ardhaṁ ca bhavata ity-ādinā sa vapurviraheṇa paraṁ brahmābhavat, tvaṁ tu vapuṣaiva paraṁ brahma iti vastu, iti kavi-prauḍhoktiś catur-vidhā.*

**Перевод:**

**This is kavi-praudhokti (since those pastimes are not ordinary). The words “Your foot water made its abode on Siva’s head” suggest the atisayokti ornament (statement of superexcellence): “Therefore only You are a worthy object of praise. No one else exists above all.” Consequently, an implied idea is: “Siva attained Brahman by separating himself from his body—in reference to “by offering one half of his body to Uma and the other half to You”—, but You are Brahman in living form.”**

**Thus the four kinds of kavi-praudhokti have been shown.**

### 3.24

*kavi-nibaddha-vaktṛ-prauḍhoktir yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**Now the artha-sakti-bhu dhvani which is kavi-nibaddha-vaktr- praudhokti (created by the uncommon words of a speaker invented by the poet) will be illustrated. \[Here a vastu-dhvani occasions an alankara-dhvani: \]**

*paripuṭṭe paripuṭṭaṁ jhīṇe jhīṇaṁ samammi samaṁ*  
*māhava tīe aṅgaṁ tujjha siṇeheṇa ghaḍiaṁ va*  
*(Śaurasenī Prakrit)*

*paripuṣṭe paripuṣṭaṁ kṣīṇe kṣīṇaṁ same samam*  
*mādhava tasyā aṅgaṁ tava snehena ghaṭitam eva*  
*(Sanskrit rendering)*

**Пословный перевод:**

paripuste—when \[Your love for her\] increases; paripustam—\[her body is\] expanded; ksine—when \[Your love for her\] decreases; ksinam—\[her body is\] emaciated; same—when \[Your love for her\] is normal; samam— \[her body is\] normal; madhava—O Madhava; tasyah—her; angam—body; tava snehena—according to Your love; ghatitam—is fashioned; eva—certainly.

**Перевод:**

**Madhava, that girl’s body changes shape in accordance with Your love for her. When Your love increases, her body becomes plump; when Your love decreases, her body becomes thin; and when Your love is as usual, her body stays normal.**

*atra sā āyuṣā jīvatīti na, api tu tava snehenaiveti vastu. “tujja siṇeheṇa ghaḍiaṁ va” iti tasyā aṅgaṁ tvat-snehopādānam iti aṅgāntarād vyatiriktaṁ tad-aṅgam iti vyatirekālaṅkāraḥ, iti vastunālaṅkāraḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**In this verse, the vastu is: “This girl is living by Your love, not by the measure of her lifespan.” The words “Her body changes shape in accordance with Your love for her” suggest that since Krsna’s love is the fundamental ingredient of her body, her body is very different than others’. This is the vyatireka ornament (contrast). In this way a vastu suggests an alankara.**

### 3.25

*śruti-yugam abhidhatte śrīla-vṛndāvane ’sī-*  
*ty anu diśam iti netra-dvandvam ātmā hṛdīti*  
*kva nu bhavasi mahātman brūhi kaṣṭāsavo ’mī*  
*tvad-anusaraṇa-pānthāḥ kaṇṭha eva bhramanti*

**Пословный перевод:**

sruti—of ears; yugam—the pair; abhidhatte—says; srila- vrndavane—in Sri Vmdavana; asi—You are; iti—thus; anu disam—in every direction; iti—thus; netra-dvandvam—the pair of eyes; atma—intelligence; hrdi—is in the heart; iti—thus; kva— where; nu—actually; bhavasi—are You; mahatman—O great soul; bruhi—please tell; kasta—paining; asavah—life airs; ami—these; tvat—You; anusarana—follows; panthah—\[the life airs\] whose path; kanthe—in the throat; eva—only; bhramanti—wander.

**Перевод:**

**My ears say You’re in Vrndavana, my eyes say You’re everywhere, and my intelligence says You’re in the heart. Tell me, O magnanimous one, where actually are You? My irritating life airs, which follow You, are bewildered and keep wallowing in my throat.**

*atra kavi-nibaddhānurāginī bālā vaktrī. asyāḥ prauḍhoktau śabdapratyakṣānubhava-rūpaṁ pramāṇa-trayaṁ paraspara-vyāhatam api sarvam eva pramā-karaṇam, na tu kutrāpi aprāmāṇyam iti vastu, tena ca tvaṁ vyāpako ’sīti vastu, tena ekasya sarvānugatatvād virodhe virodhālaṅkāro vyatireko vā.*

*kva nu bhavasīti praśnena sandehālaṅkāraḥ, tena mahātmann iti kadācid yadi na brūṣe, tadā kapaṭī tvam iti hetv-alaṅkāraḥ. tena kaṣṭāsavo ’mī tvad-anusaraṇa-pānthāḥ kaṇṭha eva bhramantīti mad-asavaḥ saṁsthānaṁ tyaktavanta eva nirṇayam avijñāya kaṇṭha eva ghūrṇante, ato nirṇīya kathayatām iti vastu. idaṁ padyam asmad-guroḥ. iti kavi-nibaddha-vaktṛ-prauḍhoktiś caturdhā.*

**Перевод:**

**In this verse, the speaker is a passionate girl imagined by the poet. In this girl’s uncommon speech (praudhokti), the three pramanas (sabda,pratyaksa and anumana), although conflicting with one other, remain means of obtaining correct knowledge. The suggested idea is that nothing is impossible in Krsna. The idea implied by that is: Krsna is all pervading.**

**The virodha ornament (contradiction) is implied by that idea, since there is a contradiction in stating that one person is everywhere at the same time. Or \[if we consider that Krsna’s pastimes are transcendental,\] there is only the vyatireka ornament (contrast) (Krsna is incomparable).**

**The sandeha ornament (doubt) occurs due to the question “Where actually are You?” The reason He is not present is referred to in mahatman (O great soul). That is an implied hetu ornament (explanatory reason). The sense of mahatman is: “\[If you tell me, then you’re a magnaminous person, but\] if somehow you don’t tell me, then you’re not a magnanimous person, you’re just a cheater.”**

**Because of the sandeha, the statement “My paining life airs, which follow You, are wallowing in my throat” suggests the idea: “Giving up their proper places, my life airs are not sure where You are. Therefore tell me.”**

**This verse was written by my guru (Srinatha Pandita). Thus the four kinds of kavi-nibaddha-vaktr-praudhokti have been exemplified.**

### 3.26

*śabdārtha-bhūr eka eva (12a)*

**Перевод:**

**There is only one variety of ubhaya-sakti-bhu dhvani (implied sense arisen by both the power of a word and the power of a meaning).**

*śabdārthobhaya-śakty-uttho dhvanir eka eva. keṣāñcin mate ’trāpi vastv-alaṅkāra-sad-bhāvād aneka-vidhatvaṁ syāt, tannirāsāya eva-kāraḥ. kintu tan mataṁ na saṅgacchata iti na, tena likhiṣyamāṇa-bhedād adhikyam api bhedānām.*

**Перевод:**

**There is only one type of dhvani in this category. But some scholars think that ubhaya-sakti-bhu dhvani can be manifold in consideration of vastu and alankara. In this sutra, the word eva (only) is used to reject their opinion. However, it’s not that their opinion doesn’t make sense. For this reason, there are more varieties than the one illustrated below.**

### 3.27

*yathā,*

*aśeṣa-santāpa-haro janur-bhṛtāṁ*  
*sadābalā-kāmada-medura-dyutiḥ*  
*tviṣāṁ cayair mādhava jīvana-prado*  
*bhavān bhuvaṁ śyāmayate ghano nabhaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

asesa—all; santapa—suffering; harah—takes away; janur- bhrtam—of those who have bodies; sada—always; abala- kama-da—who gives lusty desires to ladies (or balaka-mada— which maddens the cranes); medura—is glossy; dyutih—whose effulgence; tvisam—of effulgence; cayaih—with masses; madhava—O Madhava; jivana-pradah—giver of life (or giver of water); bhavan—You; bhuvam—the ground; syamayate—makes dark); ghanah—a cloud; nabhah—the sky.

**Перевод:**

**Madhava, You dispel everyone’s suffering, and clouds do so too. Your effulgence is glossy and You always make women lusty, whereas clouds have a glossy luster that makes cranes constantly excited. You give life to all living beings, and the clouds send forth rain. With much effulgence You make the ground dark blue, while the clouds make the sky dark with their masses of effulgence.**

*para-mate ’trāpi vastv-alaṅkāra-sadbhāvaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**In the opinion of others, an ubhaya-sakti-bhu dhvani can be a vastu.**

**Комментарий:**

The verse features the artha-slesa ornament (pun) (8.88). Here it is combined with sabda-slesa (literal double meaning), as in verse 7.74. The way the verse works as an artha-slesa is: “O Madhava, You, as well as a cloud, dispel everyone’s suffering. You, as well as a cloud, are sadabala-kama-da-medura-dyuti. You, as well as a cloud, are jlvana-prada. Due to a mass of splendor, You darken the ground, and a cloud the sky.” Artha-slesa is based on artha-sakti, and sabda-slesa on sabda-sakti.

Visvanatha Cakravarti expounds: What is suggested in this verse is the ornament of meaning called upama (simile), a comparison between a cloud and Krsna, and there is no further suggestion. This suggestion arises because of the words’ power, since the suggesting is done through words that cannot be changed, such as balaka and jlvana. The suggestion also arises by the power of meanings because the suggesting is done by meanings that are produced from modifiers which can be changed, such as asesa-santapa-hara and tanu-bhrtam. In the elaboration, Kavi Karnapura refers to some poets who, with difficulty, posit the existence of vastus and alankaras in this category also.

### 3.28

*yathā vā,*

**Перевод:**

**Another example of**  
**ubhaya-sakti-bhu dhvani:**

*madhv-anta-kṛt sumanasām*  
*āmodair ghrāṇa-tarpaṇaḥ*  
*rādhādy-apara-paryāyo*  
*mādhavaḥ kasya na priyaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

madhu—of the demon Madhu (or of the month of Caitra); anta— the end; krt—it makes; sumanasam—of the sweet-hearted \[girls\] (or of the flowers); amodaih—with the aromas; ghrana—of the nose; tarpanah—causes satisfaction; radha-adi-apara-paryayah— whose synonyms are Radha and so on (or radha-adya-para- paryayah—the following of Radha done by whom is the first and the best); madhavah—Madhava (or Vaisakha); kasya—to whom; na priyah—not dear.

**Перевод:**

**\[First interpretation:\]**

**Who doesn’t like the month of Vaisakha? It brings the month of Caitra to an end. In Vaisakha, floral aromas satisfy the nose. This month is also known by other names such as Radha.**

**\[Second interpretation:\]**

**Who doesn’t like Madhava? He killed Madhu. With His bodily fragrance, He satisfies the noses of beautiful girls. He is Radha’s first and foremost follower.**

**Комментарий:**

Here also there is only one suggestion: Because of slesa (literal double meaning), which arises from sabda-sakti, there is an implied simile (upama alankara-dhvani) between Krsna and the month of Vaisakha. This suggestion arises by the power of words that cannot be changed without altering the implied sense: madhu, sumanas, radhady-apara-paryaya, and madhava. The suggestion also arises by the power of meanings (artha-sakti), since the simile is implied by means of words that can be changed, such as anta-krt, amoda, and ghrana.

### 3.29

*vākye ’ṣṭādaśadhā tv ime (12b)*

**Перевод:**

**The aforesaid eighteen varieties of dhvanis occur in a sentence.**

*ime ’ṣṭādaśadhā dhvanayo vākye bhavantīty arthaḥ. aṣṭādaśadhāsya tu avivakṣita-vācyasya dvau bhedau arthāntarasaṅkramitam atyanta-tiraskṛtaṁ ceti. vivakṣita-vācyasya ṣoḍaśa— asaṁlakṣya-krama-vyaṅgya ekaḥ, saṁlakṣya-krama-vyaṅgyaṁ ca pañcadaśa. tatra śabda-śakty-udbhavo dvau, artha-śakty-udbhavā dvādaśa, ubhaya-śakty-udbhava ekaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**The eighteen varieties of dhvanis are: The two kinds of avivaksita-vacya (laksana-mula), namely arthantara-sankramita and atyanta-tiraskrta, and the sixteen kinds of vivaksita-vacya (abhidha-mula).**

**The sixteen kinds of vivaksita-vacya are: one asamlaksya-krama- vyangya (rasadi-dhvani) and fifteen samlaksya-krama-vyangyas. Those fifteen are the two types of sabda-sakti-bhu dhvanis, the twelve kinds of artha-sakti-bhu dhvanis, and the one variety of ubhaya-sakti-bhu-dhvani.**

### 3.30

*vākya eva dvi-śakty-utthaḥ (13a)*

**Перевод:**

**A suggestion arisen from ubhaya-sakti can only occur in a sentence.**

*śabdārthobhaya-śakty-udbhavo dhvanir vākya eva. “idha vṛndāaṇa-majjhe” ity-ādi tad-udāharaṇam.*

**Перевод:**

**The implied sense that arises from both the power of words and the power of meanings occurs only in a sentence. For example:**

**In this forest of Vrndavana, the pleasure groves along the Yamuna, where the peacocks and deer sleep without any fear and the flowers are enjoyed only by the bees, is especially charming. (2.38)**

### 3.31

*pade saptadaśāpare (13b)*

**Перевод:**

**The seventeen other kinds can also occur in a word.**

*ubhaya-śakty-utthaṁ vināpare saptadaśa-pade ’pīty arthaḥ. tathā ca, “pada-dyotyena su-kaver dhvaninā bhāti bhāratī, ekenaiva prasūnena navevodyāna-ketakī” iti.*

**Перевод:**

**This means ubhaya-sakti-bhu dhvani is excluded.**

**It is said: “Just as a good poet’s composition with a first-rate implied sense hinted at with one word is resplendent, so a young ketaki tree in a garden is beautiful simply with one flower.”**

### 3.32

*tatra diṅ-mātram udāhriyate,*

**Перевод:**

**Now the concept is shown in a general way:**

*pārṣadāḥ pārṣadā yasya*  
*lakṣmīr lakṣmīḥ kṛpā kṛpā*  
*avatāro ’vatāraś ca*  
*sa devaḥ kair na sevyate*

**Пословный перевод:**

parsadah—associates; parsadah—always by His side; yasya— whose; laksmih—opulence; laksmih—always present; krpa— mercy; krpa—unconditional; avatarah—descent; avatarah— devoid of birth and death; ca—and; sah—that; devah—Lord; kaih—by who; na sevyate—is not served.

**Перевод:**

**The Lord’s entourage is an entourage, His opulence is opulence, His mercy is mercy, and His Avatara is an Avatara. Who will not serve Him?**

*atra dvitīya-pārṣadādi-śabdā nirantara-pārśva-sthatvanirapāyitva-nirupādhitva-janma-maraṇa-bhāva-rahitatveṣv arthāntareṣu saṅkramitāḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**The verse illustrates arthantara-sankramita-vacya: The literal meaning of each second word turns into a different sense. The second word parsada (entourage) has the figurative sense of “always being nearby.” The second word laksmi (opulence) transforms into the figurative meaning of “never decreasing”. The second word krpa (mercy) transforms into the figurative sense of “causeless.” The second word avatara (Descent) has the sense of “devoid of birth, death, and material existence.”**

**Комментарий:**

In plain words: “The Lord’s associates are always by His side, His opulence is always present, His mercy is unconditional, and His Descent does not involve birth and death. Who will not serve Him?”

Visvanatha Cakravarti explains: What is suggested by the figurative meaning of parsada (namely “always at the side”) is that the Lord’s associates are the best of all kinds of associates. Similarly, in every instance the figurative meaning leads to the implied sense of “better than anything of its kind.”

*ratir na dīrghā mama dīrgham eva te*
