tava—Your; anukampa—mercy; tu—but; tava—to You; eva—only; sobhate—appears; mama—my; api—even; daurjanyam—badness (“the quality of being a bad person”); aho—how amazing; mama— to me; api—also; hi—only; ratih—love; na—is not; dlrgha—deep; mama—my; dlrgham—deep; eva—only; te—Your; prema—love; priya—dear beloved; aham—I am; tava—Your; krsna—O Krsna; kim—what?; bruve—\[can\] I say.

**Перевод:**

**Your mercy is unique to You. And how amazing! My badness is unique to me. My love is shallow, whereas Your love is deep. I am Your beloved. Krsna, what can I say?**

*atrānukampānanukampā, daurjanyam adaurjanyam, na dīrghā dīrghā, dīrgham adīrgham, priyāpriyeti atyanta-tiraskṛtam ity ubhaya-pada-gamyam. “phalam api phalam ākandānām” ityādau, “saubhāgyam etad adhikam” ity-ādau cobhayor vākya eva viśrāntir iti bhedaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the words anukampa, daurjanyam, na dirgha, dirgham, and priya mean exactly the opposite of the literal meaning. Thus it is understood that the literal meanings are completely obliterated. In the verses that begin phalam api phalam (3.5) and saubhagyam etad adhikam (3.7), the overall meaning culminates in the sentence (the last dhvani has more depth because of the previous dhvanis). That is the difference.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: By viparita-laksana, the word anukampa (mercy) means “lack of mercy”, and so it is suggested that, since lack of mercy is unique to Krsna, He is a bad person on account of his hard-heartedness. Similarly, by viparita-laksana, daurjanyam (being a bad person) means “being a good person” and so it is suggested that, since goodness is unique to her, she is better. Similarly, by viparita-laksana her love is deep, His love is shallow, and she is not dear to Him, which suggests that He shouldn’t approach her.

### 3.34

**Перевод:**

**\[This illustrates pada-gata abhidha-mula vastu-dhvani:\]**

*taṁ va-aṇaṁ so paphaṁso taṁ rūaṁ taṁ sarīra-sorabbhaṁ*  
*te ahara-mahurimāṇo dāṇiṁ hālāhalaṁ jāaṁ*  
*(Śaurasenī Prakrit)*

*tad vacanaṁ sa sparśas tad rūpaṁ tac charīra-saurabhyam*  
*te ’dhara-madhurimāṇa idānīṁ hālāhalaṁ jātam*  
*(Sanskrit rendering)*

**Пословный перевод:**

tat—those; vacanam—words; sah—that; sparsah—touch; tat— that; rupam—form; tat—that; sarira-saurabhyam—fragrance of the body; te—those; adhara—of the lips; madhurimanah— sweetnesses; idanim—now; halahalam—poison; jatam—have become.

**Перевод:**

**Those words, that touch, that form, that bodily fragrance, and that sweetness of His lips have now become poison.**

*atra tad-ādi-padāny anubhava-gocarān arthān prakāśya pūrvam amṛta-vad āsīt sarvam iti vastu prakāśayantīti pada-gato dhvaniḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the pronouns “those” and “that”, which refer to things in the scope of a previous experience, convey this idea (vastu): “Previously all these things were like nectar.” This is a pada- gata dhvani (implied sense derived from one type of word).**

**Комментарий:**

On this topic, Mammata says his example illustrates the suggestiveness of one word, and in his elaboration he specifies that the implied sense arises by the suggestiveness of many pronouns. Thus here pada-gata means “derived from one type of word.”

The vastu-dhvani in the verse is the form of a smrti vyabhicari- bhava (remembrance). Commenting on Mammata’s example, similar to the above, Nagesa Bhatta says the vyabhicari-bhava called smrti enhances the vipralambha. Thus Kavi Kamapura’s verse illustrates a pada-gata abhidha-mula rasa-dhvani (vipralambha- srngara). In that regard, vyadhi (specific mental agony), is one of the stages of vipralambha (5.35; 5.66).

### 3.35

*śabda-śakty-udbhavo yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**This illustrates an implied meaning arisen by sabda-sakti:**

*mugdhe padmini kula-je*  
*mā kārṣīr atra viśvāsam*  
*anavasthito ’ti-madataḥ*  
*so ’yaṁ sākṣād aneka-paḥ kṛṣṇaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

mugdhe—O innocent girl; padmini—O padmini heroine; kula-je—O you who were born in a respectable family; ma akarsih—don’t do (don’t put); atra—in this \[Krsna\]; visvasam—faith; anavasthitah— very unsettled (loose in His conduct); ati-madatah—because of much rut fluid (which emanates from the temples of an elephant in rut) (or because of great pride); sah ayam—that notorious; saksat— directly; aneka-pah—elephant; krsnah—Krsna.

**Перевод:**

**Innocent padmim born in a respectable family, don’t trust that notorious Krsna, an elephant unsettled because of much mada.**

*atrāneka-pa-śabda ekārtho ’pi kavi-nibaddha-vaktṛ-prauḍhoktivaśād anekārthatāṁ gataḥ san mugdhe ity-ādi-sambodhanatrayārthena sādhanena sādhyaṁ sva-gatam anavasthitatvādikam. yathā—tvaṁ mugdhā, ayam anavasthitaḥ, tvaṁ kula-jā, ayam ati-madaḥ, tvaṁ padminī, ayam aneka-po hastīty artha-trayaṁ bodhayati. anekaṁ pātīti, anekena pibatīti ca, aneka-vadhū-patir matta-hastī ca. padminīti nāyikā-viśeṣaḥ, kamalinīti ca. tvaṁ kulajā, ayam anekaṁ pibatīti mattaś ca, tenātra viśvāsaṁ mā kārṣīr yato ’ti-madato ’navasthitaḥ. mado dānaṁ garvaś ca, tena tvām avaśyaṁ mardayiṣyatīti vastv-anantaraṁ vastv-antaraṁ ca. hastisādharmyād upamālaṅkāraḥ, anavasthita iti hetv-alaṅkāraḥ, anekasya bharteti svabhāvokty-alaṅkāraḥ—ity alaṅkāravyañjakaḥ śabda-śakty-udbhavaḥ pada-gataḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Here aneka-pa becomes a word with multiple meanings because although it usually has only one meaning (elephant), the verse is kavi-nibaddha-vaktr-praudhokti (bold words of a speaker created by the poet). First of all, Krsna’s attributes, such as being unsettled, are substantiated by the qualities mentioned in the three vocatives: She is innocent whereas He is unsettled, She is from a respectable family whereas He has become maddenned, and she is a padmin whereas He is an elephant.**

**In the verse, the word aneka-pa has three meanings: (1) anekampati, “He maintains many”, which means He has many ladyloves, (2) anekena pibati, “It drinks through more than one” (it drinks through its mouth and trunk), which denotes a mad elephant, and (3) anekam pibati, “He drinks many” (He drinks the lips of many girls), which refers to Krsna who is mad with lust.**

**The term padmin denotes one of the four kinds of ladyloves. It also means lotus. (He is an elephant and you’re a lotus.) Moreover: “You were born in a respectable family, whereas He drinks the lips of many girls and is thus mad with lust, therefore don’t trust Him, since He’s unsettled due to excessive mada.” The word mada signifies “rut fluid” and “pride.” The gist is: “He will certainly crush you.” In this way a vastu is derived from a vastu.**

**In addition, a simile between Krsna and an elephant is implied. The hetu ornament (explanatory reason) is also implied since His behaving badly is a cause. And by the meaning of aneka-pa in the sense of Krsna being a lover of many girls, there is the svabhavokti ornament (the nature).**

**Thus the verse features an implied sense derived by the power of a single word and suggestive of ornaments.**

**Комментарий:**

According to Kavi Karnapura, here the sabda-sakti is pada-gata (based on a single word) because the force of the paronomastic word aneka-pa is such that it creates a domino effect on the meaning of the other words. Here the simile between Krsna and an elephant is implied insofar as it is a metaphor.

In effect, here Kavi Karnapura rejects his statement that, unlike artha-sakti-bhu dhvani, sabda-sakti-bhu dhvani cannot be uttamottama-kavya (one implied sense occasions another) (3.12).

### 3.36

*pada-gatārtha-śakty-udbhavaḥ svataḥ-sambhavī yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**This illustrates an implied sense which could occur in day-to­day life and is derived from the power of the meaning, based on a single word:**

*ṇihu-aṇa-kadhāhiṁ dhaṇṇā ṇia-parivāraṁ suhāventi*  
*apapāṇaṁ pi ṇa hu tadā sumara-idāṇiṁ bhaṇādu kiṁ bhodī*  
*(Śaurasenī Prakrit)*

*nidhuvana-kathābhir dhanyā nija-parivāraṁ sukhāpayanti*  
*ātmānam api na hi tadā smaratīdānīṁ bhaṇatu kiṁ bhavatī*  
*(Sanskrit rendering)*

**Пословный перевод:**

nidhuvana—about sexual union; kathabhih—by talks; dhanyah— are fortunate; nija-parivaram—own associates; sukhapayanti— they make happy; atmanam—the body; api—even; na hi—doesn’t; tada—at that time; smarati—she remembers; idanim—now; bhanatu—can say; kim—what; bhavati—you.

**Перевод:**

**\[Some gopis address their leader:\]**

**By talking about their intercourse, those fortunate girls make their friends happy. But in your case, since in union you’re not even aware of your body, what can you say now?**

*atra na tā dhanyās tvam eva dhanyā, tāsāṁ sakhībhyo vayam ati-sukhinyaḥ, tvad-ānandāveśād eva vayam akathanenāpy ānanda-bhājaḥ. tās tu tat kathayaiveti dhanyā-pada-gataḥ svataḥsambhavī. apare tūhyā, grantha-gaurava-bhayān nodāhriyante. vākya-gatāḥ pūrvam eva kiyanto darśitāḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the implied sense derived from the word dhanya (fortunate) is: “They aren’t fortunate, only you are fortunate. We, your friends, are happier than the friends of those leaders. Simply by being absorbed in your bliss, we partake of the bliss even without talks about union. But those friends of other girls become blissful only through such talks.”**

**This dhvani is svatah-sambhavi (it could occur in day-to-day life), and is pada-gata because of the word dhanya.**

**The other examples of pada-gata dhvani should be inferred in the same way. They will not be illustrated out of fear of increasing the size of the treatise. Examples of vakya-dhvani, however, have been shown.**

*ato hetoḥ sapta-catvāriṁśad bhavanti.*

*prabandhe diṅ-mātram udāhriyate,*

*sahanti gandhaṁ vi ṇa vai jaṇāṇaṁ ṇava-ppasūā sa-alā hi gāo*  
*na teṇa doho ṇa pa-a-ppasaṅgo ajje bahūo tuha viṇṇaventi*  
*(Śaurasenī Prakrit)*

*sahante gandham api na vai janānāṁ nava-prasūtāḥ sakalā hi gāvaḥ*  
*na tena doho na payaḥ-prasaṅga ārye vadhvas tvāṁ vijñāpayanti*  
*(Sanskrit rendering)*

**Пословный перевод:**

sahante—tolerate; gandham—the scent; api—even; na—cannot; vai—indeed; jananam—of people; nava—recently; prasutah—that have given birth; sakalah—all; hi—indeed; gavah—cows; na— there is no; tena—therefore; dohah—milking; na—there is no; payah—for milk; prasangah—occasion; arye—O respectable lady; vadhvah—the young women; tvam—you; vijnapayanti—inform.

**Перевод:**

**“O respectable lady, the young women wish to inform you that all the cows that have recently given birth cannot even tolerate the scent of people. Therefore, since they cannot be milked, there is no milk available.”**

*atra vadhūbhiḥ preṣitā śvaśrū-dhātryā naptrī tāsāṁ śvaśrūṁ prati kathayati.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the context is: The grand-daughter of the mother-in­law’s old nurse was sent by the young women. She informs the mother-in-law about those girls.**

### 3.41

*tac chrutvā sāpi jaratī tām āha,*

**Перевод:**

**Hearing this, the old mother-in-law says to the grand-daughter of the old nurse:**

*karemi kiṁ ṇattiṇi dhattiāe vaessarīṁ lambhia viṇṇavehi*  
*tuhāṇa savvaṁ maha gohaṇādi dhaṇaṁ jaṇāo vi suhaṁ ca dukkhaṁ*  
*su-duppaāhā mada savva gāo puttā vidūre kim ahaṁ karemi*  
*viloaṇādo tuha ṇandaṇassa su-duppaāhāvi sa-appaohā*  
*(Śaurasenī Prakrit)*

*karomi kiṁ naptri dhātryā vrajeśvarīṁ labdhvā vijñāpaya*  
*yuṣmākaṁ sarvaṁ mama go-dhanādi-dhanaṁ janā api sukhaṁ ca duḥkham*  
*su-duṣpradohā mama sarva-gāvaḥ putrā vidūre kim ahaṁ karomi*  
*vilokanāt tava nanda-nandanasya su-duṣpradohā api svayam-pradohāḥ*  
*(Sanskrit rendering)*

**Пословный перевод:**

karomi kim—what can I do; naptri—O grand-daughter; dhatryah— of a nurse; vraja-isvarim—the queen of Vraja; labdhva—having approached; vijnapaya—you should inform; yusmakam—your; sarvam—all; mama—my; go-dhana-adi—such as the wealth of cows and so on; dhanam—the wealth; janah—people; api—also; sukham—are happy; ca—and; duhkham—are unhappy.

su-duspradohah—are very difficult to milk; mama—of mine; sarva-gavah—all the cows; putrah—sons; viclure—are far away; kim aham karomi—what can I do; vilokanat—because of seeing; tava—your; nanda-nandanasya—the son of Nanda; su-duspradohah—are very difficult to milk; api—even; svayam-pradohah—\[cows that\] give milk by themselves

**Перевод:**

**“What can I do? Go to the queen of Vraja and inform her: “Your cows and other types of wealth are in good condition and your people are happy, whereas my cattle business is not going well and my people are unhappy. All my cows are hard to milk. My sons are far away. But simply by seeing Nanda’s son, even the cows that are the most difficult to milk give milk by themselves.”**

### 3.42

*iti jaraty-uttarānte goṣṭheśvarīṁ gatvā tayā yad uktaṁ tat kathayati,*

*evvaṁ kkhu tāe bhaṇidā gadāhaṁ vaessarīṁ uttavadī samatthaṁ*  
*utteṇa tāe kumareṇa uttaṁ gosaṁ ppaoho mama ṇa kkhu hoi*  
*(Śaurasenī Prakrit)*

*evaṁ khalu tayā bhaṇitā gatāhaṁ vrajeśvarīm uktavatī samastam*  
*uktena tayā kumāreṇoktaṁ gosaṁ pradoho mama na khalu bhavati*  
*(Sanskrit rendering)*

**Пословный перевод:**

evam—in this way; khalu—indeed; taya—by her (the old lady); bhanita—being addressed; gata aham—I went; vraja-isvarim—to the queen of Vraja; uktavati—\[and\] told; samastam—everything; uktena—who was spoken to; taya—by her (Mother Yasoda); kumarena—by the son; uktam—what was said; gosam—in the morning; pradohah—milking; mama—done by me; na—not; khalu—indeed; bhavati—is.

**Перевод:**

**Hearing the old lady speak, the grand-daughter of the old nurse goes to meet the queen of Vraja. Afterward, the grand­daughter comes back and tells the young women what Mother Yasoda said to Krsna:**

**“Being thus addressed by the old lady, I went to Mother Yasoda and told her everything she said. This is what Krsna replied after Yasoda spoke to Him: “I don’t milk cows in the morning.””**

*iti catuḥ-saṁvāda-prabandhe vadhūbhiḥ kṛṣṇa-sandarśanārtham upāyam anavekṣya prākaraṇika-duṣpradoha-go-dohābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ śvaśrūṁ prati vijñāpitaḥ. atrāpahnuti-nāmālaṅkāraḥ. tathā ca go-dohopāyaṁ cintayitvā he dhātrikā-naptri, goṣṭheśvarīṁ gatvā vijñāpayety uttaraṁ dattam ity uttarālaṅkāraḥ. tataś ca “su-duṣpradohā mama sarva-gāvaḥ” iti svabhāvokty-alaṅkāraḥ. vilokanād ity-ādinātiśayoktiḥ. tathā ca sukha-dohe pariśramas tasya na bhaviṣyatīti vastu. gosaṁpradohaḥ prabhāta-pradoho matto na bhavatīti niścayālaṅkāreṇa sāyaṁ-dohas tu mayā kartavya iti vadhūnām āśayaṁ jñātvā chalena saṅketaḥ kṛta iti vastu—iti catuḥ-ślokyā samuditaḥ prabandho hi mukhyo vyañjakaḥ.tathā hi “janānāṁ gandham api na sahante” ity anyair adohyatvaṁ vastu. atra nava-prasūtā iti hetor hetv-alaṅkāraḥ. tena “kṛṣṇaṁ vinā nāsāṁ dohaḥ” iti śvaśrvā kṛṣṇa ānāyitavya iti vastv-antaram, “na tena doha” ity anena payo-’bhāvād vayam akriyāḥ smaḥ. atra mā kopaṁ kārṣīr iti ca vastv-antaram. “tuhāṇa savvam” ity-ādinā vinaya-mahimnā kṛṣṇo ’vaśyaṁ vrajeśvaryā preṣayitavya iti vastu. evaṁ nāṭakādiṣu ceti tad-bheda-kathanenānantya-prasaṅga iti nātra likhitaḥ. evaṁ prabandhe ’py anya ekādaśāpi boddhavyāḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**In this prabandha that contains four conversations, the young women, not seeing any way to meet Krsna, inform the mother­in-law that the cows, which are difficult to milk, are not giving milk. Therein occurs the apahnuti ornament (concealment).**

**In addition, the uttara ornament (giving an answer) occurs because the mother-in-law, thinking of a way to milk the cows, gives the answer “O grand-daughter of my old nurse, go to the queen of Vraja and inform her of the situation.”**

**Moreover, the svabhavokti ornament occurs in the words “All my cows are very difficult to milk.” Further, the words “Simply by seeing Nanda’s son, even the cows that are the most difficult to milk give milk by themselves” constitute the atisayokti ornament. This suggests the idea that Krsna won’t have to exert Himself while performing such easy milking.**

**On account of the niscaya ornament (certainty): “I don’t milk cows in the morning,” which means that He milk cows in the evening, this idea (vastu) arises: Knowing the young women’s intention, Krsna, on a pretext, fixed the time for the tryst. This is the main suggestion in this prabandha of four verses.**

**Other suggestions are as follows. By the words “All the cows that have recently given birth cannot even tolerate the scent of people,” there is the idea (vastu) that these cows cannot be milked by anyone other than Krsna. The reason these cows cannot be milked by anyone else is that they have given birth:**

**This is an instance of the hetu ornament (explanatory reason).**

**There is another idea (vastu): Since the cows cannot be milked without Krsna, He should be brought by the mother-in-law. Further, because of the words “Milking cannot be done,” an additional vastu arises: The young women say “Due to a lack of milk, we have no work. Don’t be angry at us for this.” In addition, with the words “Your cows and other types of wealth are in good condition and your people are happy,” there is the idea that Krsna will definitely be sent by the queen of Vraja due to her magnanimous behavior.**

**There would be an infinite number of varieties if we also discussed the varieties of suggestions in dramaturgy and so on, thus we have not written about them here. Thus, the other eleven types of artha-sakti-bhu dhvanis occurring in a prabandha should be understood this way.**

### 3.43

*padāṁśādyā rasāñjakāḥ (14d)*

**Пословный перевод:**

pada-amsa—a part of a word; adyah—those whose beginning is; rasa—rasa; anjakah—suggest.

**Перевод:**

**Parts of a word and so on evoke rasa.**

*padāṁśa-varṇa-racanā iti tritayam api rasasya vyañjakaṁ bhavati. raso ’trāsaṁlakṣya-kramaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**A padamsa (part of a word), the type of phonemes (varna) (sweet, harsh, or soft), and the style of compounding (racana) enhance the rasa. Here the word rasa only means asamlaksya- krama in general (anything whose order of appearance is not perceived).**

**Комментарий:**

The sweet phonemes are in the category of madhurya-guna, which evokes particular rasas. The harsh phonemes are in the category of ojas guna (vigor), which evokes vira-rasa and so on. The styles are based on the gunas. The gunas are expounded in chapter six and the styles in chapter nine.

### 3.44

*tena tasya trayo bhedāḥ prabandhe ’pi sa kathyate (15)*

*so ’saṁlakṣya-kramaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

tena—therefore; tasya—of that \[rasa\]; trayah—three; bhedah— varieties; prabandhe—in a short story; api—also; sah—that; kathyate—is said.

**Перевод:**

**Therefore the category of asamlaksya-krama dhvani has three varieties (padamsa, varna, and racana) (and rasa, vastu-dhvani, alankara-dhvani). It also occurs in prabandhas.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti elucidates: Vastus and alankaras are asamlaksya-krama only when the understanding is conveyed by a part of a word, by a particular type of phoneme or by the style of compounding \[on account of the subtle nature of the suggestion\]. However, the sequence of appearance of vastus and alankaras is perceivable when the understanding is conveyed through a sentence (vakya) or by a word (pada) (Subodhini). Ideally, the implied vastus and alankaras in the category of asamlaksya-krama as well should evoke the rasa.

### 3.45

*bhedās tenaika-pañcāśat (16a)*

**Перевод:**

**Thus there are fifty-one varieties.**

*tena pūrva-likhita-sapta-catvāriṁśatā caturbhir etaiś caikapañcāśad bhavanti.*

**Перевод:**

**There are fifty-one categories of dhvanis, because these four kinds (padamsa, varna, racana, and prabandha) are added to the forty-seven kinds (3.39).**

### 3.46

*padāṁśāḥ padaika-deśāḥ. te ca,*

*prakṛtiḥ pratyayaḥ kālo vartamānādir eva yaḥ*  
*sambandho vacanaṁ cāpi puruṣa-vyatyayo ’pi ca*  
*taddhitaṁ copasargaś ca nipātaḥ sarvanāma ca*  
*karma-bhūtādhikaraṇam avyayī-bhāva eva ca*  
*tathā pūrva-nipātaś ca padāṁśāḥ parikīrtitāḥ*  
*racanā ca tridhā dīrgha-madhya-rikta-samāsataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The term padamsa means “one part of a word.” The padamsas are:**

**♦   The word base (verbal or nominal) (prakrti),**  
**♦   A suffix (pratyaya),**  
**♦   The time: past, present, or future (kala),**  
**♦   The relation of possession (sambandha, esp. sva-svami- bhava),**  
**♦   The number (single, dual, plural) (vacana),**  
**♦   Disparity of number in the subject-verb relation (purusa- vyatyaya),**  
**♦   A taddhita suffix,**  
**♦   A prefix (upasarga),**  
**♦   A preposition (such as ca or va) (nipata),**  
**♦   A pronoun (sarvanama),**  
**♦   A location which is the object of the verb (karma- bhutadhara),**  
**♦   An avyayi-bhava compound, and**  
**♦   Irregular placement as the first word in a compound (purva-nipata).**

*dīrgha-samāsā madhya-samāsāsamāsā cety arthaḥ. varṇā mṛdukaṭhorādyās te paścāt pratipāditāḥ. ādya-śabdān madhurāḥ. eṣāṁ vyañjakatve diṅ-mātram udāharaṇam*

**Перевод:**

**The style of compounding has three categories: (A) a long compound, (B) compounds of medium length, and (C) no compound. The phonemes are either soft, harsh, or sweet. They will be expounded later. Now some examples of suggestive padamsas will be shown.**

### 3.47

*tatra prakṛter yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**This illustrates the suggestiveness of a word base \[and of a suffix\]:**

*mā kuru mānini mānaṁ*  
*suhṛdāṁ vacanaṁ praveśaya śravaṇe*  
*gokula-mahendra-tanayo*  
*bhavatu sa-nāthaḥ prasādam āsādya*

**Пословный перевод:**

ma kuru—don’t do; manini—O sulky girl; manam—loving anger; suhrdam—of the friends; vacanam—the words; pravesaya—make enter; sravane—in your ears; gokula-maha-indra—of the king of Gokula; tanayah—the son; bhavatu—may He become; sa- nathah—one who has a master (You); prasadam—\[Your\] mercy; asadya—having obtained.

**Перевод:**

**Sulky girl, don’t be in mana. Listen to your friends’ advice. Let the prince of Gokula obtain your grace and become your obedient servant.**

*atra kṛñ-prakṛtyā kṛter aicchikatvam, tena tan-māna-karaṇaṁ tvad-iṣṭādhīnam eva, na tu sāhajikatvam, tasyāparādhābhāvāt, tena vibhāvanālaṅkāraḥ, tasmān mā kuru, tyajety arthaḥ. suhṛdvacanaṁ tava śravaṇe praviśad api na praveṣṭum śaknoti, tvanmanasaḥ śravaṇena sahāsaṁyogāt. tat praveśaya, mano dīyatām. suhṛt-sambandhitvena vacanasya śravaṇa-praveśo yukta eveti ṇicpratyaya-dhvaniḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**On account of the verbal base \[du\]kr\[n\] (in kuru), it’s understood that the activity is done because of a desire. Therefore, “Your implementing the state of mana is only based on your desire; the mana isn’t arising by itself since Krsna hasn’t committed any offense.”**

**That constitutes the vibhavana ornament (a result without a normal cause). Hence the words “Don’t be in mana” mean “Give up your mana .”**

**“Even though the words of Your friends seemingly enter your ears, they cannot go in since your mind isn’t connected to your ears. So make them enter. Pay attention. It’s your friends’ advice, therefore it’s proper that it should enter your ears.” This suggestion arises on account of the causative suffix \[n\]i (in pravesaya, “Make it enter”).**

### 3.48

*pratyayasya yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**A suffix is suggestive:**

*āṇia bha-aṇa-duāraṁ dharaṇīe pāiāni kusumāiṁ*  
*pia-sahi kiṁ iti vasīdasi puṇo vi cala tattha kumumatthaṁ*  
*(Śaurasenī Prakrit)*

*ānīya bhavana-dvāraṁ dharaṇyāṁ pātitāni kusumāni*  
*priya-sakhi kim iti viṣīdasi punar api cala tatra kusumārtham*  
*(Sanskrit rendering)*

**Пословный перевод:**

aniya—having brought; bhavana—of the house; dvaram—to the door; dharanyam—on the ground; patitani—were made to fall; kusumani—the flowers; priya-sakhi—O dear friend; kim iti—why; visidasi—are you so depressed; punar api—once again; cala—go; tatra—there; kusuma—flowers; artham—for the purpose of.

**Перевод:**

**Upon bringing the flowers to the entrance of the house, you made them fall to the ground. Sakhi, there is no need to be despondent. Go there again to collect flowers.**

*atra kusumāharaṇa-cchalena vṛndāvanaṁ gatvā saṅketa-sthale kṛṣṇam āgataṁ vīkṣya kusumāny ādāyaiva gṛham āgatāṁ punaḥ saṅketa-muralī-svana-śravaṇānantaraṁ punar-gamanotkaṇṭhayā vyājena pātita-kusumāṁ kāñcit prati hṛdaya-jñā sakhī vadati— priya-sakhi, kim iti viṣīdasi bhūmi-pātitāni kusumāni deva-deyāni na bhavanti, punar api tatra kusumārthaṁ gaccha. mayā te gurujano bodhanīyaḥ, na kiñcid api te bhayam iti ṇic-pratyayasyaiva dhvaniḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**A gopi went to the woods of Vrndavana on the plea of picking flowers. She came back after collecting flowers and seeing Krsna who had come to the appointed meeting place. Then, hearing the sound of the flute in the appointed meeting place, she makes the flowers fall as a pretext, out of eagerness to go out again.**

**Another sakhi, reading her mind, speaks the above words: “Dear friend, why are you despondent? Flowers fallen on the ground can’t be offered to the deity. Go there again to pick flowers. I’ll explain everything to your elders. Don’t be afraid.” The implied sense arises due to the causative suffix \[n\]i (in patitani, “were caused to fall”).**

### 3.49

*kālasya yathā*

**Перевод:**

**The time is suggestive:**

*sahajam aruṇaṁ netra-dvandvaṁ svabhāvata eva te*  
*satata-muralī-dhvāna-krīḍā-vidhau vraṇito ’dharaḥ*  
*vana-viharaṇe rātrau gātraṁ sa-kaṇṭaka-lāñchanaṁ*  
*katham iva kṛtaḥ svāmin svātmāparādha-visaṁṣṭhulaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

sahajam—natural; arunam—red; netra-dvandvam—pair of eyes; svabhavatah—by nature; eva—simply; te—your; satata— constantly; murali-dhvana—of the flute sound; krida—the pastime; vidhau—while doing; vranitah—wounded; adharah—lip; vana— in the forest; viharane—while wandering; ratrau—at night; gatram—body; sa-kantaka-lanchanam—endowed with marks of thorns; katham—why; iva—as if; krtah—was made; svamin—O master; sva-atma—your body; aparadha—because of offenses; visamsthulah—withered.

**Перевод:**

**\[A gopi speaks to Krsna:\]**

**Svami, Your eyes are naturally red. Your lips are bruised due to constantly playing the flute. And Your body was scratched by thorns because You wander in the forest at night. Why does it seem that Your body was withered because of an offense?**

*atra kṛta iti kta-pratyayenoktātīta-kālena mat-sammukhāgamāt pūrvam evātmanas tavāparādha-visaṁṣṭhulyatā jātā. tataḥ param eva mat-sammukha-bhāgato ’sīty atiśayokty-alaṅkāraḥ. tena ca māṁ prati tava bhayādhikyam, tāṁ prati tava premādhikyam iti vastu.*

**Перевод:**

**The past tense expressed by the past passive participle \[k\]ta in krta (was made) is suggestive. The gopi says: “Even before coming here, Your body was withered (lit. “was made withered”) on account of Your offense.” That is the atisayokti ornament. Therefore the implied idea is: “You’re afraid of me, and You love that girl very much.”**

**Комментарий:**

The atisayokti occurs in the sense that the effect took place before its cause: The gopi means to say: “Your eyes are red because she kissed your eyes, and so on, but Your eyes assumed their natural redness a long time ago in anticipation of such an offense to me.”

Visvanatha Cakravarti comments: Krsna says to a gopi “Dear girl, although I did not commit any offense, you imagine that I did. If you’re angry, let it be. Nevertheless, your grace is My only means of deliverance from this imaginary offense.” The gopi replies, “You didn’t commit an offense just now. It was commited prior to Your coming in my presence.” To clarify her statement, the proud gopi ironically speaks the above words (in the verse). She exclaims:

“Krsna, Your eyes and lips are naturally red. They didn’t become red by the kiss mark of some girl with red lipstick. And Your marks are caused by thorns, not by the nails of some passionate girl.” With the words “You’re afraid of me”, what is meant is: “That you are lying to me even when such marks of union are clearly visible indicates that You’re afraid of me.”

### 3.50

*sambandhasya yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**A case ending that expresses ownership is suggestive:**

*a-i piasi goviāṇaṁ peaṁ kaṇhassa ahara-palla-aṁ murali*  
*ṇia-parivivea-kusalā ammo ṇo honti sa-cchiddāo*  
*(Śaurasenī Prakrit)*

*ayi pibasi gopikānāṁ peyaṁ kṛṣṇasyādhara-pallavaṁ murali*  
*nija-para-viveka-kuśalā aho na bhavanti sa-cchidrāḥ*  
*(Sanskrit rendering)*

**Пословный перевод:**

ayi—O; pibasi—you drink; gopikanam—by the gopis; peyam— that should be drunk; krsnasya—of Krsna; adhara—that are the lips; pallavam—the buds; murali—O flute; nija—what belongs to oneself; para—and what belongs to another; viveka—in discriminating; kusalah—those who are expert; aho—how amazing; na bhavanti—are not; sa-chidrah—endowed with faults (or holes).

**Перевод:**

**O flute, you drink Krsna’s blossom-like lips, which should really be drunk by the gopis. Those who are expert in discriminating between what belongs to themselves and what belongs to others have no holes.**

*atra gopikānām eveti sva-svāmi-bhāva-sambandhaḥ, gopikābhir eva pātuṁ yujyate, na tvayeti vyatirekālaṅkāraḥ. arthāntaranyāsenāpi tvaṁ sa-cchidrā, iti vyatirekaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the word gopikanam expresses a relationship of owned and owner. The sense is: “The lips should be drunk only by the gopis, not by you.” The vyatireka ornament (contrast) thus takes place. The contrast also occurs in the second sentence, by the arthantara-nyasa ornament (corroboration) (here a general statement supports the specific statement), so that the sense is: “You’re full of holes”.**

### 3.51

*vacanasya yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**The number is suggestive:**

*vilāsa-ceṣṭāḥ sakhi keśi-nāśino*  
*hālāhalābhāḥ pradahanti me manaḥ*  
*kṛntanti marmāṇi guṇā ghuṇā iva*  
*premā vikārī hṛdi hṛd-vraṇo yathā*

**Пословный перевод:**

vilasa-cestah—pastimes; sakhi—O friend; kesi-nasinah—of the killer of Kesi; halahala—poison; abhah—are like; pradahanti— burns; me—my; manah—heart; krntanti—bite; marmani—the vital parts; gunah—the qualities; ghunah—woodworminsects, with razor-sharp teeth, that eat timber ; iva—are like; prema—love; vikar!— which is transforming; hrdi—in the heart; hrd—of the heart; vranah— a wound; yatha—just like.

**Перевод:**

**Sakhi, Krsna’s pastimes are like a poison that burns my heart. His gunas (qualities) are like ghunas (woodworms) which cut to the quick. In my heart, His love for me turns into a sore.**

*atra premā ity eka-vacanaṁ, premṇa eka-niṣṭhatva-vyañjakam, tena tasya mayy eva premā, ata eva vikārī. ata vacana-kramabhaṅga-doṣo guṇa eva.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the word prema is singular, whereas the pastimes and the qualities are in the plural. The singular suggests that the love is based on only one person. The sense is: “His love is uniquely for me, therefore His love is constantly changing in my heart.” In this verse, the fault of breaking the sequence of number (plural, plural, singular) becomes a quality.**

**Комментарий:**

In Mammata’s example, the usage of the singular in the word ‘love’ suggests that the love was uniform:

*teṣāṁ guṇa-grahaṇānāṁ tāsām utkaṇṭhānāṁ tasya premṇaḥ*  
*tāsāṁ bhaṇitīnāṁ sundaredṛśaṁ jātam avasānam*

**“My friend, those instances of appreciating the good qualities; those longings; that love; and those conversations have come to an end.” (Kavya-prakasa, verse 102)**

Govinda Thakkura explains that both the singular in the word “love” and the plural in the other words suggest that the love was uniform (constant): atra guna-grahanadmam prema-hetunam nana-prakaratve ’pi karyam premaika-jatiyam eva na kadacid anyatha-bhavam praptam iti bahu-vacanaika-vacanabhyam vyajyate. (Kavya-pradipa)

### 3.52

*puruṣa-vyatyayasya yathā*

**Перевод:**

**The disparity of number in the subject-verb relation is suggestive:**

*gatāstam arko virataś ca gharmo*  
*vanaṁ na dūre su-labhaṁ ca puṣpam*  
*calantu puṣpāharaṇāya sarvāḥ*  
*pūjāstu deve śaśi-khaṇḍa-cūḍe*

**Пословный перевод:**

gata- astam—has reached the setting point; arkah—the sun; viratah—has stopped; ca—and gharmah—the heat; vanam— the forest; na dure—is not far; su-labham—are easily available; ca—and; puspam—flowers; calantu—let everyone go; puspa- aharanaya—for collecting flowers; sarvah—all; puja—worship; astu—let there be; deve—toward the Lord; sasi—of the moon; khanda—there is a part; cude—on whose crest.

**Перевод:**

**The sun has set and the heat has ceased. The woodland isn’t far, and flowers are readily available. Let us all go to pick flowers so that we may worship the Lord who has a crescent moon on his head (or the Lord of gods, who wears a peacock feather on His head).**

*atra calāma ity arthe calantūttama-puruṣa-vyatyayena prathamapuruṣa-nirdeśaḥ, tena yūyam eva vayam ity apṛthag-bhāvo vastu. deve śaśi-khaṇḍa-cūḍa iti pṛthag dhvaniḥ—deveśaś cāsau śikhaṇḍa-cūḍaś ceti.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the verb calantu (may they go) is used instead of calamah (let us go). This is a switch between the third person plural and the first person plural. Because of this different usage of person, there is an idea of nondifference: All of you are like all of us.**

**Another suggestion is implied due to the words deve sasi- khanda-cude. By sabhanga-slesa (paronomasia by differently separating the letters) the words become devesa-sikhanda- cude, a karma-dharaya compound meaning “He is the Lord of the gods and wears a peacock feather on His head.”**

**Комментарий:**

This is Mammata’s example ofpurusa-vyatyaya (switch of person):

*re re cañcala-locanāñcita-ruce cetaḥ pramucya sthira-*  
*premāṇaṁ mahimānam eṇa-nayanām ālokya kiṁ nṛtyasi*  
*kiṁ manye vihariṣyase bata hatāṁ muñcāntarāśām imām*  
*eṣā kaṇṭha-taṭe kṛtā khalu śilā saṁsāra-vārāṁnidhau*

**“Hey there O heart of mine, why do you give up the blessed state of real love and begin to dance at the sight of that fawn-eyed woman? I see you’ve developed a liking for that fickle-eyed beauty. Ha, you think you will take pleasure? Goodness gracious, let go of this despicable desire. In the ocean of material life, she turns out as a boulder tied to your neck.”**

Mammata elaborates: atra prahasah, “There is ridicule here” (Kavya-prakasa, verse 103 vrtti). This refers to the usage of the verb manye (I think): kim manye viharisyase, “You think (lit. I think) you will take pleasure?”, by the rule that manye can be used in the sense of deriding the hearer: prahase ca manyopapade manyater uttama eka-vac ca (Astadhyayi 1.4.106).

### 3.53

*taddhitasya yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**A taddhita suffix is suggestive:**

*cira-viraha-dahana-dagdhaṁ*  
*priya-sakhi bhasmaiva bhāvi vapur etat*  
*tad anena viracanīyaṁ*  
*tat-kara-mukurasya mārjanaṁ tvayakā*

**Пословный перевод:**

cira -viraha—of long separation; dahana—by the fire; dagdham— being burned; priya-sakhi—O dear friend; bhasma—ashes; eva— just; bhavi—will become; vapuh—body; etat—this; tat—therefore; anena—with this \[ash\]; viracaniyam—should be done; tat- kara-mukurasya—of His hand mirror; marjanam—the cleaning; tvayaka—by you.

**Перевод:**

**Dear sakhi, this body of mine, burned by the fire of prolonged separation, will become ashes, so you should polish His silver mirror with them.**

*atra tvayaketi taddhitena aka-pratyayena mad-vicchedena tvam api śocyā bhaviṣyasi, mat-praṇayena hi tvam etāvantaṁ kālaṁ tad-aṅga-mārjana-saubhāgya-bhājanam āsīḥ, mayi mṛtāyāṁ tu te tathā-vidha-saubhāgyaṁ kva? tena yadi mukurādi-mārjanayogyatā bhavati, tadaiva kāryam iti śocyatā vyajyate.*

**Перевод:**

**Owing to the taddhita suffix ak in tvayaka (by you), the implied sense is: “In separation from me, you too will become pitiable. Simply because of Krsna’s love for me, for all this time you have been a recipient of the good fortune of anointing His limbs. But when I’ll have kicked the bucket, where will such good fortune be? Therefore, if at any time you obtain the privilege of cleaning His mirror, you should polish it with my ashes.” Mournfulness is suggested this way.**

**Комментарий:**

The suffix ka is applied after a word in the sense of contempt, compassion, or smallness, but for indeclinables and pronouns the suffix ak\[ac\] is applied instead, before the last letter: tvaya + ak = tvayaka. Panini’s rule is: avyaya-sarvanamnam akac prak teh (Astadhyayi 5.3.71). In this verse the meaning of ak is anukampa (compassion, endearment).

### 3.54

*upasargasya yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**A prefix is suggestive:**

*pataty asre sāsrā bhavati pulake jāta-pulakāḥ*  
*smite bhāti smerāḥ su-malimaṇi jāte su-malināḥ*  
*anāsādya svālīr mukuram abhivīkṣya sva-vadanaṁ*  
*sukhaṁ vā duḥkhaṁ vā kim api kathanīyaṁ mṛga-dṛśaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

patati—are falling; asre—when tears; sa-asrah—they have tears; bhavati—when there is (7.1 form of bhavat\[r\]); pulake— horripilation; jata—have occurred; pulakah—they by whom goose bumps; smite—when a smile; bhati—shines forth; smerah—they are smiling; su-malimani—when extreme dirtiness; jate—occurs; su-malinah—they are extremely dirty; anasadya—not attaining; sva-alih—your friends; mukuram—a mirror; abhiviksya—after seeing; sva-vadanam—your face; sukham—happiness; va—or; duhkham—unhappiness; va—or; kim api—some; kathaniyam— should be told; mrga-drsah—O doe-eyed girls.

**Перевод:**

**\[In an assembly of gopi leaders (yuthesvarls), a girl describes the excellence of their sakhts’ love for them:\]**

**Doe-eyed girls, when you cry, they cry. When you have goose bumps, they too have thrills. When you smile, they smile. And when you get dirty, they too get dirty. If your friends aren’t nearby, then bring a mirror, look at your face, and say whether you’re happy or sad. \[But if your friends are nearby, you don’t need a mirror.\]**

*atra sūpasargeṇa mālinyātiśayo vyajyate, tena ca sakhīnāṁ praṇayādhikyam.*

**Перевод:**

**A high degree of dirtiness is suggested by the prefix su (very) (in su-malimani and in su-malinah) (really dirty: soiled with dirt by working outside). Therefore the friends’ great love is suggested.**

### 3.55

*nipātasya yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**Here a nipata is suggestive:**

*daṭṭhūṇa tassa va-aṇaṁ kkhaṇa-metteṇa kkhu hāriaṁ hia-aṁ*  
*evvaṁ via accariaṁ turiaṁ laddhaṁ a ta-dhia-aṁ*  
*(Śaurasenī Prakrit)*

*dṛṣṭvā tasya vadanaṁ kṣaṇa-mātreṇa khalu hāritaṁ hṛdayam*  
*evam evāścaryaṁ tvaritaṁ labdhaṁ ca tasya hṛdayam*  
*(Sanskrit rendering)*

**Пословный перевод:**

drstva—having seen; tasya—His; vadanam—face; ksana—a moment; matrena—for just; khalu—indeed; haritam—stolen; hrdayam—the heart; evam—in this way; eva—certainly; ascaryam— how amazing; tvaritam—quickly; labdham—is obtained; ca—and; tasya—His; hrdayam—heart.

**Перевод:**

**I saw His face, and my heart was taken away. How amazing, I immediately stole His heart in the same way.**

*atra ca-śabda-rūpa-nipātena tulya-yogitālaṅkāraḥ. nija-hṛdayahāraṇa-sama-kālam eva tad-dhṛdayaṁ labdham, ato ’haṁ hṛdayaśūnyā nābhavam iti, tasya hṛdayaṁ mad-dhṛdayam eveti vastunā dvayor evautsukyaṁ vastu pratīyate.*

**Перевод:**

**The tulya-yogita ornament (8.138) occurs due to the particle ca (and): “I stole His heart at the same time that he stole mine. I wasn’t left without a heart. His heart is my heart.” This idea suggests another: the eagerness of both.**

### 3.56

*sarvanāmno yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**A pronoun is suggestive:**

*madhye sūkṣma-dhiyaḥ sakhī-pariṣado dhṛtvā sakhī-bhūmikām*  
*abhyaṅgāya gṛhīta-pāṇi-kamalaṁ sparśena māṁ jānatī*  
*aho dūram apehi nāsi kuśalā snātuṁ ca vāñchādya me*  
*nety antaḥ-kupitā yad īhitavatī tat kena vismaryate*

**Пословный перевод:**

madhye—in the middle; suksma—is very fine; dhiyah—whose intelligence; sakhi—of lady friends; parisadah—of the assembly; dhrtva—having assumed; sakhi—of a lady friend; bhumikam—the dress; abhyangaya—for massaging \[with oil\]; grhita—by whom is held; pani-kamalam—the lotus hand; sparsena—by the touch; mam—Me; janati—She is recognizing; aho—Oh; duram—very far; apehi—go away; na asi—You are not; kusala—an expert \[woman\]; snatum—to bathe; ca—and; vancha—desire; adya— now; me—My; na—is not; iti—thus; antah-kupita—She who is angry within; yat—what; ihitavati— She did; tat—that; kena—by whom?; vismaryate—could it be forgotten.

**Перевод:**

**I infiltrated the assembly of witty sakhis by dressing like them and took hold of Radha’s hand to massage Her, but She recognized Me by My touch. She said: “Oh, Get out of here! You’re not an expert girl. Anyway, I don’t want to take another bath now.” How can I forget that act of this sulky girl?**

*atra yad-tadbhyāṁ vāg-agocaratvaṁ vyaṅgyam.*

**Перевод:**

**A state of being beyond words is suggested by the use of the correlative pronouns yad (what) and tad (that).**

**Комментарий:**

Arguably, the words yad and tad should have been juxtaposed to achieve that effect (10.60; 10.52). Mammata’s example of the suggestiveness of a pronoun is the usage in the sense of prasiddha (well-known) (Kavya-prakasa verse 109): asau khara-dusanadi- hantrtvenatiprasiddhah (Uddyota). An example was seen earlier: so ’yam saksad aneka-pah krsnah, “That notorious Krsna elephant,” where so’yam (that very one) has the sense of “well- known, notorious” (3.35)

### 3.57

*karma-bhūtādhikaraṇasya yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**A location which is the object of the verb is suggestive:**

*adhivasasi tasya hṛdayaṁ*  
*priya-sakhi rādhe sa cāpi tava hṛdayam*  
*dvāv eva pūrṇa-hṛdayau*  
*praviśāmo vāṁ kathaṁ hṛdaye*

**Пословный перевод:**

adhivasasi—You dwell; tasya hrdayam—in His heart; priya- sakhi—O dear friend; radhe—O Radha; sah—He; ca—and; api— also; tava hrdayam—in Your heart; dvau—Both of You; eva— certainly; purna-hrdayau—have full hearts; pravisamah—we enter; vam—of You two; katham—how can; hrdaye—in the heart.

**Перевод:**

**Dear friend Radha, You live in Krsna’s heart, and He lives in Yours. Both of You have full hearts, so how can we enter them?**

*atra ādhārasya karma-bhūtatve sarva-vyāpanaṁ vyaṅgyam. grāme vasatīti grāmaika-deśo gamyate, grāmam adhivasatīti grāmaṁ vyāpyaiveti camatkāraḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**In adhivasasi here, since the adhikarana (location) has become the karma (object), the all-pervasiveness of the residing is suggested. (She owns His heart, and He owns Hers.)**

**As another example, in grame vasati (He lives in the village) it is understood that this person lives somewhere in the village. However, in gramam adhivasati (He rules the village) it is understood is that he pervades the village (as a leader). This creates astonishment.**

**Комментарий:**

The rule is: upanv-adhy-anbhyo vasa adharah karma, “When the verbal root vas is prefixed by either upa, anu, adhi, or a\[n\], the location connected with it takes the accusative case instead of the locative” (Hari-namamrta-vyakarana 651) (upanv-adhy-an-vasah, Astadhyayi 1.4.48). Here the suggestiveness lies in the usage of the prefix adhi.

### 3.58

*avyayī-bhāvasya yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An avyayi-bhava compound is suggestive:**

*katy āyānti kati prayānti kati vā tiṣṭhanti mūrtā iva*  
*prauḍhānanda-mahotsavā yad-itare śrī-dvārakāyāṁ puri*  
*strī-ratnair anu-saudha-ratna-nikaraṁ niścintam ākrīḍitaṁ*  
*te yātāḥ kila vāsarā mama sakhe yeṣu vraje krīḍitam*

**Пословный перевод:**

kati—how many; ayanti—come; kati—how many; prayanti—go; kati—how many; va—and; tisthanti—remain; murtah—incarnate; iva—as if; praudha-ananda—of great bliss; maha-utsavah—great festivals; yat—than which \[bliss in Vrndavana\]; itare—which are different; sri-dvarakayam puri—in the city of Dvaraka; stri- ratnaih—with the best of women; anu-saudha-ratna-nikaram—in every jeweled palace; niscintam—without anxiety; akriditam—the playing (the enjoying of pastimes); te—those; yatah—are gone; kila—indeed; vasarah—days; mama—done by Me; sakhe—O friend; yesu—in which; vraje—in Vraja; kriditam—the playing.

**Перевод:**

**My friend, in Dvaraka City the great festivals are different than those in Vrndavana. How many of them come, how many go, and how many remain as if incarnate? Without anxiety, I enjoyed pastimes in every jeweled palace with the best women. But alas, those days when I played in Vraja are gone.**

*atrānu-saudha-ratna-nikaram ity avyayī-bhāvenāṣṭottaraśata-ṣoḍaśa-sahasratvaṁ vyajyate. yātā eva tāsāṁ punarāgamanābhāvāt.*

**Перевод:**

**The avyayi-bhava compound anu-saudha-ratna-nikaram (in every jeweled palace) hints at the 16,108 palaces. Moreover, “those days are gone” means they’ll never come back.**

**Комментарий:**

The avyayi-bhava compound suggests the eminence of Vrndavana. In an avyayi-bhava compound, the meaning of the first word is grammatically predominant. Thus here the word anu in that compound is predominant, and so the second word (saudha- ratna-nikara) (lit. a multitude of palace jewels) is secondary. This secondariness implies the eminence of Vrndavana.

### 3.59

*pūrva-nipātasya yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**Apurva-nipata is suggestive:**

*ānandātiśayena vismṛti-vaśād vyastānupūrvī-kramā*  
*ccheka-ccheka-śukāṅganābhir udayat-kautūhalaṁ smāritā*  
*śrī-rādhā-hari-keli-kautuka-kathā prātaḥ sakhī-maṇḍale*  
*pratyāvartayate gatām api niśāṁ sākṣād-vidhatte ca tau*

**Пословный перевод:**

ananda-atisayena—because of great bliss; vismrti-vasat—because of forgetfulness; vyasta—was disarranged; anupurvi-krama—by whom the order of sequence; cheka—clever; cheka—domesticated; suka-anganabhih—by the female parrots; udayat—arising; kautuhalam—in such a way that there is joy; smarita—was caused to be remembered; sri-radha-hari—of Sri Radha and Sri Hari; keli—of the pastimes; kautuka—about the festival; katha—talks; pratah—in the morning; sakhl-mandale—amidst the sakhis; pratyavartayate—made to return (i.e. drove back); gatam—it had come; api—although; nisam—the night; saksat-vidhatte—directly makes (directly experienced); ca—and; tau—They two.

**Перевод:**

**In the morning, a gopi narrating the events of the previous night forgot about the sequence, since she was elated. The smart domesticated parrots corrected her in a manner so everyone’s joy increased. The talk among the sakhis of the pastime festivals of Sri Radha and Sri Hari drove back the night although it had already arrived, and caused them to have a realization about Radha and Krsna.**

*atrālpa-svaratvena cārcitatvena ca hari-śabdasyaiva pūrvanipāta ucitaḥ. tad-anyathā-bhāve śrī-rādheti pūrva-nipāto hi tasyā vaidagdhyātiśaya-dyotakaḥ. iti padāṁśāḥ. racanāyā varṇānāṁ ca rīti-granthe vyañjakatvaṁ darśayiṣyate.*

**Перевод:**

**The word hari in the compound sri-radha-hari should have been placed first because the word hari has fewer syllables and because Hari is more worshipable. Since it has not been placed first here, this purva-nipata (placing Radha first) suggests the excellence of Her cleverness.**

**Here ends the discussion on the padamsas. The suggestiveness of the phonemes and of the styles will be expounded in the section on the styles.**

**Комментарий:**

By rule, the compound sri-radha-hari should have been sri-hari- radha. The grammatical meaning is the same (Sri Hari and Sri Radha), but the semantic import differs. The word hari should have been placed first for three reasons: (1) The words ends in the letter i, (2) It has a light syllable, whereas radha does not, and (3) The old-school convention is that a man is more honorable than a woman.

*saṅkareṇa tri-rūpeṇa saṁsṛṣṭyā caika-rūpayā*

iti—thus; purvaih—by the previous \[teachers\]; vilikhitam—it has been written; na—not; sarvesam—of all \[of them\]; udahrtih— examples; bhavet—possible; yogyatva—capability; matratvat— because of the mere; adhikyam—an abundance; api—even; gamyate—it should be understood.

### 3.65

*tatra tri-rūpaḥ saṅkaro yathā,*  
*saṁśayāspadatānugrāhyānugrāhakatāpi ca*  
*eka-vyañjaka-saṁśleṣaḥ saṅkaras tri-vidho mataḥ (20)*

**Пословный перевод:**

samsaya—of doubt (i.e. a choice between two options); aspadata— which has the state of being a place (i.e. an object); anugrahya— and facilitated; anugrahakata—which has the state of being a facilitator; api—also; ca—and; eka—only one thing; vyanjaka— which suggests; samslesah—which has a double meaning of a word (sabda-slesa); sankarah—mixing; tri-vidhah—threefold; matah—is known.

**Перевод:**

**Sankara (mix of dhvanis) has three varieties:**
