### 3.66

*udāharaṇam,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of sankara:**

*padminy ahaṁ kumudinī kila saiva satyaṁ*  
*satyaṁ bhavāṁś ca madhusūdana eva mattaḥ*  
*vāmena tām asukhayan niśi dakṣiṇena*  
*prātaḥ prabodhayati mām api locanena*

**Пословный перевод:**

padmini—a lotus; aham—I; kumudini—a night-blooming lotus; kila—indeed; sa—she; eva—only; satyam—truly; satyam—truly; bhavan—You; ca—and; madhusudana—O Krsna (or O bee); eva—only; mattah—maddened (or self-satisfied); vamena—with the left (or with an inferior; or with a crooked); tam—her; asukhayat—he made happy; nisi—at night; daksinena—with the right (or with a greater; or with a direct); pratah—in the morning; prabodhayati mam—he causes me to wake up; api—even; locanena—with the eye (or with a darsana (“showing oneself”); or with a glance).

**Перевод:**

**Truly, I am a day lotus, she is a night lotus, and You, Madhusudana, are maddened. You make her happy at night with Your left eye, and You wake me up in the morning with Your right eye.**

*atra padminy-ādi-śabdārthayoḥ śabdārtha-śaktyudbhavānudhvaneḥ saṅkara-trayam. tathā hi—māṁ prati bhavato ’nurāgo mahān, yato māṁ dakṣiṇena udāreṇa locanena darśanena prabodhayati. tāṁ prati tathā nānurāgaḥ, yato vāmena darśanena tāṁ niśi asukhayat—atra hetv-alaṅkāro vyaṅgyaḥ. yato ’haṁ padminī, sā kumudinī, padminy-apekṣayā kumudinī nikṛṣṭaiva. kiṁ vāhaṁ padminī nāmnaiva padminī, na tu vastuta iti, anyathā mayy eva tvam anurakto ’bhaviṣyaḥ. sā tu nāmnaiva kumudinī, na tu vastuta iti ca satyam, anyathā tasyāṁ nānurakto ’bhaviṣya iti saṁśayaḥ. atha padminy aham, kumudinī saiveti rūpakālaṅkāreṇa tad-dhetūpanyāsa-dvārā prātar māṁ prabodhayasi, niśi tām asukhayat—iti hetv-alaṅkāro vyaṅgyaḥ. bhavān madhusūdana eveti madhusūdanasya bhramarasya tavobhayataḥ samarāgatayā na doṣaḥ, kintu mamaiva doṣaḥ, yato ’haṁ padminī, padminyāḥ prātar eva bhramareṇa saha sandarśanam iti madhusūdana-śabdadyotyena vastunā punar api rūpakālaṅkāro dhvanitaḥ. ity anayor mitho ’nugrāhyānugrāhakatayā saṅkaraḥ. evaṁ madhusūdana eva bhavān mattaḥ svatas tṛptaḥ, “mada” tṛpti-yoge dhātuḥ. tava kutrāpi nāpekṣeti svabhāvokty-alaṅkāreṇa tava dakṣiṇaṁ cakṣuḥ sūryātmakam, yatas tena padminīṁ māṁ prabodhayasi, vāmaṁ tu candrātmakam, yena kumudinīṁ tām asukhayaḥ—ity ekasminn eva vyañjake madhusūdana-pada-saṁśleṣa eka-vyañjanānupraveśaḥ. atha dakṣiṇena saralena darśanena māṁ prabodhayasi, tena te mayi rāgo nāsti, vāmena kuṭilena tām asukhayaḥ, tena tasyām eva te rāga iti vastunā svabhāvato madhusūdano bhramaro jñānaśūnyas tatrāpi matta iti svabhāvoktiḥ. tathā-vidhasya tava kuto vivekaḥ, tena tvam avidagdho ’sīti svabhāvākhyānākṣepayoḥ saṁsṛṣṭiḥ. evaṁ pada-vākya-dyotyair garva-dhairya-dainyaglāni-nirvedāvahitthādi-bhāva-dhvanibhiś ca saṁsṛṣṭiḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**There are three sankaras in the verse. The first two arise by the sabda-sakti and the artha-sakti of padmini and so on and the third one is a subsequent dhvani that emerges from both sabda-sakti and artha-sakti.**

**The first sankara is a samsaya (the doubt: Is this dhvani occurring or is that dhvani occurring?). The first possible dhvani is understood as follows: “You have much love for me, because in the morning You wake me up by straightforwardly (daksinena = udarena) looking (locanena = darsanena) at me, whereas Your love for her is not like that because You give her pleasure at night by crookedly (vamena = anudarena) looking at her.” In that way, the hetu ornament (explanatory reason), the first possible dhvani, is implied: “because I am a padmini, but she is a kumudini insofar as a kumudini is inferior to a padmini.” The second possible dhvani is: “I am a padmini in name only, not truly, otherwise why are You dispassionate toward me? And she is a kumudini in name only, not truly, otherwise why do You love her so much?”**

**The second sankara is anugrahya anugrahakata (facilitated and facilitator). The double metaphor in the verse, “I am a padmini and she is a kumudini,” implies the hetu ornament (explanatory reason): “\[because\] You wake me up in the morning and make her happy at night.” In addition, the double metaphor is suggested by the following vastu (idea), which is hinted at by the word madhusudana in bhavan madhusudana eva (You’re just a bee): “Your having an equal love for both of us is not faulty, since You’re a bee. Rather the fault is mine, because I’m a padminT in the sense that a lotus is seen with a bee in the morning.”**

**The third sankara, eka-vyanjaka anupravesa (two dhvanis in one word), signifies the subsequent entrance of Suggestiveness in the same suggestive word: madhusudana. At first, the svabhavokti ornament (the nature) occurs: “You, Madhusudana, are self­satisfied (mattah = svatas trptah): You don’t require anything.” The verbal root is mad trpti-yoge. On account of that svabhavokti, she says: “Your right eye is of the nature of the sun. And that is because by means of it You wake up the day lotus that I am. But Your left eye is of the nature of the moon, by means of which You delighted the night lotus that she is.”**

**The verse also features samsrsti (combination of separate dhvanis). At first, this idea is apparent: “You make me up with a straightforward (daksinena = saralena) glance, therefore You do not feel passionate toward me, whereas You make her happy with a crooked (vamena = kutilena) glance, and so You feel passionate toward her.” This vastu gives rise to the svabhavokti ornament: “By nature You’re a bee, so You’re ignorant. Besides, You’re mad (mattah).” Additionally, this rebuke is implied: “Since You, whose nature is such, have no proper discrimination, You’re not clever.” This constitutes a samsrsti of svabhavokti and aksepa.**

**Moreover, another samsrsti takes place between vyabhicari- bhavas, such as: garva (overweening pride), dhairya (steadfastness of the heart), dainya (meekness), glani (witheredness of body), nirveda (self-disparagement), and avahittha (concealment), which are implied from single words and from the overall sense.**

### 3.67

*yathā vā,*

**Перевод:**

**Another example of samsrsti:**

*ucchūna-stanitasya sarva-sukha-daḥ kṛṣṇāmbudasyodayo*  
*vātāḥ śīkara-vāhinaḥ sumanasāṁ vīthī vikāśaṁ gatā*  
*snigdhā bhūr gata eva saṁjvara-bharaḥ śyāmāyamānā diśaḥ*  
*sphītaṁ gokulam unmadāś ca saritaḥ śītā giri-droṇayaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

ucchuna—loudly; stanitasya—\[of the clouds\] that are rumbling (or ucchuna-stani tasya, where ucchuna-stani means “O girl with raised breasts,” and tasya means “his”); sarva-sukha-dah—gives happiness to everyone; krsna-ambudasya—of the blackish cloud (or of the cloud along with Krsna); udayah—the appearance; vatah—the breezes; sikara—drops of water (i.e. mist); vahinah—are carrying; sumanasam—of flowers; vithi—the row (the multitude); vikasam gata—has reached the state of blooming; snigdha—is moist (soft); bhuh—the ground; gatah—has gone away; eva—only; samjvara- bharah—excessive heat; syamayamanah—have become blackish; disah—the directions; sphitam—is flourishing (i.e. greatly happy); gokulam—\[the inhabitants of\] Gokula; unmadah—are extravagant; ca—and; saritah—the rivers; sitah—are cool; giri—mountains; dronayah—and valleys.

**Перевод:**

**The appearance of a loudly rumbling blackish cloud makes everyone happy. The breeze is carrying mist and the flowers have bloomed. The earth has become moist and the excessive heat has been dispelled. The directions have become dark, the bliss of Gokula has greatly increased, the rivers are boisterous, and the mountains and the valleys have become cool.**

*atra śabda-śakty-udbhavārtha-śakty-udbhava-dhvanyoḥ saṁsṛṣṭyā dhvani-saṁsṛṣṭiḥ, tathālaṅkārāṇāṁ vastunāṁ ca saṁsṛṣṭiḥ.tathā hi—guru-samīpa-sthitāṁ govardhana-nikaṭanagara-nāgarīṁ prati giri-kandarāsaṅketa-sthaṁ śrī-kṛṣṇaṁ vijñāpayituṁ vyājena daivopanataṁ meghodayaṁ lakṣyī-kṛtya kācit sakhī vadati. vācyārthaḥ sphuṭa eva. atroddīpana-vibhāvaś ca sphuṭo bhavan tulya-yogitālaṅkāraṁ vyanakti. śrī-kṛṣṇaś ca saṅketa-sthaḥ, ambudodayaś cābhūd iti yaugapadya-pratipattyā tulya-yogitā, karma-dhārayopalakṣaṇa-tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa-padamātrayoḥ saṁsṛṣṭiḥ. kṛṣṇāmbudayoḥ sādharmyād upamālaṅkāro vyaṅgyaḥ. ucchūna-stanitasyeti—ucchūna-garjitatvenāmbudasya varṣukatvam, tena ca śīghram abhisareti vastu vyaṅgyam. he ucchūna-stani, tasyeti sa-bhaṅga-saṁśleṣeṇa sambodhayamānajanasya prauḍhatvam, tena ca stana-bharākrāntatayā gamanamāntharyam, tena ca nātaḥ paraṁ vilambanīyam iti dhvanipratidhvany-anudhvananam, tasyeti—sarvanāmno mahimnā kṛṣṇasya parama-durlabhatā, tathā ca bahu-vallabhatvam. sarvasukha-da iti hetor hetv-alaṅkāro vyaṅgyaḥ, tasmān nātaḥ paraṁ vilamba-kārya iti vastu. vātāḥ śīkara-vāhina iti svabhāvākhyānam, tena ca surata-śrama-jala-kaṇāpahāriṇaś caite bhaviṣyantīti vastu. sumanasāṁ mālatīnām iti pūrva-vat svabhāvākhyānam.*

*tena sumanasāṁ māna-rahitānām, anyāsām aṅganānāṁ ca vīthī samūhaḥ kṛṣṇo ’bhisartavya iti yo vikāśaḥ prasādas taṁ gateti vastu. tena ca yāvat kāpi taṁ nābhisarati, tāvat tvam abhisareti vastu. snigdhābhūr iti—caraṇa-saṁcaraṇa-sukha-datvam, paraṁ ca—snigdhā abhūḥ, tava manasi vāmyaṁ ca nāsti, tat katham ataḥ paraṁ vilambasa iti vastu. snigdhātve hetuḥ—gata eva saṁjvara-bhara iti hetv-alaṅkāraḥ. tena ca tvad-ākāreṇaiva mayā tvad-antaḥ-karaṇaṁ jñātam iti sva-cāturya-prakaṭanam. śyāmāyamānā diśa ity alakṣyā bhūtvā gamiṣyasi, tena na kāpi śaṅketi vastu.vyaṅgya-pakṣe, gokulaṁ—vraja-sthalī, sphītaṁ— janākīrṇam, tenātra tam ānetuṁ na śaknomi. sarito yamunādyā utpūrāḥ, tena taṭādau ca na saṅketa-yogyatā. tarhi pāriśeṣyāt śītā giri-droṇaya iti bhaṅgyā tatraivābhisāraḥ kriyatām. tatraivāgato ’sti kṛṣṇa iti vyañjakānāṁ saṁsṛṣṭir eva. evaṁvidhā eva dhvanaya uttamottama-kāvya-lakṣaṇa-bījam. dhvaner vyāpāra-yugalaṁ dhvananam anudhvananaṁ ca. yatra kevalaṁ dhvananam, tad uttamaṁ kāvyam, yatra tu dhvananānudhvanane, tad uttamottamam. prācīnais tu sarveṣām uttamatvaṁ likhyate, tat tu nāsmākam abhīṣṭam, yataḥ “tvām asmi vacmi” ity-ādau vacer arthāntara-saṅkramita-vācya-dhvaneḥ, “snigdha-śyāmalakānti-lipta-viyataḥ” ity-ādeś cānudhvanana-rūpārthāntarasaṅkramitātyanta-tiraskṛta-saṁsṛṣṭyā ca mahā-dhvaner eka evāsvādaś cel labhyate, tais tu labhyatāṁ nāma, na tv asmābhiḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**There is a samsrsti by the combination of sabda-sakti-bhu dhvani and artha-sakti-bhu dhvani. There are also combinations between alankara-dhvanis and vastu-dhvanis.**

**\[This is the background story:\] A certain sakhi speaks to a her group leader, who is in a village near Govardhana, in the presence of her elders. The sakhi points to a cloud which had appeared by chance. On the pretext of speaking about the cloud, she talks about Krsna, indicating that now He is in a cave of Govardhana, the scheduled meeting place. The literal meaning of the verse is clear.**

**The uddipana (stimulus) is also very clear, and it suggests the tulya-yogita ornament: The cloud has risen and Krsna has come to the meeting place. Both happened at the same time.**

**There is a combination (samsrsti) of a karma-dharaya compound (krsnambuda is taken to mean “blackish cloud”) with an indicative trtiya-tatpurusa compound (krsnambuda is taken to mean “the cloud along with Krsna”).**

**On account of a similitude between Krsna and a dark cloud, a simile is implied.**

**The word stanitasya in ucchuna-stanitasya means garjitasya (rumbling). \[The sakhi means to say:\] “The cloud is about to shower because it is rumbling. You should quickly go to the meeting place.” This is an implied idea.**

**The compound ucchuna-stanitasya can also be taken as ucchuna-stani (O you who have raised breasts) and tasya (His). The excellence of the person who is addressed is thus implied by the different breakup of these words. Therefore: “Your going will be slow since your breasts are heavy.” “So don’t delay any longer.” A dhvani occasions another that way.**

**Additionally, the word tasya suggests that Krsna is difficult to attain; this suggestion is due to the force of the pronoun. And that is because Krsna has many lovers.**

**Due to the word sarva-sukha-da (it gives pleasure to all), the hetu alankara “since He makes everyone happy” is suggested. The idea implied by that is: “You shouldn’t delay any longer.**

**The description of the wind conveying mist is an instance of the svabhavokti ornament. This alankara suggests the following vastu: The breeze will dissipate the drops of perspiration caused by exertion during lovemaking.**

**When it is said that the flowers (sumanas), such as jasmines, are blooming, that is another instance of the svabhavokti ornament. The word sumanasam can also be interpreted as su-manasam, “\[the blooming state (vikasa)\] of women who have a good mind,” in other words: “of the other girls, who have no pique.”**

**The word vithi simply means “multitude,” and vikasa can signify prasada (sastisfaction, peace of mind). Thus the vastu behind the clause sumanasam vithi vikasam gata is: “Many other girls who had no mana attained peace of mind knowing they will meet Krsna.” A further vastu is: “As long as some girl doesn’t meet Him, you should go and meet Him right away.”**

**The words snigdha bhuh (the earth is moist) means the ground is a pleasure to walk on. The same words may be interpreted as snigdha abhuh, meaning “You have become amiable: there is no haughtiness in your heart.” The vastu suggested is: “Why are you delaying?”**

**The reason the earth is moist is expressed by the words “The excessive heat has been dispelled.” This is the hetu alankara. By that too she shows her cleverness to her group leader: “I read your mind because you have the exact same form (you have become moist).”**

**The vastu suggested by the words syamayamana disah (the directions have become dark) is: “By remaining unseen, there is no doubt that you’ll be able to go unnoticed, so don’t worry.”**

**There are additional implied ideas. Gokula refers not to the inhabitants of Gokula but to the land of Vraja, and sphltam (greatly) signifies that Gokula, meaning Vraja, is crowded with people. Therefore “You cannot bring Krsna here.”**

**Additionally, the word saritah (rivers) denotes the Yamuna and so on, and in this sense sphitam means “overflowing”, thus “It’s not appropriate to organize a rendezvous on a riverbank.”**

**By a process of elimination (only the words sita giri-dronayah are left to analyze), what is inferred is that the hills and the valleys are the only suitable places to meet Krsna. The idea is that Krsna has already arrived there.**

**There are combinations (samsrsti) of many suggestions that way. Dhvanis like these are the reason poetry is called uttamottama- kavya (one first-rate implied sense occasions another).**

**There are two kinds of dhvanis: a single dhvani and an anudhvani (subsequent implied sense). When there is a single dhvani, the poetry is called uttama-kavya (excellent poetry), but when there is a dhvani and an anudhvani, the poetry is classed as uttamottama-kavya (superexcellent poetry).**

**All the previous poetical theorists only spoke of uttama kavya. But we do not agree with this. If the delight they feel by perceiving the arthantara-sankramita-vacya-dhvani in: tvam asmi vacmi, “I am talking to you” (“All-important I am talking to you”) (Kavya-prakasa verse 23) is the same as the delight they feel from a maha-dhvani by the samsrsti of an arthantara- sankramita-dhvani, in the form of an anudhvani, and an atyanta-tiraskrta-vacya-dhvani in the verse that begins snigdha- syamala-kanti, then let them have such a uniform relishment if they want; we relish those meanings differently.**

**Комментарий:**

This is the verse:

*snigdha-syamala-kanti-lipta-viyato vellad-balaka ghana*  
*vatah slkarinah payoda-suhrdam ananda-kekah kalah*  
*kamam santu drdham kathora-hrdayo ramo ’smi sarvam sahe*  
*vaidehi tu katham bhavisyati ha ha ha devi dhira bhava*

“The clouds smear the sky with a loveliness, a glossy dark color. The breezes carry mist. The cranes are going in the sky, and the peacocks, the friends of the clouds, blissfully make the sweet sound keka at will. Let it be. My heart is unwaveringly hard. I am Rama. I tolerate everything. But how will Sita be able to live? Alas, alas, Devi, be patient!”’

The verse is suggestive of vipralambha. Anandavardhana comments: arthantara-sankramita-vacyo yatha, snigdha-syamala \[...\] ity atra rama-sabdah, anena hi vyangya-dharmantara- parinatah samjm pratyayyate, na samjni-matram, “Here the word Rama is arthantara-sankramita-vacya: He who has the name Rama is made to be understood as one who changed in terms of having another, implied attribute (being able to naturally tolerate heavy sorrow), but it is not that only He who is so named is made to be perceived” (Dhvany-aloka 2.1).

Mammata elaborates: atra lipteti payoda-suhrdam iti catyanta- tiraskrta-vacyayoh samsrstih. tabhyam saha ramo ’smity arthantara-samkramita-vacyasyanugrahyanugrahaka-bhavena rama-pada-laksanaika-vyanjakanupravesena carthantara- samkramita-vacya-rasa-dhvanyoh samkarah, “There is a samsrsti of two atyanta-tiraskrta-vacya-dhvanis, in “The sky is smeared by clouds” and “the peacocks are friends of the clouds” (these are two virodha ornaments). There is a sankara of arthantara-sankramita- vacya-dhvani and rasa-dhvani (vipralambha) both by the mode of “facilitated and facilitator” between those two atyanta-tiraskrta- vacya-dhvanis on the one hand and the arthantara-sankramita- vacya-dhvani in the word Rama on the other and by the mode of “two dhvanis in the same word”.” (Kavya-prakasa, verse 112)

The poetical theorists are known to indulge in splitting hairs. The arthantara-sankramita-vacya-dhvani in the word Rama amounts to a vibhava (namely a quality of the hero): It partly evokes the vipralambha, but here Mammata classes it as the rasa-dhvani itself when he says “two dhvanis in the same word” (the arthantara- sankramita-vacya-dhvani and the vibhava). Further, the two virodha ornaments act like uddipanas and thus evoke the vipralambha.

*ity alankara-kaustubhe dhvani-nirnayo nama trtiyah kiranah.*

**Перевод:**

**Here ends the third ray in Alankara-kaustubha, entitled “A disquisition on dhvani.”**

## Fourth Ray - Second-rate Poetry

### 4.1

*atha guṇī-bhūta-vyaṅgya-nirṇayaḥ. atha guṇī-bhūta-vyaṅgyāni kiyanti bhavantīty ākāṅkṣāyāṁ teṣāṁ bhedān āha. yadyapi “madhyame tatra madhyamam” iti pūrvoktasya madhyamakāvyasyaiva guṇī-bhūta-vyaṅgyatvam, tathāpi dhvaner avaiśiṣṭye vaiśiṣṭye ca hetv-antaropādhito guṇa-bhāvād guṇī-bhūtatvam iti cvy-artha eva dvaividhyaṁ bodhayati. tatrāvaiśiṣṭye bhedo nāsti, eka-rūpatvāt, dvitīye tu bhedo’ṣṭadheti sūtrayati—*

**Перевод:**

**Now, in response to the anticipated question: “How many kinds of second-rate poetry are there?”, he describes them. The concept of second-rate implied meaning was mentioned earlier: “Poetry is average when the dhvani is average” (1.14).**

**The suffix cvi in the term guni-bhuta (second-rate, literally: it has become secondary) indicates two stages: An implied sense became secondary because a secondariness was attributed to it, for diverse reasons.**

**An implied sense is either excellent or nonexcellent. There is no subdivision of a nonexcellent implied sense, but there are eight varieties of an excellent implied sense that has become secondary.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti explains: The derivation of guni-bhuta is: aguno guni-bhavati, “What was not secondary becomes secondary” (Subodhini). The rule of thumb is that a dhvani is average when it is not more astonishing than the expressed meaning of the sentence.

An implied sense in third-rate poetry, though lifeless by nature, can still be classed either as a vastu-dhvani, an alankara-dhvani or a rasa-dhvani. For example, in Kavi Kamapura’s illustration of third-rate poetry he says the dhvani is lifeless (1.18). That dhvani is a raudra-rasabhasa. Kavi Karnapura raised the standards of poetry. In Mammata’s methodology, raudra-rasabhasa corresponds to the urjasvi ornament, which belongs to the aparanga variety of second-rate implied sense (4.5). A third-rate implied sense is “obvious”, meaning it is even more obvious than the sphuta variety of second-rate implied sense (4.3). In Mammata’s methodology, third-rate poetry is simply characterized either by an ornament of sound or by an ornament of meaning in which the implied sense, if any, is negligible. Some ornaments of meaning inherently contain an implied sense, such as an implied similarity, therefore the poetry might be ugraded to second-rate depending on the quality of that implied sense.

### 4.2

**Перевод:**

**The eight varieties are made into a sutra as follows:**

*sphuṭam aparāṅgaṁ vācya-prapoṣakaṁ kaṣṭa-gamyaṁ ca sandigdha-prādhānyaṁ tulya-prādhānya-kāku-gamye ca amanojñaṁ ceti guṇī-bhūta-vyaṅgyasya bhedāḥ syuḥ (1)*

**Перевод:**

**The eight kinds of second-rate implied meanings are:**

**1. sphuta (obvious),**

**2. aparanga (an aspect of another) (a main rasa is a subsidiary aspect of a minor rasa),**

**3. vacya-praposaka (substantiating a literal meaning in the sentence),**

**4. kasta-gamya (understood with difficulty),**

**5. sandigdha-pradhanya (a doubt about which implied sense is predominant),**

**6. tulya-pradhanya (the literal meaning and the implied meaning are equally predominant),**

**7. kaku-gamya (understood with a modulation of the voice), and 8. amanojna (not as charming as the literal meaning of the text).**

### 4.3

*krameṇodāharaṇāni,*

**Перевод:**

**Examples are shown in order.**  
**(1)  \[This illustrates sphuta (obvious):\]**

*dṛṣṭā bhāgavatāḥ kṛpāpy upagatā teṣāṁ sthitam taiḥ samaṁ*  
*jñātaṁ vastu viniścitaṁ ca kiyatā premṇāpi tatrāsitam*  
*jīvadbhir na mṛtaṁ mṛtair yadi punar martavyam asmādṛśair*  
*utpadyaiva na kiṁ mṛtaṁ bata vidhe vāmāya tubhyaṁ namaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

drsta—was seen; bhagavatah—the Lord’s devotees; krpa—mercy; api—too; upagata—was attained; tesam—their; sthitam—situated; taih—with them; samam—together; jnatam—was understood; vastu—the thing; viniscitam—ascertained \[as the essence of all (says VCT)\]; ca—and; kiyata—with how much; premna—love; api—also; tatra—there; asitam—sitting; jivadbhih—by those who are living; na—does not occur; mrtam—death; mrtaih—by those who are dead; yadi—if; punah—moreover; martavyam—dying; asmadrsaih—by people like us; utpadya eva—right after taking birth; na—is there no; kim—why?; mrtam—death; bata—alas!; vidhe—the creator (or Providence) (vidhe = vidhatre); vamaya— crooked (cruel); tubhyam—unto you; namah—obeisances.

**Перевод:**

**I saw the devotees of the Lord and attained their mercy. I was with them. I understood the real thing that was ascertained by them as the essence of all. I used to sit among them with so much love. If persons like us don’t die while we’re in a good condition, and moreover if we’ll have to die in a miserable state, then why don’t we just die after taking birth? Alas, O cruel fate, obeisances to you.**

*atra jīvadbhir iti snigdhāvasthaiḥ, mṛtair iti tad-viparītāvasthair ity arthāntara-saṅkramita-vācyam, tat tu sphuṭam iti guṇī-bhūtam.*

**Перевод:**

**Here jivadbhih (by those who are alive) signifies “by those who are in a happy stage of life.” And the word mrtaih (by those who passed away) signifies “by those in a miserable stage of life.”**

**These two suggestions are instances of arthantara-sankramita- vacya (the literal meaning slightly changes). However, those suggestions are obvious (sphuta), and so they are secondary (guni-bhuta).**

**Комментарий:**

The sphuta variety of second-rate suggestions was already illustrated in text 2.29, because sphuta corresponds to the agudha variety (not subtle) of purposeful figurative usage. But sphuta is broader inasmuch as figurative usage need not be involved (1.17).

### 4.4

*yathā vā,*

**Перевод:**

**Another example of sphuta (obvious):**

*śayana-sahacarīṇāṁ locanair arcyamānā-*  
*ny atirati-jaya-lakṣmī-lakṣmabhiḥ pakṣmalāni*  
*rahasi sa-bahu-mānaṁ cumbyamānāni dṛgbhyāṁ*  
*svajata iva mṛgākṣī svāṅgakaiḥ svāṅgakāni*

**Пословный перевод:**

sayana—while taking rest; sahacarmam—of those who accompany (the servants); locanaih—by the eyes; arcyamanani—are worshiped; ati-rati—in the eminent \[battle of\] love; jaya—during the victory; laksmi—of beauty; laksmabhih—with signs; paksmalani—reddish (“they have saffron”); rahasi—in a secret place; sa-bahu- manam—with great respect; cumbyamanani—are being kissed (seen); drgbhyam—by the eyes; svajate—is embracing (touching); iva—as if; mrga-aksi—the doe-eyed girl; sva-angakaih—with her soft limbs; sva-angakani—her soft limbs.

**Перевод:**

**This doe-eyed girl attained glory in the battle of love. Her limbs, colorful due to marks that reveal the resplendence of her triumph, are worshiped by the eyes of her maidservants while she takes rest in a secret location. With much reverence she kisses her limbs with both eyes. She as if embraces her limbs with her limbs.**

*atra “arcyamānāni” “pakṣmalāni” “cumbyamānāni dṛgbhyāṁ” “svajate” ity-ādīny arthāntara-saṅkramita-vācyāni, tāni sphuṭāny eva.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the words arcyamanani (are worshiped), paksmalani (colorful), cumbyamanani drgbhyam (kissed with both eyes), and svajate (she embraces) are instances of arthantara- sankramita-vacya (the literal meaning changes to another sense). The changes of meaning are obvious (sphuta).**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: The sense of arcyamanani (are worshiped) is: sva-saphalya-mananena sadaram drstani, “Her maidservants very respectfully look at her limbs by thinking that their lives have become successful.” In paksmalani, the implied sense is that her limbs are colorful due to signs of lovemaking. The sense of cumbyamanani drgbhyam (she kisses her limbs with both eyes) is: asakti-purvakam drstani (she looks at her limbs with much fondness), and this suggests this idea (vastu-dhvani): “Today I have become successful.” The sense of svajate (she embraces) is: punah punah sprsati (she repeatedly touches them). All these changes of meaning are obvious (Subodhim).

The word arcyamanani (are worshiped) is an instance of atyanta- tiraskrta-vacya. Nonetheless, the figurative meaning is sphuta. The same applies to “kissed with both eyes”. They are two virodha ornaments (semblance of a contradiction).

The literal meaning ofpaksmalani is “reddish”. By the convention of poets, the idea is that her lover’s nail marks on her skin add color to it. Most of the time, paksma means eyelashes. According to Kavi Karnapura, when a word that has a strong conventional sense is used in a lesser-known meaning, that is a form of figurative usage; he gave the word mandapa as an example (2.10).

### 4.5

*aparāṅgaṁ yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**(2)  An example of aparanga (a main rasa is a subsidiary aspect of a minor rasa):**

*kope yathātilalitaṁ na tathā prasāde*  
*vaktraṁ vidhis tava tanotu sadaiva kopam*  
*ity ākalayya dayitasya vaco-vibhaṅgīṁ*  
*rādhā jahāsa vihasatsu sakhī-janeṣu*

**Пословный перевод:**

kope—when there is anger; yatha—as; atilalitam—very charming; na tatha—not like that; prasade—when there is serenity; vaktram— face; vidhih—the creator; tava—Your; tanotu—may he make; sada—always; eva—only; kopam—anger; iti—(end of citation); akalayya—after noticing (hearing); dayitasya—of the male beloved; vacah—of speech; vibhangim—the crookedness; radha— Radha; jahasa—laughed; vihasatsu sakhl-janesu—among Her friends, who were laughing (or while Her friends were laughing).

**Перевод:**

**“Your face is not as exceedingly charming when You are serene as it is when You are angry. The creator should always make You angry.” Hearing these crooked words of Her beloved, Radha laughed among Her friends, who burst into laughter.**

*atra vipralambha-śṛṅgāro hāsyasyāṅgam. “rādhā vivartitā vinamra-mukhī babhūva” iti cet, tadā kopa-praśamo vrīḍodayaś ceti dhvanir eva syāt.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the vipralambha-srngara-rasa is an aspect of hasya-rasa (humor). If the words radha jahasa vihasatsu sakhi-janesu (Radha laughed among Her friends, who burst into laughter) were replaced with radha vivartita vinamra-mukhi babhuva (Radha turned around and lowered Her face), the implied meanings would be that Her anger dissipated and a rise of bashfulness occurred.**

**Комментарий:**

The verse features vipralambha in the sense that Krsna was not present: The sakhls reiterated His words. In the replacement clause, the hasya-rasa is removed, therefore the implied meanings (bhava-santi and bhavodaya) are first-rate.

### 4.6

*yathā vā,*

**Перевод:**

**Another example of aparanga:**

*mugdhe parihara mānaṁ*  
*mānaya vacanaṁ priyāli-vṛndasya*  
*yauvanam idam ambhoruha*  
*dala-jala-bindūpamaṁ viddhi*

**Пословный перевод:**

mugdhe—O simple girl; parihara—remove; manam—anger; manaya—pay heed; vacanam—to the words; priya-ali—dear friends; vrndasya—of your many; yauvanam—youth; idam—this; ambhah-ruha—of a lotus (“which grows on water”); dala—on the petal; jala-bindu—a drop of water; upamam—resembles; viddhi— you should know.

**Перевод:**

**Simple girl, give up your mana and pay heed to your dear friends’s advice: You should know that youthfulness is fleeting like a drop of water on a lotus petal.**

*atrāpi vipralambha-śṛṅgāra-dhvaniḥ śānta-rasasyāṅgam. “arcaya yauvana-kusumair devaṁ kuñje-caraṁ kim api” ity ukte dhvanir eva syāt.*

**Перевод:**

**Here also the vipralambha-srngara-rasa-dhvani is a subordinate element of another rasa: santa. If the last half of the verse (“You should known that youthfulness is fleeting like a drop of water on a lotus petal”) were replaced with: arcaya yauvana-kusumair devam kunje-caram kim api, “Worship with the flowers of your youth a certain god who wanders in the pleasure groves,” then the implied sense (the vipralambha) would be first-class.**

### 4.7

*vācya-prapoṣakaṁ yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**(3)  An example of vacya-praposaka**  
**(substantiating a literal meaning in the sentence):**

*kvāhaṁ gopa-vadhūḥ smarāyuta-jayī gopendra-sūnuḥ kva vā*  
*sārdhaṁ tena ratir mamābhavad iti bhrāntaiḥ paraṁ bhaṇyate*  
*ity evaṁ guru-karṇa-gocaratayā sakhyā samaṁ nirmitāṁ*  
*vāṇīm anyathayāñcakāra pulakī gaṇḍaḥ kuraṅgī-dṛśaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

kva—where?; aham—am I; gopa—of a cowherd; vadhuh—the wife; smara—of Cupids; ayuta—ten thousands; jayi—who defeats; gopa-indra—of the king of cowherds; sunuh—the son; kva—where is?; va—and; sardham tena—with Him; ratih—love; mama—my; abhavat—occurred; iti—end of citation; bhrantaih—by people who are mistaken; param—loudly; bhanyate—it is said; iti—thus; evam—in this way; guru—of her elders; karna-gocarataya—within the range of the ears; sakhya samam—with a friend; nirmitam— that occurred; vanim—the words; anyathayancakara—altered \[her words\] (made her words false); pulaki—which has horripilation; gandah—the cheek; kurangi-drsah—of the doe-eyed girl.

**Перевод:**

**“I am just the wife of a cowherd, and He, the son of the king of cowherds, excels thousands of Cupids! Some foolish people say I love Him.” A doe-eyed girl spoke these words to a sakhi within earshot of her elders, but her cheeks, which had goose bumps, made her words false.**

*atra “anyathayāñcakāra” ity asya vācyasya gaṇḍasya pulakitatvaṁ prapoṣakam. “ity evaṁ guru-karṇa-gocaratayā sakhyā samaṁ jalpane romāñcotkiram añcalena su-mukhī gaṇḍa-sthalīm āvṛṇot” ity ukte dhvanir eva syāt.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the mention of horripilation on the cheeks virtually reiterates the literal meaning: “made her words false”. However, if the second half of the verse were modified as follows:**

*ity evaṁ guru-karṇa-gocaratayā sakhyā samaṁ jalpane*  
*romāñcotkiram añcalena su-mukhī gaṇḍa-sthalīm āvṛṇot*

**Перевод:**

**“While thus talking to her friend within earshot of her elders, the beautiful girl covered her cheeks, replete with goose bumps, with the edge of her sari,” then the dhvani would be first-class.**

**Комментарий:**

In the new version, her covering her cheeks is an instance of avahittha vyabhicari-bhava-dhvani (concealment). And this eminently suggests that she loves Krsna.

### 4.8

*yathā vā,*

**Перевод:**

**Another example of vacya-praposaka:**

*kāṭhinyaṁ guṇa eva yena bhavatī kāntasya keśa-grahaṁ*  
*sneho dūṣaṇam eva yena labhate daipī daśā dagdhatām*  
*tubhyaṁ kaṅkatike namo ’stu dhig iti snehām iti vyāja-vāg*  
*vinyāsā cikura-prasādhana-vidhau kṛṣṇena sā sasvaje*

**Пословный перевод:**

kathinyam—hardness; gunah—quality; eva—actually; yena— because of which \[hardness\]; bhavati—you; kantasya—of the beloved (Krsna); kesa-graham—taking the hair; snehah—softness (or oilyness); dusanam—is a fault; eva—actually; yena—because of which \[softness (or oilyness)\]; labhate—attains; daipi—of a lamp; dasa—the ghee wick; dagdhatam—the state of being burnt; tubhyam—to you; kankatike—O comb!; namah—obeisances; astu— may there be; dhik—fie on you; iti—thus; sneham—softness (or oiliness); iti—in this way; vyaja—is on a pretext; vak—of words; vinyasa—she whose placement (utterance); cikura—of the hair; prasadhana—the arrangement (combing); vidhau—while doing; krsnena—by Krsna; sa—she; sasvaje—was embraced.

**Перевод:**

**“Hardness is actually a quality because you are able to comb the beloved’s hair. Sneha (oilyness or softness) is actually a fault because, on account of sneha, a ghee wick ends up burnt. Obeisances to you, comb. Fie on sneha!” A young woman thus spoke under a pretext while combing Krsna’s hair. Then Krsna embraced her.**

*atra vipakṣa-ramaṇīṁ prati kāṭhinyādi-doṣa-prasañjanena prāgalbhyātiśaya-prakaṭanena vāsūyā. ātmānaṁ prati snehamayatva-guṇāropeṇa svādhika-santāpa-prakaṭanena dainyam. kāṭhinya-snehayor guṇa-doṣatvāropeṇātyanta-tiraskṛtavācya-dhvanitvam. kaṅkatikāṁ prati vipakṣa-ramaṇītvāropeṇa samāsoktiḥ. “tubhyaṁ namo ’tisnigdhāṁ dhik” iti hāsa-nirvedayoḥ śābalyam. evaṁ bhūyasām api vilakṣaṇenottamottamam api kāvyaṁ “vyāja-vāg-vinyāsā” ity ekasyaiva padasya vācyasya poṣakatvād uttamottamatvaṁ vihāya kevala-guṇībhūta-vyaṅgyatvenottamatvaṁ jātam, kintu “dhig iti snehām itīṣat-smitaṁ jalpantī cikura-prasādhana-vidhau” ity-ādi cet tadāsyottamottamatvam eva.*

**Перевод:**

**Here jealousy toward a rival heroine is indicated by the attribution of faults such as hardness and by the speaker’s manifesting much boldness (by combing His hair at the same time). She exhibits meekness toward herself by revealing her affliction, by means of attributing softness to herself. The attribution of a quality to hardness and of a fault to softness are atyanta-tiraskrta-vacya dhvanis (implied sense where the literal meaning is totally obliterated).**

**By superimposing a rival girl on the comb, there is the samasokti ornament (concise statement).**

**In addition, there is a bhava-sabalya-dhvani (conflicting mix) (5.263) of sneer (hasa) and self-disparagement (nirveda): “Obeisances to you” and “Fie on sneha”.**

**Even though the poetry could be classed as uttamottama (superexcellent) on account of the distinctiveness of many dhvanis that way, still, simply because this one word, vyaja-vag- vinyasa (she spoke under a pretext), reiterates what is stated (Obeisances to you, comb), the verse is only classed as uttama (excellent) due to this one instance of gunl-bhuta-vyangya (second-rate poetry).**

**However, if the words dhig iti sneham iti vyaja-vag-vinyasa (“Fie on sneha!” A heroine thus spoke under a pretext) were replaced with: dhig iti sneham itisat-smitam jalpanti (while whispering this with a slight smile: “Fie on sneha”), then the verse would be uttamottama-kavya (superexcellent poetry).**

**Комментарий:**

The real problem with the verse is that the term vyaja-vag-vinyasa (she spoke under a pretext) gives away the occurrence of the implied meaning:She is really talking about a rival girl.

The implied sense is based on Denotation, not Indication, because the meanings “Hardness is a quality” and “Sneha is a fault” literally make sense.

Visvanatha Kaviraja classes the fault in a separate category, without naming it: yatra ca sabdantaradina gopana-krta-carutvasya viparyasah, “Second-rate poetry also occurs when the literary beauty constructed by a concealment is marred by another word” (Sahitya-darpana 4.14) (Bhakti-rasamrta-sesa 3.63).

Kavi Karnapura’s previous verse too falls in this category: The words “Her cheeks, which had goose bumps, made her words false” give away the significance (implied sense) of the horripilation: Her words are false.

In Mammata’s and Visvanatha Kaviraja’s methodologies, the category of second-rate poetry named vacya-siddhy-anga is so called because an implied sense justifies a literal meaning in the sentence. This often occurs in a one-word metaphor which is part of a paramparita-rupaka (serial metaphors). For instance: tvan- manase kanaka-pankajinitayasau, “She is a golden lotus on the Manasa Lake of Your mind” (8.80). Here the one word manasa (mind; Manasa Lake) makes an implied metaphor: “His mind is a Manasa Lake.” This metaphor justifies the literal meaning “She is a lotus”. In Kavi Kamapura’s methodology, this can also be classed in the category of tulya-pradhanya (4.11). Kavi Kamapura’s tulya- pradhanya differs from Mammata’s, and so does his sandigdha- pradhanya (4.10). Visvanatha Kaviraja follows Mammata. Visvanatha’s example of vacya-siddhy-anga is a paramparita- rupaka.

### 4.9

*kaṣṭa-gamyam asphuṭatayā kleśa-gamyam ity arthaḥ. yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**(4)  The category called kasta-gamya means an implied sense is understood with difficulty because it is not obvious. For instance:**

*tvad-abhiramitā dvitīyā*  
*jagaty abhūd advitīyaiva*  
*anumatir apy ananumatis*  
*tithir atithir me niśāpy aniśā*

**Пословный перевод:**

tvat—by you; abhiramita—being made happy; dvitiya—the other woman (the rival); jagati—in the world; abhut—has become; advitiya—unrivalled; eva—only; anumatih—full moon; api—also; ananumatih—without a permission; tithih—the time; atithih—a guest; me—for me; nisa—night; api—even; anisa—continuous (forever long).

**Перевод:**

**Delighted by You, that other girl (dvitiya) has become unrivalled (advitiya). The time of the full moon (anumatih tithih) became a guest without permission (ananumatih atithih). For me, the night (nisa) became perpetual (anisa).**

*atra virodhābhāsena tava prakṛti-vaikṛtya-kāriṇī kāpi śaktir astīti. dvitīyā sapatnīty arthaḥ. ato me mamānumatiḥ kalona-candrā pūrṇimā-tithir anumati-hīnā satī atithir jātety arthaḥ. niśāpi me aniśā śāśvatī aprabhātevāsīd ity arthaḥ. paryāya-prāptāpi me pūrṇimā tithis tvayānanumatiḥ kṛtā, anādṛteti mama jīvanam eva vyartham iti sphuṭam. pratipadam aham apratipadam upāgatā tvat-prabhāveneti ced dhvanir eva. prati padaṁ prati vyavasāyam, apratipadam apratipattim aham upāgatety arthaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the suggestion, hinted at by a semblance of a contradiction (an implied virodha ornament), is: “You, Krsna, have some special power that changes the nature of things.” Anumati signifies the full moon (purnima-tithi), which is less by a kala. Being inadmissible (ananumati), it became a guest (atithi). “In my case, even the night (nisa) became perpetual (anisa), as if it didn’t have any morning.”**

**The full moon is obtained as a synonym: anumati. She says: “You made my time of the full moon (anumati = purnima tithi) a time that is not admissible (ananumati).” She disregarded that time, thus it is obvious that she thinks “My life is useless.”**

**If the second half of the verse were replaced by: prati padam aham apratipadam upagata tvat-prabhavena, “By Your influence, I become confused about a rendezvous that was made for sure,” then the dhvani would be first-class.**

**Комментарий:**

Krsna had set up the night of the full moon as the time of a rendezvous with her, but she did not go because she found out that He cheated on another girl. She regrets not having met Him— this is an obvious implied sense, according to Kavi Karnapura— but on the other hand she addresses Him by implying mockery.

The implied mockery is less difficult to catch in the new version especially because the purport of “inadmissible guest” (ananumatih atithih) in the first version is not clear.

This variety of second-rate implied sense, kasta-gamya, is the same as the literary fault called kasta (10.108) except that kasta-gamya occurs in an implied meaning.

### 4.10

*sandigdha-prādhānyaṁ yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**(5)  An example of sandigdha-pradhanya**  
**(a doubt about which implied meaning is predominant):**

*he bhadra bhādrapada-māsa-caturthikendo*  
*tubhyaṁ namo ’stu na kadāpi mayāsi dṛṣṭaḥ*  
*śyāmena tena katamena navena yūnā*  
*sākaṁ tathāpi mama kiṁ prathitaḥ pravādaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

he—O; bhadra—auspicious one; bhadrapada—of Bhadra (August-September); masa—in the month; caturthika—on the fourth \[day\]; indo—O moon; tubhyam—to you; namah—obeisances; astu—may there be; na kada api—never; maya—by me; asi drstah—you have been seen; syamena—the dark blue one; tena—with Him; katamena—exquisite; navena—fresh; yuna—youth; sakam—with; tatha api—still; mama—of me; kim—why; prathitah—widespread; pravadah—rumor.

**Перевод:**

**O inauspicious moon of the fourth day of Bhadra, obeisances to you. I have never seen you! Why then are there widespread rumours about my being with Him, the dark blue exquisite fresh youth?**

*atra tava darśanena pravādo bhavatīty anaikāntikam, api tu tathāvidhādṛṣṭa-dvāraiveti. kiṁ vā nāyaṁ pravādaḥ, satyaiveyaṁ kiṁvadantī, yato bhavad-darśanam antareṇāpi janaiś ced udghuṣyata iti sandigdhaṁ prādhānyaṁ yasya idaṁ guṇī-bhūta-vyaṅgyam apy āsvādasya camatkāritayā dhvani-dharmaṁ bhajata iti na kṛtāsya parivṛttiḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**In this verse, there is a doubt about what is predominant. Is this predominant: “A slanderous rumor occurs by seeing you. But this is not universally true, since rumors occur even by not seeing you,” or is that predominant: “What people are gossiping about is not slander: It is true because even though I didn’t see you, people are talking”?**

**This poetry is guni-bhuta-vyangya (second-rate). Although what the main thing is here is doubted that way, the poetry partakes of the quality of dhvani (first-rate poetry) insofar as the relishment generates astonishment. Therefore no replacement clause is made here.**

**Комментарий:**

The moon on the fourth day of the bright half of the month of Bhadra (August-September) is called Ganesa caturthi, a day considered to be his birthday. Once, Soma, the moon god, feeling very proud of his beauty, ridiculed Ganesa in the assembly of gods. Ganesa uttered the curse that whoever would see him on that day (Ganesa caturthi) would become an object of criticism. Moreover, there is a popular belief that on Ganesa caturthi, Krsna saw the moon reflected in His cup. That is why He became an object of slander; Krsna was accused of stealing the Syamantaka jewel.

### 4.11

*tulya-prādhānyaṁ yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**(6)  An example of tulya-pradhanya (the literal meaning and the implied meaning are equally predominant):**

*smara-samara-samāptau vakratāṁ bhrūr ahārṣīd*  
*ajaniṣata mṛgākṣyā vīta-lakṣyāḥ kaṭākṣāḥ*  
*dhanur iva kusumeṣor jyā-vimuktaṁ tadāsīd*  
*viviśur iva niṣaṅge mukta-śeṣāḥ pṛṣatkāḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

smara—of Cupid; samara—of the battle; samaptau—at the end; vakratam—crookedness; bhruh—eyebrows; aharsit—took away (gave up); ajanisata—became; mrga-aksyah—of the doe-eyed girl; vita—has vanished; laksyah—whose target; kata-aksah—sidelong glances; dhanuh—a bow; iva—like; kusuma-isoh—of Cupid (“he has flower arrows”); jya—from the bowstring; vimuktam—released; tada—then; asit—became; vivisuh—entered; iva—as if; nisange— in the quiver; mukta-sesah—remaining; prsatkah—arrows.

**Перевод:**

**At the end of the battle of love, the doe-eyed girl’s eyebrows gave up their crookedness, like Cupid’s bow returns to normal when its bowstring is released, and her sidelong glances became glances without a target, like remaining arrows enter back into the quiver.**

*atrotprekṣālaṅkāreṇopamālaṅkāro dhvanitaḥ. tau svaprādhānyena sthitāv iti tulya-prādhānyam.*

**Перевод:**

**In this verse, the upama ornament (simile) is implied by the utpreksa ornament (fanciful assumption). Both ornaments are equally important. This is tulya-pradhanya.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: Once the ladylove lets go of her mana, she and Krsna can enjoy intimate pastimes, but even then a trace of mana subsists. However, at the end of the battle of love, mana disappears (Subodhini).

The utpreksa occurs twice, signified by the two words iva (like), and so does the implied upama. Only two utpreksas are expressed. Generally, the word iva denotes a simile, but when the comparison is very fanciful it is called an utpreksa. The two utpreksas form the entire verse. The two implied similes are: “Her eyebrows are like Cupid’s bow” and “Her glances are like Cupid’s arrows.”

### 4.12

*kāku-gamyaṁ kākv-ākṣiptam, tad yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**(7)  Kaku-gamya (understood by kaku) means kaku-aksipta (implied by a modulation of the voice). For example:**

*kati na patitaṁ pādopānte na cāṭu katīritaṁ*  
*kati na śapathaḥ śīrṣṇo dattaḥ kṛtā kati na stutiḥ*  
*tad api na gataṁ vāme vāmyaṁ labhasva kṛtārthatāṁ*  
*bhavatu tava tu preyān māno na mānini mādhavaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

kati—how much; na—was not done; patitam—falling; pada— of the feet; upante—near the edge; na—was not; catu—flattery; kati—how much; iritam—spoken; kati—how many; na—were not; sapathah—promises; slrsnah—to the head; dattah—given; krta— done; kati—how much; na—was not; stutih—praise; tat api—still; na gatam—did not attain; vame—O crooked girl; vamyam— contrariness; labhasva—may you attain; krta-arthatam—success; bhavatu—let it be; tava—your; tu—but; preyan—dear; manah— pique; na—not; manini—O proud girl; madhavah—Madhava.

**Перевод:**

**No one fell at your feet (?). No flattery was said to you (?). No promise was sworn on the head (?). No one uttered any praise to you (?). Still, O crooked girl, you do not give up your huffiness. So be it, proud girl, may you be successful: Let mana, not Madhava, be your beloved.**

*atra na patitam, api tu patitam eveti nañ-kākuḥ, tayākṣiptam. nedam acamatkāri, tathāpi “kati nipatitaṁ pādopānte kṛtaṁ kati cāṭu vā, kati kati mayā śīrṣṇaḥ śaptaṁ kati stutir īhitā”—iti paṭhanīyam.*

**Перевод:**

**There is a modulation of the voice on the negative particle. For example: na patitam (no one fell at your feet) has the sense of patitam eva (indeed someone fell at your feet).**

**It is not that this does not create astonishment. Still, a wording without kaku is as follows:**

*kati nipatitaṁ pādopānte kṛtaṁ kati cāṭu vā*  
*kati kati mayā śīrṣṇaḥ śaptaṁ kati stutir īhitā*

**Перевод:**

**“So much falling at your feet and so much flattery was done, so many oaths I swore on my head and so much praise was said.”**

**Комментарий:**

The category of kaku-gamya, called kaku for short, was also exemplified in text 2.47. Usually it involves a modulation of the voice on the negative particle, na\[n\], so that a statement is turned into a rhetorical question.

*amanojñam asundaram, tad yathā,*

**(8)  This illustrates amanojna, which means asundara (not beautiful) (not as beautiful as the literal meaning of the text):**

*jappantī a guruhiṁ vācātthambho bahūa samvṛtto*

*śruta-pūrvam api nikāmaṁ harer muralī-ravaṁ śrutvā*  
*jalpantyā gurubhiḥ samaṁ vāk-stambho vadhvā saṁvṛttaḥ*  
*(Sanskrit rendering)*

**Пословный перевод:**

sruta-purvam—heard previously; api—even though; nikamam— freely (as much as one likes); hareh—of Hari; murali-ravam— the sound of the flute; srutva—having heard; jalpantya—who was talking; gurubhih samam—with her elders; vak—of speech; stambhah—faltering; vadhva—by the young bride; samvrttah— happened.

**Перевод:**

**While chatting with her elders, the girl choked up while hearing the sound of Hari’s flute though she had listened to it many times before.**

*atra nikāmaṁ śruta-pūrvam apīti tat-kālīna-muralī-ravasya saṅketa-kāritvam. tena gurubhiḥ samaṁ kathayantyā vadhvā vākstambho jātaḥ. tatra gantum aśaktatvān moho jāta ity arthaḥ. ato vāk-stambho jāta iti vācyārtha eva camatkārī, vyaṅgyārthas tu sann api tathā na camatkarotīty asundaram, evam anyo’pi.*

**Перевод:**

### 4.14

*prāg-ukta-dhvani-saṁkhyā ebhir guṇitās tathāṣṭābhiḥ*  
*kha-yugartu-vahni-vasavo dhvani-sāṅkaryāt punar dvedhā (2)*

**Пословный перевод:**

prak—previously; ukta—mentioned; dhvani—of suggestions; samkhyah—the numbers; ebhih —by these \[eight\]; gunitah— multiplied; tatha—in the same way; astabhih—by the eight; kha— zero (void); yuga—four (Ages); rtu—six (seasons); vahni—three (fires); vasavah—eight (vasus); dhvani-sankaryat—on account of the mixing of dhvanis; punah—moreover; dvedha—twofold.

**Перевод:**

**When multiplied by eight, the aforesaid number of dhvanis (10,455) (3.63) makes a total of 83,640 possible combinations. Further, on account of the combinations of dhvanis, the total becomes 167280 varieties of dhvanis.**

*aṣṭā prakārā guṇī-bhūta-vyaṅgya-dhvanayaḥ. śareṣu yuga-khendu bhedair dhvanibhiḥ pratyekam abhisambadhyante. tena khayugartu-vahni-vasavo bhavanti. ete punar dhvani-sāṅkaryeṇa dvedhā bhavanti.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the number eight denotes the eight varieties of second- rate poetry. Each is multiplied by 10,455; the result is 83,640 possible varieties. On account of the combinations of dhvanis, this total is multiplied by two (in consideration of sankara and samsrsti) for a grand total of 167,280 varieties of dhvanis.**

### 4.15

*tena,*  
*vyoma-diṅ-nāga-pakṣārka-hayartu-rajanī-karāḥ*  
*guṇī-bhūta-vyaṅgya-bhedā vijñeyāḥ sūkṣma-buddhibhiḥ (3)*

**Пословный перевод:**

vyoma—zero (the void); dik-naga—eight (elephants in the directions); paksa—two (wings); arka-haya—seven (horses of the sun-god) rtu—six (seasons); rajani-karah— \[the dhvanis are one whose number is\] one (the moon, “night-maker”); guni-bhuta— that have become secondary; vyangya—of suggestions; bhedah— varieties; vijneyah—are to be understood; suksma-buddhibhih—by those whose intelligence is subtle.
