*ity alaṅkāra-kaustubhe guṇī-bhūta-vyaṅgya-nirṇayo nāma caturthaḥ kiraṇaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Here ends the fourth ray in Alankara-kaustubha, entitled: “an analysis of second-rate poetry.”**

## Fifth Ray - Rasa

### 5.1

*atha rasa-bhāva-tad-bheda-nirūpaṇaḥ. atha “ātmā kila rasaḥ” ity uktasya kāvya-puruṣasyātmano rasasyābhivyakti-lakṣaṇaṁ bharata-muni-sūtraṁ pramāṇayann āha, “vibhāvānubhāvavyabhicāri-saṁyogād rasa-niṣpattiḥ” iti. vibhāvayaty utpādayatīti vibhāvaḥ kāraṇam, anu paścād bhāvo bhavanaṁ yasya so ’nubhāvaḥ kāryam, viśeṣeṇābhimukhyena carituṁ śīlaṁ yasyeti vyabhicārī sahakārī. eteṣāṁ saṁyogāt sambandhād rasasya niṣpattir abhivyaktiḥ. kāraṇa-kārya-sahakāritvena loke yā rasaniṣpatti-sāmagrī, saiva kāvye nāṭye ca vibhāvādi-vyapadeśā bhavatīti sampradāyaḥ. kāraṇam atra nimittam.*

**Перевод:**

**Here is the dissertation on rasa, bhava, and their varieties. In text 1.7, it was said that rasa is the soul of the Kavya-purusa. At first, to prove that the definition of the manifestation of rasa is Bharata Muni’s sutra, he quotes it: vibhavanubhava- vyabhicari-samyogad rasa-nispattih, “The manifestation of rasa comes about due to the combination of vibhava, anubhava, and vyabhican” (Natya-sastra 6.32).**

**A vibhava is so called because it causes (vibhavayati = utpadayati). Thus a vibhava is the cause. An anubhava is so called because its existence occurs afterward (anu = pascat). Thus an anubhava is an effect. A vyabhican is so named because its nature is to favorably (abhi = abhimukhyena) move (carin = caritum silam yasya) in special ways (vi = visesena). Thus a vyabhican is an accompanying element. Due to the combination of these three, the manifestation (nispatti = abhivyakti) of rasa occurs.**

**The ingredients for the manifestation of rasa, which in the world are known as causes, effects, and accompanying elements, are the same in poetry and in dramaturgy but are called vibhava, anubhava, and vyabhicari. This is the teaching of the tradition of poets. In this context, vibhava is the cause in terms of being an instrumental cause.**

**Комментарий:**

In poetics, the term rasa has two main meanings: aesthetic delight, and rapture (10.139). The first meaning was expounded above. In other words, when the sthayi-bhava in the text is implied by appropriate vibhavas and by an anubhava and a vyabhicari, the sthayl is called rasa because it has become relishable. The second meaning of rasa relates to a deeper experience of delight and is expounded ahead (5.11). Therefore in the next karika, Kavi Karnapura, explaining the first meaning, says the sthayl acts like rasa (rasayate).

### 5.2

*vibhāvādīnāṁ svarūpam āha,*

**Перевод:**

**He describes the natures of vibhava and so on:**

*vibhāvo dvi-vidhaḥ syād ālambanoddīpanākhyayā*  
*ālambanaṁ tad eva syāt sthāyi-nāmāśrayo hi yat*  
*yat tān evoddīpayati tad uddīpanam iṣyate (1)*  
*ebhir eva vyañjakais tu tribhir udrekam āgataiḥ*  
*āsvādāṅkura-kando ’sau bhāvaḥ sthāyī rasāyate (2)*

**Пословный перевод:**

vibhavah—vibhava; dvi-vidhah—has two kinds; syat—is; alambana-uddlpana-akhyaya—by the name alambana and uddlpana; alambanam—alambana (support, resting place); tat—that; eva—only; syat—is; sthayi-nama—of the things called sthayin; asrayah—is the foundation; hi—only; yat—which; yat—which; tan eva—those same ones (the sthayins); uddlpayati—inflames (or excites); tat—that; uddipanam—uddipana; isyate— is desired (is called); ebhih eva—because of these same ones; vyanjakaih—suggestive elements; tu—only; tribhih—three; udrekam—an upsurge; agataih—which have reached; asvada— of relishment; ankura—of the sprout; kandah—the root cause; asau—that; bhavah—the mood; sthayi—foundational (“it stays”); rasayate—acts like rasa.

**Перевод:**

**There are two kinds of vibhavas: alambana (asraya, subject, and visaya, object) and uddipana (excitant). An alambana is that taking support of which the sthayi takes place. An uddipana is so called because it inflames the sthayi.**

**Because the aforesaid three suggestive elements have reached a perceptible manifestation, the sthayi-bhava, the cause of the beginning of the relish, acts like rasa (turns into rasa).**

*etena rasasya kāraṇa-kāryādīni naitāni, api tu anubhāvasya kāryasya kāraṇaṁ vibhāvaḥ, vyabhicārī yaḥ, so ’py anubhāvasya sahakārī. traya eva samuditāḥ santaḥ sthāyinaṁ rasī-bhāvam āpādayanti. sthāyī samavāyi-kāraṇam, ālambanoddīpanavibhāvau nimitta-kāraṇam. sthāyino vikāra-viśeṣo ’samavāyikāraṇaṁ rasābhivyakter eva bhavati, na tu rasasya.*

**Перевод:**

**These three are neither the cause nor the effect of rasa. Rather, vibhava is the cause of anubhava, the effect, and vyabhicari- bhava is the accompanying element of anubhava. When those three have simultaneously risen, they cause the sthayi-bhava to become rasa.**

**The sthayi is the inherent cause (ingredient cause), and the two vibhavas, namely the alambanas and the uddipanas, are instrumental causes. A particular modification because of the sthayi (namely an anubhava or a vyabhicari) is a noninherent cause. They are the causes of the manifestation of Rasa, but not of Rasa.**

**Комментарий:**

Here the two meanings of the term rasa are taken. Since Rasa (rapture), a form of bliss, is inherent in the soul, there is no question of causing its existence.

In Nyaya, there are three types of causes (inherent, non-inherent, instrumental): karanam tri-vidham, samavayy-asamavayi-nimitta- bhedat (Tarka-sangraha 3.26). The analogy is this: The sthayl is the yarns; the vibhavas are the spinning wheel (or the shuttle); and the anubhava and the vyabhicari are the combining of the yarns to make the garment. An asamavayi-karana (noninherent cause) is either an action or a quality. An example of the above in the scope of an action is: The combining of the yarns makes the garment. An example in the scope of a quality is: The color of the yarns makes the color of the garment.

The analogy of direct causation functions for the rasa which is aesthetic delight. At first, however, the sthayi-bhava is implied by the vibhavas and so on. Thus Bhatta Lollata, cited by Mammata, says that the sthayi brought to light by vibhavas; rendered perceivable by means of an anubhava; and enhanced by a vyabhicari-bhava is rasa (aesthetic delight). Abhinavagupta remarks that Lollata’s viewpoint is the standard interpretation of Bharata Muni’s rasa- sutra and was present in seed form in the works of Dandin and of other ancients.

In this matter, there is a well-known analogy: The sthayl with the vibhavas and so on is called rasa like yogurt mixed with tasty ingredients such as sugar, pepper and camphor is called rasala (yogurt drink) (lassi in Hindi).

Visvanatha Kaviraja remarks that relishing the sthayl requires having a predisposition to feel the sthayi: na jayate tad-asvado vina raty-adi-vasanam (Sahitya-darpana 3.8). He says only a connoisseur can experience that the sthayi enhanced by those three becomes rasa (aesthetic delight).

Those three causes are not causes of rapture, but of the manifestation of it: They facilitate the manifestation of the soul’s bliss in the mind. The rapture, Rasa, is a mix of bliss and astonishment, and has the nature of the sthayi like a ray of light becomes a particular color. Baladeva Vidyabhusana points out that the soul is Rasa, and adds that in the context of bhakti, transcendental potency (cit-sakti) is involved in the bliss. Similarly, Visvanatha Cakravarti says this potency, acintya-sakti, is a factor in the transformation of a sthayi-bhava of bhakti into bhakti-rasa.

The sattvika-bhavas are classed in the category of anubhava (bodily reaction) (5.259). The anubhavas are expounded from text 5.256 and the vyabhicaris from text 5.261.

### 5.3

*atha ko ’sau bhāvaḥ sthāyī bhavatīti taṁ nirūpayati,*

**Перевод:**

**What is a sthayi-bhava? He describes it:**

*āsvādāṅkura-kando ’sti dharmaḥ kaścana cetasaḥ*  
*rajas-tamobhyāṁ hīnasya śuddha-sattvatayā sataḥ (3)*  
*sa sthāyī kathyate vijñair vibhāvasya pṛthaktayā*  
*pṛthag-vidhatvaṁ yāty eṣa sāmājikatayā satām (4)*

**Пословный перевод:**

asvada—of relish; ankura—of the sprout (beginning); kandah—the root in the form of cause; asti—is; dharmah—attribute; kascana— some (special); cetasah—of the mind; rajah-tamobhyam—rajo- guna (the mode of action / passion) and tamo-guna (the mode of darkness); hinasya—which is devoid of; suddha-sattvataya—in terms of being transcendental existence; satah—which is existing; sah—that; sthayi—the thing that stays; kathyate—is told; vijnaih— by those who have realized the matter; vibhavasya—of vibhava; prthaktaya—due to the separateness; prthak-vidhatvam—the state of variegatedness; yati—reaches; esah—this (sthayi); samajikataya— in terms of being spectators; satam—of good persons.

**Перевод:**

**The learned say a sthayi-bhava, the cause of the beginning of the relish felt by good persons who are spectators or readers, is some uncommon attribute of a mind which has pure sattva and is devoid of rajo-guna and tamo-guna. There are many kinds of sthayi-bhavas because there are many kinds of vibhavas.**

*sāmājikatayā satāṁ samājikānām eka eva kaścid āsvādāṅkurakando manasaḥ ko ’pi dharma-viśeṣaḥ sthāyī. sa tu vibhāvasyoktaprakāra-dvi-vidhasya bhedair eva bhidyate. anukāryāṇāṁ tu svatantrā eva sthāyino nānā-vidhāḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**There are two broad kinds of vibhavas. And because of their multiple subvarieties (those of alambana-vibhava), there are various categories of sthayi-bhavas.**

**In the case of the characters, however, they have various sthayi- bhavas, but their sthayidoes not depend on the sthayiof another.**

**Комментарий:**

Other poetical theorists use the term sattva instead of suddha-sattva (pure sattva). In his definition of rasa, in the context of bhakti, Rupa Gosvami uses the term sattva, which Jiva Gosvami explains as suddha-sattva. There are two kinds of sattva. In Bhagavatam, for instance, depending on the context the word sattva denotes either sattva-guna (asuddha-sattva) or suddha-sattva (transcendental existence). Jiva Gosvami established the distinction. There are another two broad kinds of rasa: material rasa and bhakti-rasa. In the material rasa which is aesthetic delight, sattva-guna is involved. In the bhakti-rasa which is aesthetic delight, sattva-guna and suddha-sattva are involved. In Rasa (rapture), sattva-guna is involved in terms of being the facilitator of the manifestation of the soul’s bliss. And in the bhakti-rasa which is rapture, suddha-sattva is involved.

But in all cases, the term sattva also includes another meaning of the word sattva: good vibrations (the vibes). For instance, the sattvika-bhavas are so called because they arise from sattva. The same applies to the twenty emotional ornaments of women (5.165): yauvane sattvajas tasam alankaras tu vimsatih (Ujjvala- nilamani 11.2). In addition, Bharata Muni wrote: vag-anga- sattvopetan kavyarthan bhavayantiti bhavah, “The bhavas are so called because they infuse \[into the spectators\] the meanings of the poetry which are endowed with speech, with bodily movements, and with sattva” (Natya-sastra 7.1).

Bhatta Nayaka, cited by Mammata, and Visvanatha Kaviraja say Rasa manifests because the awareness is imbued with bliss which arises due to an upsurge of sattva. Visvanatha Kaviraja explains: rajas-tamobhyam asprstam manah sattvam ihocyate ity ukta-prakaro bahya-meya-vimukhatapadakah kascanantaro dharmah sattvam. tasyodreko rajas-tamasau abhibhuya avirbhavah. atra ca hetus tatha-vidhalaukika-kavyartha-parisilanam.

“Sattva is some other kind of mental attribute which makes one indifferent to external things, by the dictum: “In this matter, a mind untouched by either rajo-guna or tamo-guna is called sattva (Sarasvati-kanthabharana 5.20).” “An upsurge of sattva” means sattva manifests after dominating rajas and tamas. And the reason for that is the fact of taking interest in the meanings of extraordinary poetry” (Sahitya-darpana 3.2-3).

A connoisseur is someone who has thus developed the propensity to feel sattva (good literary vibrations).

### 5.4

*yathā,*  
*śṛṅgāre ratir utsāho vīre syāc choka-vismayau*  
*karuṇādbhutayor hāso hāsye bhītir bhayānake*  
*jugupsā bībhatsa-saṁjñe kopo raudre ’ṣṭa-nāṭya-gāḥ (5)*

**Перевод:**

**The eight sthayi-bhavas in dramaturgy are: Rati (romantic pleasure) in srngara-rasa (romance, erotics), utsaha (zeal) in vira-rasa (heroism), soka (sorrow) in karuna-rasa (lamentation), vismaya (wonder) in adbhuta-rasa (astonishment), hasa (humor) in hasya-rasa (comical), bhiti (cold feet) in bhayanaka-rasa (fear), jugupsa (disgust) in bibhatsa-rasa (abhorrence), and kopa (anger) in raudra-rasa (fierceness).**

*ete ’ṣṭau sthāyino ’ṣṭāsu nāṭya-rasesv iti kecit. kecit tu “nirvedasthāyi-bhāvo ’sti śānto ’pi navamo rasaḥ” iti śanto ’pi nāṭya-rasaḥ. bhojas tu vatsalatā-premabhyām ekādaśa-rasān ācaṣṭe. vātsalye mama-kāraḥ, premaṇi citta-dravaś ca sthāyī. ekādaśaiva dṛśye śravye ’pi ca rasika-saṁsadaḥ preṣṭhāḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Some say these are the eight sthayis in the eight rasas of dramaturgy. But other authorities say santa as well is a rasa in dramaturgy: nirveda-sthayi-bhavo ’sti santo ’pi navamo rasah, “Although its sthayi-bhava is nirveda (disgust toward material life), santa (peacefulness) is the ninth rasa” (Kavya-prakasa 4.35).**

**Bhoja, however, counts eleven rasas, by adding vatsalya and prema. In that regard, mama-kara (possessiveness) is the sthayi in vatsalya-rasa (affection of a superior for a junior), and citta- drava (the melting of the heart) is the sthayi in prema-rasa (love). In dramaturgy and in poetry, these eleven are very dear to connoisseurs.**

### 5.5

*tatra ratir yathā,*

*ratiś ceto-rañjakatā sukha-bhogānukūlya-kṛt*  
*sā prīti-maitrī-sauhārda-bhāva-saṁjñāṁ ca gacchati (6)*

**Пословный перевод:**

ratih—affection; cetah—of the mind (or heart); ranjakata—the state of being a delighter; sukha—of happiness; bhoga—for the enjoyment; anukulya—a favorableness; krt—it makes; sa—that; priti-maitri-sauharda-bhava-samjnam—the names priti, maitri, sauharda, and bhava; ca—and; gacchati—attains.

**Перевод:**

**The term rati denotes a state of delighting the heart, a state conducive to the enjoyment of happiness. That state of delighting the heart has other names: priti (affection), maitri (friendship), sauharda (goodheartedness), and bhava (mind­set).**

**saiva ceto-ranjakata. The word sa refers to ceto-ranjakata.**

**Комментарий:**

The rati in the tradition of poetics is different from the rati in Rupa Gosvami’s system in the sense that in the former, rati is only one type of sthayi-bhava, whereas in the latter it is a synonym of sthayi- bhava. Kavi Karnapura follows the tradition and incorporates therein Rupa Gosvami’s concepts.

Kavi Karnapura mostly follows Mammata, who subdivided rati in two: Affection between lovers and affection of other kinds. In Mammata’s methodology, only the first kind of rati can reach the level of rasa (srngara-rasa). Rupa Gosvami’s sakhya-rati corresponds to Kavi Karnapura’s maitri.

### 5.6

*yā samprayoga-viṣayā sā ratiḥ parikīrtitā*  
*samprayogaḥ strī-puruṣa-vyavahāraḥ satāṁ mataḥ*  
*asamprayoga-viṣayā saiva prītir nigadyate (7)*  
*sakhi-patnyāṁ pati-sakhe draupadī-kṛṣṇayor yathā*  
*dvayoḥ sakhīṣu sakhiṣu saiva maitrī nigadyate (8)*

*dvayoḥ strī-puruṣayoḥ, strīṇāṁ sakhīṣu, puruṣāṇāṁ sakhiṣu.*

**Перевод:**

**Of those, affection in the scope of sex is called rati (romantic pleasure). Civilized persons consider that sex is an interaction between a woman and a man.**

**The rati which is not in the scope of sex is calledpriti (affection). It occurs between a married woman and a male friend, or between a married man and a female friend. An example is the affection between Krsna and Draupadi.**

**When a man and a woman are friends, or when women are friends, or when men are friends, the rati is called maitri (friendship).**

### 5.7

*mano-vṛtti-mayī prītir maitrī sparśādikocitā*  
*nirvikārā sadaikābhā sā sauhārdam itīṣyate (9)*

**Пословный перевод:**

manah-vrtti—a frame of mind; mayi—consists of; pritih— affection; maitri—friendship; sparsa-adika—for touching and so on; ucita—suitable; nirvikara—in which there is no change; sada— always; eka-abha—whose appearance is one; sa—that (pleasure); sauhardam—goodheartedness; iti—thus; isyate—is desired (is called).

**Перевод:**

**Priti is a particular frame of mind, whereas touching, seeing up close, and so on, are suitable only in maitri. Sauharda (goodheartedness) is uniform and involves no change of behavior even on those occasions.**

*sadaikābhā sadaika-rūpā sā ceto-rañjakatā sauhārdam, sā ca strīsakhīnāṁ pati-sakhīnāṁ ca paraspara-viṣayā.*

**Перевод:**

**The state the pleasing the heart is called sauharda when that state is uniform. Goodheartedness occurs between women and between men.**

### 5.8

*saiva devādi-viṣayā ratir bhāvaś ca kathyate (10)*

**Перевод:**

**The rati in the scope of affection for the Lord, etc., is called bhava.**

*saiva ceto-rañjakatā, ādi-śabdād guru-prabhṛti-vṛttiś ca.*

**Перевод:**

**The state of pleasing the heart which is devadi-visaya rati is called bhava (mind-set). The word adi (etc.) stands for affection for a guru, and so on.**

**Комментарий:**

In text 5.25, Kavi Karnapura says bhakti-rasa is the twelfth rasa and this type of rati (deva-visaya rati) is one of its sthayi-bhavas. He thus modified Mammata's methodology. Kavi Karnapura's deva-visaya rati corresponds to Rupa Gosvami's santa-rati and dasya-rati.

### 5.9

*yā samprayoga-viṣayā sāpy avasthā-viśeṣataḥ*  
*pākāt pākāntaraṁ prāpya carame paryavasyati (11)*

**Пословный перевод:**

ya—which \[rati\]; samprayoga—sex; visaya—whose scope; sa—that one; api—too; avastha-visesatah—because of specific proclivities; pakat—after a level of development; paka-antaram— another level of development; prapya—after achieving; carame— in the last one; paryavasyati—it culminates.

**Перевод:**

**The rati in the scope of srngara has subdivisions too because of specific proclivities. It develops from one state to the next until the last stage.**

*carame pāke, yataḥ paraṁ pākāntaraṁ nāsti, yathekṣu-rasaḥ sitopalā-pākāvadhiḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Carame signifies “the last stage”, meaning the stage after which there is no other one. For example, the last stage of sugarcane juice is refined sugar.**

### 5.10

*yad uktam,*

*yathekṣūṇāṁ raso hy āmaḥ pākāt pākāntarair guḍaḥ*  
*guḍo ’pi pākataḥ pāke carame syāt sitopalā*  
*tathā ratir bhāva-pūrva-rāga-rāgākhya-pākataḥ*  
*anurāgaḥ sa praṇaya-premabhyāṁ pākam āgataḥ*  
*sneha-pākam atho yāti mahā-rāgo ’yam ucyate*

**Перевод:**

**Raw sugarcane juice is cooked into molasses through various stages. Molasses is cooked further and reaches the final state: refined sugar. In the same way, rati matures through the stages of bhava, purva-raga, raga, anuraga, pranaya, prema, and sneha, and reaches the highest stage: maha-raga.**

*“nirvikārātmake citte bhāvaḥ prathama-vikriyā” ity ukte rateḥ prathamaḥ pāko bhāvaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**The first development of rati is called bhava. The referential statement is: “The first change in a mind that was changelessness by nature is called bhava.” (5.166) (Sahitya-darpana 3.93) (Ujjvala-nilamani 11.6)**

**Комментарий:**

This bhava is the first alahkara among the alahkaras of srhgara (5.165) (Ujjvala-nilamani 11.6). Visvanatha Cakravarti explains that the mind had felt no change in the sense that before youth, no feeling of amorous love entered the mind: citte kidrse? nirvikaratmake pauganda-vayastvena kandarpa-pravesabhavat tad-vikara-hina ity arthah (Ananda-candrika 11.6).

Rupa Gosvami says this rati, the state before bhava, is also called sattva because there is no transformation: cittasyavikrtih sattvam (Ujjvala-nilamani 11.7).

Rupa Gosvami’s sequence is: rati, prema, sneha, mana, pranaya, raga, anuraga, and mahabhava. But he also says that sometimes the sequence is: raga, anuraga, sneha, mana, and pranaya. Kavi Karnapura describes mana in the context of vipralambha (5.36). Purva-raga as well is a variety of vipralambha.

### 5.11

*ko ’sau rasaḥ, yasyābhivyaktaye vibhāvādīnāṁ kāraṇatvam ity apekṣāyāṁ tat-svarūpam āha,*

**Перевод:**

**“What is the rasa for the sake of the manifestation of which the vibhavas and so on are causes?” With this in mind, he describes the nature of Rasa:**

*bahir-antaḥkaraṇayor vyāpārāntara-rodhakam*  
*sva-kāraṇādi-saṁśleṣi camatkāri sukhaṁ rasaḥ (12)*

**Пословный перевод:**

bahih-antah-karanayoh—of outer senses (bahih-karana) and of the mind (i.e. mind, intellect, ego, subconscious); vyapara-antara— another function; rodhakam—it blocks; sva-karana-adi—of its causes and so on; samslesi—it has the combination; camatkari—it astonishes; sukham—joy; rasah—rapture.

**Перевод:**

**The joy which numbs both the sensory functions and the intellect, which is accompanied with the causes and which produces astonishment is Rasa.**

*ayaṁ tūttama-prakṛtīnām anukāryāṇāṁ svataḥ siddha eva, kāvyādau tu sāmājikānām eva, teṣāṁ sarva-rasābhivyakti-śālī eka eva pūrvoktaḥ kaścanāsvāda-kandaś ceto-dharma-viśeṣaḥ sthāyī. tatra yuktir darśayiṣyate.*

**Перевод:**

**This Rasa is natural for characters of the highest nature. The connoisseurs experience it in poetry and in drama. Their sthayi abounds in the manifestation of all the rasas and, as mentioned before, is a special attribute of the mind, an attribute which is the root cause of the relish. The logical reasoning in that regard is going to be illustrated.**

### 5.12

*rasasyānanda-dharmatvād aikadhyaṁ bhāva eva hi*  
*upādhi-bhedān nānātvaṁ raty-ādaya upādhayaḥ (13)*

**Пословный перевод:**

rasasya—of Rasa; ananda-dharmatvat—because of being an attribute of bliss; aikadhyam—the onefoldness; bhavah—sthayi- bhava; eva—the same one; hi—only; upadhi—of limiting attributes; bhedat—because of the difference; nanatvam—\[attains\] manifoldness; rati-adayah—rati and the others; upadhayah—are limiting attributes.

**Перевод:**

**Rasa is one, since it is an attribute of bliss. However, there are various types of bhavas because of the difference of limiting characteristics. Rati and the other sthayi-bhavas are the limiting characteristics.**

*raty-ādayaḥ sthāyinaḥ. yathā nānā-vidha-śarāva-salila-tāratamye ’pi taraṇi-bimba-pratibimba eka-rūpa eva, tathopādhi-gata eva bhedaḥ, nānanda-gato rasasya. ukta-prakāreṣu sthāyiṣu kaścid ubhaya-niṣṭhaḥ, kaścid eka-niṣṭhaḥ, kaścid eka-niṣṭha ubhayaniṣṭhaś ca. tatra raty-ādir ubhaya-niṣṭhaḥ, jugupsādir ekaniṣṭhaḥ, krodhādir eka-niṣṭho dvi-niṣṭhaś ca. ity anukāryāṇām eva sāmājikānām eka evety uktatvāt.*

**Перевод:**

**For example, the reflection of the sun is really one, but it appears manifold on account of the water in plates, for instance. Thus, variety relates to things that have limiting characteristics, not to the bliss related to Rasa.**

**Among the sthayis, whose varieties have been mentioned, some have a double foundation, some have a single foundation, and some can have either a single foundation or a double foundation. Rati has a double foundation (each of two persons is the visaya and the asraya). Jugupsa (disgust) has a single foundation (only one person is an asraya). Krodha (anger) has either a single foundation or a dual foundation. This applies to the characters. As for the spectators (and the readers), their relish is of only one kind, since it was said above that the connoisseurs experience rasa in poetry and in drama. (The spectators’ aesthetic delight is more or less uniform from one rasa to the next and their rapture is uniform.)**

**Комментарий:**

In real life, the various manifestations of srngara-rasa, for instance, such as purva-raga, mana, and sambhoga, are distinctly felt. But the readers’ relishment of those narrations is not so distinct. In addition, in real life the pleasure markedly increases from enjoyment to rapture: The enjoyment has various degrees, the rapture has various degrees, and the stages between the two are more pronounced than in the relishment of poetry.

The analogy in the first paragraph of the elaboration is taken from Rupa Gosvami, but the context is different: Bhakti-rati manifests in a particular form in a devoteee like the sun manifests as a certain reflection in a particular recipient: vaisistyam patra-vaisistyad ratir esopagacchati, yatharkah pratibimbatma sphatikadisu vastusu (Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu 2.5.7). In the topic under discussion, at first aesthetic delight occurs, then rapture manifests. The rapture takes the form of the sthayl involved in the aesthetic delight. In a similar way, for the most part the fifth ray treats of the rasa associated with the fifth musical note.

Still, this kind of rapture is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. The realistic goal of reading poetry and of watching a play or a movie is to achieve a state of relishment between aesthetic delight and rapture: In the intermediate state, the bliss of the soul filters into the consciousness.

### 5.13

*prākṛtāprākṛtābhāsa-bhedād eṣa tridhā mataḥ (14)*

**Перевод:**

**Rasa has three categories: prakrta (material), aprakrta (transcendental), and abhasa (semblance).**

*eṣa rasaḥ, prākṛto laukiko mālatī-mādhavādi-niṣṭhaḥ, aprākṛtaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa-rādhādi-niṣṭhaḥ. ābhāsas tv anaucityādi-pravartitaḥ. sa cābhāsas tri-vidhaḥ, prasiddha-kṛtrima-siddha-bhedāt. ādyaḥ prākprasiddhi-mātropahataḥ, na tu sampatsyamānaḥ, sa ca rasābhāso bhavann api rasa-poṣakaḥ. yathā nandana-sambandha-prasiddhau mālatyā mādhave rati-puṣṭir iti prākṛte. aprākṛte tu śiśupālasambandha-prasiddhau śrī-rukmiṇyāḥ śrī-kṛṣṇe rati-puṣṭiḥ. kṛtrimas tu nandanaṁ prati mālatī-veśa-dhāriṇo makarandasya vāmyaprakaṭanādiḥ. siddhas tv anaucitya-pravartita eva. anaucityaṁ caikasyā aneka-kānta-niṣṭhatvam. yad uktam, “yadyapy ayaṁ rasābhāsaḥ paroḍha-ramaṇī-ratiḥ, tathāpi dhvani-vaiśiṣṭyād uttamaṁ kāvyam eva tat.” tathāpi “raso bhāvas tad-ābhāso bhāva-śāntyādir akramaḥ” ity ādy-ukta-diśā “ābhāso ’pi camatkāra-daśāyāṁ dhvani-bhāg bhavet” iti dhvani-maryādayaivottama-kāvyatvam, na tv anaucitya-rītyā iti prākṛte. aprākṛte tu paroḍha-ramaṇī-ratir eva sarvottamatayā bhūyasī śrūyate, na tasyā anaucitya-pravartitattvam. alaukikatva-siddher bhūṣaṇam eva, na tu dūṣaṇam iti nyāyāt, tarkāgocaratvāc ca. tathā ca “alaukikāś ca ye bhāvā na tāṁs tarkeṇa yojayet” iti ca.vraja-vadhūnāṁ kṛṣṇaikatāna-mānasatvena sva-patiniṣṭhatvābhāvāt teṣāṁ ca māyā-kalita-tac-chāyānuśīlanena tad-aṅgasaṅgamāt, pratyuta kevalānurāga-mātropādhitayā ceto-rañjakatāyāḥ śuddhatvam eva.*

**Перевод:**

**The material rasa is based on characters such as Malati and Madhava. The transcendental rasa is based on real-life characters such as Sri Radha and Sri Krsna. A semblance of a rasa, however, is founded on inappropriateness.**

**There are three kinds of rasabhasa: prasiddha (well-known), krtrima (fake), and siddha (real). The first kind means the rasa is only hindered by a previous well-known fact; this rasabhasa is not in the process of taking place. This rasabhasa enhances the relishment. An example is in Malati-madhava (by Bhavabhuti): Given that everyone knows Malati has a connection with Nandana (the king desires that his minister’s daughter Malati marry a youth called Nandana), her love for Madhava increases, thus the relishment is enhanced. This is in the scope of the material rasa. An example in the scope of the transcendental rasa is as follows: Given that everyone knows Sri Rukmini has a connection with Sisupala (RukmT decided to give Rukmini to Sisupala) (Bhagavatam** [**10.52.25**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/52.25)**), her love for Sri Krsna increases, thus the rasa is enhanced.**

**An example of the second kind of rasabhasa is in Malati- madhava, where Makaranda dresses like Malati and exhibits a contrary mood toward Nandana.**

**The third kind of rasabhasa is founded on inappropriateness. This means one woman has many lovers. Moreover, it is said: “Although this rasabhasa is the love for a woman married to another, it constitutes first-rate poetry because of the specialty of the first-rate implied sense (srngara-rasa).” Still, it is first- rate poetry only because of the established usage of dhvani with respect to this statement: “Rasabhasa becomes dhvani if it produces astonishment,” along the lines of texts such as: “The dhvani called alaksya-krama-vyangya has these varieties: rasa- dhvani, bhava-dhvani, rasabhasa-dhvani, bhavabhasa-dhvani, bhava-santi-dhvani, and so on” (3.10). The above applies to the material rasa. In the transcendental rasa, however, it is heard from the scriptures that the love for a woman married to another is topmost. That love is not founded on inappropriateness, by the logic that this love is indeed a good thing, since the state of transcendence occurs and since that love is out of the scope of logical argumentation, for instance: “One should not analyze transcendental bhavas by using material logic.” (Mahabharata 6.6.22) (Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu 2.5.93)**

**The love of the married gopis for Krsna is pure because its sole characteristic is ardent love for Him exclusively: Those gopis did not love their husbands. The gopis’ bodies touched by those men were replicas made by Maya.**

### 5.14

*atra rasa-granthe kāvyam adhikṛtyaiva vicāraḥ. kāvyaṁ—dṛśyaṁ śravyaṁ ca. dṛśye śabdopāttā vibhāvādayo ’bhināyakāśrayāḥ, abhineyāśrayāś ca, śravye kevalaṁ śabdopāttāḥ. kuto ’trānukārya-gato rasaḥ? nāpy anukartṛ-gataḥ, teṣāṁ śikṣābhyāsaprakaṭana-mātra-kauśalenāsvādakatvābhāvāt. yadi tu vigalitavedyāntaratvam anukartṝṇām api dṛśyate, tadā teṣām api sāmājikatvam eva, anukaraṇaṁ tu saṁskāra-vaśād eva jīvanmuktānām āhāra-vihārādi-vat. tena sāmājikānam eva rasaḥ. tathā hi, naṭenānukriyamāṇānukārya-carita-darśana-śravaṇa-janitacamatkārātiśayena vigalita-vedyāntaratayā tad-eka-sphūrtisanāthena adbhutam idaṁ rāma-sītayo rati-kalā-kauśalam, adbhutam idaṁ rāma-rāvaṇayor yuddham, adbhutam idaṁ preta-raṅkādi-viceṣṭitam ity-ādinā sarveṣv eva raseṣu “rase sāraś camatkāro yaṁ vinā na raso rasaḥ, tac-camatkāra-sāratve sarvatraivādbhuto rasaḥ” ity ādi-diśā camatkāra-pūrvakam adbhutatvātiśaya-sphūrtau samyaṅ-mithyā-saṁśaya-sādṛśyapratyayātiriktena pratyaya-viśeṣeṇa citrotkīrṇābhirūpapratimādiṣv iva ime rāma-sīte, rāmo ’yaṁ sītā-śoka-viśīrṇaḥ, rāma-rāvaṇāv etau, vyāghro ’yaṁ janopaplāvakaḥ, śmaśānam idaṁ śava-samūhāntra-māṁsādy-aśana-mattonmatta-piśācādinṛtya-saṅkulam iti kṛtrimeṣv api teṣu vibhāvādiṣv akṛtrima-vat pratīyamāneṣu, svagata-rasa-vāsanā-dhauta-rajas-tamastayā svacchatareṣu teṣāṁ cetaḥsu eka evānando jāyate. na tu teṣām ekasminn eva cetasi raty-ādayaḥ sarve sthāyi-bhāvāḥ santi, teṣāṁ paraspara-visadṛśānāṁ yugapad ekatra sthiter abhāvāt. nāpi yaty-ādeś cetasi rateḥ sthāyitvam, na ca śamināṁ teṣāṁ bhayaśokādi-sattā, api tu sarva-rasa-camatkāra-grāhaka eka evāsvādakandaḥ kaścana ceto-dharma iti. ato bhayānaka-bībhatsādeḥ kāvya-nāṭyayor eva rasatā, na loke. ata evoktam “aṣṭau nāṭye rasāḥ smṛtāḥ” nāṭya evāṣṭau, loke tu śṛṅgārādīnāṁ kiyatām eva, pūrvokta-rasa-lakṣaṇāśrayatvāt.*

**Перевод:**

**Now let us examine rasa from the perspective of literature. There are two kinds of literature: drsya-kavya (dramaturgy, “worth seeing”) and sravya-kavya (poetry, “worth hearing”). In dramaturgy, the vibhavas and so on are obtained from the words and their existence depends on the actors and on acting techniques. In poetry, however, the vibhavas and so on are only obtained from the words.**

**To whom does the rasa (relishment) belong in a drama? It cannot possibly belong to the characters. It does not belong to the actors either, because relishment does not occur simply by showing expertise as a result of training and practice. When it is seen on occasion that the actors lose external awareness, that is explained by considering them to be spectators, and at that time their acting takes place only by the force of their predisposition, much like the way liberated souls eat, take pleasure, and so on. Therefore the rasa only belongs to the spectators.**

**The explanation is this: Given that there is astonishment in every rasa, on account of the spectators’ profuse wonder which is produced by the actor’s imitating the character’s deeds and actions of seeing and hearing and which is accompanied with a mental focus only on him since all other perceptions vanish at that time, the spectators think, for instance: “The elegance of Rama’s and STta’s expertise in romance is amazing”, “This fight between Rama and Ravana is amazing”, “The doings of the hungry ghost are astonishing”, and so on. Therefore it is said:**

*rase sāraś camatkāro yaṁ vinā na raso rasaḥ*  
*tac-camatkāra-sāratve sarvatraivādbhuto rasaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**“When there is a rasa, the essence is astonishment, without which a rasa is not a rasa. In all cases the rasa is only adbhuta, since it is the essence of the wonder in a rasa.”**

**Once the absorption in astonishment reaches a high level, being preceded by wonderment as mentioned above, the vibhavas and so on, though unreal—for example: “Those two are Sita and Rama”, “This is Rama, and His heart is rent by STta’s sorrow”, “These two are Rama and Ravana”, “This is a tiger that assails people”, “This is a slab of stone on which the carnivorous ogrish beast maddened by the entrails and the flesh on the corpses dances” and so on—, seem to be real like the beautiful designs in a bas-relief seem to be real, owing to the spectators’ distinct perception of those vibhavas and so on, a perception which is entirely distinct from: (1) The concept of sameness: “He is Rama in person,” (2) The concept of falsehood: “He is not Rama,” (3) A doubt: “Is he Rama or not?” and (4) The concept of similarity: “He is similar to Rama”, a unique type of bliss is produced in the spectators’ minds. Their minds had become clearer than before inasmuch as the rajo-guna and the tamo-guna were cleansed by the spectators’ predisposition to feel the rasa which they relate to.**

**It cannot be said that a spectator feels all the sthayi-bhavas at once, because the sthayis are mutually distinct, and so they cannot exist in the same place at the same time. Nor can it be said that a lifetime renunciant has the rati which is the sthayi of srngara, not to mention that an ascetic knows neither fear, sorrow, and so on. Rather, what happens is that the spectators have some indescribable inner attribute which is the unique cause of relishment and which includes the wonder involved in every rasa.**

**Consequently, bhayanaka (fear), bibhatsa (abhorrence), and so on, reach the level of rasa only in poetry and in drama, but not in day-to-day life. Therefore it is said: astau natye rasah smrtah, “In dramaturgy, there are eight rasas” (Kavya-prakasa 4.29).**

**In day-to-day life, however, sometimes several rasas, such as srngara, occur at the same time. And that is in conformity with the aforesaid definition of rasa.**

### 5.15

*atha nāṭya-rasānāṁ bhedeṣu śṛṅgārasyāditvena samucite ’pi prāṅ-nirdeśese saviśeṣa-varṇanīyatvāt, alaukikatvenaiva pratipādanīyatvāc ca paścād eva nirūpaṇaṁ kariṣyate. samprati vīra-krameṇāha. tatra ca prakṛtāprākṛtatvena jñāpite ’pi bhede ’prākṛtam evodāhariṣyāmaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Now, the discussion on the rasas will begin from vira (heroism) because although srngara should be mentioned first in the list of rasas (5.4), it will be expounded last since it has many details and since it ought to be explained only in terms of its transcendent nature. We will only illustrate vira-rasa in the scope of the transcendental plane, although vira-rasa as well has varieties both as a material rasa and as a transcendental rasa.**

*aprākṛto ’pi dvi-vidhaḥ pratyālambana-bhedataḥ*  
*sajātīyaṁ vijātīyaṁ pratyālambanam iṣyate (15)*

**Пословный перевод:**

aprakrtah—transcendental; api—although; dvi-vidhah—it has two varieties; prati-alambana-bhedatah—on account of the difference of each alambana; sajatiyam—of the same class; vijatiyam—of different classes; prati-alambanam—each alambana; isyate—is desired (is called).

**Перевод:**

**The transcendental rasa has two varieties on account of the difference of each alambana. Thus the alambanas are either of the same nature or of a different nature.**

### 5.16

*tatra vijātīyālambano ’prākṛta-vīro yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**This is an example of transcendental vira-rasa where the natures of the alambanas are respectively different:**

*guṇaṁ karṇākṛṣṭaṁ kara-kiśalayaṁ tūṇa-śikhare*  
*dhanuś cakrī-bhūtaṁ nipatad iṣu-vṛndaṁ tata itaḥ*  
*ripūn bhūmau suptān kalayati samaṁ deva-nikare*  
*jarāsandhasyājau jayati bhuja-vīryaṁ murabhidaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

gunam—the bowstring; karna-akrstam—pulled up to the ear; kara- kisalayam—the lotus in the form of a hand; tuna—of the quiver; sikhare—at the top; dhanuh—the bow; cakri-bhutam—which had become a cakra; nipatat—falling; isu-vrndam—the multitude of arrows; tatah—there; itah—here; ripun—the enemies; bhumau—on the ground; suptan—sleeping; kalayati—while \[the gods\] counted; samam—in such a way that it was the same; deva-nikare—while the multitude of gods; jarasandhasya—related to Jarasandha; ajau—in the battle; jayati—is supereminent; bhuja—of the arms; viryam— the prowess; mura-bhidah—of Krsna (“the destroyer of Mura”).

**Перевод:**

**The prowess of Krsna’s arms was supereminent in the battle with Jarasandha’s forces. The gods saw both His bowstring pulled to His ear and His right lotus hand at the top of His quiver at the same time. They saw that His bow had become a cakra. They observed the arrows that were falling here and there, and they counted the same number of enemies put to sleep on the battlefield.**

*atra prakṛte utsāhaḥ sthāyī, sa ca dvi-niṣṭhaḥ. ālambana-vibhāvo jarāsandhaḥ, tasya ca kṛṣṇaḥ. uddīpanam anyonya-śauṭīryādi, anubhāvaḥ—bāṇa-varṣaṇe hasta-lāghavam, vyabhicārī— garvogratāmarṣa-cāpalyādi. etaiḥ paripuṣṭaḥ sthāyī rasatāṁ prāptaḥ. sa cānukārye bhagavati prakṛte parokṣaḥ, kāvya-śravaṇāt sāmājike pratyakṣa iti sarvatronneyam. sajātīyālambanas tūhyaḥ. kaiścit sakhibhiḥ saha yuddham udāhriyate, tat tu līlā-viśeṣa iti prakṛte na likhyate. eṣa ca yuddha-dāna-dayā-dharma-pūrvakatvāc caturdhā. sarvatrotsāhaḥ sthāyī. ūhyāny udāharaṇāni.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the zeal in the subject of description is the sthayi. And this sthayi has a dual foundation because Jarasandha is one alambana-vibhava (the visaya of Krsna) and Krsna is his alambana-vibhava (the visaya of Jarasandha) (Krsna and Jarasandha are each other’s alambana). The uddipanas include the manliness shown to each other. An anubhava is the dexterity of the hand in shooting arrows. The vyabhicaris are garva (overweening pride), ugrata (arrogance), amarsa (indignation), capalata (restlessness), and so on. The sthayi, enhanced by these three, reaches the state of rasa (enjoyment, aesthetic delight).**

**And that rasa is indirectly perceivable in the character, the Lord, who is the subject of description, and is directly perceivable in the readers due to reading the poetry and in the spectators by hearing the same. It should be understood this way in every instance. An example of vira-rasa where the alambanas have the same nature can be inferred.**

**Some eminent scholar illustrates vira-rasa by describing a fight between Krsna and His friends (Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu 4.3.6­8). But that is only a particular type of pastime, and so it is not emphasized in this discourse. There are four categories of vira- rasa: yuddha-vira (a hero in battle), dana-vira (a hero in giving), daya-vira (a hero of compassion), and dharma-vira (a hero of moral ethics). In all cases the sthayi is utsaha (zeal). Examples of the last three can be looked into.**

**Комментарий:**

The verse describes Krsna’s heroism from the gods’ viewpoint. The gods’ adbhuta-rasa is implied, and Krsna’s vira-rasa is an aspect of it, but ultimately the vira-rasa ends up first-rate due to its superexcellence. Pandita-raja Jagannatha explains that although technically it might be second-rate, sometimes an implied sense is first-rate simply because it is outstanding.

### 5.17

*atha karuṇaḥ,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of karuna-rasa (lamentation):**

*dor-guptāyāṁ madhu-vijayino hā kathaṁ dvāravatyām*  
*anyāyo ’syām ayam udabhavad dhanta niṣkalmaṣāyām*  
*jātaṁ jātaṁ sutam apaharaty eṣa me ’kāla-mṛtyuḥ*  
*ko māṁ trātā hari hari ha hā hā hatā hā hatāḥ smaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

doh—by the arms; guptayam—which is protected; madhu- vijayinah—of Krsna; ha—alas; katham—why?; dvaravatyam—in Dvaravati; anyayah—bad occurrence; asyam—in this; ayam—this; udabhavat—occurred; hanta—alas; niskalmasayam— \[in Dvaraka,\] which is pure; jatam jatam—each one that was born; sutam—son; apaharati—takes away; esah—this; me—of mine; akala-mrtyuh— death at the wrong time; kah—who?; mam—me; trata—saves; hari hari—alas, alas; ha ha ha—alas, alas; hatah—struck; ha—aaah; hatah—struck; smah—we are.

**Перевод:**

**Ah, why has this grave misfortune occurred in saintly Dvaraka? The city is protected by Krsna’s arms. Alas, Death has taken my sons one after the other the minute they were born. Who will protect me? Hari hari, alas, alas, I have been struck by fate. Aaah.**

*atra śokaḥ sthāyī, eṣa eka-niṣṭhaḥ. putra-nāśaḥ—ālambanam, putra-gata-mamatādy uddīpanam. anubhāvaḥ—śiras-tāḍanādi. vyabhicārī—viṣāda-dainya-glāny-ādiḥ. ayaṁ tu sāmājika-gata eva, nānukārya-gataḥ parokṣe ’pi. ayaṁ sāmājika-gato ’py aprākṛtaḥ, kṛṣṇāśrayatvāt.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the sthayi is sorrow. The sthayi has a single foundation: The son’s death is an alambana (visaya alambana). The feeling of possessiveness toward the son is an uddipana. An anubhava is the beating on the head. Vyabhicaris include visada (despair), dainya (feeling miserable) and glani (weakness of body). This rasa only relates to the readers (by empathy); it does not relate to the character, although it is indirectly perceivable in him. Even though the rasa relates to the readers, it is transcendental insofar as it is based on Krsna.**

**Комментарий:**

Rupa Gosvami as well says one’s relatives can be an object of karuna-bhakti-rasa (Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu 4.4.3). But if karuna were fully transcendental in this instance, the character’s lamentation would be an obscure form of the character’s delight. Rupa Gosvami discusses this topic regarding karuna, bhayanaka and bibhatsa (Bhakti-rasamrta-smdhu 2.5.77; 2.5.122-127; 4.4.16). An example with bhayanaka is given ahead (5.21).

Alternatively, here the character’s karuna-rasa simply translates as “his taste of lamentation”. The same applies to bhayanaka and bibhatsa. However, Kavi Karnapura pointed out that in the material rasa, the character has no enjoyment (rasa) of either karuna, bhayanaka or bibhatsa (5.14). Visvanatha Kaviraja says that in those three, the rasa exists, but it is only in the reader (and not in the character); and only a connoisseur can experience it. He says this is one reason the causes, the effects, and the assistants, so called in day-to-day life, are named vibhava, anubhava, and vyabhicari-bhava in poetry and in dramaturgy.

In literature, jugupsa reaches the point of aesthetic delight, but does not attain the level of rapture. Therefore Rupa Gosvami says that in truth all the nine sthayis of the tradition except srngara and santa are actually vyabhicari-bhavas. He lists jugupsa and the rest as sthayi-bhavas (gaum rati) only in deference to Bharata Muni.

Moreover, the anubhava mentioned by Kavi Karnapura is not mentioned in the verse. Visvanatha Kaviraja explains that if an anubhava or a vyabhicari-bhava is necessarily implied, there is no discrepancy: sad-bhavas ced vibhavader dvayor ekasya va bhavet, jhatity anya-samaksepe tada doso na vidyate (Sahitya-darpana 3.16-17). In addition, the occurrence of many vyabhicari-bhavas compensates for the absence of an anubhava.

*sarvaṁ carvayasīva hanta vadanenodgīrṇa-pūrṇārciṣā*  
*jihvāgreṇa samagram ugra-mahasā lelihyase rodasī*  
*trastaṁ mām iha pāhi pāhi bhagavan pārtho ’py apārtho ’bhavam*

**Пословный перевод:**

damstra-koti—are millions of fangs; kathora-kuta—whose hard summits; katuna—\[by the mouth,\] which is acrid; brahmanda—of the universe; bhanda—within the casing; sthitam—located; sarvam carvayasi iva—You as if cause all to be chewed; hanta—alas; vadanena—by the mouth; udgirna-purna-arcisa—\[the mouth,\] from which whole flames are ejected; jihva-agrena—with the tip of the tongues; samagram—the entirety; ugra-mahasa—\[the tip,\] whose power is impetuous; lelihyase—You are repeatedly licking; rodasi—heaven and earth; trastam—afraid; mam—me; iha—at this time; pahi pahi—protect, protect; bhagavan—O Lord; parthah— Partha; api—although; aparthah—useless; abhavam—I became.

**Перевод:**

**Alas, with Your acrid mouths, whose millions of fangs are hard summits, and from which whole flames shoot forth, You are as if predigesting everything within the universal shell. With the tips of Your tongues, whose power is impetuous, You are repeatedly licking heaven and earth in their entirety. O Lord, protect me. Save me. I am terrified. Though I am Partha, I have become apartha (useless).**

*atha arjunasya bhayaṁ sthāyī, sa caika-niṣṭhaḥ. ālambanaṁ— viśva-rūpa-pradarśakaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ, uddīpanaṁ—tad-gatadaṁṣṭrādi, anubhāvaḥ—pāhi pāhīti kātaryam. vyabhicārī— apārtho ’bhavam iti dainyam. eṣa ca kṛṣṇālambanatvāt sāmagrīsānnidhyenānukārye ’pi rasatāṁ prāk-prāpta eva. bhaye ’pi kṛṣṇasphūrtes tat-sambandhād ānanda evety aprākṛta eva, na tu mālatyādau śārdūlādy-ālambanena makarandasya bhayaṁ vinānandaḥ. sati śaurye utsāha eva sthāyī bhavati. tena kadācid ānando jāyate, na bhayataḥ. tena prākṛte na rasatā.*

**Перевод:**

**Here Arjuna’s fear is the sthayi, which has a single foundation: The alambana is Sri Krsna who is showing the Universal Form. An uddipana is the fangs in that mouth. An anubhava is the agitation in “Protect me. Save me.” The vyabhicari is dainya (meekness): “I have become useless.” The rasa had already reached the level of rasa in the character due to the presence of all the constituent parts, since Krsna is the alambana. Although he had fear, Arjuna’s bliss occurred on account of a connection with Krsna, since he had a vision of Krsna that way, so obviously the rasa is transcendental.**

**In Malati-madhava, it is not that Makaranda had bliss without fearing the tiger, the alambana. When prowess is involved, the sthayi is only utsaha (zeal). Thus sometimes bliss occurs that way, but not because fear is the sthayi. Therefore material fear does not reach the level of rasa.**

**Комментарий:**

Usually an anubhava is a bodily reaction. The agitation in “Protect me. Save me” can be interpreted as the vyabhicari-bhava called trasa (sudden fear). This is indicated in the verse with the word trasta (terrified). Another important vyabhicari in bhayanaka is avega (mental flurry): iha santrasa-marana-capalavega-dinatah, visada-mohapasmara-sankadya vyabhicarinah (Bhakti-rasamrta- sindhu 4.6.11). According to Rupa Gosvami, the significant anubhavas in bhayanaka include the drying of the mouth, heavy breathing, and becoming unsteady; and specifically, all the sattvika- bhavas except tears manifest.

As Kavi Karnapura points out, Arjuna’s delight arose due to his relation with Krsna. It was not caused by fear itself. It cannot be said that Arjuna has cold feet oftentimes, thus there is no question of a sthayl-bhava proper. In Rupa Gosvami’s methodology of transcendental rasa, the seven gaunl ratis can only appear in someone who has a mukhya rati (Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu 4.1.5). Jiva Gosvami explains that those seven are figuratively called sthayi-bhavas: so’pi bhava-viseso ratir ucyate. kintu sa mancah krosantlti-vat gaunl aupacariklty arthah (Durgama-sangamanl 2.5.39). Rupa Gosvami says that in truth each one of those seven is the form of a vyabhicari-bhava (Commentary 5.14). In that regard, Rudrata and Bhoja propounded the theory that a vyabhicari-bhava can reach the level of rasa (aesthetic delight).

Moreover, the expression partho ’py apartho ’bhavam (Though I am Partha, I have become useless) is a slesabhasa-mula virodha ornament (seeming contradiction based on a semblance of paronomasia) (Sahitya-kaumudl 10.133) (Bhakti-rasamrta-sesa 4.279). In addition, the verse features the utpreksa ornament (fanciful assumption) (8.58): sarvam carvayaslva, “You are as if predigesting everything”. This shows that ornaments are important factors in raising the sthayl to the level of rasa. This understanding relates to the concept of aucitya (appropriateness): prasiddhaucitya-bandhas tu rasasyopanisat para, “A literary construction based on a well-known appropriateness is the highest secret teaching for the relishment of a rasa” (Dhvany-aloka 3.14)

(10.136). Another factor that increases the relishment of the sthayi is the usage of certain phonemes that are suitable to it: This is the topic of chapters six and nine.

The vyabhicaris include mati (thoughtfulness based on the scriptures), smrti (remembrance) and dhrti (steadfastness of the heart). This rasa is indirectly perceivable in the character and directly perceivable in the spectators. This one causes wonder. It is said:**

*yac ca kāma-sukhaṁ loke yac ca divya-sukhaṁ mahat*

**“Whatever delight of love is on earth, and whatever is the great delight in heaven, they are not worth the sixteenth part of the pleasure which springs from the cessation of all desires.” (Mahabharata 11.268.6)**

**Intense bliss is the result of intense wonder. And if this rasa becomes useful for bhakti, then the rasa is transcendental. Just as nirveda, though a vyabhicari-bhava, becomes the sthayi in santa and reaches the level of rasa, so the devadi-visaya rati, though a bhava (mind-set) in a technical sense (5.8), becomes the sthayi-bhava and, in combination with appropriate vibhavas and so on, turns into bhakti-rasa. Thus there are twelve rasas. And bhakti-rasa has ten varieties, considering that there are ten sthayi-bhavas, counting from rati (5.4) (the eight beginning from srngara-rati, as well as deva-visaya rati and nirveda). In this one, Sri Krsna is the foundation. The details can be looked into in another treatise.**

*atha prema-rasaḥ,*

**Перевод:**

*atra citta-dravaḥ sthāyī, sa cobhaya-niṣṭhaḥ. ālambanam anyonyam, uddīpanam anyonya-guṇa-parimalaḥ, anubhāvaḥ— viśiṣya nirvacanābhāvaḥ, vyabhicārī—maty-autsukyādiḥ. parokṣaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa-rādhayoḥ, sāmājikānāṁ pratyakṣaḥ. premarase sarve rasā antarbhavantīty eṣa mahīyān eva prapañcaḥ. grantha-gaurava-bhayād diṅ-mātram uktam. keśāñcin mate śrīrādhā-kṛṣṇayoḥ śṛṅgāra eva rasaḥ. tan-mate ’py etad udāharaṇaṁ nāsaṅgatam. śṛṅgāro ’ṅgī, premāṅgam, aṅgasyāpi kvacid udriktatā. vayaṁ tu premāṅgī śṛṅgāro ’ṅgam iti viśeṣaḥ. tathā ca,*

The rasa is indirectly perceivable in Sri Krsna and in Sri Radha and is directly perceivable in the readers.**

**All the rasas are included in prema-rasa. This entails a huge elaboration. Only the general idea is pointed out here out of fear of increasing the size of the treatise. Some persons opine that only the srngara between Sri Radha and Sri Krsna is the rasa. Even in their opinion, the above example is not incoherent: srngara is the angi and prema is the anga. Sometimes the anga exceeds the angi. In our estimation, prema is the angi and srngara is the anga. That is the difference. The explanation is:**

*unmajjanti nimajjanti premṇy akhaṇḍa-rasatvataḥ*  
*sarve rasāś ca bhāvāś ca taraṅgā iva vāridhau*

**Перевод:**

**“All the rasas and all the bhavas rise and fall in love like waves in an ocean, since love is the reservoir of rasa.”**

**atra deva-visayatvac ceto-ranjakata ratir eva bhavah. sa eva sthayi, alambanam—sn-krsnah, uddipanam—tan-mahimadi, anubhavah—hrdaya-dravadih, vyabhicari—nirveda-dainyadih. parokso bhaktanam, samajikanam tupratyaksah. yadyapi bhagavan sarva-rasa-kadamba-samvalitah, tathapi murtah srngara eva, savarnyat tad-daivatattvac ca. tatha hi “rasah srngara-namayam syamalah krsna-daivatah” iti. evam ca sarvesam eva rasanam varna devatas ca boddhavyah.**

**Since the Lord is the object here, the rati, which gives pleasure to the heart, is the bhava (mind-set) (5.8). And that is the sthayi. The alambana is Sri Krsna. Uddipanas include His greatness. Anubhavas are the melting of the heart, and so on. Vyabhicaris are nirveda, dainya, and so on. The rasa of the devotees is indirectly perceivable and that of the readers is directly perceivable.**

**Although the Lord has all the rasas, He is embodied srngara because He has the same color and because He is its presiding deity. For instance: rasah srngara-namayam syamalah krsna- daivatah, “This rasa, called srngara, is dark blue and its presiding deity is Krsna.” Thus it is understood that each rasa has its own color and presiding deity. (Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu 2.5.118-119)**

### 5.33

*mugdhā sudhāṁśu-kiraṇe*  
*jāla-gate bhavana-dāha-cakitākṣī*  
*ādātum avadhi-lekhaṁ*  
*praviśati bhavanaṁ nivārya sahayāntīḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

mugdha—silly; sudha-amsu-kirane—when moonrays; jala-gate— went through the lattice window; bhavana—in the house; daha— by the fire; cakita—are alarmed; aksi—She whose eyes; adatum—to take; avadhi—last; lekham—the letter; pravisati—She enters; bhavanam—the house; nivarya—after blocking; sahayanfih—the companions.

**Перевод:**

**When She saw moonrays enter the windows, She became alarmed: She thought that the house was going to catch on fire. That bewildered girl rushed into the house to retrieve His love letter while preventing Her friends from following Her inside.**

*eṣu pūrvau sambhoge, parau vipralambe. sarvatra ratiḥ sthāyī, sa cobhaya-niṣṭhaḥ. anyonyam ālambanam, uddīpanam—anyonyalāvaṇyādi vijana-sthānādi ca. anubhāvaḥ—kara-grahaṇādiḥ. vyābhicārī—śrama-jaḍatādiḥ. vipralambhe ca ratir eva sthāyī, sa ca ubhaya-niṣṭhaḥ. viprakarṣe ’pi rates tathaiva svataḥ-siddhatvāt. ālambanaṁ pūrva-vat, uddīpanaṁ—viprakarṣo ’nyonyaduḥkhānubhavaś candra-candana-pavanādiś ca. anubhāvaḥ— citra-lekhādiḥ. vyabhicārī—viṣāda-dainyādiḥ. ubhayor evānandadharmatvād rasatvam. ānandasyātma-dharmatvād ātmanaś ca bahir-indriyāpekṣitva-mātratvābhāvāt sphūrti-para evānandaḥ. etena śṛṅgāro dvi-vidhaḥ, sambhogo vipralambhaś ceti. ādyaḥ parasparāvalokanādhara-pāna-cumbana-nakha-daśana-kṣatādiprabhūta-prabhedo ’pi eka eva gaṇyate. aparas tv abhilāṣaviraherṣyā-pravāsa-śāpa-hetuka iti pañcadhā. loka eva śāpahetukaḥ. tenālaukikaś catur-vidhaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**In these four examples, the first two illustrate sambhoga- srngara (love in meeting) and the last two vipralambha-srngara (love in separation). In sambhoga, the sthayi is rati (romantic pleasure). It has a dual foundation: The two lovers are each other’s alambana. Uddipanas are their mutual glistening beauty, a solitary place, and so on. The anubhavas are the taking of the lover’s hand, and so forth. Vyabhicaris are srama (fatigue), jadata (indolence) and so on.**

**In vipralambha also, the sthayi is rati and has a dual foundation because such is the nature of rati even when the lovers are at a distance. The alambanas are the same as those in sambhoga. Uddipanas include being at a distance; feeling one another’s unhappiness; and the moon, a breeze from a forest of sandalwood trees (8.160), and so on. An anubhava is the making of an excellent drawing (Bhagavatam** [**10.62.17**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/62.17)**) (or of a love-letter, Ujjvala-nilamani 15.62). Vyabhicaris include visada (dejection) and dainya (feeling miserable).**

**Rasa takes place because both sambhoga and vipralambha have the attribute of bliss. Since bliss is an attribute of the soul and since the soul does not depend on the outer senses, in this context the word bliss refers to an inner vibe.**

**Thus srngara has two varieties: sambhoga and vipralambha. Sambhoga is counted as one category although it has many kinds, such as glancing at each another, drinking the juice of the lips, kissing, pricking the breasts with the nails, and making marks with the teeth. Vipralambha is said to have five categories: abhilasa (longing), viraha (separation), Trsya (pique), pravasa (living away), and sapa-hetuka (imagined curse by the creator or by Providence) (Kavya-prakasa, verse 31 vrtti). The last one, sapa-ketuka, only occurs in day-to-day life, therefore the transcendental vipralambha has four categories.**

**Комментарий:**

The verse also features an implied bhrantiman ornament (erroneous perception) (8.274) because in separation She feels that moonrays are flames.

### 5.34

*abhilāṣaḥ pūrva-rāgas tasyāvasthā daśa smṛtāḥ (19)*

**Перевод:**

**Abhilasa (longing) means purva-raga (love before meeting for the first time). It has ten stages.**

### 5.35

*yathā,*  
*abhilāṣaś cintanaṁ ca smṛtiś ca guṇa-kīrtanam*  
*udvegaś ca pralāpoś conmādaś ca vyādhir aṣṭamaḥ*  
*jaḍatā navamī jñeyā maraṇaṁ daśamam smṛtam (20)*

**Перевод:**

**The ten stages are: abhilasa (longing), cintana (pondering), smrti (remembrance), guna-kirtana (mentioning the lover’s qualities), udvega (anxious agitation), pralapa (nonsensical talk), unmada (deranged state), vyadhi (sickness), jadata (indolence), and marana (death; no desire to live).**

*virahas tu bhāvī bhavan bhūtaś ceti tridhā*

**Перевод:**

**The second kind of vipralambha, viraha, has three subvarieties: bhavi (future), bhavan (present) and bhuta (past).**

**Комментарий:**

In poetics, the word smrta (remembered) is often used in sutras to signify that the information comes from the tradition. The above list of ten stages is sourced in Natya-sastra (22.170-172), except that vilapa (chatter, or lamentation) is seen instead ofpralapa. Rudrata made the change to pralapa (Kavyalankara 14.4), and this was accepted by Dhananjaya and by Visvanatha Kaviraja. Bharata Muni used the term anusmrti (constant remembrance) instead of smrti. At any rate, cintana (cinta), smrti, unmada, vyadhi, jadata, and marana are also names of vyabhicari-bhavas (5.261), but they are special in the context ofpurva-raga. The categories of vipralambha are illustrated from text 5.55, and examples of the ten stages are shown from text 5.60.

Rupa Gosvami mentions the list in the above sutra, in the context of the purva-raga in samanjasa-rati, but pralapa is replaced by vilapa (Ujjvala-nllamani 15.48-49).

This is Rupa Gosvami’s list in the context of the purva-raga in samartha-rati: lalasa (great longing), udvega (anxious agitation), jagarya (inability to sleep), tanava (thinness), jadima (indolence), vaiyagrya (mental absorption), vyadhi (sickness), unmada (deranged state), moha (infatuation), and mrtyu (no desire to live) (Ujjvala-nilamani 15.21-22). He says tanava can be replaced by vilapa (15.32).

Rupa Gosvami gives this list in the context of dasya-rasa: angesu tapa (heat in the limbs), krsata (thinness), jagarya (staying awake), alamba-sunyata (mental voidness), adhrti (lack of mental composure), jadata (indolence), vyadhi (sickness; specific mental agony), unmada (deranged state), murcchita (swoon), and mrti (no desire to live). This enumeration is based on Visvanatha Kaviraja’s second list of ten stages, which he mentions in the section on pravasa-vipralambha. Still, Visvanatha Kaviraja says his two lists apply in purva-raga and in pravasa interchangeably.

Rupa Gosvami’s list in pravasa is: cinta (pondering), jagara (sleeplessness), udvega (agitation), tanava (thinness), malinata (soiled body), pralapa (lamentation), unmada (deranged state), vyadhi (sickness), moha (fainting) and mrtyu: cintatrajagarodvegau tanavam malinangata, pralapo vyadhir unmado moho mrtyur dasa dasa. (Ujjvala-nilamani 15.167)

### 5.36

*īrśyā-śabdo ’tra māna-paraḥ, sa ca dvedhā.*

**Перевод:**

**In this regard, the word irsya means mana (pique). There are two kinds:**

*īrṣyā-praṇaya-sambhūto dvedhā mānaḥ prakīrtyate*  
*anyāsakte priyatame īrṣyā-māno bhavet striyāḥ (21)*

**Перевод:**

**Mana has two varieties: irsya-mana (pique due to resentment) and pranaya-mana (pique due to fondness). The Trsya-mana of a woman occurs when her sweetheart loves another woman.**

*yad uktam,*

*dvayoḥ praṇaya-mānaḥ syāt pramode sumahaty api*  
*premṇaḥ kuṭila-gāmitvāt kopo yaḥ kāraṇaṁ vinā*

**Перевод:**

**Pranaya-mana takes place even though the joy between the ladylove and her sweetheart is profuse. Since love moves in crooked ways, pranaya-mana is anger without a cause. (Sahitya- darpana 3.198)**

**Комментарий:**

Rupa Gosvami equates irsya-mana with sahetu-mana (pique with a cause) (Ujjvala-nilamani 15.77) and pranaya-mana with nirhetu- mana (pique without a cause) (Ujjvala-nilamani 15.100).

### 5.38

*tathā ca,*

*nadīnāṁ ca vadhūnāṁ ca bhujaṅgānāṁ ca sarvadā*  
*premnām api gatir vakrā kāraṇaṁ tatra neṣyate*

**Перевод:**

**The course of rivers, the behavior of women, the motions of snakes, and the ways of love are always crooked. No cause can account for them.**

### 5.39

*bhūta-viraheṇa saha pravāsasyāvāntara-bhedo yathodāharaṇaṁ*  
*sphuṭī-bhaviṣyati, tathobhayor eva sambhoga-vipralambhayoḥ*  
*parasparāvalokanādhara-pānādy-abhilāṣādīnāṁ*  
*krameṇodāharaṇāni.*

**Перевод:**

**It will be made clear in the examples (5.74, 5.77) that bhuta- viraha (separation in the past) combined with pravasa makes an intermediate category. From here onward the examples of sambhoga, such as glancing at each another, drinking the juice of the lips, and of vipralambha, including abhilasa, will be illustrated, by the aforesaid sequence.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Kaviraja subsumes viraha inpravasa (Sahitya-darpana 3.208). Rupa Gosvami follows him, but divides pravasa in two categories—the lover is present and the lover is not present— and includes the three varieties of viraha in the latter (Ujjvala- nllamani 15.158). But in texts 5.72-73, Kavi Karnapura shows that bhavl viraha (upcoming separation) and bhavan viraha (present separation) can occur when the lover is present.

### 5.40

*tatra parasparāvalokanaṁ yathā,*

**Пословный перевод:**

tasyah—of hers; sakhibhih—by the friends; api—even; viksya— after noticing; su-jatam—well produced; antah—inside; bhava—of emotion; udayam—rise; kam api—some indescribable; cancala— fickle; locana—of the eyes; antaih—by means of the ends; dhanyah—are fortunate; bhavan—You; iti—in this way; krta—was done; mama sammukhibhih—who were facing me; indivara—of blue lotuses; chada—coverings (petals); mayi—consisting of; puspa-vrstih—a rain of flowers.

**Комментарий:**

The verse features Pandita-raja Jagannatha’s padartha nidarsana ornament (illustration of the meaning of a word): It is a kind of metaphor where the subject of the comparison (upameya) and the standard of comparison (upamana) are stated, but the comparison is not directly expressed. Here the purport of the sentence is that the sakhls ’ eyes are blue lotuses. The metaphor is not implied because both the tenor and the vehicle are stated. In Mammata’s methodology, however, this is classed in the variety of the nidarsana ornament called asambhavad-vastu nidarsana (an unlikely connection between things causes the perception of a similarity). Mammata would say that the above culminates in a simile: The sakhls’ eyes are like blue lotuses. But in Kavi Kamapura’s methodology, this literary device is a form of the apahnuti ornament (concealment) (8.87).

And the drinking of some intoxicating beverage occurs by means of each other’s mouths.**

**Комментарий:**

The verse features rare formations of avyayi-bhava compounds: The words ankanki, kara-kari, karna-karni, skandha-skandhi, and mukha-mukhi are avyayi-bhava compounds made with the taddhita suffix i\[c\].

Here the avyayi-bhava compounds do not suggest any particular meaning, but they eminently raise the sthayito the level of rasa. As such they have the force of suggestive padamsas, like the avyayi- bhavas shown earlier (3.58). Mammata explains that sometimes the amazingness of the grammatical forms themselves enhances the relishment: atra, imanij-avyayibhava-karma-bhutadharanam svarupasya tarunatve iti dhanusah samipe iti maulau vasatiti tv adibhis tulye, esam vacakatve, asti kascit svarupasya viseso yas camatkara-kari sa eva vyanjakatvam prapnoti, “In this example, given that the literal expressions by means of the suffix iman\[ic\] in tarunimani (when the youthfulness), of the avyayi-bhava “anu- madana-dhanuh” (near Cupid’s bow) and of the karma-bhutadhara “maulim” (the top) are semantically equalled by these ordinary synonymous expressions respectively: svarupasya tarunatve (when youthfulness of the nature occurs), dhanusah samipe (near the bow), and maulau vasati (she stays at the top), only a distinct particularity of the grammatical forms that generates astonishment achieves the state of being suggestive” (Kavya-prakasa, verse 110 vrtti).

*tatra vana-vihāro yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**Of those, an example of strolling in the forest:**

*arghyaṁ kuṭmalakair maranda-paṭalaiḥ pādyaṁ parāgair madhu-*  
*syandārdrair anulepanaṁ kisalayaiḥ puṣpaiś ca bhūṣāṁ phalaiḥ*  
*naivedyaṁ pavanāhatair avayavair nṛtyaṁ madāli-svanair*  
*gītaṁ kalpayatā harir vana-gato vallī-cayenārcitaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

arghyam—the washing of the hands; kutmalakaih—with buds; maranda—of flower nectar; patalaih—with multitudes; padyam— the washing of the feet; paragaih—with pollen; madhu—honey; syanda—exuding; ardraih—soft; anulepanam—ointment; kisalayaih—with sprouts (or shoots); puspaih—with flowers; ca— and; bhusam—ornament; phalaih—with fruits; naivedyam—food offering; pavana-ahataih—struck by the wind; avayavaih—with the portions; nrtyam—dancing; mada-ali-svanaih—with the sounds of maddened bees; gitam—singing; kalpayata—\[the multitude,\] which was making; harih—Hari; vana-gatah—who had gone to the forest; valli—of creepers; cayena—by the multitude; arcitah—was worshiped.

**Перевод:**

**Hari went to the woods and was worshiped by the creepers which were offering arghya with buds, padya with flower juice, ointment with pollen softened with a drip of honey, decorations with sprouts and blossoms, naivedya with fruits, dancing with their limbs swooshed by the wind, and singing with the buzzing of excited bumblebees.**

**Комментарий:**

The format of this verse is similar to the one in verse 17.19 of Govinda-lilamrta (beginning prasveda). The commentator Vrndavana Cakravarti notes that Krsnadasa Kaviraja’s verse illustrates the parinama ornament (modification): prasvedadinam padyadi-rupena parinatir atra parinamalankarah (Sadananda- vidhayini 17.19). When the upamana (standard of comparison) (vehicle) must assume the nature of the upameya (subject of comparison) to make sense of the statement, that is the parinama ornament. Parinama occurs here because the buds must assume the nature of arghya, and so on, to make sense of the statement, otherwise it would be pointless to say that Hari was worshiped with arghya and so on. Ruyyaka invented parinama. All the poetic theorists after him, except Kavi Karnapura, acknowledge this poetic expression as the parinama ornament. Kavi Karnapura would say that the above features the rupaka ornament (metaphor). Moreover, the verse is an instance of srngarabhasa.

### 5.65

*unmādaḥ,*

**Перевод:**

*he vāsanti vilokitādya sumukhī-rādhā tvayāsmin vane*  
*vātāndolita-pallavaiḥ kara-talair nā-neti kiṁ bhāṣase*  
*yātānena pathaiva sā parimalais tasyā yad andhī-kṛtās*  
*tvat-puṣpeṣu patanty aho na madhupā bhrāmyanti sarvāḥ diśaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

he vasanti—O vasanti plant; vilokita—was seen; adya—today; su-mukhi—who has a beautiful face; radha—Radha; tvaya—by you; asmin vane—in this forest; vata—in the wind; andolita— undulating; pallavaih—which are shoots; kara-talaih—with the hand palms; na na—no, no; iti—(end of citation); kim—why?; bhasase—you say; yata—she went; anena patha eva—by this very path; sa—she; parimalaih—by the scents; tasyah—her; yat— because; andhi-krtah—made blind; tvat-puspesu—on your flowers; patanti—they fall; aho—how amazing; na—not; madhupah— the bees; bhramyanti—are wandering; sarvah—all; disah—the directions.

**Перевод:**

**O vasanti plant, you saw beautiful Radha in this forest today. Why do you say “No, no” with your hand shoots waving in the wind? She went by this path because there’s an oddity: The bees, blinded by Her fragrance, are not landing on your flowers: They’re flying everywhere.**

**Комментарий:**

The essential characteristic of unmada is that the speaker makes no difference between a person and an insentient entity: unmadas caparicchedas cetanacetanesv api (Sahitya-darpana 3.191). Similarly, Rupa Gosvami says unmada is the mistaking of one thing for another: atasmims tu tad iti bhrantir unmada iti kirtyate (Ujjvala-nilamani 15.40).

Concerning the previous verse, Visvanatha Kaviraja says pralapa is the character’s talking to someone who is not present: alaksya-vak-pralapah syac cetaso bhramanad bhrsam (Sahitya-darpana 3.192). Rupa Gosvami sayspralapa (inpravasa, 15.173) is a lamentation; it is the same as his vilapa in purva-raga (15.33). The pralapa which is a vocal reaction (vacika anubhava) is “useless talk”: vyarthalapah pralapah syat (Ujjvala-nilamani 11.87), whereas vilapa in that context is a lamentation: vilapo duhkha-jam vacah (Ujjvala-nilamani 11.83). Kavi Karnapura’s example of pralapa (5.64) corresponds to the vocal reaction. Or else that verse can be classed as an unmada bhava-santi (cessation of derangement).

*nikhilendriya-saṁvarte*

*magnānanda-vivarte*

**Пословный перевод:**

nikhila-indriya—of all the senses; samvarte—in which there is the dissolution; syama—of Syama; sudha—of ambrosia; dhama—of the body; madhurima—which is the sweetness; avarte—in which there is a whirlpool; magna—I am immersed; ananda—of bliss; vivarte—in an altered state; matah—O mother (O sakhi); na— not; atah param—after this; varte—I exist.

**Перевод:**

The verse features a yamaka (word rhyme) (7.29) of the sound varte, at the end of each line.

### 5.70

### 5.71

*nailaḥ sa eṣa kathito na kadācid dhrasati śobhate ’tyartham*  
*kausumbhaḥ sa hi viditaḥ sthitvāpaiti praśobhate pūrvam*  
*māñjiṣṭhaḥ sa hi yaḥ kila nāpaity evātiśobhate ’jasram*  
*hāridraḥ sa tu bodhyo yāty api na ca śobhate yas tu (25-26)*

**Перевод:**

**When the love is intensely resplendent and never diminishes, that is naila-raga (indigo love). When the love is resplendent at first and slack afterward, that is kausumbha-raga (safflower love). When the love is always eminently resplendent and does not go away, that is manjistha-raga (Indian-madder love). And when the love is not resplendent and goes away, that is haridra-raga (turmeric love).**

**Комментарий:**

The definitions of the first three are partly sourced in Sahitya- darpana. According to Visvanatha Kaviraja, naila-raga means the passion makes no great show (it is not highly resplendent), but never diminishes. His analogy is that a cloth colored with indigo dye will not lose its depth of color after being washed; a cloth colored with safflower dye will lose its depth of color after being washed; and a cloth colored with madder dye can stand washing, but will not be too resplendent.

The subsequent analogy is that sambhoga becomes enhanced after vipralambha, just like a cloth dipped in dye on several occasions becomes vivid in color.

### 5.72

*atha virahaḥ. sa ca tri-vidhaḥ, bhāvī, bhavan, bhūtaś ceti. tatra bhāvī yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**Now viraha is expounded. There are three kinds of separation after meeting: bhavi (in the future), bhavan (in the present) and bhuta (in the past). This illustrates bhavi viraha:**

*yāsyāmi śvaḥ sumukhi mathurām āgato rāja-dūtaḥ*  
*pratyāyātuṁ kati nu ghaṭikā hanta bhāvī vilambaḥ*  
*no jānīmaḥ prakṛti-kaṭhinaḥ kārya-bhāvas tathā cet*  
*sārdhaṁ yāntaḥ priya mad-asavaḥ kvāpi kārye niyojyāḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

yasyami—I will go; svah—tomorrow; su-mukhi—O woman with a beautiful face; mathuram—to Mathura; agatah—returned; raja- dutah—the king’s messenger; pratyayatum—to return; kati—how many; nu—possibly; ghatikah—\[after\] hours; hanta—alas; bhavi—will be; vilambah—a delay; no—not; janimah—we know; prakrti—by nature; kathinah—is difficult; karya-bhavah—the procedure of the task; tatha—in that way; cet—if; sardham—along (with you); yantah—which are going; priya—O beloved; mat- asavah—my life airs; kva api—at some point in time; karye—in the task; niyojyah—let them be engaged.

**Перевод:**

**“Lovely woman, I’ll depart tomorrow. The king’s messenger arrived in Mathura. Alas, it might take a while before I come back. I’m not sure how many hours the task will require. By nature, it is difficult.” “In that case, sweetheart, let my life force, which follows you, be engaged in your task somehow or other.**

*bhavan yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**Пословный перевод:**

yami—I depart; iti—(end of citation); krsna-vacane—when Krsna’s utterance occurred; pranaih—by the life airs; viniruddha—was congested; kantha-kuharayah—of she the hollow of whose throat; bahih—outside; iva—as if; bhavitum—to become; asaktam— unable; prati-uttaram—a reply; antah—inside; eva—only; vijughurne—wobbled.

**Пословный перевод:**

sardham—with; yat—which; nija-daivatena—along with your presiding deities; na gatam—did not go; dauratmyam—bad behavior; etat hi—this very; vah—your; janita—you all should know; avadhi-vasaram—(avadhi-vasarah) the last day (the day of the return); ca—and; ganana—by counting; gamyah—knowable; asti—is; lekhasu—in lines; yah—which; iti—this; akarnya—after hearing; viyukta—separated; gopa-sudrsah—of a beautiful-eyed girl of a cowherd; pranaih samam—with the life airs; samkatham— the talk; eka-ekam—each one; prati-vasaram—each day; priya- sakhi—a dear friend; rekham—a line; rahah—secretly; lumpati— erases.

If he doesn’t come back by then, I’m going to abandon you by force.” Hearing this talk of a heartbroken gopi to her life airs, every day her confidante secretly opens her friend’s book and erases a line.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Kaviraja says his example was composed by his father:

*cintābhiḥ stimitaṁ manaḥ kara-tale līnā kapola-sthalī*

Which lover, though hard to petition, could tolerate that his beloved is in such a condition?” (Sahitya-darpana 3.208)**

### 5.75

*atha praṇaya-mānaḥ,*

**Перевод:**

*tat kenāpi hṛtaṁ tvayā nahi nahi śraddhā para-sve mama*  
*aṅge cet tava dṛśyate bhavati cen nūnaṁ tvayaivārpitaṁ*  
*nītvā gaccha mukhe tavāsti yad ayaṁ rāgas tadā saṅga-jaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

manah—pique; tisthatu—it should remain; radhike—O Radhika; tava—your; hrtam—taken away; raktam—red (or enamored); manah—the mind (heart); dehi—give; me—to me; tat—that; kena api—by someone (i.e. by whom?); hrtam—taken away; tvaya— by you; nahi—no; nahi—no; sraddha—interest; para-sve—in another’s possession; mama—my; ange—in the body; cet—if; tava—your; drsyate—is seen; bhavati—is; cet—if; nunam— indeed; tvaya—by you; eva—only; arpitam—placed; nitva—after taking; gaccha—go; mukhe—in the mouth; tava—your; asti—is; yat—because; ayam—this; ragah—redness; tada—at that time; sanga-jah—produced by the contact.

The raga (love) in Krsna’s heart is produced by His contacting the raga (redness) on Her lips. Visvanatha Cakravarti comments: “The implied sense is: “My heart abides on Your lips because both have the attribute of raga. Allow Me to get it back.” It’s understood that He kissed Her.” (Subodhini)

*gavyāny atti tathā kavoṣṇam adhikaṁ rādhe śvasity eva saḥ*  
*tvat-pallī-prativeśa-paṇya-janatā-krayyaṁ tu dadhy-ādikaṁ*  
*krītvā sampratipāditaṁ priya-janair aśnāti hṛṣṭāntaraḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

nana-kausalatah—with various types of expertise; krtani— made; suhrdam—of friends; vrndena—by the multitude; na—not; anandatah—with pleasure; gavyani—dairy goods; atti—he eats; tatha—in that way; kavosnam—warm; adhikam—to a high degree; radhe—O Radha; svasiti— sighs; eva—only; sah—he; tvat-palli— of your small village; prativesa—in the neighborhood; panya- janata—by business people; krayyam—made available to buy; tu—but; dadhi-adikam—yogurt and so on; kritva—after buying; sampratipaditam—delivered; priya-janaih—by the dear people; asnati—eats; hrsta-antarah—he whose heart is joyful.
