### 5.78

*atha sāmānyato varṇitasya vibhāvasyālaukikatayā viśeṣam āha. tatrālambanaṁ nāyako nāyikāś ca. tatra ko ’sau nāyakaḥ, kāś ca nāyikā ity apekṣāyāṁ nāyakam āha,*

**Перевод:**

**The vibhavas of srngara-rasa were described in a general way. Now he details the vibhavas in the transcendental aspect. Of the two types of vibhavas, the alambana consists of the lover and the ladyloves. What is the lover like and what are the ladyloves like? With that in mind, he depicts the lover:**

*sarva-śuddha-rasa-vṛnda-kandalaḥ*  
*sarva-nāyaka-ghaṭā-kirīṭa-gaḥ*  
*atyalaukika-guṇair alaṅkṛto*  
*gokulendra-tanayaḥ sunāyakaḥ (27)*

**Перевод:**

**He is root cause of all the varieties of pure rasa, is the best of all lovers, and is adorned with very uncommon qualities. The prince of Gokula is a superb lover.**

*sarva-śuddha-rasa-vṛnda-kandalatvaṁ “śṛṅgārī rādhikāyāṁ” ity-ādi. sarva-nāyaka-ghaṭeti sarva-śabdo dhūrta-nāyakavarjana-paraḥ. atyalaukika-guṇair iti viruddhāviruddha-nityacamatkāri-guṇavān, viruddha-vad bhāsate, na tu viruddhaḥ, sa viruddhāviruddhaḥ. eko ’nekaḥ, paricchinno vyāpīty-ādi-vat. alaukika-guṇavati laukika-guṇā api jñeyāḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Being the root cause of all the varieties of pure rasa was illustrated: “He loves Radhika” etc. (5.29). The word ’all’ in “all lovers” serves to exclude mischievous lovers.**

**The sense of “with very uncommon qualities” is this: He has qualities that always astonish and that are both contradictory and noncontradictory. He seems to be self-contradictory, but He is not so. He is both self-contradictory and noncontradictory. For instance, though one, He is many. And although He is delimited due to having a body, He is all-pervading. Moreover, common qualities should also be understood to be in Him, who has uncommon qualities.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: Although the qualities of a dhlroddhata lover and those of a dhlra-santa lover are mutually contradictory, they are not contradictory in Sri Krsna (Subodhinl). The Acarya also points out that usually a dhlra-santa lover cannot be a dhlra-lalita lover (Bhakti-sara-pradarsinl 2.1.225). The ladyloves are particularized from text 5.106.

The theory in this section on alambana-vibhavas in srngara-rasa continues up to text 5.253. It is not found in Kavya-prakasa. Here, for the most part Kavi Karnapura follows Visvanatha Kaviraja and Rupa Gosvami. For this reason, the author of Bhakti-rasamrta-sesa, which is a remake of Sahitya-darpana with examples from Gopala-campu, Govinda-lllamrta and so on, skipped Visvanatha Kaviraja’s chapter on rasa. Visvanatha’s chapter, based in part on Singhabhupala’s Rasarnava-sudhakara, was the most important reference used by Rupa Gosvami in composing Ujjvala-nllamani.

### 5.79

*te yathā,*  
*kṛtī kulīnaḥ sa-śrīkas tyāgī yauvana-rūpa-bhāk*  
*dakṣo ’nurakta utsāhī tejo-vaidagdhya-bhūṣitaḥ (28)*

**Перевод:**

**The uncommon qualities are: krti (learned), kulina (well- mannered), sa-srika (very beautiful), tyagi (having a sense of renunciation), yauvana-rupa-bhak (having a youthful physique), daksa (expert in getting things done quickly), anurakta (loving), utsahi (enthusiastic), and tejo-vaidagdhya-bhusita (adorned with effulgence and wit).**

### 5.80

*adhikās tu,*

*satyaṁ śaucaṁ dayā kāntir āstikyaṁ dhairyam eva ca*  
*audāryaṁ praśrayaḥ śīlaṁ kṣāntiḥ prahvo ’nahaṅkṛtiḥ (29)*

**Перевод:**

**Additional common qualities are: satya (honesty, sincerity), sauca (integrity), daya (compassion), kanti (splendor), astikya (piousness), dhairya (fortitude), audarya (elevated mentality), prasraya (respectfulness), sila (being good-natured), ksanti (tolerance),prahva (humility), anahankrti (not being conceited).**

*ity-ādayo nityāḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**These and other qualities always exist in Him.**

### 5.81

*tatra nāyaka-ghaṭeti tad-bhedān āha,*

**Перевод:**

**A multitude of lovers was referred to above (5.78). He mentions the varieties:**

*udātta uddhataś caiva praśānto lalītas tathā*  
*sarve ’mi dhīra-śabdādyāś catvāro nāyakāḥ smṛtāḥ (30)*  
*dhīra-śabdādyā iti dhīrodāttādaya ity arthaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**The four varieties of lovers are: dhirodatta (intelligent and virtuous), dhiroddhata (intelligent and boastful), dhira-prasanta (intelligent and peaceful), and dhira-lalita (intelligent and fun­loving).**

**Комментарий:**

The term dhira means either intelligent or self-controlled. Bhoja says the term dhira denotes dhairya (self-control, fortitude): uddhato lalitah santah udatto dhairya-vrttitah, satho dhrsto ’nukulas ca daksinas ca pravrttitah. (Sarasvati-kanthabharana 5.109)

### 5.82

*tatra dhīrodāttādayo yathā,*  
*ātma-ślāghā-rahitaḥ kṣamī gambhīro mahā-sattvaḥ*  
*dhīrodāttaḥ stheyān nigūḍha-māno dhṛḍha-vrataḥ suvacāḥ*  
*ātma-ślāghā-nirato māyī caṇḍaś capalaś ca*  
*dhīroddhataḥ sa kathito ’haṅkṛti-jhaṅkāra-niḥśaṅkaḥ*  
*ubhaya-guṇa-vyatirikto bhūyān sādhāraṇaiś ca guṇaiḥ*  
*dhīra-praśānta-saṁjño bhavati dvija-vaiśya-jātikaḥ sādhuḥ*  
*mṛdulaḥ kalā-kalāpo niścinto madhura-vaidagdhyaḥ*  
*prathama-rasa-pradhāno lalita-katho dhīra-lalitaḥ syāt*  
*sarve ’nukūla-dakṣiṇa-śaṭha-dhṛṣṭatvena ṣoḍaśadhā (31-34)*

**Перевод:**

**The dhirodatta does not praise himself. He is tolerant, profound, noble-minded and resolute. He does not show his pride. He is dedicated to performing vows and is eloquent.**

**The dhiroddhata likes to praise himself. He is deceitful, impetuous and restless. He is careless about conceited remarks.**

**The dhira-prasanta has neither the dhirodatta’s qualities nor the dhiroddhata’s qualities. He abounds in common qualities. He is a good person who is either a Brahmana or a Vaisya.**

**The dhira-lalita is gentle, well-versed in the arts, carefree, witty in romance, mostly concerned with srngara-rasa, and a sweet talker.**

**The four categories of lovers make a total of sixteen categories because each type of lover is either anukula (chaste), daksina (soft toward another woman) (or expert in treating many ladyloves equally), satha (a cheat) or dhrsta (an impudent cheater and liar).**

**Комментарий:**

Kavi Karnapura paraphrased Visvanatha Kaviraja’s definitions.

### 5.83

*keśāñcin mate dhīra-lalitasyaivānukūlādi-bhedāḥ, na sarveṣām. eṣāṁ lakṣaṇam,*

**Перевод:**

**Some authorities say the four categories beginning from anukula only relate to the dhira-lalita lover. The definitions of those four are:**

*ekāśrīto ’nukūlaḥ sama-rāgo dakṣiṇas tu sarvāsu*  
*śaṭha ekatraiva rato bahir anyatra priyo ’priyo manasi*  
*aparāddhaś ca viśaṅko dṛṣṭe doṣe ’pi mithyā-vāk*  
*tarjana-tāḍanayor ’pi kṛtyor nirlajja eva dhṛṣṭaḥ syāt*  
*ṣoḍaśa-vidhās ta ete punas tridhā cottamādi-bhedena*  
*aṣṭādhika-catvāriṁśad bhedā nāyakāḥ kathitāḥ*  
*punar ete syur divyā divyādivyā adivyāś ca*  
*sa catuś-catvāriṁśac-chatam ekaṁ tena tad-bhedāḥ*  
*dhīrapraśānta-śaṭhayor dhṛṣṭasya ca bheda-varjitair aparaiḥ*  
*līlā-vaśataḥ sarvair aviruddhatvād viruddhe ’pi*  
*gokula-rāja-kumāras tena paraṁ sarva-nāyakādhīśaḥ*  
*dhīrodātto guruṣu jñātiṣu dhīroddhato vipakṣeṣu*  
*māyāviṣu niyatam asau vraja-pūryāṁ dhīra-lalitaḥ syāt*  
*anukūlo rādhāyāṁ sarvāsv aparāsu dakṣiṇaḥ kathitaḥ*  
*līlā-vaśāt kadācana dhṛṣṭo ’pi śaṭhaś ca kutrāpi (35-41)*

**Перевод:**

**The anukula lover has a single woman, whereas the daksina lover has equal affection for all women. The satha lover is one who, being enamored of only one woman, outwardly shows affection to the other woman and is unkind to her heart. The dhrsta lover is prone to commit offenses, but he does not worry about that. He speaks lies even when the woman sees through his lies. He feels no shame even in pointing with the finger and in chastising.**

**These sixteen categories are multiplied by three in consideration of the varieties of uttama (first-class), madhyama (second-class) and adhama (third-class). These forty-eight categories are again multiplied by three with regard to the varieties of divya (divine), divyadivya (divine and human) and adivya (human). This makes a grand total of 144 categories of lovers.**

**The prince of Gokula is characterized by all the categories except dhira-prasanta, satha, and dhrsta. But sometimes, depending on the kind of pastime, He has those moods too. Although they are contradictory, there is no contradiction in Him. For this reason, He is by far the best of all lovers. He is dhirodatta toward superiors and relatives. He is dhiroddhata toward adversaries and sorcerers. He is always dhira-lalita in Vraja. He is anukula toward Radha, but toward all other women He is daksina. Depending on the pastime, sometimes He is dhrsta, and on occasion He is satha.**

### 5.84

*anukūlādīnāṁ krameṇodāharāni.*  
*tatrānukūlo yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**The four categories beginning from anukula will be illustrated. This is an example of anukula (favorable, faithful):**

*nānyasyāḥ sadanaṁ prayāti sa mayā samprārthyamāno ’pi ca*  
*prāyo me hṛdayaṁ dunoti lalite tāsāṁ manas-tāpataḥ*  
*ārāme ramate mamaiva satataṁ mad-vartma saṁvīkṣyate*  
*svapne ’pi pratikūlatāṁ na gatavān kṛṣṇaḥ sa-tṛṣṇo mayi*

**Перевод:**

**Lalita, Krsna never goes to another woman’s place even if I ask Him to. This almost pains My heart, because those women are upset over it. He always takes pleasure in My courtyard. When I’m away, He keeps an eye on My path. He never has a bad mood, even in dreams. Krsna is sa-trsna for Me (thirsty).**

### 5.85

*evam ekatra rato ’py alaukika*  
*nāyakatvād dakṣiṇo ’pi. tad yathā*

**Перевод:**

**Although He is enamored of one woman, He is also daksina because He is a transcendental lover. For example:**

*śyāmāṅke caraṇau kaloruphalake śīrṣaṁ surekhāṅgulau*  
*keśāṁś cāmara-cālikā-bhuja-taṭe dṛṣṭiṁ priyoktau śrutim*  
*tāmbūlārpaṇikā-kare kara-puṭīṁ kastūrikorasy uraś*  
*candrā-vakṣasi pṛṣtham arpayad aho nidrāti nīlaṁ mahaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

syama-anke—on Syama’s lap; caranau—both feet; kala- uruphalake—on Kala’s thighbone; slrsam—the head; surekha- angulau—on Surekha’s finger; kesan—the hairs; camara-calika— of the woman who waves a fan; bhuja—of the arms; tate—at the edge; drstim—the glance; priya-uktau—on the beloved’s statement; srutim—the ears; tambula-arpanika—of the woman who offers betelnut; kare—on the hand; kara-putim—joined hands; kasturika- urasi—on Kasturika’s chest; urah—the chest; candra-vaksasi—on Candravali’s chest; prstham—the back; arpayat—while placing; aho—how amazing; nidrati—sleeps (takes rest); nilam—dark blue; mahah—effulgence.

**Перевод:**

**How amazing is the resting of the dark blue effulgence! Each foot is laid on Syama’s lap, the head on Kala’s thigh, the hair in Surekha’s fingers, each eye on the arms of the woman waving the camara, each ear on the beloved’s words, the fingers in the palm of the woman offering betelnut, the chest next to Kasturika’s, and the back on Candravali’s breasts.**

### 5.86

*evaṁ dakṣiṇo ’pi līlā-vaśāt*  
*kadācid dhṛṣṭo ’pi bhavati. tad yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**Even though He is daksina that way, depending on the pastime on occasion He is dhrsta (saucy). For instance:**

*candrāvalīti kapaṭena nigadya rādhāṁ*  
*jātāparādha iva saṅkucitaḥ sakhībhiḥ*  
*santarjito ’pi sa tayā śravaṇotpalena*  
*santāḍito ’pi vijahāsa na saṁvibhāya*

**Перевод:**

**“Hey Candravali!” So trickily addressing Radha, He shrunk as if He had committed a wrong. Although the sakhis rebuked Him and although She chastised Him by a lily on the ear, He laughed without fear.**

### 5.87

*evaṁ kutracic chaṭho ’pi, yathā*

*vaṁśī-kūjita-sūcitātinibhṛtaṁ candrāvalīṁ lambhayan*

**Пословный перевод:**

ekatra—in one place; eva—only; krta-asane—by whom a seat was made; nija-nijaih—with the respective; ali-janaih—friends; kutracit—somewhere; krida-kunja—which was a pleasure grove for pastimes; grha—of the abode; angane—in the courtyard; vyavahitah—hidden; durena—from afar; drstva—after seeing; priye—the two ladyloves; vamsi—of the flute; kujita—by the sounding; sucita—hinted at; atinibhrtam—very concealed; candravalim—Candravali; lambhayan—while causing to attain; sanketam—the secret location; tarasa—with speed; rasat—out of zest; abhisaran—while making love; radham—to Radha; harih patu—may Hari protect; vah—you all.

With zest, He then hurried to the pleasure grove and made love to Radha. May He protect you all.**

### 5.88

*atha vibhāva-prasaṅge nāyakasya sahāyāḥ sakhāyaḥ. evaṁ nāyikāyāḥ sakhyaḥ. tenādau nāyakasya sahāyā ucyante.*

**Перевод:**

**Now, in the context of a discourse on vibhava, the lover’s assistants, who are his friends, and a ladylove’s confidantes will be described. At first, the lover’s friends are detailed:**

*sahāyāḥ syuḥ sahacarās te bhavanti catur-vidhāḥ*  
*sakhāyaś ca priya-sakhās tathā narma-sakhā api*  
*priya-narma-sakhāś cānye teṣu dūtas tridhā mataḥ*  
*nisṛṣṭārtho mitārthaś ca tathā sandeśa-hārakaḥ*  
*dvayor iṅgitam ādāya svayam uttara-dāyakaḥ*  
*suśliṣṭaṁ kurute kāryaṁ nisṛṣṭārthaḥ sa ucyate*  
*pramitaṁ vakti kāryāsya cāntaṁ yāti mitārthakaḥ*  
*yathoktam eva vadati yaḥ sa sandeśa-hārakaḥ (42-45)*

**Перевод:**

**The assistants are the companions. There are four types: sakha (friend), priya-sakha (dear friend), narma-sakha (funny friend) and priya-narma-sakha (dear funny friend).**

**Among them, there are three kinds of messengers: nisrstartha, mitartha, and sandesa-haraka. The nisrstartha messenger is one who understands the signs of the lover and of the ladylove and gives a reply. He nicely accomplishes the task. The mitartha messenger is one who speaks concisely. He also achieves the end of the task (the meeting of the lovers). The sandesa-haraka messenger is one who speaks only in the way he is told to speak.**

*evaṁ dūtyo ’pi yathodāhariṣyante.*

**Перевод:**

**The female messengers are like that too. The varieties will be illustrated later on.**

**Комментарий:**

The theory about the three types of messengers is sourced in Sahitya-darpana. Visvanatha Kaviraja’s list of the lover’s companions is: ceta (servant), vita (cunning companion), and vidusaka (buffon), to which Rupa Gosvami added priya-narma-sakha (Ujjvala-nilamani 2.1). The pithamarda is the lover’s companion, but he does not directly assist the lover in the scope of srngara-rasa (Ujjvala- nilamani 2.10). Rupa Gosvami mentions these three—sakha, priya-sakha, and priya-narma-sakha—in the context of sakhya- rasa (Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu 3.3.21).

### 5.89

*atha nāyakānām ukta-niyata-sāmānya-guṇād atiriktāḥ sattva-jā guṇā ucyante,*

**Перевод:**

**Now the sattvika qualities of a lover which are distinct from the usual ones, mentioned earlier (5.79), are enumerated:**

*śobhā vilāso mādhuryaṁ gāmbhīryaṁ dhairya-tejasī*  
*audāryaṁ lalitaṁ ceti guṇā aṣṭaiva sāttvikāḥ*  
*śauryaṁ dākṣyaṁ ca satyaṁ ca mahotsāho ’nuraktā*  
*ghṛṇā nīce ’dhike śraddhā sā śobhā militocyate (46-47)*

**Перевод:**

**These are eight sattvika qualities: sobha (glory), vilasa (liveliness), madhurya (sweetness), gambhirya (depth of char­acter), dhairya (steadfastness), tejas (influence, fiery energy), audarya (uprightness) and lalita (gallantry).**

**When heroism, cleverness, sincerity, great zeal, complaisance, compassion for lower beings, and trust in socially higher beings combine, that is sobha.**

**Комментарий:**

Henceforth Kavi Karnapura illustrates these eight qualities. The theory about these qualities is sourced in Sahitya-darpana, and is rendered in Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu, but Rupa Gosvami replaced gambhlrya with mangalya (auspiciousness) and used the word sthairya instead of dhairya (2.1.251-252). Gambhlrya (gambhlra) was listed as one of Krsna’s sixty-four qualities (BRS 2.1.114). Sthairya is practically the same as the twenty-third quality: sthira.

Kavi Karnapura added the list in text 5.80. Dhairya and audarya are found there too. Terms have various shades of meaning: The word tejas, which also occurs in the first list (5.79), has two meanings: effulgence and influence: tejo dhama prabhavas cety ucyate dvividham budhaih (BRS 2.1.55). As before, the term sattva, from which the word sattvika is made, has the senses of “pure sattva” (either suddha-sattva, in the case of Krsna, or unadulterated sattva- guna) and “good vibrations” (5.3).

The sattvika qualities are distinct from the sattvika-bhavas. Nonetheless, according to Bhoja, the sattvika-bhavas are so called because they exist in sattva (the mind devoid of both rajas and tamas) and emanate therefrom to delight it: rajas-tamobhyam asprstam manah sattvam ihocyate, nivrtaye ’sya tad-yogat prabhavantlti sattvikah. (Sarasvatl-kanthabharana 5.20)

The sattvika qualities do not exclude rajas and tamas. It is a matter of predominance. In the material rasa and in day-to-day life, this topic, srngara, is in the scope rajo-guna, and a gradation of sattva, rajas, and tamas occurs in that scope. Thus Bhoja says a lover has one of three natures since a lover is primarily influenced by either sattva-guna, rajo-guna or tamo-guna. This is Bhoja’s example of a lover whose nature is mostly rajasika:

*samanta-mauli-mani-ranjita-sasanankam*  
*ekatapatram avaner na tatha prabhutvam*  
*asyah sakhe caranayor adhigamya samyag*  
*ajnakaratvam aham adya yatha krtarthah*

**“My friend, today my life is a success: I attained her feet and became her servant. This is even better than sovereignty over the world, a sovereignty in the form of one kingly parasol whose curved sides are colored by gems which were on the crowns of feudatory kings and represent rulership.” (Sarasvati-kanthabharana 5, illustration 361)**

### 5.90

*yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of sobha (glory):**

*śauryaṁ śatruṣu dākṣyam ātma-kuhake satyaṁ bhuvo dhūḥ-kṣaye*  
*rāgo gokula-madhya-vartiṣu mahotsāho girer dhāraṇe*  
*śraddheyaṁ pitṛ-mātṛ-bandhuṣu hare śobhaiva te sarvathā*  
*nīce mayy aghṛṇeti kevalam asāv ekāṅga-hīnābhavat*

**Перевод:**

**O Hari, You showed heroism in fighting enemies, cleverness in Your tricks, sincerity in upholding Your vow of diminishing the earth’s burden, complaisance to the Gokula residents, great zeal in holding Govardhana, and trust in Your mother, father and relatives. Your sobha takes place in every way, except for one thing: You are not compassionate to me, a lowly being. Therefore Your sobha lacks one aspect.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Kaviraja illustrates each characteristic of sobha separetely. His example of anuragita (complaisance; or popularity) is a verse by Kalidasa:

*aham eva mato mahlpater iti sarvah prakrtisv acintayat*  
*udadher iva nimnaga-satesv abhavan nasya vimanana kvacit*

**“Every one of the king’s subjects reasoned: “He thinks highly of me.” He never disrespected anyone, like the ocean does not disrespect any of the hundreds of rivers.” (Sahitya-darpana 3.51)**

### 5.107

*parakīyeti nāyikādau dvidhā matā*

There are three kinds of svakiya ladyloves: mugdha (innocent), madhya (intermediate), pragalbha (bold). There are an additional six categories since the madhya ladyloves and the pragalbha ladyloves are either dhira (astute in mana), adhira (not astute in mana), or dhiradhira (astute and not astute).**

*madana-madāndhā yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An instance of being blinded by the exhilaration of passion:**

*śliṣṭā śliṣyati gokulendra-tanayena cumbitā cumbati*  
*svacchandaṁ likhitā nakhair nakha-padair ābhūṣayaty aṅgakam*  
*śikṣitvā tata eva puṣpa-dhanuṣaḥ saṁgrāma-vidyām iyaṁ*  
*tasya kṣobha-karī yad aiṣṭa tad iyaṁ vidyā guru-kṣobhikā*

**Пословный перевод:**

slista—embraced; slisyati—she embraces; gokula-indra- tanayena—by the son of the king of Gokula; cumbita—kissed; cumbati—she kisses; svacchandam—at will; likhita—written; nakhaih—with fingernails; nakha-padaih—with scratches (“abodes of fingernails”); abhusayati—adorns; angakam—the body; siksitva—after learning; tatah eva—from that same one; puspa- dhanusah—of Cupid; samgrama—of the battle; vidyam—the science; iyam—she; tasya—of his; ksobha—the trembling; kari— produces; yat—because; aista—she manifested might; tat— therefore; iyam—this; vidya—science; guru—great; ksobhika—is an agitator.

**Перевод:**

**Embraced by the prince of Gokula, she embraces Him. Kissed by Him, she kisses Him. Scratched at will by His nails, she adorns His body with nail marks. Upon learning the science of the battle of Cupid from Him thus, she demonstrates mastery and makes Him tremble. Therefore this science shakes things up.**

**Комментарий:**

An example by Visvanatha Kaviraja:

*dhanyasi ya kathayasi priya-sangame ’pi*  
*visrabdha-catuka-satani ratantaresu*  
*mvim prati pranihite tu kare priyena*  
*sakhyah sapami yadi kincid api smarami*

**“Sakhi, you are fortunate: When you meet your lover, you say hundreds of pleasing intimate words, even during a pause in lovemaking. As for me, I swear I do not remember anything the minute my lover puts his hand on the knot of my girdle.” (SD 3.60)**

### 5.127

*rati-raṇa-kuśalā yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of being expert in the battle of love:**

*anyonya-praṇaya-prakāśa-parayor anyonya-nirmālyayoḥ*  
*śyāmā-mādhavayor nirīkṣya vapuṣor lakṣmīṁ rajanyāḥ kṣaye*  
*sakhyā eva manoja-saṅgara-jaya-śrī-sūcakācāryake*  
*sāmānādhikaraṇyam apratihataṁ mene sakhīnāṁ gaṇaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

anyonya-pranaya—of each other’s love; prakasa—to the manifestation; parayoh—who are dedicated (“whose highest thing”); anyonya-nirmalyayoh—which were each other’s remnants of flower offerings (i.e which had consumed one another: each body was used up); syama-madhavayoh—of Syama and Madhava; nirlksya—after seeing; vapusoh—of the two bodies; laksmlm—the splendor; rajanyah—of night; ksaye—at the end; sakhyah eva—of the same lady friend (Syama); manoja—of Cupid; sangara—battle; jaya—of the triumph; srl—the splendor; sucaka—who hints at; acaryake—in the matter ofbeing a teacher; samanadhikaranyam— the state of being in the same place; apratihatam—unimpaired; mene—thought; sakhlnam—of lady friends; ganah—the group.

**Перевод:**

**At the end of night, the two bodies of Syama and Madhava, who were intent on manifesting their love for one other, became each other’s nirmalya. Observing this resplendence, the sakhis thought that the unimpeded state of being in the same location was such that only the sakhi turned out as the tutor, one who intimates the splendor of triumph in the battle of Eros.**

*iyam eva dara-vrīḍā-bhāvonnatādiḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Only the pragalbha is dara-vrida (a tad bashful), bhavonnata (eminently emotional), and so on.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: In a real war, however, where Krsna and the other fighter do not share an exact same location, only Krsna has the resplendence of triumph (Subodhinl). Here the word nirmalya is used in the technical sense of “the remnants of flowers offered to the deity,” but the resultant sense is that each body completely enjoyed the other. Visvanatha Cakravarti glosses anyonya-nirmalyayoh as paraspara-sambhuktayoh (Subodhinl). Each body is a collection of lotus eyes, lotus face, etc.

Further, Bhoja remarks that the gradation of mugdha, madhya and pragalbha is based on both age and expertise: mugdha madhya pragalbha ca vayasa kausalena ca (Sarasvari-kanihabharana 5.110).

### 5.128

*atha madhyā-pragalbhayor dhīrādi-bheda-kathanam. tatra madhyā dhīrā yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**Now the categories called dhira and so on will be mentioned. At first, the dhira-madhya (astute and intermediate ladylove) is described:**

*prīyaṁ vaidagdhya-vakroktyā madhyā dhīrā vaded ruṣā (71)*

**Перевод:**

**The dhira-madhya talks to her sweetheart by using crooked and witty words, with anger.**

*sā yathā “padminy ahaṁ kumudinī kila saiva satyam” ity-ādi.*

**Перевод:**

**An example of that is verse 3.66.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: The categories called dhira, adhira, and dhiradhira only relate to the ladylove’s expression of mana (pique) (in a conversation with her lover).

### 5.129

*dhīrādhīrā tu ruditaiḥ (72a)*

**Перевод:**

**The dhiradhira-madhya as well talks to her sweetheart by using crooked and witty words, but she weeps.**

### 5.130

*yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of dhiradhira-madhya:**

*utkhātaṁ guru-gauravaṁ kulavatī-rītiś ca niḥsāritā*  
*kṛṣṇa tvat-praṇayeṇa tat katham idaṁ kāpaṭyam ālambase*  
*ity ālapya tadīya-pīta-vasanenāvṛtya vaktrāmbujaṁ*  
*bālā kevalam aśru-miśrita-mukhī cāru-svaraṁ roditi*

**Перевод:**

**“The gravity in being a venerable person was uprooted, and the etiquette of well-mannered girls went out the window. Krsna, with all the love You have, why are You deceitful?” So saying, the girl covered her lotus face with His yellow garment and wept by emitting beautiful sounds.**

### 5.131

*adhīrā niṣṭhuroktibhiḥ (72b)*

**Перевод:**

**The characteristic of the adhira-madhya is that she speaks harsh words.**

### 5.132

*yathā,*  
*sākṣād vartini jīvite mama kathaṁ śaṭhyaṁ tvam ālambase*  
*dhiṅ māṁ tvāṁ ca dhig āvayoḥ sujanatāṁ dhik prema dhik tad-yaśaḥ*  
*kiṁ brūmaḥ puruṣottamo ’si jagatāṁ bhartāsi mayy eva te*  
*dhūrtatvaṁ nahi tena te guṇa-gaṇaḥ kiñcittarāṁ hīyate*

**Перевод:**

**\[One day, Narada arrived to Dvaraka with a parijata flower and gave it to Krsna, who in turn offered it to Rukmini. Narada told this to Satyabhama. She became incensed. Later, Krsna promised that he would bring a whole parijata tree for her. She replied:\]**

**Given that we live together, how dare You behave as a cheat? Fie on You, fie on me, and fie on our good mannerisms. Fie on our love, and fie on its renown too. Shall I remind You that You are Purusottama, the sustainer of the worlds? Your underhand scheme at my expense is not right, so Your good qualities have lost their glamour to some degree.**

*satyabhāmoktiḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**These are the words of Satyabhama.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: The renown is that Krsna is submissive to Satyabhama’s love (Subodhinl).

Similarly, Rupa Gosvami says the characteristics of the dhlra- madhya are crooked words and irony, the characteristic of the adhlra-madhya is harsh words, and the characteristics of the dhiradhira-madhya are crooked words, and tears (Ujjvala-nllamani 5.35-39).

Visvanatha Cakravarti remarks that the dhlradhlra-madhya is partly dhira and partly adhlra therefore she does not have the irony aspect of the dhira nor the harsh aspect of the adhlra, rather a trace of anger culminates as tears, whereas the mugdha ladylove weeps without talking. According to him, the term dhira signifies that the ladylove has dhrti (self-control), meaning she is profound. Sesaraja Sarma, however, says dhira means clever in love: dhira = vidusl, surata-panditeti bhavah (Candrakala-tlka 3.67)

In this matter, Bhoja says ladyloves are divided in an additional set of four categories with regard to the affluence of the pique: uddhata (haughty), udatta (noble-minded), Santa (quiet), and lalita (playful): dhlradhlra tu dhairyena svamyadlya parigrahat, udhanudhopayamanat kramaj jyestha kanlyasl. mana-rddher uddhatodatta santa ca lalita ca sa. (Sarasvatl-kanthabharana 5.111-112)

### 5.133

*atha pragalbhā dhīrādi-lakṣaṇam*

**Перевод:**

**The dhira-pragalbha (self-controlled and bold ladylove) turns away from real anger by hiding it and by displaying indifference to romance. She outwardly shows respect.**

### 5.134

*yathā,*  
*kiṁ pādāntam upaiṣi nāsmi kupitā naivāparāddho bhavān*

**Перевод:**

**Why do You fall at my feet? I’m not angry, nor did You commit an offense. An intelligent person is neither angry nor offensive without a cause. The women who are suitable for You are those who are fit objects for Your enjoyment, and so there is nothing wrong in our being separate. Therefore, O prince of Gokula, You’re free to go.**

*yathā vā,*

**Перевод:**

When I smiled and said something, she softly spoke, somewhat slowly, words that effuse nectar. When I sat on half of the seat, she let me know she felt fortunate. When I gave her a hug, she gave me one too. Her noncontrary mood only revealed her contrary mood.**

**The dhiradhira-pragalbha, however, very much afflicts her lover with many significant remarks (especially sarcastic remarks).**

### 5.144

I talked to her by using soft words, but she lowered the lotus of her face. I touched her, but she trembled. I could not discern whether that slender girl is daksina (compliant) (or straightforward) or vama (prone to be in mana) (or crooked).**

### 5.148

*atha pragalbhā-traividhyam,*

When I smiled and said something, she softly spoke, somewhat slowly, words that effuse nectar. When I sat on half of the seat, she let me know she felt fortunate. When I gave her a hug, she gave me one too. Her noncontrary mood only revealed her contrary mood.**

*atigūḍha-mānatvād iyaṁ pragalbhāgrima-daśā-sthitaiva.*

**Перевод:**

### 5.149

**Перевод:**

**An example of a madhya-pragalbha:**

*no saṅgītakam ālapanti na śukīr adhyāpayanty ālayo*

Scratched at will by His nails, she adorns His body with nail marks. Upon learning the science of the battle of Cupid from Him thus, she demonstrates mastery and makes Him tremble. Therefore this science shakes things up.”**

### 5.150

*athāsām avasthā-bhedenāṣṭa-vidhatvam ucyate. lakṣaṇenaiva saṁjñā gamyā. atha virahotkaṇṭhitādi-kramaḥ,*

**Перевод:**

**Now, eight further subcategories of ladyloves will be described because of the well-known eight states. The names are understood by the definitions. (And the definitions are understood from the names.)**

**Virahotkanthita**

**Перевод:**

**The sequence begins from virahotkanthita (longing in separation):**

*gāḍhānurāgā prāg eva labdha-saṅgāpi haituke*  
*virahe vardhitotkaṇṭhā virahotkaṇṭhitā matā (76)*

**Перевод:**

**The woman whose love is already deep, who met her lover previously in her life, and whose longing has increased given that the separation has a cause is called virahotkanthita.**

*haituka iti mānādi-hetuke, na tu kevale virahe.*

**Перевод:**

**The cause of the separation is mana and so on. There is no mere separation.**

**Комментарий:**

Jiva Gosvami remarks that mana is not in the scope of the state of utkanthita: anagaslti—sagasi tu mana eva bhavati na tutkantheti jnapakam (Locana-rocani 5.79). Visvanatha Cakravarti explains that the virahotkanthita is a separated ladylove whose mana has subsided and who longs for her lover: prathamatah krodhadhma- mana-janya-virahe sati pascat kope sante sati ca kantena saha milanena vardhita utkantha yasyah sa virahotkanthita jneya (Subodhinl).

According to Rupa Gosvami, the eight states of a ladylove are: (1) abhisarika (going to the tryst), (2) vasa-sajja (waiting for her lover at the appointed meeting place), (3) unkanthita (virahotkanthita) (longing for the lover, who hasn’t showed up), (4) khandita (devastated), (5) vipralabdha (separated), (6) kalahantarita (she no longer sustains the quarrel), (7) prosita-bhartrka (or prosita- preyasl) (her lover went away on a trip), and (8) svadhma-bhartrka (she controls her lover) (Ujjvala-nilamani 5.68-69).

The term virahotkanthita, instead of utkanthita, is also used by Visvanatha Kaviraja and Rupa Gosvami. Jiva Gosvami says the terms are synonymous: virahotkanthiteti paryayantaram (Locana-rocanl 5.79).

The difference between these three states—virahotkanthita, vipralabdha, and kalahantarita—are subtle. Kavi Karnapura perfected the methodology: If the separation is not caused by mana, the ladylove is simply called vipralabdha (5.155). The difference between virahotkanthita and kalahantarita is the longing.

### 5.151

*yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of virahotkanthita:**

*antaḥ kṛntati marma murmurayati prāṇān pinaṣṭīva me*  
*daurātmyād yad anādaro ’dya vihitaḥ kṛṣṇe mayā mūḍhayā*  
*taṁ vā saṅgamayasva sundari mayā maj-jīvitaṁ tena vā*  
*dvābhyāṁ nāparam asti kiñcid api me santāpa-nirvāpakam*

**Перевод:**

**The disrespect that I, being very foolish, showed to Krsna due to my bad attitude pinches my heart, burns my vital organs and grinds my life airs. O beautiful confidante, either make me meet Him or make Him meet me. There is no other means to assuage my affliction.**

**Abhisarika**

### 5.152

*saṅketa-sthaṁ priyaṁ jñātvā saha sakhyaikikāthavā*  
*gata-bhīr yābhisarati sā bhaved abhisārikā (77)*

**Перевод:**

**The woman who, knowing that her lover is at the appointed meeting place, fearlessly goes to meet him is the abhisarika ladylove. Either she goes by herself or she is accompanied by a sakhi.**

### 5.153

*yathā,*  
*śyāma tvām abhisartum andha-tamase pādārpaṇa-prakrame*  
*srasto nīla-nicolakas tanu-rucā nirdhūtam andhaṁ tamaḥ*  
*viśvaṁ tāvad ilāvṛtāyitam abhūd gaure ’milad gaurimā*  
*tenālakṣitam ājagama sutanuḥ premṇas tavedaṁ yaśaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Syama, when that slender girl began to place her feet in the dense darkness to go meet You, her blue blouse slackened, the dense darkness was wiped out, and indeed the whole region looked like Ilavrta. The goldenness of her body joined golden Vrndavana, therefore she went unnoticed. Such is the glory of love for You.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: Ilavrta is the land right next to Sumeru, therefore, owing to the golden effulgence of Sumeru, Ilavrta is always yellowish (Subodhim). Sumeru is within Ilavrta: esam madhye ilavrtam namabhyantara-varsam yasya nabhyam avasthitah sarvatah sauvarnah kula-giri-rajo meruh (Bhagavatam 5.16.7). The verse features the samanya ornament (identical) (8.282).

**Khandita**

### 5.154

*anyāsaktena kāntena khaṇḍitāśā tu yā niśi*  
*prātas tad-bhoga-cihnāni vīkṣyodvignā tu khaṇḍitā (78)*

**Перевод:**

**She whose hopes at night are shattered (khandita) because her lover, attracted to another woman, does not show up to the rendezvous and who in the morning is shocked upon seeing on his body the signs of his romance with the other woman is called khandita (devastated).**

*yathā “padminy ahaṁ kumudinī kila saiva” ity-ādi.*

**Перевод:**

**An example is verse 3.66.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: The lover, Sri Krsna, comes back in the morning to try to explain why He did not show up. Upon seeing the signs of His other romance, she becomes manini due to anger. She is the khandita ladylove (Subodhini).

Visvanatha Kaviraja’s example of the khandita is the same as his example of the dhira-madhya ladylove, just as verse 3.66 is also Kavi Karnapura’s example of the dhira-madhya (5.128).

Similarly, Visvanatha Cakravarti says Rupa Gosvami’s example of the khandita also describes the dhrndhira-pragalbha (Ananda- candrika 5.86). Visvanatha Kaviraja’s illustration is a verse by the poet Magha:

*tad avitatham avadir yan mama tvam priyeti*  
*priya-jana-paribhuktam yad dukulam dadhanah*  
*mad-adhivasatim agah kaminam mandana-srir*  
*vrajati hi sa-phalatvam vallabhalokanena*

**“In saying to me “You’re my sweetheart”, you spoke truly, because you have come to my bower dressed in the gown belonging to your inamorata. Verily, by being beheld by the beloved, the beauty of a lover’s ornaments attains its end.” He had left all his trappings behind.**

**Vipralabdha**

### 5.155

*tībhiḥ prārthyamāno ’pi gantāsmīty uktavān api*  
*daivān nāyāti yat-kānto vipralabdheti sā smṛtā (79)*

**Перевод:**

**The vipralabdha is a woman whose lover does not come to the rendezvous, on account of fate, though he was requested by the messengers and though he said “I will go”.**

### 5.156

*yathā,*  
*sumukhi sa kim avādīd eṣa yāmīti tasmāt*  
*katham ajani vilambo mā sma bhūḥ sandihānā*  
*kathaya kim u bhavatyā yāsyate tatra bhūyaḥ*  
*kim atha mad-asubhir vā tulyam etad dvayaṁ me*

**Перевод:**

**“Confidante, did He really say “I’m going?” If so, why is He late?” “Don’t worry. He will come.” “But how can I know for sure? Tell me whether you should go there again to bring Him here or my life force should leave. In my mind, you and my life force are equal.”**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: The implied sense is: “If my life force leaves, due to being unable to withstand the conflagration of separation, then you will miss me and become sorrowful, so it’s better if you leave.”

**Kalahantarita**

### 5.157

*kopenāntaritā yā tu kalahāntaritā tu sā (80)*

**Перевод:**

**The ladylove who is no longer angry is called kalahantarita (she no longer sustains the quarrel).**

### 5.158

*yathā,*  
*asmābhiḥ saha cāṭu-kṛn na gaṇitaḥ pādānato mādhavaḥ*  
*kopo ’yaṁ bahu-mānito na ca vayaṁ prāṇeśvaro nāpy asau*  
*candraś candana-mārutaḥ pika-rutaṁ sambhūya sarvaṁ yadā*  
*tām udvejayitā tadaiṣa sakalaṁ kopaḥ samādhāsyate*

**Перевод:**

**Madhava who is flattering her and who falls at her feet does not count, and neither do we. She only esteems her anger. She neither listens to us nor pay attention to Him, the god of her life. When the moon, the breeze from the Malaya Hills and the cooing of cuckoos will occur at the same time, they will tear her apart. Then her anger will completely subside.**

**Vasaka-sajja**

### 5.159

*vāsa-gehe veśa-bhūṣā-tāmbūla-vasanādibhiḥ*  
*susajjāpekṣate kāntaṁ sā syād vāsaka-sajjikā (81)*

**Перевод:**

**The vasaka-sajjika is a ladylove who, expecting her lover to arrive at her domicile, is nicely ready there with attire, jewelry, betel nut, dress, and so on.**

**Комментарий:**

The suffix ka is added after the word vasa (residence) in the sense of alpa (small): alpe (Astadhyayi 5.3.85). By the etymology, the vasaka-sajjika is a ladylove who equips (adorns) her small domicile (bedroom). This implies that she is embellished too, according to Rupa Gosvami. By the etymology, the vasaka-sajja adheres to her small domicile. There is a difference of suffixes. The verbal root is sanj sange (to adhere): It is causative in the first instance (to cause to adhere means to equip): sva-vasaka-vasatkante samesyati nijam vapuh \| sajjl-karoti geham ca ya sa vasaka-sajjika \|\| (Ujjvala-nilamani 5.76). The causative form of the verbal root sanj means to equip: sajjayaty api sannahe (Prayuktakhyata-manjarl 2.3.21).

### 5.160

*yathā,*  
*tāmbūla-mālya-vasanābharaṇānulepāḥ*  
*sampāditās tava kṛte svayam etayā ye*  
*te hy eva tāṁ tvayi vilambini tat-kṣaṇena*  
*santāpayanti vitudanti vimohayanti*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, for Your sake she put a betel nut in her mouth, placed a garland on her neck, donned a dress, and put on ornaments and make-up. But now that You are delaying, the betel nut, the garland, the dress, the ornaments and the make-up afflict, puncture, and confound her.**

**Prosita-bhartrka**

### 5.161

*kāryāntareṇa pravāsaṁ gate sati mano-’dhipe*  
*tan-manaskaiva yā tiṣṭhet sā syāt proṣita-bhartṛkā (82)*

**Перевод:**

**The woman who only thinks of the man of her heart when he has gone far away because of duty is called prosita-bhartrka.**

**Комментарий:**

This category corresponds to pravasa-vipralambha (5.77).

### 5.162

*yathā,*  
*na vāṇī na spando na ca nayana-paṅkeja-laharī*  
*na vīṇāder gāna-śrutir api na cālī-jana-kathā*  
*kurūn yāte kṛṣṇe puri puri mahiṣyaḥ samabhavan*  
*paṭe citrotkīrṇā iva viraha-vaidhurya-tanavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**There was no utterance and no movement. There were no waves from lotus eyes. A lute was never heard. And all their friends stopped talking. When Krsna went to the land of the Kurus to see the Pandavas, the queens in the palaces became inert: They looked like figures etched in a bas-relief. They became emaciated due to the misery of separation.**

**Svadhina-bhartrka**

### 5.163

*ntaraṁ prema-vaśāt pārśva-vartīva yat-priyaḥ*  
*vāg-vaśaḥ prāya ābhāti sā syāt svādhīna-bhartṛkā (83)*

**Перевод:**

**The svadhma-bhartrka is a woman whose lover is under the control of her love and, being mindful of what she says, is as if always at her side.**

### 5.164

*yathā,*  
*iyaṁ mama sakhī priyā racaya veśam asyāḥ svayaṁ*  
*prasādaya sakhīm imāṁ mayi vṛthaiva jāta-krudham*  
*iti praṇaya-kautukād iva niyojito rādhayā*  
*cakāra rasikāgraṇīr atha tathā tathā mādhavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**“This is My dear friend. Fix her dress. Soothe this other friend: She’s angry at Me for no reason.” Thus given tasks by Radha as if because of the conviviality of intimate love, Madhava, the topmost rasika, did as He was told.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Kaviraja’s example of the svadhma-bhartrka is the same as his illustration of the anukula type of lover (5.83):

*asmakam sakhi vasasi na rucire graiveyakam nojjvalam*  
*no vakra gatir uddhatam na hasitam naivasti kascin madah*  
*kintv anye ’pi jana vadanti subhago ’py asyah priyo nanyato*  
*drstim niksipatiti visvam iyata manyamahe duhsthitam*

**“Sakhi, my clothes are not lively, the ornamental lines on my neck are not exquisite, my gait is not undulant, my laughter is not high, and I have no overweening pride, yet people say: “This woman’s lover is a gentleman: He never casts a glance at another woman,” so I think that everybody else is not as fortunate as I.” (Srngara- tilaka 1.25) (Sahitya-darpana 3.37; 3.74)**

### 5.165

*athāsām alaṅkārāḥ,*

**Перевод:**

**Now the emotional ornaments of the ladyloves will be described:**

*yauvane sattvajās tāsām aṣṭā-viṁśati-saṅkhyakāḥ*  
*alaṅkārās tatra bhāva-hāva-helās trayo ’ṅgajāḥ*  
*śobhā kāntiś ca dīptiś ca mādhuryaṁ ca pragalbhatā*  
*audāryaṁ dhairyam ity ete saptaiva syur ayatnajāḥ*  
*līlā vilāso vicchittir vivvokaḥ kila-kiñcitam*  
*moṭṭāyitaṁ kuṭṭamitaṁ vibhramo lalitaṁ madaḥ*  
*vikṛtaṁ tapanaṁ maugdhyaṁ vikṣepaś ca kutūhalam*  
*hasitaṁ cakitaṁ kelir anubhāvād ime pṛthak (84-87)*

**Перевод:**

**In youth, ladyloves have twenty-eight emotional ornaments, which arise from sattva. Among them, these three: 1. bhava (feeling) (first development of rati), 2. hava (allurement) (rati is more apparent) and 3. hela (coquetry) (rati is obvious), relate to body parts (especially eyes, brows, and neck), and these seven: 4. sobha (loveliness), 5. kanti (splendor), 6. dipti (radiance), 7. madhurya (sweetness), 8. pragalbhata (boldness), 9. audarya (uprightness) and 10. dhairya (steadfastness), arise spontaneously. The other alankaras are: 11. lila (imitating manneurisms etc.), 12. vilasa (charming demeanor), 13. vicchitti (amazingness of the outfit), 14. vivvoka (disregard for a desired thing), 15. kilakincita (hysterical delight), 16. mottayita (indication of longing), 17. kuttamita (fake repulse), 18. vibhrama (fluster), 19. lalita (elegance of movement), 20. mada (overweening pride), 21. vikrta (implying by a gesture), 22. tapana (pining), 23. maugdhya (feigned ignorance), 24. viksepa (distractedness), 25. kutuhala (ardent curiosity), 26. hasita (chuckle), 27. cakita (trepidation), and 28. keli (sportiveness). They are distinct from anubhavas (physical reactions).**

*yadyapy eṣu kecid anubhāva-sadṛśāḥ santi, tathāpi pṛthak. te tu rasābhivyañjakāḥ, ete tu rasābhivyañjakatve ’pi svataḥ samarthāḥ, tenālaṅkārā eva.*

**Перевод:**

**Although some of them resemble anubhavas, they are distinct: The anubhavas bring out the rasa, but these ones are able to bring out the rasa by themselves, therefore they are alankaras (“They adorn \[the rasa\]”).**

**Комментарий:**

Here also the term sattva has the two meanings of good vibrations, i.e. “the mind overcome by moods arisen from Krsna’s actions,” and suddha-sattva, in the case of Krsna’s ladyloves, or sattva-guna as regards the material srngara.

Kavi Karnapura follows Visvanatha Kaviraja (Sahitya-darpana 3.92), whereas Rupa Gosvami lists twenty main alankaras (Ujjvala- nilamani 11.2)—in conformity with Bharata Muni (Natya-sastra 22.5-13) and Singabhupala—in addition to Visvanatha’s maugdhya and cakita (Ujjvala-nilamani 11.64). Rupa Gosvami left out mada, tapana, viksepa, kutuhala, hasita, and keli. Some of the eight additional ornaments were introduced in the theory by Bhoja.

Visvanatha Kaviraja remarks that the first ten alankaras can also occur in a lover: purve bhavadayo dhairyanta dasa nayakanam api sambhavanti (Sahitya-darpana 3.93). Earlier, Kavi Karnapura mentioned these as qualities of a lover: kanti (5.80), dhairya, audarya (5.80; 5.89), sobha, madhurya, and lalita (5.89). On occasion, the other alankaras can apply to the lover, according to Rupa Gosvami.

Rupa Gosvami says the alankaras are anubhavas, which also include udbhasvaras (external transformations). In Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu, he says the anubhavas are mostly udbhasvaras. Visvanatha Kaviraja says an anubhava is an external transformation.

Rupa Gosvami referred to this definition: anubhavo bhava- bodhakah, “An anubhava is that which makes others understand the emotion in the person’s heart” (Amara-kosa 1.7.21). Nagesa Bhatta writes: anubhavayanti, sthayi-bhavam sucayanti, “An anubhava hints at the sthayi-bhava” (Uddyota 4.28).

Similarly, Kavi Karnapura said vibhava is the cause of anubhava (5.2). Later he says an anubhava is an effect of the sthayi-bhava (5.256). In addition, sometimes an anubhava is an effect of a vyabhicari. In poetics, often the word anubhava is a technical term for “effect”.

The bhava alankara is not an anubhava (external transformation). In his commentary on Alankara-kaustubha, Visvanatha Cakravarti paraphrases Kavi Kamapura’s opinion, but in his commentary on Ujjvala-nilamani he only says Kavi Karnapura distinguishes bhava from anubhavas: alankara-kaustubha-krdbhis tv anubhavad idam evaprthag iti laksitam (Ananda-candrika 11.6). Bhoja says the alankaras are anubhavas in the sense that they occur afterward (anu = pascat) (after seeing a vibhava, 5.1), but he implicitly excludes bhava. Ahead, Kavi Karnapura says some alankaras can be classed as anubhavas (5.256).

The alankaras of srngara-rasa relate to the characters themselves, but they are not in the category of kavya alankara (poetical ornament) (chapters 7 and 8). An emotional alankara can involve vibhavas, anubhava and vyabhicari, considering that a vyabhicari can be implied by its effect.

**1.   Bhava**

### 5.166

*tatraiṣāṁ lakṣaṇam bhāvo yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**They are defined as follows.**  
**This is the definition of bhava:**

*nirvikārātmake citte bhāvaḥ prathama-vikriyā*  
*ālambanoddīpanottha-bhāvād api sa ca dvidhā (88)*

**Перевод:**

**The first change in a mind that had been changelessness by nature is called bhava (feeling) (5.10). There are two kinds: Bhava arises either from an alambana (Krsna, the object of the love) or from an uddpana (excitant).**

**Комментарий:**

The bhava alankara is distinct from the sthayi-bhava (rati), but the definitions are the same: vikaro manaso bhavah, “Bhava is a transformation of the heart” (Amara-kosa 1.7.21). Jiva Gosvami gives the derivation of the word bhava (feeling) in bhava alankara in the instrumental voice, from the root bhu sattayam (to exist): kintv atra bhavyate vyajyate ’neneti karane ghan, “In this context, bhava is that by means of which \[the rati\] is made to exist, i.e. is revealed” (Locana-rocam 11.6). Or else this word bhava is formed by adding the suffix ghan after the verbal root bhu avakalpane (to think) in the passive impersonal voice (“thinking” i.e. “feeling”).

The word bhava (permanent mood) which means sthayi-bhava is derived as “It makes one think \[about things\],” from the root bhu avakalpane: bhavah, pum, bhavayati cintayati padarthan iti. bhu + nic + pac-ady ac (Sabda-kalpadruma).

### 5.167

*tatrālambanottho yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of bhava arisen from an alambana:**

*ā-dhūli-keli śataśaḥ saha yena yeyaṁ*  
*prāgalbhya-cāru suciraṁ kalahāyate sma*  
*taṁ śyāmasundaram apūrvaṁ ivekṣamāṇā*  
*sā gaṇḍayoḥ pulaka-maṇḍalikāṁ tanoti*

**Перевод:**

**Looking at Him as if She had never seen Him, the same Syamasundara with whom She had pretended to quarrel on hundreds of occasions in bold and beautiful ways for a long time as in the game of throwing powders at one another in childhood, She unintentionally caused Her cheeks to become adorned with goosebumps.**

### 5.168

*uddīpanottho yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of bhava arisen from uddipanas:**

*etāni tāni nalinī-vipināni vāpyām*  
*ete ta eva madhupā nalinānaneṣu*  
*ā-bālyam eva kalitāni kim adya rādhā*  
*naivāvakarṣati vilocanam eṣu lagnam*

**Перевод:**

**These are the same clusters of lotuses in the pond and these are the same bees on the faces of lotus flowers that She has always seen from childhood, so now why can Radha not take away Her gaze which is fixed on these?**

**Комментарий:**

The bees are the darts of Krsna’s glances, and a lotus represents a gopl. This is Visvanatha Kaviraja’s example of bhava:

*sa eva surabhih kalah sa eva malayanilah*  
*saiveyam abala kintu mano ’nyad iva drsyate*

**“This is the same springtime as before, this is the same breeze from the Malaya Hills, and she is the same girl that she was, yet it’s as if she has a different mind.” (Sahitya-darpana 3.93)**

Verse 5.168 can also be analyzed as an implied atisayokti ornament of the second variety (8.116), whereas Visvanatha’s verse follows the scheme of the utpreksa ornament (8.58).

**2.   Hava**

### 5.169

*hṛn-netrādi-vikārais tu vyakto ’sau yāti hāvatām (89)*  
*asau bhāvaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**When the bhava is revealed by changes in the heart, in the eyes, and so forth, the bhava becomes hava (allurement).**

**Комментарий:**

This word hava is formed by irregularly applying samprasarana after the verbal root hve\[n\] sabde (to call) and by adding the suffix ghan in the instrumental voice. Thus hava is “that by means of which there is calling (alluring).”

### 5.170

*lolena kiñcid alasena ca kiñcid akṣṇā*  
*sā yad vibheda hṛdayaṁ vraja-rāja-sūnoḥ*  
*tasyās tadaiva hṛdayena samaṁ tad-antas*  
*tenādhvanaiva nu viveśa navānurāgaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**With eyes partly fickle and partly indolent, She pierced the heart of the prince of Vraja. Right then Her new love for Him entered His soul by the same path along with Her heart.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Kaviraja’s example is a verse by Kalidasa:

*vivrnvati saila-suta bhavam angaih*  
*sphurad-bala-kadamba-kalpaih*  
*saci-krta carutarena tasthau*  
*mukhena paryasta-vilocanena*

**“While the hairs on her skin which were erect like the filaments of young kadamba blossoms betrayed her feeling, Parvati, becoming crooked, held a pose with her prettier face turned sideways and glanced here and there.” (Kumara-sambhava 3.68) (Sahitya- darpana 3.94)**

**3.   Hela**

### 5.171

*helā sa evābhilakṣya-vikāraḥ parikīrtyate (90)*  
*sa eva hāva eva*

**Перевод:**

**When the changes caused by hava can be perceived, that is called hela (coquetry).**

**Комментарий:**

This term hela is made from the verbal root hil bhava-karane (to express amorous desire): hela, stri. hil + ghan, tap. strmam srngara-bhavaja-kriya-visesah (Sabda-kalpadruma). However, the fourth type of namabhasa called helana (hela) is made from the verbal root hed\[r\] anadare (to disrespect): The letter d changes to l, since those two letters are interchangeable: hela, hed bhave, dasya lah (Apte). In the context of srngara-rasa, disrespect constitutes the ornament called vivvoka (5.196).

### 5.172

*yathā,*  
*ekam apy atiraho ’pi tam ekā-*  
*py utsukāpi sakhi nāham apaśyam*  
*komalaṁ kuvalayād api hanyāt*  
*sāhasena katamena kaṭākṣaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Although it was a solitary place, although He was alone and although I was by myself, I did not look at Him even though I wanted to. Sakhi, He is even softer than a lotus. My killer glance would have hurt Him.**

**Комментарий:**

An example by Visvanatha Kaviraja:

*taha te jhatti pautta bahue savyanga-bibbhama saala*  
*samsa-i-amuddha-bhava hoi ciram ja-i sahinam pi (Prakrit language)*

*tatha tasya jhatiti pravrtta vadhvah sarvanga-vibhramah sakalah*  
*samsayita-mugdha-bhava bhavanti ciram yatha sakhinam api (Sanskrit ren*

“All the limbs of that young woman quickly developed a well- rounded flirtatious style, and for a while her sakhls wondered whether she was still a mugdha.” (Sahitya-darpana 3.95)

**4.   Sobha**

### 5.173

*helaiva śobhā lāvaṇya-rūpa-veśādibhir yutā (91)*

**Перевод:**

**When hela is endowed with glistening beauty, a lovely physique, an attire, and so on, it is called sobha (loveliness).**

### 5.174

*yathā,*  
*veśo navaḥ pratinavaṁ ca vayo navīnaṁ*  
*lāvaṇyakaṁ madhurimā ’pi navīna eva*  
*kṛṣṇānurāga-sarasī-satatāvagāhe*  
*tasyā babhūvur atidhauta-nirāvilāni*

**Перевод:**

**Her dress is new, Her age is ever youthful, Her glistening beauty is novel, and so is Her sweetness. When She continuously plunged in the lake of love for Krsna, they took on a sheen and lost their lackluster.**

**Комментарий:**

Rupa Gosvami copied Visvanatha Kaviraja’s definition: rupa- yauvana-lalitya-bhogadyair anga-bhusanam, sobha prokta, “Sobha is the grace of the limbs derived from beauty, youthfulness, elegance, sensuality and the like” (SD 3.96). Of these, Visvanatha illustrates the loveliness of youthfulness with a verse by Kalidasa:

*asambhrtam mandanam anga-yaster*  
*anasavakhyam karanam madasya*  
*kamasya puspa-vyatiriktam astram*  
*balyat param satha vayah prapede*

**“She thus passed the years of innocence and came of age. Youth became a natural adornment of her creeper-like body, an alcohol-like means of elation yet with a different name, and a weapon exceeding the power of Cupid’s flower arrows.” (Kumara-sambhava 1.31)**

**5.   Kanti**

### 5.175

*śobhaiva manmathonmāthāt kāntir uddīpita-dyutiḥ (92)*

**Перевод:**

**When sobha’s dazzle is kindled by Cupid’s churning, it is called kanti (splendor).**

### 5.176

*yathā,*  
*ko veda re sakhi lagiṣyati dṛṣṭa eva*  
*ko veda jīvam apaneṣyati lagna eva*  
*preṅkholibhiḥ parimalaiḥ sahasāndhayāsau*  
*śyāmo rasaḥ paricito vada ko ’parādhaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Who knew that He adheres to the eyes upon being seen? And who knew that He takes away one’s vitality upon sticking to the eyes? Blinded by force by His all-pervading aromas, I amassed Syama-rasa. So tell me, sakhi, what is wrong in doing that?**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Kaviraja’s example of kanti is the same as his example of the madhya ladylove:

*netre khanjana-ganjane sarasija-pratyarthi pani-dvayam*  
*vaksojau kari-kumbha-vibhrama-karim atyunnatim gacchatah*  
*kantih kancana-campaka-pratinidhir vani sudha-syandini*  
*smerendivara-dama-sodara-vapus tasyah kataksa-cchata*

**“Her eyes put wagtail birds to shame. Her hands rival lotuses. Her breasts have achieved a height which gives the impression that they are the temples of a ruttish elephant. Her splendor resembles what the splendor of a campaka flower turned golden would look like. Her words effuse nectar. And the series of her sidelong glances is akin to a garland of open lotuses.” (Sahitya-darpana 3.59; 3.96)**

**6.   Dipti**

### 5.177

*kāntir evātivistīrṇā dīptir ity ucyate budhaiḥ (93)*

**Перевод:**

**When kanti is greatly increased, the learned call that dipti (radiance).**

### 5.178

*yathā,*  
*dhautāśrubhiḥ prasava eva kaṭākṣa-bhūmir*  
*ucchvāsa eva kuca-ratna-khaniḥ prataptā*  
*bālaṁ vayas tad anurāga-bhara-kṣamatvam*  
*adhyāpya kena guṇinaivam akāri rādhe*

**Перевод:**

**\[Paurnamasi speaks:\] Radha, right at the time of casting Your sidelong glances, Your eyes become lubricated by tears. And only when You breathe, the two knobs of Your treasure chest are as if complaining. Your childish age gave instructions on becoming competent in love because of which meritorious man?**

**Комментарий:**

However, Rupa Gosvami gives a similar verse to illustrate hela (Ujjvala-nilamani 11.12). Visvanatha Kaviraja says his example is from his play called Candrakala:

*tarunyasya vilasah*  
*samadhika-lavanya-sampado hasah*  
*dharani-talasyabharanam*  
*yuva-jana-manaso vasi-karanam*

**“She is the play of youthfulness, the laughter of much superior beauty, the ornament of the earth, and the subjugation of the minds of young men.” (Sahitya-darpana 3.96)**

Visvanatha Kaviraja shows the same verse to illustrate his hetu ornament (cause, i.e. a cause is expressed in terms of being identical with its effect) (Sahitya-darpana 10.63): The words “She is the subjugation of the minds of young men” mean she is the cause of the subjugation of their minds. The three other clauses are metaphors in English, but are virodha ornaments in Sanskrit (8.168), because in Sanskrit the metaphor must be based on a well- known standard of comparison.

**7.   Madhurya**

### 5.179

*sarvāsasthā-viśeṣeṣu mādhuryam ramanīyatā (94)*

**Перевод:**

**Being delightful in any situation is called madhurya (sweetness).**

### 5.180

*yathā,*  
*jalāvagāhe cyuta-mekhalāyāḥ*  
*śaivāla-vallyaiva babhau nitambaḥ*  
*akaitavaṁ rūpam ahetu-hārdaṁ*  
*sarvāsv avasthāsu sadaika-rūpam*

**Перевод:**

**The hips of that woman whose girdle fell while she plunged in the water was resplendent with only a creeper of moss. Beauty which is for real is heart-ravishing for no other reason and always has the same form in every circumstance.**

**Комментарий:**

The verse features the arthantara-nyasa ornament (corroboration) (8.165). Visvanatha Kaviraja shows a verse by Kalidasa describing Parvati’s dress in her practice of austerities:

*sarasijam anuviddham savalenapi ramyam*  
*malinam api himamsor laksma laksmim tanoti*  
*iyam adhika-manojna balkalenapi tanvi*  
*kim iva hi madhuranam mandanam nakrtlnam*

**“A lotus is lovely even when laced with algae. Even the dark spot on the moon adds charm. This slender woman is even more beautiful by being clad in bark. Indeed, for those who have elegant bodies, what does not serve as an ornament?” (Abhijnana-sakuntala 1.18)**

Rupa Gosvami, however, says madhurya means the gestures are beautiful: madhuryam nama cestanam sarvavasthasu caruta (Ujjvala-nilamani 11.19). This is in conformity with Singabhupala, who says madhurya means the gestures are tender: madhuryam nama cestanam sarvavasthasu mardavam (Rasarnava-sudhakara 1.197). Bharata Muni says madhurya signifies that the gestures are not disproportionate (neither excessive nor insufficient): sarvavastha-visesesu diptesu lalitesu ca, anulbanatvam cestaya madhuryam iti samjnitam. (Natya-sastra 22.29)

**8.   Pragalbhata**

### 5.181

*pragalbhatā nirbhayatvam (95a)*

**Перевод:**

**Pragalbhata (boldness) means being fearless.**

*yathā “śliṣṭā śliṣyati” ity-ādi.*

**Перевод:**

**An example is verse 5.126.**

**Комментарий:**

Kavi Karnapura referred to that verse as an example of the antima-pragalbha (bold ladylove in the highest stage) (5.149). It is based on Visvanatha Kaviraja’s illustration of pragalbhata. In conformity with Bharata Muni and Singabhupala, Rupa Gosvami says pragalbhata means being fearless in love games: atha pragalbhata—nihsankatvam prayogesu budhair ukta pragalbhata (Ujjvala-nilamani 11.21).

The gradation of alankaras, especially with regard to the categories of ladyloves, ends here. The sequence in Natya-sastra is: madhurya, dhairya, pragalbhya, and audarya (22.26).

**9.   Audarya**

### 5.182

*audāryaṁ vinayaḥ sadā (95b)*

**Перевод:**

**Audarya (uprightness) means having a sincerely good disposition at all times.**

### 5.183

*yathā,*  
*sakhyo nijair eva guṇair bhavad-vidhā*  
*mayy eva tanvanty anurāga-saurabham*  
*na cānya-sādguṇyam apekṣya sauhṛdaṁ*  
*prakāśayantīha nisarga-sādhavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Sakhis, with your kind of qualities, girls of your type sustain the fragrance of love in me. Persons who are good by nature show goodheartedness without expecting others to have good qualities.**

**10.   Dhairya**

### 5.184

*sukhe duḥkhe ’pi mahati dhairyaṁ syān nirvikāratā (96)*

**Перевод:**

**Dhairya (steadfastness of the heart) means being even-minded in happiness and remaining unchanged even in great sorrow.**

### 5.185

*yathā,*  
*āstāṁ tadīya-nava-yauvana-pūrṇa-vāpī*  
*kāpīyam atra na karomi nimajjanecchām*  
*icchāmi taṁ kam api kālam alajjam uccair*  
*ākrandituṁ sumukhi hā priya hā priyeti*

**Перевод:**

**Beautiful confidante, His ever fresh youthfulness is some incredible lake filled to the brim. I don’t wish to plunge in it. I simply wish for some particular time when I will unreservedly exclaim with loud weeping “Ah sweetheart, ah sweetheart”.**

**Комментарий:**

The dhairya alankara is a twist on the vyabhicari-bhava called dhairya (or dhrti, steadfastness) (5.262) (Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu 2.4.144). Rupa Gosvami follows Singabhupala’s opinion that the dhairya alankara is the constant elevatedness of the heart: sthira cittonnatir ya tu tad dhairyam iti kirtyate (Ujjvala-nilamani 11.26). Similarly, Visvanatha Kaviraja says it is the firmness of mind-set which does not involve boasting: muktatma-slaghana dhairyam manovrttir acancala (Sahitya-darpana 3.98). This follows Bharata Muni’s definition.

Visvanatha’s example is a verse by Bhavabhuti:

*jvalatu gagane ratrau ratrav akhanda-kalah sasi*  
*dahatu madanah kim va mrtyoh parena vidhasyati*  
*mama tu dayitah slaghyas tato janany amalanvaya*  
*kulam amalinam na tv evayam jano na ca jivitam*

**\[Malati speaks to her friend Lavangika:\] “Let the full moon burn lonely women every night. Let Cupid scorch me: What can he possibly do after my death? My father is dear to all and is praiseworthy; my mother comes from a pure lineage; even my extended family is taintless. But not I. Nor is life. (I won’t keep on living if I have to marry someone other than the man I love.)” (Malati-madhava 2.2)**

**11.  Lila**

### 5.186

*aṅgair veśair alaṅkārair līlā kāntānukāritā (97)*

**Перевод:**

**Lila (imitating manneurisms etc.) is the imitation of the lover by means of supplementary articles, of attires, and of adornments.**

*sā ca dvidhā, sva-gatā sakhī-gatā ca. sva-gatā ca dvidhā, svakartṛkā priya-kartṛkā ceti.*

**Перевод:**

**Lila has two varieties: The imitator is either oneself or a sakhi. The first variety has two categories: The imitation is done either by the ladylove or by her lover.**

### 5.187

*krameṇodāharaṇe,*  
*barheṇa baddha-cikurā kara-klṛpta-veṇur*  
*āmucya pīta-vasanaṁ vana-mālikāṁ ca*  
*kastūrikācita-tanū rabhasād iyeṣa*  
*rādhā svam aṅgam upagūhitum aṅgakena*

**Перевод:**

**She bound Her topknot with a peacock’s tail feather, held the flute in Her hand, donned a yellowish outfit, wore a garland of sylvan flowers, and covered Her body with musk. Out of merriment, Radha sought to conceal Her limbs \[from the sakhis\] by means of these articles.**

**Комментарий:**

The dual sense of the words iyesa radha svam angam upaguhitum angakena (Radha sought to conceal Her limbs by means of these articles) is: “She wanted to embrace Her limbs with Her limbs.”

### 5.188

*kāñcit sakhīṁ kuvalayodara-sodarāṅgīṁ*  
*kṛṣṇākṛtiṁ samupakalpya vibhūṣaṇādyaiḥ*  
*āliṅgitaṁ kṛta-matiḥ svayam eva rādhā*  
*dvedhā vibhaktam upalabdhavatī pramodam*

**Перевод:**

**Some sakhi resembled the color of a blue lotus. Radha made up Her mind: She herself turned her friend into Krsna’s character by using adornments. In that way Her pleasure of embracing doubled.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: She felt joy in embracing Her friend and thereby also felt the joy of embracing Krsna.

### 5.189

*sva-gata-priya-kartṛkā yathā,*  
*sīmanta-cāru dayitasya babandha veṇīṁ*  
*rādhā śikhaṇḍa-valayaiḥ sa ca maulim asyāḥ*  
*anyonya-veśa-parivartana-kauśalena*  
*dvābhyām alabhyata viśeṣa-rateḥ pramodaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Radha braided His hair after drawing a beautiful line of separation, and He fashioned a crest for Her with a peacock’s tail feather and with other oval decorations. By the expertise of switching their attires, They achieved the joy of unique amorous pleasure.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: Radha, thinking She was Krsna, felt high- flown like Krsna is. And Krsna, thinking He was Radha, exhibited the mood of being adverse and thus developed the quality of being hard to get (Subodhini). The imitation of the ladylove by the lover is Kavi Karnapura’s innovation in poetic theory.

**12.   Vilasa**

### 5.190

*yāna-sthānāsanādīnāṁ mukha-netrādi-karmaṇām*  
*viśeṣo dayitāloke vilāsaḥ parikīrtyate (98)*

**Перевод:**

**When the lover is seen, the special movement or pose of the face, of the eyes, and so on, or a peculiarity in sitting is called vilasa (charming demeanor).**

### 5.191

*yathā,*  
*kaiścic cāmara-pāṇibhiḥ katipayais tāmbūla-pātrī-karaiḥ*  
*kaiścic cāsana-dhāribhiḥ parijanair dhṛtātapatraiḥ paraiḥ*  
*saṁvītā maṇi-yānato ’varuruhuḥ śrīśe nikhātekṣaṇā*  
*yoṣin-mauli-maṇī-varā iva kurukṣetraṁ sametyāṅganāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing Krsna from afar, the queens, who had arrived in Kuruksetra, alighted from their jewel-studded chariots and fixed their gaze on Him. Those crest-jewel of women were surrounded by their entourage: Some servants whisked camara fans, others held caskets containing betel nuts, some carried cushions for sitting, and yet others held parasols.**

### 5.192

*yathā vā,*  
*sakhyaikayā mūrdhni dhṛtāṁśukāñcalā*  
*saṁvījyamānā dala-mālayānyayā*  
*avekṣamāṇā dayitaṁ vidūrataś*  
*cinoti mandaṁ kusumāni rādhikā*

**Перевод:**

**When Radhika spotted Her beloved at a distance, one sakhi held the edge of her sari above Her face, another cooled Her with a portion of a garland shaped into a hand fan, and She innocently picked flowers.**

### 5.193

*kecit tu yānaṁ gatiḥ, sthānaṁ sthitiḥ, āsanam upaveśaḥ. tan-mate yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**Some scholars, however, say that in the definition yana means gati (going), sthana means sthiti (standing, posture), and asana means upavesa (sitting). This is an example:**

*sthitir mada-bharālasā na garimāṇam ālambate*  
*gatiḥ prakṛti-mantharā tvarata īṣad eva kramāt*  
*sa-līlam avalokitaṁ namati vaṅkate śaṅkate*  
*svabhāva iva laṅghitaḥ priya-samīpato rādhayā*

**Перевод:**

**In Her sweetheart’s presence, Radha as if transgresses Her nature: Her posture is informal due to the weight of her excitement, She does not have a heavy mood, Her gait becomes naturally slow, and She hurries a little, in sequence. Her playful glance bows, wanders, and hesitates.**

**13.  Vicchitti**

### 5.194

*stokāpy ākalpa-racanā vicchittiḥ kānti-poṣa-kṛt (99)*

**Перевод:**

**Fashioning an accessory, or simply putting one on, which enhances the splendor is called vicchitti (amazingness of the outfit). (Sahitya-darpana 3.100)**

### 5.195

*yathā,*  
*dvi-trāṇi pāṇyor maṇi-kaṅkaṇāni*  
*kṛtvā parityakta-samasta-bhūṣā*  
*ekaṁ dadhe vakṣasi nīla-ratnaṁ*  
*tenaiva rādhā nitarāṁ vireje*

**Перевод:**

**Setting aside all other embellishments, Radha placed two or three bracelets on each wrist and wore a sapphire on Her chest. She looked dazzling that way.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Kaviraja’s example is a verse by Magha:

*svacchambhah-snapana-vidhautam angam*  
*osthas tambula-dyuti-visado vilasininam*  
*vasas ca pratanu viviktam astv itiyan*  
*akalpo yadi kusumesuna na sunyah*

**“The limbs rendered immaculate by a shower, the nether lip glossed with the sheen of betel nut, and a gown thin and elegant—let only these be the adornments of amorous women, unless the man is not possessed by the flower archer.” (Sisupala-vadha 8.70)**

Moreover, Rupa Gosvami says this alankara can apply to Krsna (Ujjvala-nilamani 11.36).

**14.   Vivvoka**

### 5.196

*garveṇa vastunīṣṭe ’pi vivvokaḥ syād anādaraḥ (100)*

**Перевод:**

**Vivvoka means being indifferent, on account of overweening pride, to a desired thing.**

**Комментарий:**

The term vivvoka, also written bibboka and vibboka, is a Prakrit loanword.

### 5.197

*yathā,*  
*saurabhya-hānir vapuṣo ’nulepanaiḥ*  
*saundarya-hrāso maṇi-bhūṣaṇair iti*  
*anādarā teṣv api tāni sakhyāḥ*  
*premoparodhena babhāra rādhā*

**Перевод:**

**Her bodily fragrance is lessened by the scent of cosmetics and Her natural beauty is diminished by jewel-studded ornaments, therefore Radha has no regard for them. Still, She wore them to reciprocate Her sakhis’ affection.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: The sakhis only had in mind to conform to worldly norms: People think “If we don’t wear ornaments, we look poor.”

### 5.198

*yathā vā,*  
*kṛṣṇena harṣād upaḍhaukitāni*  
*nirmāya puṣpābharaṇāni yāni*  
*uccair abhīṣṭāny api tāni rādhā*  
*naicchad gabhīra-praṇaya-smayena*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna designed floral decorations and joyfully presented them to Her, but although they were highly desirable She didn’t care for them due to the vanity of Her deep love.**

**15.   Kila-kincita**

### 5.199

*amarṣa-hāsa-vitrāsa-śuṣka-rodana-bhartsanaiḥ*  
*niṣedhaiś ca ratārambhe kila-kiñcitam iṣyate (101)*

**Перевод:**

**The mix of indignation, smiling, fear, dry weeping, rebuke and a prohibition at the outset of an amorous exchange is called kila-kincita (hysterical delight).**

### 5.200

*arālā bhrū-vallī smita-sumadhurā bhartsana-giro*  
*mṛṣā kampaḥ śuṣkaṁ ruditam abhilāṣe ’pi mahati*  
*niṣedho nety asyāḥ kara-kamala-rodhena sakalaṁ*  
*harer āsīd etat kusuma-dhanuṣo ’nugraha iva*

**Перевод:**

**Although she had a great desire, she blocked Hari’s hand: The creepers of her brows were crooked; her smiling was sweet; she uttered a rebuke; she had a false tremor and dry weeping; and she rejected His advances by saying “No”. And all this was as if the outcome of winning the favor of Cupid.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Kaviraja says kila-kincita involves dry weeping and quotes a verse by Magha to prove it. Alternataively, the crying is tears of joy because the ladylove wants to embrace her lover yet she pretends to not play along: Most other poetical theorists mention “weeping” instead of dry weeping and point out that all the emotions are triggered by joy. Thus the cluster of emotions called kilakincita matches Rupa Gosvami’s example of bhava- sandhi arisen from one cause (Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu 2.4.242). Often, the vyabhicari-bhavas are expressed by means of their anubhavas.

Essentially, kila-kincita is kuttamita (fake repulse) (5.206) plus weeping. In addition, everyone agrees that kuttamita is necessarily characterized by the lover’s touching a body part of his ladylove: kesa-stanadharadi-grahanad duhkhe ’pi sukha-buddhi-cesta kuttamitam (Sarasvatī-kaṇṭhābharaṇa 5, illustration 157 preliminary).

Visvanatha Cakravarti says kila-kincita occurs when the couple is being looked at, otherwise the rejection is classed as kuttamita: stanadharadity atra vivikta iti seso deyah. sakhl-drsti-pathe tu kila-kincitam eva syad iti jneyam (Ananda-candrika 11.49). But the examples of Singabhupala and Visvanatha Kaviraja do not conform to his explanation.

**16.  Mottayita**

### 5.201

*tad-bhāva-bhugna-manaso vallabhasya kathādiṣu*  
*moṭṭāyitaṁ samākhyātaṁ karṇa-kaṇḍūyanādikam (102)*

**Перевод:**

**When the ladylove whose heart has become crooked, due to love for her beloved, rubs her ear, etc., upon hearing news or bits of conversation about him, that is properly called mottayita (indication of longing).**

*ādi-śabdāj jṛmbhā-gātra-moṭanādi.*

**Перевод:**

**The etceteras include yawning, and crushing the body.**

**Комментарий:**

The term mottayita is irregularly formed from the verbal root mut sancurnane (to crush) and means “being as if crushed”: mottayitam, kli, mut + bhave ghan. bahulakat ghanas tut. tato bhrsaditvat kyan. *tato bhave ktah, strmam svabhavika-dasa-vidhalankarantar- gatalankara-visesah, iti hemacandrah. tal-laksanam yatha ujjvala- nilamanih* (Sabda-kalpadruma). In the above elaboration and in texts 5.203 and 5.205, Kavi Karnapura equates mottayita with gatra-motana (crushing the body \[during intercourse\]), and so his interpretation of mottayita is unique. Other scholars say mottayita is the ladylove’s subtle and involuntary bodily manifestation of her longing: svabhilasa-prakatanam mottayitam itiritam (Rasarnava- sudhakara 1.204); *kanta-smarana-vartadau hrdi tad-bhava- bhavatah, prakatyam abhilasasya mottayitam udiryate* (Ujjvala-nilamani 11.47). Kavi Karnapura hints that mottayita occurs in the lover’s presence, but others indicate that mottayita only occurs in the lover’s absence (Sahitya-darpana) (Ujjvala-nilamani).

### 5.202

*yathā,*

*jhaṅ-kurvāṇa-vilola-kaṅkaṇa-bhṛto vāmasya doṣṇaḥ śanair*  
*utkampena kaniṣṭhayā vidadhatī karṇasya kaṇḍūyanam*  
*puṣpeṣoḥ pṛtaneva saṅgara-jaya-śrī-sūcanaṁ vyātanod*

**Пословный перевод:**

**17.  Kuttamita**

### 5.206

*stana-grahāsya-pānādau kriyamāṇe priyeṇa cet*

**Комментарий:**

According to Visvanatha Kaviraja, anger is not an essential characteristic. His interpretation conforms to Bharata Muni’s definition: kesa-stanadharadi-grahanad atiharsa- sambhramotpannam, kuttamitam vijneyam sukham api duhkhopacarena (Natya-sastra 22.30). The term kuttamita literally means “measured (mita) by a divide (kutta).” The verbal root is kutt chedane (to cut, divide).

### 5.215

*yathā,*  
*samprārthyamānāpi mayānuvelaṁ*  
*na vaktum iṣṭām api vakti vāṇīm*  
*ruṣā hriyā veti na vedmi sakhyo*  
*jānantu rādhā-hṛdayaṁ bhavatyaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Although I repeatedly implored Her to speak Her mind, She did not say anything. Sakhis, I could not discern whether this was due to anger or to bashfulness. Only you know Radha’s heart.**

**Комментарий:**

This is Visvanatha Kaviraja’s illustration:

*dūrāgatena kuśalaṁ*  
*pṛṣṭā novāca sā mayā kiñcit*  
*paryaśruṇī tu nayane*  
*tasyāḥ kathayāmbabhūvatuḥ sarvam*

**“My friend, when I came back from my long trip I asked her about her well-being, but she did not utter a word. Her eyes brimmed with tears and thus said everything.” (Sahitya-darpama 3.106)**

The theorists other than Kavi Karnapura say that the difference between vikrta and mottayita is that in vikrta the lover is present. Rupa Gosvami reiterates Singabhupala’s opinion that vikrta has one of three causes: irsya (antagonism), mana (pique), or lajja (bashfulness). Morever, Bharata Muni said the ladylove remains silent either because of her nature (bashfulness, or joy) or because of a pretext. Rupa Gosvami and Singabhupala say the essential characteristic of vikrta is that the ladylove implies what she means to say by means of a gesture. Singabhupala’s example of vihrta caused by antagonism is a verse by Kalidasa: Raghu-vamsa 6.82. Henceforward the previous verses are also shown:

*asau kumāras tam ajo ’nujātas*  
*triviṣṭapasyeva patiṁ jayantaḥ*  
*gurvīṁ dhuraṁ yo bhuvanasya pitrā*  
*dhuryeṇa damyaḥ sadṛśaṁ bibharti*

*kulena kāntyā vayasā navena*  
*guṇaiś ca tais tair vinaya-pradhānaiḥ*  
*tvam ātmanas tulyam amuṁ vṛṇīṣva*  
*ratnaṁ samāgacchatu kāñcanena*

*tataḥ sunandā-vacanāvasāne*  
*lajjāṁ tanū-kṛtya narendra-kanyā*  
*dṛṣṭyā prasādāmalayā kumāraṁ*  
*pratyagrahīt saṁvaraṇa-srjeva*

*sā yūni tasminn abhilāṣa-bandhaṁ*  
*śaśāka śālīnatayā na vaktum*  
*romāñca-lakṣyeṇa sa gātra-yaṣṭiṁ*  
*bhittvā nirākrāmad arāla-keśyāḥ*

*tathāgatāyāṁ parihāsa-pūrvaṁ*  
*sakhyāṁ sakhī vetra-bhṛd ābabhāṣe*  
*ārye vrajāmo ’nyata ity athaināṁ*  
*vadhūr asūyā-kuṭilaṁ dadarśa*

**\[Indumati sees the contenders at her Svayamvara ceremony. Next in line is Aja. At first, Sunanda describes him to Indumati:\] ““This prince, Aja, is born of Raghu as Jayanta is born of Indra. With his father, Aja bears the heavy burden of the world like a young bull aided by an experienced bullock pulls a heavy cart. In terms of family, beauty, youthfulness, and qualities the foremost of which is having a good disposition, he is equal to you, therefore select him. Let the jewel be united with gold.” The minute Sunanda stopped talking, the princess thinned out her bashfulness and, with a glance pure due to satisfaction, chose this prince as her husband. Her glance was like the garland used on such an occasion. Since she was well-mannered, the princess was unable to express her love for him. But at last, the love this curly-haired damsel felt for that young man pierced her slender frame and came out under the guise of goosebumps. Seeing that her friend Indumati had turned out this way, Sunanda said in jest: “Dear young lady, let us go to the next contender.” Instantly the young woman gave her a crooked glance of displeasure.” (Raghu-vamsa 6.78-82)**

The next verse eminently concludes the scene:

*sā cūrṇa-gauraṁ raghu-nandanasya*  
*dhātrī-karābhyāṁ karabhopamorūḥ*  
*āsañjayāmāsa yathā-pradeśaṁ*  
*kaṇṭhe guṇaṁ mūrtam ivānurāgam*

**“Then the princess, whose thighs compared to the trunks of two elephants, properly placed the garland on the neck of Raghu’s son with the help of Sunanda, who was akin to a nurse. The garland was as if Indumati’s love incarnate.” (Raghu-vamsa 6.83)**

### 5.217

*yathā,*  
*śīta-prayogair bahir īhyamānair*  
*antar-gato vardhata eva dāhaḥ*

sita—of cold; prayogaih—with applications; bahih—outside; ihyamanaih—being done; antar-gatah—gone within; vardhate— increases; eva—only; dahah—conflagration; bahih—outside; vilepaih—with coverings; bahih—outside; aprakasi—does not manifest; projjrmbhate—intensely expands; antah—inside; puta- paka—from the method of cooking in a rounded hollow; jah— arisen; agnih—the fire.

### 5.233

**Пословный перевод:**

pratyekam—each one; sapta-vimsatya—with the twenty-seven; yoge—in combining; asta-vimsatih—the twenty-eight; tu—same; amt—these ones; rasa—six (six tastes in Ayurveda); bana—five (five arrows); rsi—seven (seven Rsis); sankhyah—they whose number is; syuh—are; te—they; punah—moreover; sa-ingitah— combined with the erotic symptoms; yadi—if; paksa—two (two wings); indu—one (one moon); isu—five (five arrows); indu—one (one moon); sankhyah—they whose number is; syuh—become; anyonya—with one another; gunitah—multiplied; nanu—indeed.

**Перевод:**

**The number of combinations of these alankaras is 756, by multiplying the twenty-eight by twenty-seven. The same number is added by considering that one of the ecstatic symptoms, which are about to be described, is mentioned. Thus the total number of combinations is 1512.**

*te ’nyonya-guṇitā alaṅkārā vakṣyamāṇair iṅgitaiḥ sahitā yadi bhavanti. grantha-gaurava-bhiyā nodāhriyante.*

**Перевод:**

**Not all the possibilities will be illustrated out of fear of increasing the size of the treatise.**

**Комментарий:**

Kavi Karnapura follows Visvanatha Cakravarti’s category called ingita (erotic symptom) (Sahitya-darpana 3.111-127). They include Rupa Gosvami’s udbhasvaras (change in the body or on the body) (Ujjvala-nilamani 11.69). Rupa Gosvami points out that some of the udbhasvaras are already included in the descriptions of alankaras (esp. the traditional mottayita, and vilasa): yadyapy ete visesah syur mottayita-vilasayoh, sobha-visesa-positvat tathapi prthag iritah (Ujjvala-nilamani 11.77). Neither Bharata Muni, Visvanatha Kaviraja nor Rupa Gosvami specifies that combinations of alankaras can be made.

### 5.234

*na ca vaktavyaṁ “nirvikārātmake citte bhāvaḥ prathama-vikriyā” iti bhāvasya tathā-vidhatvāt kathaṁ hāvādi-sāṅkaryam? yataḥ kanyānām eva tathā kramaḥ, paroḍhā-madhyādīnāṁ śrī-kṛṣṇaṁ prati prāṅ-nirvikārātmake citte yadaiva bhāva utpannas tadaiva hāvādi-sāṅkaryam api.*

**Перевод:**

**Someone might argue: “Since bhava was defined in this way: “The first change in a mind that had been changelessness by nature is called bhava” (5.166), how can bhava possibly be combined with hava or with any other alankara?” That remark is wrong because the sequence of bhava, hava, and so on only applies to the kanyas (virgins) (5.110-112). However, in the case of the parodha-madhyas, and so on, the other alankaras occur at the same time that bhava for Sri Krsna appears for the first time, so they can be combined.**
