*yaḥ keśavasyāpi ca keśa-rañjanaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

vrtha—useless; akrthah—you made; yavakam—the lac; anghri- pankaje—on the lotus-like feet; svah—own; eva—very; ragah— redness; asya—of this (the feet); drsam—of the eyes; rasayanah—a tonic; kintu—but; ekah—one; eva—only; asti—there is; gunah—a quality; asya—of this (the lac); radhike—O Radhika; yah—which; kesavasya—of Kesava; api—even; ca—(verse filler); kesa—of the hair; ranjanah—the maker of redness.

**Перевод:**

**Radhika, You rendered the lac on Your lotus-like feet useless. The natural redness of Your feet is a tonic for the eyes. Still, the lac has one quality: It reddens Kesava’s hair.**

### 5.249

*na saṅkocaṁ yayā yāti kāntena śayitotthitā*

**Перевод:**

**The sakhi in the company of whom the ladylove neither feels shy to go to sleep with the lover nor feels embarrassed to rise from bed naked thereafter is the priya-narma-sakhi. She is a second form of the ladylove.**

### 5.250

*yathā,*  
*anyonya-grathitāṅgulī-kisalayau vinyasya sakhy-aṁsayor*  
*bāhū gātra-vimoṭanaṁ vidadhatī kṛtvā stanāgre stanau*  
*yat kṛṣṇasya jaye samarjitavatī pauṣpāyudhe saṅgare*  
*tat saubhāgya-dhanaṁ nyadhād vidhu-mukhī svāṅgāt tad-aṅgeṣv iva*

**Пословный перевод:**

anyonya—together; grathita—are connected; anguli—\[in the form\] of two fingers; kisalayau—in which the two shoots; vinyasya— after placing; sakhi-amsayoh—on the friend’s shoulders; bahu— two arms; gatra—of the body; vimotanam—the crushing; vidadhati—while making; krtva—by making (putting); stana— of the breasts; agre—in front; stanau—two breasts; yat—what; krsnasya—of Krsna; jaye—in the defeating; samarjitavati—she earned; pauspayudhe—of Cupid; sangare—in tha battle; tat—that; saubhagya—of good fortune; dhanam—the wealth; nyadhat— placed; vidhu-mukhi—the moon-faced girl; sva-angat—from her own limbs; tat-angesu—unto her limbs; iva—as if.

**Moon-faced Radha put Her breasts in front of those of Her friend, placed Her arms around her neck and intertwined Her shoot fingers. She thus as if transferred from Her limbs to hers the wealth of conjugal felicity that She earned by defeating Krsna while crushing His body in the battle of love.**

*etā api catur-vidhāḥ sakhyo nāyikā-guṇair anyūnā eva.*

**Перевод:**

**All in all, there are four kinds of sakhis. Their qualities are not lesser than those of the ladyloves.**

Rupa Gosvami elaborates in Ujjvala-nllamani 8.124-137.

### 5.251

*viśeṣatas tu,*  
*dūtī-bhāvaḥ samaye parijana-bhāvas tu veśa-bhūṣādau*  
*upadeṣṭṛtā ca māne tasmin gāḍhe tu garhakatvaṁ ca (125)*

**Перевод:**

**And specifically, a sakhi becomes a messenger when the occasion presents itself, becomes part of the ladylove’s retinue at the time of applying makeup to her face, dressing her up, etc., instructs the ladylove in the matter of pique, and reprehends her when her pique is over-the-top.**

*tāsām iti bhāvaḥ. dūtī-bhāvas tu tridhā. lakṣaṇaṁ tu prāg-uktasamānam eva. tatra nisṛṣṭārthā yathā “ucchūna-stanitā” ity-ādau. mitārthā yathā“tāmbūla-mālyā” ity-ādau.*

**Перевод:**

**There are three kinds of messengers (duti): nisrstartha, mitartha, and sandesa-harika. The definitions are the same as those given earlier (5.88): The nisrstartha messenger is one who understands the signs of the lover and of the ladylove and gives a reply. She nicely accomplishes the task. The mitartha messenger is one who speaks concisely. She also achieves the end of the task (the meeting of the lovers). The sandesa-harika messenger is one who speaks only in the way she is told to speak.**

**Of those, an example of the nisrstartha messenger is verse 3.67. An instance of the mitartha messenger is verse 5.160.**

**Комментарий:**

Rupa Gosvami remarks that a messenger’s words involve either an implied sense or only expressed meanings: vacyam vyangyam iti dvedha tad dutyam ubhayor api (Ujjvala-nilamani 7.72).

### 5.252

*sandeśa-hārikā yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**This illustrates the sandesa-harika:**

*tvad-uktam uktaṁ sakhi kṛṣṇa-sannidhau*  
*tad-uktam etac ca nivedayāmi te*  
*prasādanenālam anena nigraho*  
*’py anugraho ’yaṁ mama yaḥ kṛtas tayā*

**Перевод:**

**Sakhi, I related your message to Krsna. Now listen to His reply to you: “What is the use of My conciliatory manners? I am done with them. Your bad temper is a favor to Me.”**

### 5.253

*parijana-bhāvo yathā “ādarśe ’nucarī” ity-ādi. mānopadeṣṭṛtā yathā “sakhyā śikṣita-pāṭhitāni” ity-ādi. tasmin gāḍhe garhakatvaṁ yathā “kati na patitaṁ pādopānta” ity-ādau, “asmābhiḥ saha cāṭu-kṛt” ity-ādau vā. ukta ālambana-vibhāvaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**An example of having the mood of being in the ladylove’s retinue is verse 5.223. An instance of being an instructor of the ladylove in the matter of pique is in the words sakhya siksita- pathitani and so on (5.116). An example of reprehending the ladylove’s pique when it is over-the-top is verse 4.12. Another illustration of the same is verse 5.158.**

**Here ends the section on alambana-vibhavas (visaya, object, and asraya, subject).**

**Комментарий:**

Ultimately, the purport of the section on the alankaras of srngara, and so on, is that true love is about relishing the nature, more so than the beauty, of the other person.

### 5.254

*uddīpana-vibhāvo yathā,*  
*vṛndāvanaṁ ṣaḍ-ṛtavaḥ saha-vartamānāḥ*  
*kuñjā maṇīndra-gṛhato ’pi mano-vinodāḥ*  
*karpūra-bhāṁsi yamunā-pulināni haṁsa-*  
*kāraṇḍavādi lalitaṁ nalinī-vanaṁ ca (126)*  
*candraś ca candana-maruc ca manoharāṇi*  
*govardhanādi-giri-kandara-mandirāṇi*  
*rolamba-kokila-mayūra-nināda-miśrair*  
*nānā-vihaṅga-virutair harito ’pi hṛdyāḥ (127)*

**Перевод:**

**These are examples of uddipana-vibhavas (excitants) in Vrndavana: The six seasons existing together; pleasure groves that delight the mind even more than jewel-studded palaces do; the banks of the Yamuna which are as bright as camphor; splendid animals such as swans and ducks; charming clusters of lotuses; the moon; a cooling breeze; lovely caves in Govardhana Hill and so on; and the pleasant chirping of various birds here and there along with the buzzing of bees, the cooing of cuckoos and the screams of peacocks.**

### 5.255

*tatra ṣaṇṇām ṛtūnām ekatra-vartitā yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**Of those, this illustrates the six seasons existing at the same time:**

*śirīṣeṇāsaktā sthala-kamalinī kunda-latikā*  
*ratā lodhre nīpaḥ svayam anusṛto mādhavikayā*  
*aho vṛndāraṇye viṭapi-mithunānāṁ vihasatāṁ*  
*kim īdṛg dāmpatyaṁ sphurati racite kuñja-bhavane*

**Перевод:**

**The land lotuses are in touch with the sirisa flowers, the jasmine creepers appreciate the lodhra flowers, and the kadamba trees are automatically followed by the madhavika creepers. How amazing is Vrndavana! Are the merry pairs of plants in the occupied pleasure groves in wedlock?**

*evam anye ’py anusartavyāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The other types of uddipanas can be looked into in this way.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: The sirisa flower blooms in the summer (grisma), the land lotus in the fall (sarad), the lodhra in the cold season (hemanta), the jasmine creeper in the winter (sisira), the nipa tree in the rainy season (pravrs), and the madhavika in the spring (vasanta). Here the lotus in bloom is connected with (asakta = saha asakta) a man in the form of a sirisa flower (Subodhini).

The first half of the verse features the samasokti ornament (concise statement), especially due to the genders of the words (Commentary 8.91): The sirisa flower, the lodhra flower, and the kadamba tree represent men since the words sirisa, lodhra, and nipa (kadamba) are masculine, and a lotus, a jasmine creeper, and a madhavika creeper represent women since the words kamalini, latika, and madhavika are feminine.

*athānubhāvāḥ,*

**Перевод:**

**Depending on the occasion, some of the alankaras of srngara can be classed as anubhavas, and so can the ecstatic symptoms.**

*tatra kaṭākṣo yathā,*

*unmāda-moha-mada-dāha-visarpa-śūla-*  
*tṛṣṇānvito jvara ivātmani me praviṣṭaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

tasyah—Her (Radha’s); trapa—bashfulness; bhaya—fear; visada— languor; viveka—discernment; dhairya—steadfastness of the heart; dainya—meekness; abhilasa—longing; bhara—in the form of an abundance of; korakitah—is filled with flower buds; kata-aksah— sidelong glance; unmada—derangement; moha—stupefaction; mada—intoxication; daha—burning; visarpa—the disease called visarpa (a skin eruption); sula—acute pain; trsna—thirst; anvitah— endowed with; jvarah—a fever; iva—like; atmani—in the heart; me—My; pravistah—has entered.

**Перевод:**

*kṛṣṇoktiḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna speaks. This is another example:**

### 5.258

*yathā vā,*  
*tava śaśimukhi rādhe dakṣiṇādakṣiṇābhyāṁ*  
*śravaṇa-patham upāttaḥ preṅkhayāyaṁ kaṭākṣaḥ*  
*nibhṛta-rabhasa-vegāropitaḥ śāṅkhikānāṁ*  
*krakaca iva mamoccaiḥ kṛntati svānta-śaṅkham*

**Пословный перевод:**

tava—your; sasimukhi—O moon-faced girl; radhe—O Radha; daksina-adaksinabhyam—from the right and left \[eyes\]; sravana— of the ears; patham—the path; upattah—which has reached; prenkhaya—by the swinging (the movement); ayam—this; kata- aksah—crooked glance; nibhrta—in a solitary place; rabhasa— due to joy; vega—by speed; aropitah—raised; sankhikanam—of those who cut conchshells; krakacah—the saw; iva—like; mama— my; uccaih—highly; krntati—cuts; sva-anta—\[in the form\] of my mind; sankham—the conchshell.

**Перевод:**

**Moon-faced Radha, by the motion of Your eyes, Your sidelong glance reaches the path of Your ears. Intensified by speed due to elation in a solitary place, it completely cuts the conchshell of My mind as if it were a saw of the conchshell cutters.**

*evam anye ’py anusartavyāḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**The other anubhavas can be looked into in this way.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: In common parlance, the sankhikas are called sankhari (cutters of conchshells). The distinct meaning here is: An ordinary saw cuts one way, but the saw of a person who is a conchshell cutter cuts on the way out and on the way in (Subodhim). The coming and going of Her eyes acted like the motion of a saw. The tip of a conch shell is cut in order to blow the conch. The implied sense is: It’s as if Krsna was now ready to signal the beginning of the battle of love.

### 5.259

*sāttvikā api ye ’nye ’ṣṭau te ’pi yānty anubhāvatām (130)*  
*te yathā,*  
*stambhaḥ svedo ’tha romāñcaḥ svara-bhedaś ca vepathuḥ*  
*vaivarṇyam aśru-pralaya ity aṣṭau sāttvikāḥ smṛtāḥ (131)*

**Перевод:**

**The sattvika-bhavas, eight in number, are in the category of anubhava. They are: stambha (being stunned), sveda (perspiration), romanca (horripilation), svara-bheda (faltering voice), vepathu (trembling), vaivarnya (a change in color), asru (tears), and pralaya (loss of consciousness, owing to happiness). (Sahitya-darpana 3.135) (Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu 2.3.16)**

**Комментарий:**

Both the sattvika-bhavas and the other anubhavas arise from sattva.

The difference is that the other anubhavas arise due to volition.

### 5.260

*udāharaṇam,*  
*svinnā gadgada-bhāṣiṇī pulakitā stabdhā sphurad-vepathuḥ*  
*sāśrur mlāna-rucir yad adya jaladāloke ’bhavad bhāvinī*  
*tan manye sphuṭam indranīla-mahasaḥ kasyāpi līlā-nidher*  
*vṛndāraṇya-vilāsino dyuti-bharair eṣā parābhūyata*

**Пословный перевод:**

svinna—perspiring; gadgada-bhasini—she whose speech is faltering; pulakita—she has developed horripilation; stabdha— stunned; sphurat-vepathuh—she whose trembling is manifesting; sa-asruh—weeping; mlana-rucih—she whose radiance has faded; yat—since; adya—today; jalada-aloke—upon seeing a cloud; abhavat—became; bhavini—the emotional woman; tat—therefore; manye—I think; sphutam—obviously; indranila-mahasah—of He whose effulgence resembles that of a sapphire; kasya api— of someone (of some indescribable one); lila-nidheh—who is a reservoir of pastimes; vrnda-aranya-vilasinah—who sports in Vmda’s forest; dyuti-bharaih—by much splendor; esa—she; parabhuyata—was overcome.

**Перевод:**

**Upon seeing a cloud today, this emotional young lady perspired, her speech faltered, she had goosebumps, she became stunned, she manifestly trembled, she wept, and her glow faded. Therefore I think that obviously she was overcome by the profuse splendor of that special someone who is effulgent like a sapphire, who is a reservoir of pastimes, and who sports in Vrnda’s forest.**

### 5.261

*atha vyabhicāriṇaḥ,*

**Перевод:**

**Now, the vyabhicari-bhavas are detailed:**

*nirveda-glāni-śaṅkāś ca madāsūyā-śramā atha*  
*ālasya-dainya-cintāś ca mohaḥ smṛti-dhṛtī api*  
*vrīḍā capalatā harṣa āvega-jaḍate tathā*  
*viṣādausukya-garvāś ca nidrāpasmāra eva ca (132-133)*  
*vimarṣa-supty-amarṣāś cāpy avahitthogratety api*  
*unmāda-vyādhi-matayo vitarka-maraṇe punaḥ*  
*trāsaś ceti trayas-triṁśad ucyante vyabhicāriṇaḥ (134)*

**Перевод:**

**The thirty-three vyabhicari-bhavas are: 1. nirveda (self­disparagement) (disgust toward material life), 2. glani (weakness) (or mlani), 3. sanka (apprehension), 4. mada (intoxication; being crazed), 5. asuya (jealousy; resentment; fault-finding coupled with disrespect), 6. srama (fatigue), 7. alasya (laziness), 8. dainya (meekness, feeling miserable), 9. cinta (pondering), 10. moha (acute bewilderment), 11. smrti (remembrance), 12. dhrti (steadfastness of the heart) (or dhairya), 13. vrTda (bashfulness, shame) (or lajja), 14. capalata (fickleness), 15. harsa (joy), 16. avega (confusion, mental flurry), 17. jadata (indolence), 18. visada (remorse, dejection), 19. autsukya (eagerness, longing), 20. garva (overweening pride), 21. nidra (sleepiness), 22. apasmara (convulsion), 23. vimarsa (consideration), 24. supti (dreaming), 25. amarsa (indignation), 26. avahittha (concealment), 27. ugrata (arrogance), 28. unmada (deranged state), 29. vyadhi (ailment), 30. mati (thoughtfulness), 31. vitarka (conjecture), 32. marana (deathlike symptoms), and 33. trasa (sudden fear).**

### 5.262

*athaiṣāṁ lakṣaṇam,*  
*sva-jugupsā tu nirvedo glānir vikṛtir ākṛteḥ*  
*aniṣṭāśaṅkanaṁ śaṅkā mado madhv-ādi-mattatā*  
*doṣa-dṛṣṭir asūyā syād vyāyāma-klāntatā śramaḥ (135)*  
*śaktau ca karma-vaimukhyam ālasyaṁ dainyam ātmani*  
*ayogya-buddhiś cintā tu kiṁ bhāvīti vicintanam*  
*vicittatā tu mohaḥ syāt smṛtiḥ prāg-vṛtta-cintanam*  
*dhairyaṁ dhṛtis trapā vrīḍā laulyaṁ capalatā matā*  
*harṣaś cittasya visphāra āvegas tvarayā madaḥ*  
*niṣpandatvaṁ tu jaḍatā viṣādas tu viṣaṇṇatā*  
*utkaṇṭhaivautsukyam āhur garvo ’haṅkāra eva hi*  
*nidrā nidraiva skhalanaṁ phena-niṣṭhīva-pūrvakam*  
*apasmāraḥ parāmarśo vimarṣo nidrayā vinā*  
*svapnas tu suptir ity āhur amarṣaḥ kopa eva ca*  
*avahitthākāra-guptir ugratā tīvrataiva hi*  
*anavasthita-cittatvam unmādo hṛd-vyathādikaḥ*  
*vyādhir yathārtha-smaraṇaṁ matiḥ saṁśaya eva hi*  
*vitarko maraṇaṁ prāṇa-tyāgas trāso bhayodayaḥ*  
*apasmāraṁ ca nirvedaṁ maraṇaṁ ca vinā kila*  
*triṁśad evātra vijñeyāḥ śṛṅgāre vyabhicāriṇaḥ (136-143)*

**Перевод:**

**The vyabhicari-bhavas are defined: Nirveda means self­disparagement. Glani (weakness) means a bodily degradation. Sanka signifies worrying a little about what is undesirable. Mada means being drunk, and so on. Asuya means fault-finding. Srama is fatigue because of exertion. Alasya signifies that one is averse to doing something although one is able to do it. Dainya means considering oneself to be unqualified or unworthy. Cinta means pondering: “What will happen?” Moha signifies the near cessation of mental functions. Smrti means thinking about what occurred in the past. Dhairya is steadfastness. Vnda signifies bashfulness. Capalata is fickleness. Harsa denotes the expansion of the mind. Avega is a form of impairment due to the haste of the mind. Indolence is jadata. Visada means dejection. Autsukya signifies eagerness or longing. Garva means self­conceit. Nidra is sleepiness. Apasmara is a convulsion which involves having saliva at the edge of the mouth. Vimarsa means coming to a logical conclusion after deeply considering the matter. Supti (dreaming) means sleeping without deep sleep. Amarsa (indignation) is anger. Avahittha is the concealment of something. Ugrata is arrogance. Unmada means being mentally unstable. Vyadhi signifies having pain in the heart, and so on.**

**Mati means remembering the true meaning. Vitarka refers to a conjecture. Marana means giving up living. Trasa is the sudden rise of fear.**

**Except apasmara, nirveda and marana, all the vyabhicaris are also vyabhicaris of srngara-rasa, which are thus thirty in number.**

*apasmārādayas trayaḥ kramād amaṅgalatvāt śāntāṅgatvāt karuṇāṅgatvāc ca na gṛhītāḥ. tattva-jñānottho nirveda eva kevalaṁ na gṛhīta iti kecit.*

**Перевод:**

**Those three, apasmara, nirveda and marana, are not taken into account in srngara because the first is inauspicious, the second is an aspect of santa-rasa, and the third relates to karuna-rasa. Some say only the nirveda which arises from the knowledge of self-realization should not be accounted for in srngara.**

**Комментарий:**

Rupa Gosvami indicates that when nirveda means “self­disparagement”, it can be a vyabhicari of srngara (Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu 3.5.16). According to him, thirty-one vyabhicaris apply in srngara. Of the thirty-three, he discards ugrata (arrogance) and alasya (laziness): nirvedadyastrayastrimsad-bhava ye parikirtitah, augryalasye vina te’tra vijneya vyabhicarinah (Ujjvala-nilamani 13.1). But Jiva Gosvami says a ladylove has alasya after union with Krsna, and has ugrata after she loses His loyalty.

Kavi Karnapura gave the derivation of the term vyabhicarin earlier (5.1). Similarly, Visvanatha Kaviraja says a vyabhicari is so called because it favorably (abhi = abhimukhyena) moves (carin = carana) in the sthayi in special ways (vi = visesena) like waves in an ocean rise and disappear (BRS 2.4.3). In that sense, a vyabhicari is a transient emotion. Rupa Gosvami accepts this derivation (BRS 2.4.1) and also mentions Visvanatha Kaviraja’s other explanation: A sancarl, a synonym of vyabhicarl, is so called because it directs (sancarayati) the course of the sthayi-bhava: vyabhicarinah, sancarayanti bhavasya gatim sancarino ’pi (BRS 2.4.2).

### 5.263

*bhavanty ekaikaśas tv ete svātantryeṇa pṛthak pṛthak*  
*udayaḥ praśamaś cāpi pṛthag eva nirūpyate*  
*dvābhyāṁ ca bahubhiś cāpi śābalyaṁ saṁhitā dvayoḥ*  
*sandhir lakṣaṇam eteṣāṁ yathā-svam upadarśyate*  
*tātkālikaṁ hetum etya tat-kālodbhūtatodayaḥ*  
*praśamo nija-sāmagryā prāg-udbhūtasya saṅkṣayaḥ*  
*anyonyānugrāhakānugrāhyatvāt saha-saṁsthitiḥ*  
*anyonya-nirapekṣatvāt sva-sva-svātantryato ’thavā*  
*sa-pakṣāṇāṁ vipakṣāṇāṁ śābalyaṁ parikīrtitam*  
*ekasya gamanārambho hy anyasyāgamanodayaḥ*  
*sandhiḥ syād athavā tulyodayas tulya-śamo dvayoḥ (144-148)*  
*dvayos tulya-kālīna udayaḥ praśamo vā sandhir ity arthaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**The vyabhicari-bhavas occur singly, since they have their own importance. In addition, they occur singly in the categories called bhavodaya (origination of a vyabhicarl) and bhava- prasama (bhava-santi) (cessation of a vyabhicarl). A combination either of two vyabhicarls or of many vyabhicarls is called bhava-sabalya (mixing of similar or dissimilar vyabhicarls). A combination of two vyabhicarls is termed bhava-sandhi (combination of vyabhicarls).**

**They are defined: When one vyabhicarl arises at the same time that its cause is mentioned, that is bhavodaya. Bhava-prasama is the cessation of one vyabhicarl which had previously arisen with its constituents. Bhava-sabalya is the combination of similar or dissimilar vyabhicarls. And this combination has two varieties: Either one or more vyabhicarls assist another or, if no vyabhicari requires another, each one is independent. Bhava- sandhi has two categories: (1) One vyabhicari is on its way out and the other is arriving, or (2) Either two vyabhicaris arise at the same time or two vyabhicaris cease at the same moment.**

**Комментарий:**

Kavi Kamapura’s interpretations of bhava-sandhi and bhava- sabalya differ from Rupa Gosvami’s (Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu 2.4.235). Rupa Gosvami defines bhava-sabalya as a friction (conflict) between vyabhicaris: sabalatvam tu bhavanam sammardah syatparasparam (2.4.244).

### 5.264

*udayādyaiś caturbhis tu śābalyam aparaṁ bhavet*  
*tat syāt ṣoḍaśadhā tatra prastāra-krama iṣyate (149)*

**Перевод:**

**The four categories—udaya, prasama, sabalya, and sandhi— are combined in various sequences to make a total of sixteen categories.**

**Комментарий:**

This theory is not found in other treatises on poetical rhetoric.

### 5.265

*ṣoḍaśadhā yathā,*  
*sandhy-uttarāḥ syuś catvāras tathānye śabalottarāḥ*  
*catvāra evaṁ praśamottarā apy udayottarāḥ (150)*

**Перевод:**

**The sixteen categories take place as follows: Four categories end with bhava-sandhi, four end with bhava-sabalya, four end with bhava-prasama, and four with bhavodaya.**

### 5.266

*prastāra-darśanam,*  
*u pra śa sa \| śa u pra sa \| pra śa u sa \|*  
*pra u śa sa \| ete sandhy-uttarāś catvāraḥ \|\|*  
*sa u pra śa \| sa pra u śa \| pra u sa śa \|*  
*u pra sa śa \| ete śābalyottarāś catvāraḥ \|\|*

*u śa sa pra \| sa u śa pra \| śa sa u pra \|*  
*sa śa u pra \| ete praśamottarāś catvāraḥ \|\|*  
*śa sa pra u \| sa śa pra u \| pra śa sa u \|*  
*sa pra śa u \| ete udayottarāś catvāraḥ \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**These are the sixteen categories. The four which end with bhava-sandhi are: (1) udaya, prasama, sabalya, sandhi, (2) sabalya, udaya, prasama, sandhi, (3) prasama, sabalya, udaya, sandhi, and (4) prasama, udaya, sabalya, sandhi.**

**The four which end with bhava-sabalya are: (5) sandhi, udaya, prasama, sabalya, (6) sandhi, prasama, udaya, sabalya, (7) prasama, udaya, sandhi, sabalya, and (8) udaya, prasama, sandhi, sabalya.**

**The four which end with bhava-prasama are: (9) udaya, sabalya, sandhi, prasama, (10) sandhi, udaya, sabalya, prasama, (11) sabalya, sandhi, udaya, prasama, and (12) sandhi, sabalya, udaya, prasama.**

**The four which end with bhavodaya are: (13) sabalya, sandhi, prasama, udaya, (14) sandhi, sabalya, prasama, udaya, (15) prasama, sabalya, sandhi, udaya, and (16) sandhi, prasama, sabalya, udaya.**

**Комментарий:**

Siva-prasada Bhattacarya remarks that six categories can be made in each of the four broad kinds for a total of twenty-four. Indeed, of the above sixteen, Kavi Karnapura illustrates “prasama, sandhi, sabalya, udaya” (5.325) instead of “sandhi, prasama, sabalya, udaya” (16), and “sabalya, prasama, sandhi, udaya” (5.326) instead of “prasama, sabalya, sandhi, udaya” (15).

### 5.267

*evaṁ syād viṁśatiḥ (151a)*

**Перевод:**

**This makes a total of twenty categories.**

*kevalair udayādyaiś caturbhiḥ prastāra-gataiḥ ṣoḍaśabhis tu viṁśati-prakārāḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**The sixteen types of combinations added to the four single varieties beginning from bhavodaya make a total of twenty categories.**

*sandheḥ sandhināpy udayasya ca*  
*udayena śamasyāpi śamenāpi tridhā punaḥ (151bcd)*  
*śābalyam iti śeṣaḥ. sandhi-śābalyam udaya-śābalyaṁ praśamaśābalyam iti tridhā.*

**Перевод:**

**There are three more categories: sandhi-sabalya (a combination of a bhava-sandhi with another bhava-sandhi), udaya-sabalya (a combination of a bhavodaya with another bhavodaya), and prasama-sabalya (a combination of a bhava-prasama with another bhava-prasama).**

### 5.269

*tathaivodaya-sandhiś ca śama-sandhir iti smṛteḥ*  
*pañcaviṁśatir ete syur anyonya-sthiti-bhedataḥ*  
*pratyekam ekaika-yoge mitho ’ṅgāṅgitva-bhāvataḥ*  
*ekonatriṁśatā triṁśad bindu-sindhu-mataṅgajāḥ (152-153)*

**Перевод:**

**By adding two aforementioned categories: udaya-sandhi (two vyabhicaris arise at the same time) and prasama-sandhi (two vyabhicaris cease at the same moment), the total is twenty-five varieties.**

**Each vyabhicari can occur in combination with another by the relation of anga (subordinate) and angi (predominant). Thus the thirty vyabhicaris multiplied by twenty-nine make a total of 870 varieties.**

*nirvedādi-tritaya-varjitasya triṁśad-vyabhicāri-*  
*bhāvasyonatriṁśatā guṇitasyaite prakārā ity arthaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

*punar etaiḥ prāg-gaṇitais taiḥ seṅgita-niriṅgitaiḥ*

*śābalyena bhavanty ete bindu-veda-kara-dvipaiḥ (karāgnibhiḥ)*  
*vedāgni(bāṇāgni)-candra-saṅkhyākās teṣāṁ dig-darśanaṁ bhavet*

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: “Her love is young” means she cannot give it up, and “Her body is soft” means it cannot endure the fire of separation.

*avadhi-dinam īkṣadhvaṁ tad evāsthā-sthalaṁ hi vaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

dhairyam—steadfastness; bhajata—all of you should have; bhoh pranah—O life airs; gataih—by those that are gone; krsnah— Krsna; kva—where?; lapsyate—is desired to be obtained; avadhi— which is the end; dinam—the day; iksadhvam—you all should see; tat—that; eva—only; astha—of hope; sthalam—place; hi—very; vah—your.

**Перевод:**

**13.  Vrīḍā**

### 5.284

*vrīḍā,*  
*paśya vakṣasi me rādhe sva-mūrtiṁ pratibimbitām*  
*kopāt parāṅmukhīveti kṛṣṇoktyā sā tu tatrape*

**Перевод:**

**\[One day, it so happened that Radha had her back turned toward Krsna for a second:\]**

**“Radha, look at Your reflection on My chest. It’s as if You are averse out of anger.” She became bashful when Krsna said this.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: Krsna meant to say, “Now that You are facing away, Your image on My chest is like it was when You turned Your back toward Me due to being in a huff” (Subodhinl). What is intended to show here is that Radha became ashamed of Her bad temper: By Visvanatha Kaviraja’s definition, vrlda occurs because the lady bows the head due to misbehavior: dharstyabhavo vrlda vadananamanadi-krd duracarat (Sahitya-darpana 3.165).

**14.  Capalatā**

### 5.285

*capalatā,*  
*kṛṣṇāgamanam ākarṇya vanāt sāyaṁ vrajāṅganāḥ*  
*manaso ’pi puraś cakrur vātāyana-pathe dṛśaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Hearing at dusk that Krsna had returned from the woodland, the young women of Vraja fixed their glances on the path via the lattice windows even before their heads turned.**

**Комментарий:**

Instead of capalata (fickleness), the verse can be classed as autsukya (longing) (5.290) because the lover is not present. This is Visvanatha Kaviraja’s example of capalata:

*anyāsu tāvad upamarda-sahāsu bhṛṅga*  
*lolaṁ vinodaya manaḥ sumano-latāsu*  
*mugdhām ajāta-rajasaṁ kalikām akāle*  
*vyarthaṁ kadarthayasi kiṁ nava-mallikāyāḥ*

**“Hey bumblebee, amuse your wanton mind on other flowered creepers—those who are willing to tolerate friction. Why do you, at an inappropriate time, vainly pain the tender blossoms of the new jasmine?” (Subhasitavali 735) (Sahitya-darpana 3.169)**

This verse also illustrates the aprastuta-prasamsa ornament (indirect expression) (8.106), since here a woman is indirectly talking to the lover: She rebukes him for being fickle (he wants some action, but the ladylove, a young mugdha, is not in the mood).

ayam—this; sakhi—O friend; gatah—has gone; yamah—a period of three hours; syamah—Syama; vamah—unruly (or beautiful); sah—He; na—not; agatah—has come; uditah—has risen; yamini- nathah—the moon (“the beloved of the night”); visidanti—are becoming faint; mama—my; asavah—life airs.

*autsukyam,*

**20.   Garva**

### 5.291

*garvaḥ,*  
*munīndrāṇāṁ ca yā vandyā dhvaja-vajrādi-lāñchanā*  
*mad-āli-pakṣa-dvārānte nityāsau pada-paddhatiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The marks such as a flag and a thunderbolt which are praised by the best sages are in a series of footsteps just outside my friend’s window.**

**21.   Nidrā**

### 5.292

*nidrā,*  
*rādhā nidhuvana-śrāntā nidrāti śyāma-vakṣasi*  
*madaneneva niḥsyūtā capalā jaladopari*

**Перевод:**

**Fatigued on account of the labor of love, Radha sleeps on Syama’s chest as though She were a lightning bolt sewn by Cupid on a dark cloud.**

*suptam “pāaadi pibadi cāssam” ity ādi. nidrā-suptayor ayaṁ bhedaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**An example of supti is verse 5.42. The difference between nidra (sleep, sleepiness) and supti (dreaming) is that the latter involves dreaming (or day-dreaming).**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: Cupid is the tailor (Subodhini). This is the implied metaphor that completes the set of metaphors. That constitutes an eka-desa-vivarti rupaka (partial set of metaphors) (8.68). Here the overall rupaka ornament facilitates the utpreksa ornament (fanciful assumption) (a lightning sewn on a cloud).

**23. Vimarśa**

### 5.293

*vimarśaḥ,*  
*śritaḥ kim anyāṁ kiṁ vāsya saṅketa-sthala-vismṛtiḥ*  
*kiṁ vāham iva viklāntaḥ premṇeti vimamarśa sā*

**Перевод:**

**She thought: “Did He go out with another girl, did He forget the place of the rendezvous, or did He, like Me, become wearied due to love?”**

**Комментарий:**

Traditionally, the vyabhicari-bhava is called vibodha, not vimarsa, and signifies “waking from sleep”. Rupa Gosvami uses this meaning only for srngara-rasa (Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu 2.4.189) and calls itprabodha (Ujjvala-nilamani 13.103). In other contexts, he also calls it bodha and mostly interprets “awakening” in the figurative sense of “having a realization”: atha bodhah—avidya- moha-nidrader dhvamsodbodhah prabuddhata (Bhakti-rasamrta- sindhu 2.4.179).

The above verse illustrates vitarka (conjecture) (5.300). Ahead, Kavi Karnapura follows Visvanatha Kaviraja’s definition that vitarka is based on samsaya (doubt), but Rupa Gosvami says vitarka is based on either vimarsa (reflecting upon the cause) or samsaya—atha vitarkah, sa vimarsad yatha... samsayad yatha (Ujjvala-nilamani 13.73-74); vimarsat samsayades ca vitarkas tuha ucyate (Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu 2.4.132). Thus the verse features both aspects of vitarka. In the elaboration of verse 318, Kavi Karnapura says vitarka is involved, implicitly referring to the samsaya aspect of it, but in the elaboration of verse 322, the vitarka he refers to once again involves both aspects.

Visvanatha Kaviraja’s example of vibodha is a verse by Magha:

*cira-rati-parikheda-prāpta-nidrā-sukhānāṁ*  
*caramam api śayitvā pūrvam eva prabuddhāḥ*  
*aparicalita-gātrāḥ kurvate na priyāṇām*  
*aśithila-bhuja-cakrāśleṣa-bhedaṁ taruṇyaḥ*

**“Although they fell asleep after their lovers, the young women woke up first. Not moving their bodies, they did not unclasp the tight embrace of their lovers’ arms. Their lovers were happily sleeping as a result of the lengthy exertion of love.” (Sisupala- vadha 11.13)**

**25. Amarṣa**  
**26. Avahitthā**

### 5.294

*kopo ’vahitthā ca yathā,*  
*uttiṣṭha mucyatāṁ kṛṣṇa caraṇa-graha-nigrahaḥ*  
*naivāsmi kupitā nāpi bhavān mayy aparādhyati*

**Перевод:**

**Get up, Krsna. Stop taking a hold of My feet. I am not angry, and You did not offend Me.**

**Комментарий:**

Pique (mana, or irsya) is included in amarsa (anger, indignation): irsyamarse (Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu 2.4.194). The end of the verse exemplifies concealment (avahittha).

**27.   Ugratā**

### 5.295

*ugratā,*  
*dhik prema bhavataḥ kṛṣṇa vakṣasaḥ sahajaḥ sakhā*  
*yat pādālaktakais tasyāḥ kaustubho ’py adharī-kṛtaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

dhik—fie; prema—on love; bhavatah—your; krsna—O Krsna; vaksasah—of the chest; sahajah—natural; sakha—the friend; yat—because of which \[love\]; pada—on the feet; alaktakaih—due to much lac; tasyah—her; kaustubhah—the Kaustubha jewel; api— even; adhari-krtah—was made low.

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, shame on Your love. Because of it, she put the profuse lac of her feet on You, and so the Kaustubha, the natural companion of Your chest, lost its eminent status.**

**28.   Unmāda**

### 5.296

*unmādaḥ,*  
*itas tatas tvāṁ paśyāmi pāṇibhyāṁ na tu labhyase*  
*kim indrajālaṁ jānāsi rādhe kiṁ vā mama bhramaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Radha, I see You here and there, but I cannot catch You with My hands. Is this witchcraft or My delusion?**

### 5.297

*ayaṁ tu bahudhā bhavati. tathā ca,*  
*bhāvāntara-samāveśād ukti-vaicitryato ’pi ca*  
*uttaraṅgatayāṅgitvād unmādo bahudhā mataḥ*  
*tatra pralāpa ālāpaḥ saṁlāpo vipralāpakaḥ*  
*anulāpaḥ supralāpaḥ parilāpo vilāpakaḥ*  
*apalāpaḥ pratīlāpo vaicitryaṁ daśadhā girām (158-159)*

**Перевод:**

**Unmada (deranged state) occurs in a variety of ways. The explanation is this: Unmada has various subcategories because of an absorption in another mood, because of the amazingness of expression and because it is the main thing given that it has eminent waves. The ten types of amazingness of expression are: pralapa, alapa, samlapa, vipralapa, anulapa, supralapa, parilapa, vilapa, apalapa, and pratilapa.**

*ūhyāny udāharaṇāni.*

**Перевод:**

**Examples can be looked into.**

**Комментарий:**

Rupa Gosvami calls this group “citra-jalpa ” and says they are illustrated in the “Song of the Bee” (Bhagavatam 10.47.12-21) (Ujjvala-nilamani 14.197). Rupa Gosvami introduced citra- jalpa in poetical theory (considering that Ujjvala-nilamani was composed before Alankara-kaustubha). His categories of citra- jalpa are called: prajalpa, parijalpa, vijalpa, ujjalpa, samjalpa, avajalpa, abhijalpa, ajalpa, pratijalpa and sujalpa (Ujjvala- nilamani 14.196).

The ten kinds of citra-jalpa are different from the twelve vacika anubhavas (verbal reactions): alapa, vilapa, samlapa, pralapa, anulapa, apalapa, sandesa, atidesa, apadesa, upadesa, nirdesa and vyapadesa (Ujjvala-nilamani 11.78-104). Traditionally, these ones are listed after the alankaras and the udbhasvaras.

Rupa Gosvami classes citra-jalpa in his category called divyonmada (Ujjvala-nilamani 14.190): Divyonmada is a form of vipralambha (separation). Rupa Gosvami says divyonmada is more intense than unmada (Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu 2.4.85). For the most part, unmada is a type of vipralambha (5.65): unmado hrd-bhramah praudhanandapad-virahadi-jah (Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu 2.4.79).

**29.  Vyādhi**

### 5.298

*vyādhiḥ,*  
*bhramo dāhas tathonmādo vardhante yad anukṣaṇam*  
*ādhir evāviyukto ’pi vyādhir asyāḥ sphuṭo ’bhavat*

**Пословный перевод:**

bhramah—delusion; dahah—burning; tatha—and; unmadah— derangement; vardhante—increase; yat—because; anuksanam— every moment; adhih—mental pain; eva—only; aviyuktah— incessant (“not connected with a separation”); api—(used for emphasis) (or although); vyadhih—ailment; asyah—her; sphutah— clear; abhavat—became.

**Перевод:**

**Since her delusion, burning and derangement increase at every moment, her mental pain, incessant to boot, became an obvious ailment.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: As a literal double meaning: Although her mental pain (adhi = manah-plda) was not connected with the prefix vi (aviyukto ’pi = vi-upasargena ayukto ’pi ), it became an ailment (vyadhi); this is the virodha ornament (semblance of a contradiction).

**30.  Mati**

### 5.299

*matiḥ,*  
*gokulendra-kumāras tvaṁ guṇa-ratnākaraḥ svayam*  
*vaktuṁ kartum abhijño ’si tvayi kā caturāyatām*

**Перевод:**

**You, the prince of Gokula, naturally are a mine of qualities. You are eloquent and efficient. So which girl can look smart in Your eyes?**

**Комментарий:**

Mati denotes arriving at a meaning after due consideration: matir vicarottham artha-nirdharanam (Locana-rocam 13.79). In bhakti- rasa other than srngara, the consideration is often based on the scriptures: sastradnam vicarottham artha-nirdharanam matih (Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu 2.4.140).

**31.   Vitarka**

### 5.300

*vitarkaḥ,*  
*kiṁ pīyūṣaṁ kim u viṣaṁ kiṁ himaṁ kim u vānalaḥ*  
*abhūt kṛṣṇānurāgo ’syāṁ virodhi-dvaya-dharmakaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Is it nectar or poison? Is it ice or fire? In her occurred love for Krsna, which has opposite pairs of attributes.**

**Комментарий:**

The verse begins with the sandeha ornament (poetical doubt) (8.62).

**33. Trāsa**

### 5.301

*trāsaḥ,*  
*uccair garjati meghaughe rādhā cakita-locanā*  
*trasyantī mādhavaṁ kaṇṭhe bhujābhyāṁ pariṣasvaje*

**Перевод:**

**When a mass of rainclouds loudly rumbles, fickle-eyed Radha becomes alarmed and embraces Madhava on the neck with both arms.**

### 5.302

*athaiṣām aṅgāṅgi-bhāvatve dig-darśanaṁ yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**The vyabhicari-bhavas can assume a relation of “principal and subordinate” among themselves. The general idea is shown:**

*āgacchan mām abhūḥ kṛṣṇa parāsaktaḥ pathīti mām*  
*kevalaṁ nāyaśaḥ praiti tvāṁ cety āśaṅki me manaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Dear Krsna, that You, having come in my presence, are attracted to another girl on the path is a dishonor which affects not just me, but You too. I am concerned about this.**

*atra pūrvārdhe glāni-bhāvo ’ṅgī śaṅkā tv aṅgam.*

**Перевод:**

**Here, glani (weakness) in the first half of the verse is the main element, and sanka (apprehension) is subordinate.**

**Комментарий:**

Usually glani refers to weakness of body (glanir vikrtir akrteh) (5.262), but it can also be weakness caused by worrying: adhina yatha (Ujjvala-nilamani 13.17): raty-ayasa-manastapa-ksut- pipasadi-sambhava, glanih (Sahitya-darpana 3.170).

### 5.303

*evam,*  
*sarvatra samavartitvaṁ yuktam eva mahātmanām*  
*mayy eva samavartitvaṁ nānyatra puruṣottama*

**Перевод:**

**It is proper for great souls to be samavartin (impartial) at all times. You, Purusottama, are samavartin (Yama) only toward Me, not toward any other girl.**

*atra mati-bhāvo ’ṅgī asūyāṅgam.*

**Перевод:**

**Here mati (thoughtfulness) is predominant and asuya (fault­finding) is subordinate.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: Some girl in a pique speaks to Krsna. “Samavartin” is a name of Yama, according to Amara-kosa (1.1.61); the sense is He afflicts her.

### 5.304

*evam ekasyāṅgino bahūny aṅgāni bhavanti. yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**Similarly, sometimes one vyabhicari is predominant and others are secondary. For example:**

*iyaṁ gāḍhotkaṇṭhā viṣama-viṣa-digdheva hṛdi me*  
*prasūneṣor bhagnā viśikha-phalikeva sthitavatī*  
*ato me pratyaṅgaṁ jvalayati tudaty ākulayate*  
*dhunīte muṣṇīte jaḍayati ca sañcarvayati ca*

**Пословный перевод:**

iyam—this; gadha—deep; utkantha—longing; visama—dangerous; visa—with poison; digdha—smeared; iva—as if; hrdi—in the heart; me—my; prasuna-isoh—of Cupid (“his arrows are flowers”); bhagna—broken; visikha—of an arrow; phalika—the arrowhead; iva—like; sthitavatl—it stayed; atah—therefore; me— my; prati-angam—each limb; jvalayati—it burns; tudati—strikes; akulayate—disturbs; dhumte—shakes; musmte—steals; jadayati— numbs; ca—and; sancarvayati—chews; ca—and.

**Перевод:**

**My deep longing for Krsna stayed in my heart as if it were a broken arrowhead of one of Cupid’s arrows, an arrowhead which is as if smeared with a dangerous poison. Therefore it burns, bruises, troubles, shakes, robs, numbs, and masticates all my body parts.**

*atra smṛti-bhāvo ’ṅgī, moha-capalatā-glāni-jaḍatā-prabhṛtīny aṅgāni. aṅgatvena naitad bhāva-śābalyam.*

**Перевод:**

**Here smrti is predominant, and moha (acute bewilderment), capalata (restlessness), glani (weakness), jadata (indolence) and so on are subordinate. There is no bhava-sabalya because some are subordinate.**

**Комментарий:**

Alternatively, even by Kavi Kamapura’s definitions the predominant element here is vyadhi (ailment), which can include pain in the heart: hrd-vyathadikah vyadhi (5.262). Rupa Gosvomi says vyadhi is the mood that arises from what is usually known as vyadhi (sickness).

“Longing” (the word utkantha in the verse) is included in the vyabhicari-bhava called autsukya (eagerness) (5.262): autsukye kutukotkanthe, “Kutuka (curiosity) and utkantha are included in autsukya” (Bhakti-rasamrta-smdhu 2.4.195). Ahead, Kavi Karnapura refers to utkantha as a vyabhicari (5.326).

*vibhūṣyamāṇā vṛṣabhānu-putrī*  
*uro-gate nīla-maṇīndra-hāre*

ali-janaih—by the girlfriends; mandana-keli-kale—at the time of the pastime of decoration; vibhusyamana—who was being adorned; vrsabhanu-putri— Vrsabhanu’s daughter; urah-gate— went on the chest; nila-manindra-hare—when the necklace of blue diamonds; svinna—perspiring; sa-kampa—trembling; pulaka- akula—pervaded by horripilation; asit—became.

**There is a rise of joy.**

**Комментарий:**

Remembrance (of Krsna) is implied at first: mla-manmdra-hare vaksah-sthala-gate sati sri-krsna-smarandt svinnety-adi. (Subodhini)

**Bhāva-praśama**

### 5.306

*praśamo yathā,*  
*mlānāsi kiṁ preyasi māmakīnaṁ*

*spṛśann idaṁ svastham iti sma kṛṣṇo*  
*bravīti sā namra-mukhī babhūva*

**Пословный перевод:**

mlana asi kim—why are You languid?; preyasi—O beloved; mamakinam—My; hrd—heart; prccha—ask; prcchami—I ask; tat—it; iti—(end of quotation); urah—chest; asyah—Her; sprsan— while touching; idam—this; sva-stham—healthy (“abiding in itself”); iti—in this way; sma—(used for expressing the past); krsnah—Krsna; braviti—He says; sa— She; namra-mukhi— one whose face is lowered; babhuva—became.

**Перевод:**

**Radha, My love, why are You languid? “Ask My heart.” Touching Her chest, Krsna said: “I am asking it... It is healthy (svastha) (as a double meaning: It stays by itself).” She lowered Her face.**

*atra viṣāda-praśamaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**There is a cessation of despondency.**

**Bhāva-śābalya**

### 5.307

*śābalyaṁ yathā,*  
*krodhāndhā guravo janās taralitaṁ durvāram etan mano*  
*marma-ccheda-karī khalokti-racanā ramyaḥ sa vaṁśī-svanaḥ*  
*kīnāśo bhavaneśvaras trijagatī-lāvaṇya-lakṣmī-patiḥ*  
*premānanda-rasaḥ sa eva tanumān kṛṣṇaḥ kim īhe sakhi*

**Перевод:**

**The elders are blinded by anger, my fickle mind is hard to control, the manner of the wicked people’s remarks cuts to the quick, the sound of the flute is alluring, my husband is cruel, and Krsna, the proprietor of the excellence of the loveliness of the three worlds, is the personification of the Rasa of the bliss of love. Sakhi, what can I do?**

*atra bhaya-capalatā-śaṅkā-harṣāsūyautsukyāni pṛthak pṛthag eva sthitāni.*

**Перевод:**

**Here these vyabhicans take place and exist separately from one another: bhaya (fear), capalata (restlessness), sanka (apprehension), harsa (joy), asuya (fault-finding) and autsukya (desire).**

**Bhāva-sandhi**

### 5.308

*atha sandhiḥ, “mlānāsi kiṁ preyasi” ity-ādau caturtha-pādārdhe “sā namra-mukhī babhūva” iti viṣāda-nirgame lajjāgamaḥ, anayoḥ sandhiḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**An example of bhava-sandhi is in verse 306, where “She lowered Her face” signifies the rise of bashfulness while despondency was ceasing. There is a junction (sandhi) of the two. Other examples are shown:**

### 5.309

*yathā vā,*  
*suciram anucarībhiḥ pāṭhitāṁ kṛṣṇa-gāthāṁ*  
*sadasi śuka-vadhūbhiḥ śṛṇvatī gīyamānām*  
*praṇaya-sadayam ekaṁ āsu vinyasyatīyaṁ*  
*cakita-cakitam anyan netram āsye gurūṇām*

**Пословный перевод:**

suciram—for a long time; anucaribhih—by female ttendants; pathitam—recited; krsna-gatham—Krsna’s song; sadasi—in the assembly; suka-vadhubhih—by female parrots; srnvati—while listening to; giyamanam—being sung; pranaya-sadayam—in a manner of having compassion due to tenderness; ekam—one \[eye\]; asu—on them; vinyasyati—places; iyam—She; cakita-cakitam—in a manner of being more afraid than afraid; anyat netram—the other eye; asye—on the face; gurunam—of the elders.

**Перевод:**

**While listening to Krsna’s ballad sung by the female parrots for a long time and read by the female attendants in the gathering, with compassion due to tenderness She directs one eye to the parrots, and out of fright She directs the other to Her elders’ faces.**

*atrautsukya-trāsayoḥ sandhiḥ. ete cokta-prakārāḥ svayaṁ vyaṅgyā api bhāvāntara-vyañjakāḥ syuḥ. yathā “kvāhaṁ gopa-vadhūr” ityādau dainyādibhiḥ pratipada-vyaṅgyair bhāvair avahitthā-bhāva eva vyajyate.*

**Перевод:**

**This is a junction of autsukya (desire) and trasa (sudden fear).**

**Moreover, although the vyabhicari-bhavas are automatically implied in those various ways, they can suggest another vyabhicari. In verse 4.7, for instance, the vyabhicari called avahittha (concealment) is implied by dainya (meekness) and by other vyabhicaris, which are implied at every step.**

**Комментарий:**

Like any other implied sense, a vyabhicari-bhava is implied either eminently (first-rate), not so eminently (second-rate), or obviously (third-rate).

### 5.310

*yathā vā,*

*na sāvadhānā sva-nakheṣv asīti*  
*nanāndur agre nijagāda gopī*

**Пословный перевод:**

na—not; abhyanjaniyam—should be massaged; sakhi—O friend; me—my; bhavatya—by you; na—not; udvartaniyam—should be rubbed; ca—and; vapuh—body; kada api—never; na—not; savadhana—careful; sva-nakhesu—about your nails; asi—you are; iti—(end of citation); nananduh—of the sister of the husband; agre—in front; nijagada—spoke; gopi—a cowherd girl.

*atra sva-gātra-lagna-nakha-kṣata-gopanaṁ praty avahitthā vyaṅgyā, tayā ca na me gṛha-pateḥ saṅgaḥ kadāpy abhūt yenaitat sambhāvanīyam, tena kṛṣṇa-saṅga-jam eveti vrīḍā. tenaite vyaṅgyā vyaṅgyāntara-vyañjakāś ca bhavantīti.*

**Перевод:**

**The avahittha vyabhicari is implied: She is concealing the nail marks on her body. And that suggests the vrida vyabhicari (bashfulness), in this way: “I did not have intercourse with my husband, so the nail marks cannot posssibly be explained that way. Therefore my nail marks occurred while sleeping with Krsna.”**

**Thus here also it is shown that the vyabhicaris are implied and can hint at another implied sense.**

### 5.311

*atha prastāra-prakāreṇoktānāṁ ṣoḍaśa-vidhānāṁ śābalyānāṁ bhedān āha. tatra sandhy-uttarāḥ—u pra śa sa,*

**Перевод:**

**Now the sixteen categories of sabalya, enounced in the manner of a sequence (5.264-266), will be described. Of those, this illustrates the first variety in sandhi-uttara (the four which end with bhava-sandhi): udaya-prasama-sabalya-sandhi,**

*pādaṁ muñca vimuñca mānini ruṣaṁ pratyehi ruṇ me gatā*  
*śrī-gopendra-sute svabhāva-kuṭile kā roṣam ākāṅkṣati*  
*ity anyonya-kathāsu keśi-mathane bhūyaḥ padaṁ dhitsati*  
*śraddhādhikya-dhṛtena tat-kara-yugenāsyaṁ rudaty apy adhāt*

**Пословный перевод:**

padam—the foot; munca—give up; vimunca—give up; manini—O girl in a pique; rusam—anger; pratyehi—you should know; rut— anger; me—my; gata—is gone; sri-gopa-indra-sute—when the beautiful son of the king of cowherds; svabhava-kutile—who is crooked by nature; ka—which girl?; rosam—anger; akanksati— wants (or needs); iti—in this way; anyonya—mutual; kathasu— during verbal exchanges; kesi-mathane—when Krsna (“the crusher of Kesi”); bhuyah—again; padam—the foot; dhitsati—wanted to hold; sraddha—desire; adhikya—with much; dhrtena—held; tat- kara-yugena—by means of his pair of hands; asyam—the face; rudati—she is weeping; api—even; adhat—held.

**Перевод:**

**“Let go of my feet.” “Huffy girl, give up your anger.” “You should know that my anger is gone. Which girl needs anger when the beautiful prince of cowherds is crooked by nature?” Given that Krsna still wanted to clasp her feet during their verbal exchange, with tearful eyes she took His hands, which she held with great desire, and placed them on her face.**

*atra “pādaṁ muñca” ity amarṣodayaḥ, “vimuñca mānini ruṣam” iti kṛṣṇa-vākyākūtena “ruṇ me gatā” iti roṣa-praśamaḥ, tataḥ “śrī-gopendra-sute” iti matiḥ, “svabhāva-kuṭila” ity asūyā, “kā roṣam ākāṅkṣati” ity avahitthā. ebhiḥ śābalyam. “śraddhā” ityādinautsukyam, “rudati” iti dainyam. anayoḥ sandhiḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**There is a rise of indignation (amarsa bhavodaya) in “Let go of my feet.” In “My anger is gone”, there is a cessation of anger (rosa bhava-prasama) due to the purpose of Krsna’s words “Huffy girl, give up your anger.” Afterward, there is a sabalya of these three: mati (thoughtfulness) in “the beautiful prince of cowherds”, asuya (fault-finding) in “crooked by nature”, and avahittha (concealment) in “Which girl needs anger?” Then there is a sandhi of these two: autsukya (desire) in “She held His hands with great desire”, and dainya (meekness) in “tearful”.**

### 5.312

*atha śa u pra sa,*  
***(śābalya, udaya, praśama, sandhi)***

*he mugdhākṣi pariṣvajasva kaṭhinā vajrād api tvaṁ guṇās*  
*te te te kva gatā iti kṣaṇam abhūt tūṣṇīṁ tato nirvṛtaḥ*  
*sphūrtyānanda-layena tena mahatā svābhāvikenāpy aho*  
*tad-viccheda-davoṣmaṇā ca yugapad dvedhābhibhūto hariḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

he mugdha-aksi—O girl with lovely eyes; parisvajasva—embrace; kathinah—hard; vajrat—than a thunderbolt; api—even; tvam— you; gunah—qualities; te te—those various ones; te—of yours; kva—where?; gatah—went; iti—(end of citation); ksanam—for a moment; abhut—he became; tusnim—silent; tatah—after that; nirvrtah—happy; sphurtya—by a vision; ananda-layena—by a mergence in bliss; tena—by that \[mergence\]; mahata—great; svabhavikena—natural; api—even; aho—how amazing; tat- viccheda—of separation from her; dava—of the fire; usmana— by the heat; ca—and; yugapat—simultaneously; dvedha—in two ways; abhibhutah—was overcome; harih—Hari.

**Перевод:**

**\[Krsna feels the pang of separation:\]**

**“Girl with lovely eyes, give me a hug. You’re even harder than a thunderbolt. Where did all those qualities of Yours go?” Hari remained silent for a moment. Then He blissed out by having a vision of Her. How amazing, He was overcome in two ways at once: by a mergence in bliss and by the heat of the fire of separation from Her.**

*atra “pariṣvajasva” ity autsukyam, “kaṭhinā” ity-ādy asūyā, “te te guṇāḥ” iti smṛtiḥ, tribhiḥ śavalatā. “tūṣṇīṁ” iti jaḍatodayaḥ. “tato nirvṛtaḥ sphūrtyā” iti pūrva-pūrva-bhāva-praśamaḥ. tataḥ sphūrty-anantaraṁ “ānanda-layena” “viccheda-davoṣmaṇā” ca “dvedhābhibhūtaḥ” iti harṣa-viṣādayoḥ sandhiḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**There is a sabalya of these three: autsukya (desire) in “Give me a hug”, asuya (fault-finding) in “You’re hard”, and smrti in “those qualities of Yours.” There is a beginning of indolence (jadata bhavodaya) in “He became silent.” The words “Then He blissed out by having a vision” signal the cessation of the previous vyabhicaris. After the vision, there is a sandhi of these two, both referred to in “overcome in two ways” as follows: harsa (joy) in “a mergence in bliss”, and visada (dejection) in “the heat of the fire of separation”.**

### 5.313

*pra śa u sa,*  
***(praśama, śābalya, udaya, sandhi)***

*gato me santāpo bhavati hi manasy āgata iva*  
*priyaṁ te hā kaṣṭaṁ manasi katham adyāgata iti*  
*puraḥ paścāt pārśve manasi ca sadaiveti pulakiny*  
*abhūd rādhā paścād amṛta-viṣa-nadyoḥ kim aviśat*

**Пословный перевод:**

gatah—is gone; me—my; santapah—affliction; bhavati—O you; hi—indeed (or because); manasi—in the mind; agatah—has arrived; iva—as if; priyam—lover; te—your; ha—aah; kastam— the hardship; manasi—in the mind; katham—how?; adya—now; agatah—he has come; iti—(end of citation); purah—in front; pascat—behind; parsve—at the side; manasi—in the mind; ca— and; sada—always; eva—only; iti—therefore; pulakim— with gosse bumps; abhut—became; radha—Radha; pascat—afterward; amrta-visa-nadyoh—in the two rivers of nectar and poison; kim— why?; avisat—entered.

**Перевод:**

**“I saw Krsna. My pain is gone.” “Girlfriend, You mean Your lover as if came in Your mind.” “Aah. But why do you say He as if came in My mind? He’s always in front of Me, at My back, at My side and in My mind.” Radha felt an upsurge of goosebumps. But afterward why did She enter both a river of nectar and a river of poison?**

*atra sphūrtyā svāsthyānubhave “gato me santāpaḥ” iti glāneḥ praśamaḥ. tataḥ sakhī-vākyānantaraṁ “hā kaṣṭam” iti viṣādaḥ. “manasi katham” ity-ādi sakhīṁ praty asūyā, “puraḥ paścād” ity unmādaḥ. ebhiḥ śābalyam. “pulakinī” iti harṣodayaḥ. “amṛtaviṣa-nadyoḥ” iti harṣa-mohayoḥ sandhiḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**There is a cessation of weakness (glani bhava-prasama) in “My pain is gone”, given that She was in good spirits again by having such a vision. Then there is a sabalya of these three: visada (dejection) in “Aah”, asuya (fault-finding) directed at her friend in “But why do you say He as if came in My mind?”, and unmada (derangement) in “He is always in front of Me, at My back” and so on. There is a rise of joy (harsa bhavodaya) in “She had goosebumps.” There is a sandhi of harsa (joy) and moha (acute bewilderment) in “She entered a river of nectar and a river of poison”.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: She alternately entered both rivers when Her unmada was halfway: Her joy occurred due to meeting Him by a lack of proper judgement, and her bewilderment (moha) (or dejection, visada) took place due to separation from Him by properly reflecting upon the situation. The river of nectar represents the adventitious bliss derived by the unmada, and the river of poison represents the real pain of separation.

### 5.314

*pra u śa sa,*  
***(praśama, udaya, śābalya, sandhi)***

*paścād etya śanair ariṣṭa-mathanas tāṁ sasvaje sāhasāt*  
*tat-saṁsparśa-rasena sā smita-mukhī sadyo ’vicārād abhūt*  
*ālībhyaḥ pariśaṅkayāruṇa-mukhī dhig dhūrtatāṁ dhūrta te*  
*dhiṅ meti tvarayāpasārita-tanur vyāvṛtya tūṣṇīṁ sthitā*

**Пословный перевод:**

pascat—from behind; etya—approaching; sanaih—slowly; arista- mathanah—Krsna (“the pulverizer of Arista”); tam—her; sasvaje— embraced; sahasat—by force; tat-samsparsa—of touching him; rasena—by the enjoyment; sa—she; smita-mukhi—she on whose mouth is a smile; sadyah—at once; avicarat—after not considering; abhut—became; alibhyah—the friends; parisankaya—due to fearing; aruna-mukhi—red-faced; dhik—fie; dhurtatam—on being a rake; dhurta—O rake; te—your; dhik ma—fie on me; iti—(end of citation); tvaraya—with speed; apasarita-tanuh—she by whom the body is made to go away; vyavrtya—after turning around; tusnim— silent; sthita—stayed.

**Перевод:**

**Slowly approaching from behind, Krsna embraced her by force. She immediately smiled due to the joy of His touch, but without considering the matter. Then, apprehensive of her friends’ reaction, she became red-faced and exclaimed: “Fie on Your rakeness, You rake, and fie on me.” She moved aside quickly, turned around and kept silent.**

*atra “smita-mukhī” ity amarṣa-praśamaḥ. “ālībhyaḥ pariśaṅkayā” iti śaṅkodayaḥ. “aruṇa-mukhī” iti “dhig dhūrtatām” iti “dhiṅ mā” iti punar amarṣogratā-glānibhiḥ śābalyam. “tvarayāpasāritatanuḥ” iti capalatā, “vyāvṛtya tūṣṇīṁ sthitā” iti dhairyam. anayoḥ sandhiḥ. ete sandhy-uttarāś catvāraḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**There is a cessation of indignation (amarsa bhava-prasama) in “She smiled”. There is a rise of apprehension (sanka bhavodaya) in “Apprehensive of her friends’ reaction”. There is a sabalya of these three: amarsa once again, in “red-faced”, ugrata (arrogance) in “Fie on Your rakeness” and glani (weakness) in “Fie on me”. There is a sandhi of these two: capalata (fickleness) in “She moved aside quickly” and dhairya (steadiness) in “She turned around and kept silent”. This concludes the four kinds of sandhy-uttara (those that end with bhava-sandhi).**

### 5.315

*sa u pra śa,*

*stambho jātaś ciram atha sakhī-sāntvanair bodha āsīt*  
*prātaḥ kṛṣṇo ’py ahaha mathurām ity apūrṇe janokte*  
*pratyāvṛttais tribhir atha punaḥ saiva pūrṇā babhūva*

akrurah—Akrura; adya—today; agatah—has arrived; iti— therefore; mukha-mlani—witheredness of the face; hrt-kampa— and shaking of the heart; bhajah—of she who had; stambhah— the paralysis; jatah—occurred; ciram—for a long time; atha— afterward; sakhi—of the friends; santvanaih—by the soothing words; bodhah—awakening; asit—occurred; pratah—in the morning; krsnah—Krsna; api—also; ahaha—alas; mathuram— \[will go\] to Mathura; iti—in this way; apurne—was incomplete; jana-ukte—when what was said by people; pratyavrttaih—which came back; tribhih—by the three; atha—afterward; punah—again; sa eva—that same girl; purna—filled; babhuva—became.

**Перевод:**

**When she heard “Akrura has arrived”, the girl’s face withered, her heartbeat became erratic, and she was stunned for a while. She was revived by her friends’ soothing words. But when someone said “Tomorrow morning, Krsna will go to...” without completing the sentence, she was again overcome by those three states.**

*atra “mukha-mlāni-hṛt-kampa-bhājaḥ” iti glāni-śaṅkayoḥ sandhiḥ. tataḥ “stambho jātaḥ” iti jaḍatodayaḥ. “sakhī-sāntvanaiḥ” iti tat-praśamaḥ. “pratyāvṛttais tribhiḥ” iti glāni-śaṅkā-jāḍyaiḥ śābalyam.*

**Перевод:**

**There is a sandhi of glani (weakness) and sanka (apprehension) in “Her face withered and her heartbeat became erratic”. Afterward, there is a rise of inertia (jadata bhavodaya) in “She was stunned.” They cease with “She was revived by her friends’ soothing words.” There is a sabalya of glani, sanka and jadata in “She was again overcome by those three states.”**

### 5.316

*sa pra u śa,*  
***(sandhi, praśama, udaya, śābalya)***

*meghāloke pulakita-tanur vidyud-ālokane sā*  
*vyābhugna-bhrūs tad-upaśamane suprasannānanenduḥ*  
*bhūyo vidyud-valaya-kalane lohitākṣī mṛgākṣī*  
*dhārāpāte rudita-malinī-bhāva-mūrcchāḥ prapede*

**Пословный перевод:**

megha—a cloud; aloke—in seeing; pulakita—is in horripilation; tanuh—she whose body; vidyut—lighning; alokane—in seeing; sa—she; vyabhugna—are bent; bhruh—she whosebrows; tat- upasamane—when there is the cessation of that (seeing lightning); suprasanna—she is content; anana-induh—she has a moon-like face; bhuyah—again; vidyut—of lightning; valaya—the multitude; kalane—in reckoning; lohita-aksi—red-eyed; mrga-aksi—doe- eyed girl; dhara—of a downpour; apate—where there is a fall; rudita—weeping; malini-bhava—being sullied; murcchah—and fainting; prapede—she obtained.

**Перевод:**

**When the doe-eyed girl sees a cloud, she has goosebumps. When she sees lightning, she frowns. When the lightning stops, her moon-like face is happy. When she again notices lightning, her eyes turn red. And when there is a downpour, she weeps, becomes gloomy and faints.**

*meghāloke kṛṣṇāgamana-bhramāt pulakita-tanutvena harṣaḥ. vidyud-ālokanena vipakṣa-ramaṇī-buddhyāsūyā, anayoḥ sandhiḥ. tad-upaśamane suprasannety asūyā-praśamaḥ. bhūya ity-ādinā lohitākṣīty amarṣodayaḥ. dhārāpāte sati megha evāyam iti ruditeti viṣādaḥ, malinī-bhāveti glāniḥ, mūrccheti mohaḥ. ebhiḥ śābalyam.*

**Перевод:**

**There is a sandhi of these two: harsa (joy), by having goosebumps due to mistaking a cloud for Krsna, and asuya (jealousy) by mistaking lightning for a rival ladylove. When the lightning stopped, the jealousy ceased (asuya bhava-prasama), in reference to “She is happy”. There is a rise of indignation (amarsa bhavodaya) in being red-eyed after she again perceived lightning. Then there is a sabalya of these three, because when the downpour occurred she realized that the cloud was just a cloud: visada (dejection) in “She wept”, glani (weakness) in “She became gloomy”, and moha (acute bewilderment) in “She fainted”.**

**Комментарий:**

Rupa Gosvami says mistaking one thing for another is unmada (Commentary 5.65).

### 5.317

*pra u sa śa,*  
***(praśama, udaya, sandhi, śābalya)***

*asākṣād eva tvaṁ bhavasi nahi sākṣād iti ruṣe*  
*prakupyantī kṛṣṇe gatavati nirāgasy api padam*  
*tvarātaṅka-vyagrā kapaṭam iti tasmin viditavaty*  
*aho nānā-bhāva-vyatikaravatīyaṁ vijayate*

**Пословный перевод:**

asaksat—not directly (not in His presence); eva—only; tvam— you; bhavasi—exist; nahi—not; saksat—directly; iti— (end of citation); ruse—at anger; prakupyanti—angry; krsne gatavati— when Krsna was going; niragasi—who had done no wrong; api— although; padam—to the foot; tvara—by haste; atanka—and by trepidation; vyagra—she is agitated; kapatam—fake; iti—in this way; tasmin viditavati—when He understood; aho—how amazing; nana-bhava—of various emotions; vyatikaravati— who has a mix; iyam—she; vijayate—is supereminent.

**Перевод:**

**“You activate yourself when He is not here, and you deactivate yourself when He is here.” Thus getting angry at her anger when offenseless Krsna reached her feet, she became nervous with butterflies in her stomach and with trepidation. Oh, how glorious is she who had a medley of emotions when He realized that Her mana is fake!**

*atra “sākṣān na bhavasi” iti prāg-jātasyāmarṣasya praśamaḥ. tato “ruṣe kupyantī” iti roṣaṁ prati kopodayaḥ. paścāt kṛṣṇa-pādapatane “tvarātaṅka-vyagrā” iti capalatā-śaṅkayoḥ sandhiḥ. tato “nānā-bhāva-vyatikara” iti vrīḍā-mada-smṛti-śaṅkā-trāsādibhiḥ śābalyam.*

**Перевод:**

**Indignation (amarsa) had occurred at first, and there is a cessation of it in “You deactivate yourself when He is here.” Afterward, in “getting angry at her anger”, there is a rise of anger (kopa bhavodaya) at anger.**

**Subsequently, there is a sandhi of restlessness (capalata) and apprehension (sanka) in “nervous with butterflies in her stomach and with trepidation”. After that, in “the medley of emotions”, there is a sabalya of vrida (embarrassment), mada (overexcitement), smrti (remembrance), sanka (apprehension), trasa (sudden fear) and so on.**

### 5.318

*u pra sa śa,*  
***(udaya, praśama, sandhi, śābalya)***

*gaṇḍe kuṇḍala-padmarāga-mahaso bimbaṁ prati preyasaḥ*  
*pārakyo ’dhara-rāga ity aruṇitāpāṅgī calaṁ vīkṣya tam*  
*snigdhākṣī dayito ruṣaṁ viditavān no veti dolāyitā*  
*nyañcad-vaktratayā vicārya ca mṛṣā mānaṁ dadhe rādhikā*

**Пословный перевод:**

gande—on the cheek; kundala—of the earring; padmaraga—of the ruby; mahasah—of the effulgence; bimbam—to the reflection (pratibimba); prati—in reference; preyasah—of the lover; parakyah—belonging to another; adhara-ragah—the redness of the lips (because of chewing betel nut); iti—therefore; arunita—are reddened; apangi—she the corners of whose eyes; calam—moving; viksya—after seeing; tam—that \[reflection\]; snigdha-aksi—she whose eyes are affectionate; dayitah—the lover; rusam—anger; viditavan—knew; no va—or not; iti—in this way; dolayita— swinging (mentally); nyancat—is bowing; vaktrataya—by being one whose face; vicarya—after considering; ca—and; mrsa—false; manam—pique; dadhe—did; radhika—Radhika.

**Radhika thought that the reflection of the ruby inlaid in Her lover’s earring dangling on His cheek was a redness from the lips of a rival girl. Therefore Her eyes reddened. But when She saw the reflection moving, She realized Her mistake, and so Her eyes became affectionate again. Then She wondered: “Does He know that I got angry just now?” Upon considering the matter with a bowed head, She implemented a false pique.**

*atra “gaṇḍe” ity ādināmarṣodayaḥ. “calaṁ vīkṣya” iti tasya praśamaḥ. “ruṣaṁ viditavān no vā” iti śaṅkā-vitarkābhyāṁ sandhiḥ. “nyañcad-vaktratayā” iti vrīḍā. “vicārya” iti matiḥ. “mṛṣā mānam” ity avahitthā. ebhiḥ śābalyam. ete catvāraḥ śabalottarāḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**There is a rise of indignation (amarsa bhavodaya) in the first sentence. In “She saw the reflection moving”, there is a cessation of the indignation. In “Does He know that I got angry just now?”, there is a sandhi of sanka (apprehension) and vitarka (conjecture). Then there is a sabalya of these three: vrida (bashfulness) in “with a bowed head”, mati (thoughtfulness) in “upon considering the matter”, and avahittha (concealment) in “false pique”. This concludes the four kinds of sabalyottara (those that end with bhava-sabalya).**

### 5.319

*u śa sa pra,*  
***(udaya, śābalya, sandhi, praśama)***

*priyāloke dṛṣṭiṁ namayati tam anyāṁ prati lasad-*  
*dṛśaṁ snigdhārakta-pracala-nayanā paśyati vadhūḥ*  
*punaḥ paśyaty asmin smita-pulaka-saṅgopana-parā*  
*haṭhāt tenāśliṣṭā sapadi gata-vāmyā samabhavat*

priya—by the lover; aloke—when there was seeing; drstim—the eye; namayati—she bows; tam—him; anyam—another girl; prati— toward; lasat—are shining; drsam—he whose eyes; snigdha- arakta-pracala-nayana—she whose eyes are affectionate, reddish, and fickle; pasyati—she sees; vadhuh—the young woman; punah— again; pasyati asmin—when he sees; smita—on smiling; pulaka— goosebumps; sangopana—and on concealing; para—she is intent (“she whose highest thing is”); hathat—by force; tena—by him; aslista—embraced; sapadi—at once; gata-vamya—one whose contrary mood is gone; samabhavat—she became.

**When he espied her, the young woman lowered her eyes. When she looked up, she caught him casting a splendid glance at another girlfriend, and so her eyes became simultaneously affectionate, reddened, and fickle. When he again beheld the young woman, she beamed a smile and tried to conceal her goosebumps. Hugged by him by force, she immediately lost her mood of contrariness.**

*atra “dṛṣṭiṁ namayati” iti vrīḍodayaḥ. “snigdhārakta-pracalanayanā” ity autsukya-krodha-capalatānāṁ śābalyam. mām anādṛtyānyāṁ paśyatīti krodhaḥ, “smita-pulaka” iti madaharṣayoḥ sandhiḥ. “sapadi gata-vāmyā” iti krodhādi-praśamaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**There is a rise of bashfulness in “She lowered her eyes”. There is a sabalya of desire, anger, and fickleness in “Her eyes became affectionate, reddened, and fickle.” The anger (implied from reddened eyes) took place because he disregarded the girl and looked at another girl. There is a sandhi of mada (overexcitement) and harsa (joy) in “She beamed a smile and had goosebumps.” In “She immediately lost her mood of contrariness”, there is a cessation of anger.**

### 5.320

*sa u śa pra,*  
***(sandhi, udaya, śābalya, praśama)***

*yad-āloke pūrvaṁ bhujaga iti sambhrānta-cakitā*  
*priyāgre tām eva srajam urasi sadyo vidadhatī*  
*sakhīṣu smerāsu bhrū-kuṭi-taralārakta-nayanā*  
*pariṣvaktā tena druta-viśada-cittā samajani*

yat—which \[garland\]; aloke—upon seeing; purvam—before; bhujagah—a snake; iti—in this way; sambhranta—due to a delusion; cakita—afraid; priya-agre—in front of the lover; tam eva srajam—that same garland; urasi—on the chest; sadyah—at once; vidadhati—she put; sakhisu—when her friends; smerasu—were smiling; bhru-kuti—on which there are frowns; tarala—are fickle; arakta—and are reddened; nayana—she whose eyes; parisvakta— embraced; tena—by him; druta—quickly; visada—is clear; citta— one whose mind; samajani—became.
