**The sakhis offered her a garland, but she became frightened by mistaking it for a snake (“In separation from him, the garland will afflict me like a snake”). In her lover’s presence, however, she at once put the garland on her chest. Her sakhis found this amusing, but she looked at them and frowned with fickle and reddish eyes. He hugged her, and her mind quickly became serene.**

*atra “sambhrānta-cakitā” iti trāsa-capalatābhyāṁ sandhiḥ. “priyāgre tām eva srajam urasi sadyo vidadhatī” ity autsukyodayaḥ. “bhrū-kuṭi-taralārakta-nayanā” iti bhrū-kuṭir ity asūyā, taraleti capalatā, ārakteti krodhas taiḥ śābalyam. “druta-viśada-cittā” iti praśamaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**There is a sandhi of trasa (sudden fear) and capalata (fickleness) in “She became frightened due to the mistake.” There is a rise of desire in “She at once put the garland on her chest.” As regards “She frowned with fickle and reddish eyes”, there is a sabalya of asuya (fault-finding) in “She frowned”, capalata in “fickle” and krodha (anger) in “reddened”. There is a cessation of those in “Her mind quickly became serene”.**

### 5.321

*śa sa u pra,*  
***(śābalya, sandhi, udaya, praśama)***

*māṁ paśyantyās tava kim aruṇābhugna-bhagnā dṛg-antā*  
*niṣpande ’trādhara-kisalaye gūḍha-lakṣyā vivakṣā*  
*hāso jātāṅkura iva kiyat tena citte pramodo*  
*vāmatvaṁ te bahir iti harer vāci rādhā jahāsa*

**Пословный перевод:**

mam—at me; pasyantyah—who are looking; tava—your; kim— whether; aruna—red; a-bhugna—slightly crooked; bhagnah— broken (intermittent); drg-antah—sidelong glances (“corners of the eyes”); nispande—are motionless; atra—now; adhara- kisalaye—given that the bud-like lips; gudha—subtly; laksya—can be perceived; vivaksa—what is desired to be expressed; hasah— smiling; jata-ankurah—one whose sprout has occurred; iva—as if; kiyat—somewhat; tena—therefore; citte—in the mind; pramodah— pleasure; vamatvam—being contrary; te—your; bahih—outside; iti—(end of citation); hareh—of Hari; vaci—when there was the speech; radha—Radha; jahasa—laughed.

**Перевод:**

**“Honey, why are the sidelong glances that You cast at Me red, slightly crooked, and intermittent? Given that Your bud-like lips are motionless, what You mean to say is too subtle to catch. Your heehaw has somewhat sprouted. Your mind must be blissed out. Sweetheart, Your mood of contrariness has come out.” Radha laughed when Hari said this.**

*atra aruṇeti kopaḥ, ābhugnety asūyā, bhagneti trapā, tābhiḥ śābalyam. niṣpandatva-gūḍha-vivakṣābhyāṁ dhṛti-capalatayoḥ sandhiḥ. “hāso jātāṅkuraḥ” iti harṣodayaḥ. “jahāsa” iti kopapraśamaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**There is a sabalya of these three: kopa (anger) in “red”, asuya (fault-finding) in “slightly crooked”, and trapa (bashfulness) in “intermittent”. There is a sandhi of dhrti (steadfastness) and capalata (fickleness) in regard to the motionless lips and to what is subtly meant to be said. There is a rise of joy in “Your heehaw has sprouted”. And there is a cessation of anger in “She laughed”.**

### 5.322

*sa śa u pra,*  
***(sandhi, śābalya, udaya, praśama)***

*tvaṁ me prāṇāḥ katham iva vibho tvāṁ vinā naiva varte*  
*nāhaṁ yā te vasati hṛdaye saiva te prāṇa-hetuḥ*  
*tvaṁ me nityaṁ vasasi hṛdaye nā na nety aśru-pūrṇāṁ*  
*kṛṣṇo dorbhyāṁ hṛdi vinidadhe sā visasmāra vāmyam*

**Перевод:**

**“You are My life.” “How so, Vibhu?” “I cannot live without you.” “Not me. She who is in Your heart is Your purpose in life.” “You are always in My heart.” “No, no, no.” Her eyes brimmed with tears. With both arms Krsna placed her on His chest, and she forgot all about her sulkiness.**

*atra “katham iva” iti vitarkaḥ. “vibho” ity asūyā. dvābhyāṁ sandhiḥ. “nāham” iti dainyam. “yā te vasati hṛdaye saiva” ity asūyā. “prāṇa-hetuḥ” ity ugratā, ebhiḥ śābalyam. “aśru-pūrṇām” ity autsukyodayaḥ. “visasmāra vāmyam” iti kopa-praśamaḥ. ete praśamottarāś catvāraḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**There is a sandhi of these two: vitarka (conjecture) in “How so?” and asuya (fault-finding mixed with derision) in “O Vibhu”. There is a sabalya of dainya (meekness) in “Not me”, asuya in “Only she who is in Your heart”, and ugrata (arrogance) in “She is Your purpose in life”. There is a rise of desire in “Her eyes brimmed with tears”. And there is a cessation of anger in “She forgot all about her sulkiness”. This concludes the four kinds of prasamottara (those that end with bhava-prasama).**

### 5.323

*sa śa pra u,*  
***(sandhi, śābalya, praśama, udaya)***

*kīdṛg-veṇum avīvado vraja-purīty āpṛṣṭa eva priyo*  
*rukmiṇyā vraja-keli-kautuka-kathā-saṁvedanāsaṁvidoḥ*  
*sandhau bandhura-mānasaḥ punar aho romāñca-netrāmbunī*  
*saṁvṛṇvan prakṛto babhūva sa punaḥ pāriplavātmābhavat*

**Пословный перевод:**

kldrk—of which kind; venum—a flute; avlvadah—you played (2.1 form of vad in the aorist tense in the causative); vraja-puri—in the town of Vraja; iti—in this way; aprstah—asked; eva—simply; priyah—the lover; rukminya—by Rukmini; vraja-keli-kautuka- katha-samvedana—of awareness of the topics of the joviality of the games in Vraja; asamvidoh—and a lack of awareness; sandhau— in the junction; bandhura—is wavy (or charming); manasah—he whose mind; punah—moreover; aho—how amazing; romanca— the goose-bumps; netra-ambunl and the water in the eyes; samvrnvan—covering; prakrtah—natural; babhuva—became; sah—he; punah—further; pariplava—is swimming (unsteady); atma—one whose mind; abhavat—became.

**Перевод:**

**Rukmini asked her lover: “Which kind of flute did You play in Vraja?” His mind fluctuated between the two states of ‘being aware of all the pleasant things to say about the fun in Vraja’ and ‘losing awareness’. Afterward, a wonder occurred: Returning to normal consciousness, He tried to conceal the tears in His eyes and His goosebumps. Then His heart wavered.**

*atra “vraja-keli-kautuka-kathā-saṁvedanāsaṁvidoḥ sandhau” iti smṛti-jaḍatayoḥ sandhiḥ. “romāñca” iti harṣaḥ. “netrāmbu” iti viṣādaḥ. “saṁvṛṇvan” ity avahitthā. taiḥ śābalyam. “prakṛto babhūva” iti tat-tat-praśamaḥ. “pāriplavātmā” ity autsukyodayaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**There is a sandhi of smrti (remembrance) and jadata (indolence) in the clause “between the two states of being aware of all the pleasant things to say about the fun in Vraja and losing awareness.” There is a sabalya of these three: harsa (joy) in “goosebumps”, visada (low spirits) in “tears in the eyes”, and avahittha (concealment) in “concealing”. There is a cessation of those in “He returned to normal consciousness.” And there is a rise of eagerness in “His heart wavered”.**

### 5.324

*śa sa pra u,*  
***(śābalya, sandhi, praśama, udaya)***

*likhiṣyāmīty agre sphurad-abhiniveśārta-taralā*  
*tato ’śru-snātākṣī dhig iti vidhi-nindāṁ vidadhatī*  
*avaṣṭabhya svāntaṁ prakṛtim iva yātā kṣaṇam asau*  
*likhantī prāṇeśaṁ śiva śiva visasmāra sakalam*

**Пословный перевод:**

likhisyami—I will write; iti—(end of citation); agre—at first; sphurat—is manifesting; abhinivesa—she whose absorption; arta—pained; tarala—and fickle; tatah—after that; asru-snata- aksi—she whose eyes are bathed by tears; dhik iti—in this way; vidhi-nindam—the criticism of fate; vidadhati—she did; avastabhya—making firm; sva-antam—the mind; prakrtim iva—as if; yata—obtained; ksanam—momentarily; asau—she; likhanti— writing; prana-isam—to the lord of her life; siva siva—alas, alas; visasmara—she forgot; sakalam—everything.

**Перевод:**

**\[A girl has the blues because her lover is very far away.\]**

**“I’ll write to Him.” At first, she was absorbed in the idea of doing this, but then she felt pain and became restless. Afterward her eyes brimmed with tears. “Darn” she said, thus rebuking fate. She made up her mind, as if regained her composure for a moment, and began writing to the hero of her life. But then, alas alas, she forgot everything.**

*atra “sphurad-abhiniveśa” iti smṛtiḥ. “ārta” ity āvegaḥ. “taralā” ity autsukyam. ebhiḥ śābalyam. “aśru-snātākṣī” iti viṣādaḥ. “dhig iti vidhi-nindāṁ” ity asūyā. tayoḥ sandhiḥ. “avaṣṭabhya svāntaṁ” ity-ādi praśamaḥ. “visasmāra sakalam” iti mohodayaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**There is a sabalya of these three: smrti in “being absorbed”, avega (mental flurry) in “She felt pain”, and autsukya (desire) in “restless”. There is a sandhi of these two: visada (dejection) in “Her eyes brimmed with tears” and asuya (fault-finding) in “‘Darn’ she said, thus rebuking fate”. There is a cessation of those in “She made up her mind” and so on. And there is a rise of moha (acute bewilderment) in “She forgot everything”.**

### 5.325

*pra sa śa u,*  
***(praśama, sandhi, śābalya, udaya)***

*viśrāntaḥ sakhi saṁśayaḥ sa ramate naikāpi tasya kṣapā*  
*vyarthety ālapana-prayoga-samaye kṛṣṇaṁ vilokyāgatam*  
*hṛṣṭā kiṁ śrutam aśrutaṁ kim athavety āśaṅkamānā namad-*  
*vaktrā tena vicumbitātha sumukhī spandena mandābhavat*

**Пословный перевод:**

visrantah—has ended; sakhi—O friend; samsayah—the doubt; sah—he; ramate—takes pleasure; na—not; eka—one; api—even; tasya—of his; ksapa—night; vyartha—is useless; iti—in this way; alapana-prayoga—the chatter was going on; samaye—at the time; krsnam—Krsna; vilokya—after seeing; agatam—who had come; hrsta—excited; kim—whether; srutam—it was heard; asrutam—it was not heard; kim—whether; athava—or; iti—in this way; asankamana—apprehensive; namat-vaktra—she whose face is bowing; tena—by him; vicumbita—kissed; atha—afterward; sumukhi—the pretty-faced girl; spandena manda—without tremor; abhavat—became.

**Перевод:**

**“No doubt, sakhi, He’s taking pleasure with some other girl. None of His nights passes in vain.” Seeing Krsna approaching just as she was saying this, she became overjoyed, but lowered her face, being apprehensive about whether He had heard her chatter. He kissed her. Then the pretty girl remained motionless.**

*atra “viśrāntaḥ sakhi saṁśayaḥ” iti vitarka-praśamaḥ. “sa ramate” ity asūyā. “naikāpi tasya kṣapā vyarthā” ity amarṣaḥ. anayoḥ sandhiḥ. “hṛṣṭā” iti harṣaḥ. “śrutam aśrutaṁ vā” iti vitarkaḥ. “āśaṅkamānā” iti śaṅkā. “namad-vaktrā” iti vrīḍā. ebhiḥ śābalyam. “spandena mandābhavat” iti jaḍatodayaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**There is a cessation of a conjecture (vitarka bhava-prasama) in “No doubt, sakhi.” There is a sandhi of these two: asuya (fault­finding) in “He is taking pleasure” and amarsa (indignation) in “None of His nights passes in vain.” There is a sabalya of these four: harsa (joy) in “overjoyed”, vitarka (conjecture) in “Did He hear something or not?”, sanka (apprehension) in “apprehensive,” and vrida (bashfulness) in “She lowered her face”. There is a rise of indolence in “She became motionless.”**

### 5.326

*śa pra sa u,*  
***(śābalya, praśama, sandhi, udaya)***

*mano rāga-jvālā-jvara-kavalitaṁ bhasmatu cirād*  
*ayaṁ premṇe baddho ’ñjalir ajani duḥkhasya vigamaḥ*  
*gurūṇām ākṣepaḥ khala-hasitam apy etu pṛthutām*  
*iti svālī-vṛnde rudati samarodīd atha vadhūḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

manah—the mind; raga—of love; jvala—of the burning; jvara— by the fever; kavalitam—consumed; bhasmatu—let it act like ashes; cirat—for a long time; ayam—this; premne—at love; baddhah—bound; anjalih—cupping of the hands; ajani—became; duhkhasya—of sorrow; vigamah—is the departure; gurunam—of elders; aksepah—the reprobation; khala—of miscreants; hasitam— the derision; api—and; etu—may it attain prthutam—a big size; iti—thus; sva-ali-vrnde—when the group of friends; rudati—was crying; samarodit—wept; atha—after that; vadhuh—the young woman.

**Перевод:**

**“Let my mind, consumed by the fever which is the burning of love, turn into ashes forever. My obeisances to love with folded hands brought my affliction to a close. Let the elders’ rebrobations, and even the lowlifes’ derision, increase. I don’t care.” Hearing this, her friends cried. Then the young woman broke down in tears.**

*“rāga” ity utkaṇṭhā, “jvālā” iti glāniḥ, “kavalitam” iti mohaḥ, “bhasmatu bhasmevācaratu” iti dainyam, ebhiḥ śābalyam. “ayaṁ premne baddho ’ñjalir ajani duḥkhasya vigamaḥ” iti autsukya-praśamaḥ. “gurūṇām ākṣepaḥ” iti śaṅkā. “khalahasitam” ity asūyā, anayoḥ sandhiḥ. “samarodīt” iti viṣādodayaḥ. ete udayottarāś catvāraḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**There is a sabalya of these four: utkantha (longing) in “love”, glani (weakness) in “the burning”, moha (acute bewilderment) in “consumed” and dainya (feeling miserable) in “Let it turn to ashes”. There is a cessation of autsukya (desire) in “My obeisances to love with folded hands brought my affliction to a close.” There is a sandhi of these two: sanka (apprehension) in “the elders’ rebrobations” and asuya (fault-finding) in “the lowlifes’ derision”. And there is a rise of visada (depression) in “She broke down in tears.” Here end the four kinds of udayottara (those that end with bhavodaya).**

### 5.327

*athālaṅkāra-sāṅkaryeṇa ye prakārā bhavanti, teṣām api digdarśanam. tatra “huṁ mātar” ity atra, “mātar” iti trāsaḥ, “dhūrteyam” ity asūyā, “āpa bhiyam” ity avahitthā. atra śābalyaṁ maugdhyālaṅkāra-saṅkīrṇam. teṣām api seṅgita-niriṅgitatvena punar yad dvaividhyam uktam, tatra niriṅgitam udāhṛtam, seṅgitasya dig-darśanaṁ kriyate. tatra “bāhuṁ dakṣiṇam ālikaṇṭha-valaye” ity-ādau seṅgito vilāsa-nāmālaṅkāraḥ. tatra ca “prauḍha-manoja-vibhrama-bharaiḥ śrānteva vibhrājate” iti śrama-garvayoḥ sandhiḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Now the varieties of a bhavodaya, etc., combined with an alankara of srngara will be summarily illustrated. This previous verse is a starting point: ““Hum, mother! Krsna, who’s in Your thoughts?” “Sweetie, only You are reflected in Me.” “No, no, she’s some other girl.” “If so, why would she try to emulate You?” “She must be a witch.” Saying so, fickled-eyed Radha stood aghast” (5.219). Here bhava-sabalya is mixed with the maugdhya alankara (feigned ignorance). The sabalya is the mix of these three: trasa (sudden fear) in “Mother”, asuya (fault­finding) in “She must be a witch”, and avahittha (concealment) in “She stood aghast”.**

**The combinations with an alankara have two categories, since the ecstatic symptoms are either mentioned or not (5.233). An example without an ecstatic symptom was shown above. Verse 5.242 illustrates a combination with an ecstatic symptom. The vilasa alankara (charming demeanor) occurs in that verse, and there is a sandhi of srama (fatigue) and garva (pride) in “as if she were fatigued due to the weight of Cupid’s distractions.”**

### 5.328

*evam udaya-śābalyādīnāṁ dig-darśanaṁ yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**The combinations of an alankara with a mix of bhavodaya and bhava-sabalya and so on can also occur. This is an instance with udaya and sabalya:**

*niścitaṁ parisamāpitam eva*  
*prema-śāstra-pariśīlanam āli*  
*śyāma-nāma katham adya gṛhītaṁ*  
*vṛttayo yad akhilāḥ samudīyuḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Sakhi, I have truly completed my study of the treatises on pure love. How can Syama’s name be taken now, since all these moods arise at once?**

*atra “akhilā vṛttayaḥ” iti sarva eva prāg-anubhūtā viṣāda vyādhi-glāny-unmādāmarṣāsūyādayaḥ samāna-kālam uditavantaḥ. evaṁ “śyāma-nāmni viratā bhava śāntiṁ, yāntu hanta hṛdayasya vikārāḥ” iti praśama-śābalyam.*

**Перевод:**

**Here, “all these moods” denotes all the ones experienced before, such as visada (dejection), vyadhi (ailment), glani (weakness), unmada (derangement), amarsa (anger), and asuya (fault­finding). And they arise at the same time.**

**In like manner, if the second half of the verse were changed as follows, it would illustrate a combination of prasama and sabalya: “Stop taking Syama’s name, and alas all the fluctuations of the heart shall come to nil.”**

### 5.329

*evaṁ sandhi-śābalyaṁ yathā*

**Перевод:**

**Similarly, an example of a mix of sandhi and sabalya:**

*unmāda-mohāv api dainya-cinte*  
*vitarka-śaṅke sama-kālam eva*  
*dviśo dviśas tasya kathā-prasaṅge*  
*pūrvānubhūtyā kuruto ’tiduḥkham*

**Пословный перевод:**

unmada-mohau—derangement and acute bewilderment; api—and; dainya-cinte—feeling miserable, and anxiety; vitarka-sanke— conjecture and apprehension; sama-kalam—at the same time; eva— only; dvisah dvisah—enemies and enemies; tasya—him; katha—of mentioning; prasange—on the occasion; purva-anubhutya—due to a previous experience; kurutah—the two make; atiduhkham—great sorrow.

**Перевод:**

**Derangement and acute bewilderment; miserableness and anxiety; and conjecture and apprehension—On hearing something about Him, these enemies in groups of two cause unhappiness right at that time, due to a previous experience.**

*“dviśo dviśa” ity avasthā-bhedāt. tathā hi, virahe “unmādamohau”, vipralabdhāvasthāyāṁ “dainya-cinte”, vāsakasajjāvasthāyāṁ “vitarka-śaṅke”, duḥkham eva kurutaḥ. tat tatprasaṅgaṁ tyajatety arthaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**The distributive sense in “dviso dvisah” serves to express difference among the states. The three pairs cause unhappiness as follows: “Derangement and acute bewilderment” in the state of viraha (i.e. virahotkanthita) (longing for the lover, who hasn’t showed up) (5.150), “miserableness and anxiety” in the state of vipralabdha (separation), and “conjecture and apprehension” in the state of vasaka-sajja (expecting the lover to show up). The sense is: “Therefore all of you should give up any such hearing.”**

### 5.330

*evaṁ sva-buddhi-kauśalyād anumeyāḥ subuddhibhiḥ*  
*grantha-gaurava-bhītyaiva mayā nodāhṛtāḥ pare*  
*anenaiva hi mārgeṇa kavayo bhāva-kovidāḥ*  
*vidadhyur bhāva-kāvyāni tenāyaṁ prakramaḥ kṛtaḥ (160-161)*

**Перевод:**

**By the skill of one’s inteligence in this way, other varieties can be inferred by the learned. I did not exemplify them out of fear of increasing the size of the treatise. May the poets who are conversant with emotion compose emotional poetry by the model described here. The procedure is perfected by that.**

*ity alaṅkāra-kaustubhe rasa-bhāva-tad-bheda-nirūpaṇo nāma pañcamaḥ kiraṇaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Thus ends the fifth ray in Alankara-kaustubha, entitled “a dissertation on rasa, bhava, and their varieties.”**

## Sixth Ray - The Qualities

### 6.1

*atha guṇa-vivecanaḥ. atha “guṇā mādhuryādyāḥ” iti kṛtoddeśasya guṇasya lakṣaṇa-parīkṣe kariṣyan prathamato lakṣaṇam āha—*

**Перевод:**

**To make both the definition of a guna, simply mentioned by name in: “Sweetness, harshness and softness are its qualities” (1.7), and the examination of it, at first he defines a quality (guna):**

*rasasyotkarṣakaḥ kaścid dharmo ’sādhāraṇo guṇaḥ*  
*śauryādir ātmana iva varṇās tad-vyañjakā matāḥ (1)*

**Пословный перевод:**

rasasya—of the rasa; utkarsakah—an enhancer; kascit—some; dharmah—attribute; asadharanah—uncommon; gunah—a guna; saurya-adih—such as heroism; atmanah—of the soul; iva—like; varnah—phonemes; tat-vyanjakah—revealers of that guna; matah—are considered.

**Перевод:**

**As a quality, such as bravery, enhances the soul, so a guna is some particular uncommon quality that enhances the rasa. Certain phonemes bring out a certain guna.**

*ātmana iti yathā śauryādikam ātmana eva, nākārasya, tathā mādhuryādikaṁ rasasyaiva, natvākāra-rūpayoḥ śabdārthayoḥ. na hy ayam ākāraḥ śūraḥ, sthūlatvād iti sad-dhetuḥ, asthūlasyāpi śūratva-darśanāt, yathā mahā-mataṅgaja-pañcānanayoḥ. yat tu vīrasū-sutayoḥ śiśu-yūnor ākāra-gatam eva śūratvam, tac ca vayaḥ-kṛtam eva. tena sa-vyabhicāra-doṣād ākārasya śauryādir guno na bhavati, kintu tasya vyañjaka ākāraḥ, varṇa-mayatvāt. ata utkarṣatvaṁ guṇatvam iti mukhya-lakṣaṇam. sadaikarūpasyānandasya rasatvenotkarṣāpakarṣayoḥ pramāṇābhāva iti rasa-śabdo ’tra tad-āsvādārthaḥ. tena rasāsvādotkarṣakatvaṁ guṇatvam.yatha sauryadikam atmana eva, nakarasya, tatha madhuryadikam rasasyaiva, natvakara-rupayoh sabdarthayoh. na hy ayam akarah surah, sthulatvad iti sad-dhetuh, asthulasyapi suratva-darsanat, yatha maha-matahgaja-pahcananayoh. yat tu virasu-sutayoh sisu-yunor akara-gatam eva suratvam, tac ca vayah-krtam eva. tena sa-vyabhicara-dosad akarasya sauryadir guno na bhavati, kintu tasya vyahjaka akarah, varna-mayatvat. ata utkarsatvam gunatvam iti mukhya-laksanam. sadaika- rupasyanandasya rasatvenotkarsapakarsayoh pramanabhava iti rasa-sabdo ’tra tad-asvadarthah. tena rasasvadotkarsakatvam gunatvam.*

**Перевод:**

**As a quality such as bravery only enhances the soul, so a guna such as madhurya only enhances the rasa. A guna does not enhance sound and meaning, which are the body of the poetry. It is not reasonable to think that the body is brave because it is stout, since bravery is also seen in one that is not stout. For example, the prowess seen in a small lion might not be present in a huge elephant. When it is said that, out of a brave boy and a brave youth, the youth is braver, because of the body, that is only caused by age, not by the quality. Thus, on account of the fault of variability, a quality such as bravery does not relate to the body. However, the body reveals the quality. The body of poetry consists in phonemes.**

**Therefore the main definition of a guna is: An enhancer is a quality. In the definition, the word rasa means the relishment of the rasa (enhanced sthayi-bhava), because there is no proof that Rasa (rapture), which is always in the same form of bliss, can be enhanced or diminished. Thus, a quality is that which enhances the relishment of the rasa.**

### 6.2

*guṇasya vyañjakā varṇāḥ (2a)*

**Перевод:**

**Phonemes bring out a guna.**

*yathā ayaṁ śabdārtha-vyatikaraḥ kāvyatayā vyavaharaṇīyo rasātmakatvāt, iti rasātmakatva-hetumator eva śabdārthayoḥ kāvyatva-vyavahāras tathāyaṁ varṇa-samūho madhura-rasādivyañjakaḥ sukumārāditvād iti sukumāratvādi-hetumatām eva varṇānāṁ rasasya mādhuryādi-vyañjakatve vyavahāraḥ. tena samucitam eva varṇānāṁ mādhuryādi-vyañjakatvam. nanu utkarṣakatvaṁ guṇatvam iti cet tadālaṅkārāṇām apy utkarṣakatvaṁ vartate, teṣām api guṇatvam astu? satyam, yathā hārādayo hy alaṅkārāḥ kaṇṭhādy-aṅgāny evopakurvanti, nātmānam, tathā anuprāsa-svabhāvokty-ādayo ’laṅkārāḥ śabdārthāv eva, na tu rasam, evaṁ cet tadā śruti-kaṭv-apuṣṭārthādi-doṣāṇāṁ śabdārthāśrayatvena tad-apakarṣakatvam evāstu, kathaṁ rasāpakarṣakatvam, yan-mūlā teṣāṁ doṣatā? ucyate—yathaiva śauryādayo guṇās tathaiva kātaryādayo doṣā apy ātmana eva dharmās tasyaivotkarṣāpakarṣa-hetava upalabhyante, evam eva mādhuryādayo guṇāḥ śruti-kaṭv-ādayo doṣā api rasasyaiveti. dehasya kāṇatva-khañjatvādi-doṣe ’pi kāṇo ’yaṁ deha iti na kaścid api vadati, api tu kāṇo ’yaṁ devadatta ity-ādy eva, na tu devadatto dehaḥ, devadattasya deho ’yam iti pratīteḥ, tenopacārād eva doṣāṇāṁ rasāpakarṣakatvam, vastutas tu śabdārthayor eva. evaṁ tarhi alaṅkārāṇām apy upacārād rasotkarṣatāstu, tathā sati teṣām api guṇatvena bhūyatām? naivam, teṣāṁ śabdārthāv alaṅkṛtyaiva upakṣīṇatvāt kathaṁ rasāpekṣatvaṁ yenopacāreṇa bhavitavyam iti.*

**Перевод:**

**Just as sound and meaning as a whole are said to be poetry when they have the nature of rasa—that is, they are the cause of there being the nature of rasa—, so a bunch of phonemes bring out madhura-rasa and so on due to being delicate and so on: This means the phonemes which are the cause of delicateness and so on are said to bring out the sweetness, etc. of the rasa. Therefore it is proper to state that phonemes bring out sweetness and so on.**

**Someone might think: “If what is an enhancer is a quality, it follows that since the literary ornaments as well are enhancers, they too are gunas.” That is true. However, just as bodily ornaments such as a necklace enhance only the body parts such as the neck and not the soul, so the ornaments such as alliteration and svabhavokti enhance only the sounds and the meanings, and not the rasa.**

**The objector might argue: “Still, it would have to be said that the literary faults, such as sruti-katu (harsh on the ears) apustartha (irrelevant meaning), only diminish the sound and the meaning since they are based on those two, so why is a fault defined as that which diminishes the rasa (the relishment) (10.1)?”**

**The answer is this: Like bravery and other qualities, fear and other faults are only attributes of the soul (atma) (or mind). They turn out as causes of either the enhancement of or the diminution of the soul. In the same way, the qualities, such as sweetness, and the literary faults only enhance or diminish the rasa respectively.**

**In truth, there is metaphorical usage in defining a fault as that which diminishes the rasa, because they only diminish the sounds and the meanings. No one says “This body is blind”, even when there is such a fault, rather one says the person is blind, because the body belongs to the person; the body is not the person.**

**The objector might reply: “Thus, metaphorical usage also occurs in stating that the literary ornaments enhance the rasa. Such being the case, shouldn’t they be gunas ?” No, because they cease to function right after adorning the sound and the meaning respectively, so how could they look up to the rasa, as a result of which metaphorical usage could be applied?**

**Комментарий:**

Kavi Kamapura’s interpretation slightly differs from Mammata’s and Visvanatha Kaviraja’s methodologies. But all three of them agree that their definitions do not apply when the phonemes only bring out the sweetness (or the vigor) of an expressed meaning which is not potent enough to constitute a rasa (6.33); in that way there is no metaphorical usage in that definition of the function of a type of sound.

### 6.3

*varṇā mādhuryādi-vyañjakāḥ, sukumāratvād iti na tu sukumāratvaṁ komalatvam, tasya śithilatvāt. sukumāratvaṁ rañjakatvam, yathā “śithilaṁ mālatī-mālā lolāli-kalilā yathā” ity ācārya-daṇḍinaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Phonemes bring out sweetness and so on. When “delicateness” was said in that regard, the delicateness does not mean softness, because softness means sithila (relaxed word structure: no conjunct consonant), whereas delicateness means pleasingness.**

**For example, the master rhetorician Dandin wrote: “This illustrates sithila: malati-mala lolali-kalila, “The malati garland is endowed with restless bees.”” (Kavyadarsa 1.43)**

**Комментарий:**

The phoneme which is the most characteristic of the quality of softness is the consonant l by itself. Notably, there is no conjunct consonant in that example. As regards the gunas, the rhetoricians do not consider the vowels: They only class the consonants in three varieties: madhurya (sweetness), komala (softness), and ojas (vigor). A pure occurrence of komala is rare, therefore most of the time only madhurya or ojas is the focus of attention in an analysis.

### 6.4

*atrāpi,*

**Перевод:**

**Another example of softness:**

*līlālasa-lalitāṅgī laghu laghu lalanā-lalāma-mauli-maṇiḥ*  
*lalitādibhir ālibhir vilasati lalita-smita-rādhā*

**Пословный перевод:**

lila—due to pastimes; alasa—is tired; lalita-angi—whose charming body; laghu laghu—lightly, yet actively; lalana—of women; lalama—among the best; mauli-manih—who is the crest jewel; lalita-adibhih—beginning with Lalita; alibhih—with the lady friends; vilasati—plays; lalita—is lovely; smita—whose smile; radha—Radha.

**Перевод:**

**Radha has a lovely smile and is the foremost feminine leader. Now, since Her charming body is somewhat tired due to play, She enjoys light recreation with Lalita and other friends.**

*tena saukumāryaṁ nāma rañjakatvam.*

**Перевод:**

**Therefore delicateness means pleasingness.**

### 6.5

*yad uktam anyaiḥ, “kartāraḥ kāvya-śobhāyā dharmā eva guṇāḥ smṛtāḥ, alaṅkārās tad-utkarṣa-hetavaḥ syur iti kramaḥ” iti, tad api nātilalitam, yataḥ khalu guṇālaṅkārādimad-vāṅ-nirmitiviśeṣasyaiva kāvyatvāṅgīkāre na gunālaṅkārādibhyo ’nyaḥ kāvyanāmā padārtho ’sti, nāpi kāvyād anye gunālaṅkārāḥ, ke kasya śobhāyāḥ kartāro bhaviṣyanti?*

**Перевод:**

**An eminent scholar stated: “The attributes that make the resplendence of the poetry are the gunas. However, the causes of the eminence of the resplendence of the poetry are the alankaras” (Kavyalankara-sutra 3.1.1-2). That is not too good because, given that only a literary construction which has a guna, an alankara, etc., is poetry, no poetry is distinct from gunas, alankaras and so on. Nor are gunas and alankaras distinct from the poetry. So what makes the resplendence of what?**

### 6.6

*kiñca, kāvya-śobhāyāḥ kartāra ity ekasyaiva kāvyasya kiṁ sarve guṇāh śobhā-kartāraḥ, kiṁ pṛthak pṛthak? ādye asamagraguṇayoḥ pāñcālī-gauḍyoḥ kāvya-śobhā-karatvānupapattiḥ. yadi vā pṛthag eva tadā “ūrjjat-sphūrjad-garjjanaiḥ” ity-ādau saty apy ojo-guṇe nānya-śobhā, tena varṇā eva mādhuryādi-vyañjakāḥ, mādhuryādayo madhura-rasādy-utkarṣakā iti sthitam.*

**Перевод:**

**Moreover, in “The attributes that make the resplendence of the poetry are the gunas,” the poetry is one: Are the gunas the makers of the resplendence of the poetry together or separately? The first option is ruled out because if it were true, the Pancali Riti could not possibly make the resplendence since it does not have all the gunas. The same applies to the Gaudi. And if the gunas were to make the resplendence separately, then, in verse 1.18 for instance, although ojas guna occurs, there is no other resplendence, so what more can be said? Thus it is established that only the phonemes bring out the sweetness and so on; sweetness and other elements are the enhancers of madhura- rasa and so on.**

### 6.7

*te mādhuryādayaḥ punaḥ (2b)*

**Перевод:**

**The gunas are sweetness and so on.**

### 6.8

*atha ke te ity āha,*

**Перевод:**

**What are the gunas? Therefore he says:**

*mādhuryam api caujaś ca prasādaś ceti te trayaḥ*  
*kecid daśeti brūvata eṣv evāntar-bhavanti te (3)*  
*te guṇāḥ sapta, eṣv eva mādhuryādiṣv eva.*

**Перевод:**

**There are three gunas:**

**♦   madhurya (sweetness, melting),**

**♦   ojas (vigor), and**

**♦   prasada (clarity of meaning).**

**Some scholars says there are ten gunas. In that case, seven are included in the three.**

### 6.9

*ke te sapteti darṣayati,*

**Перевод:**

**What are those seven? He mentions them:**

*artha-vyaktir udāratvaṁ śleṣaś ca samatā tathā*  
*kāntiḥ prauḍhiḥ samādhiś ca saptaite taiḥ samaṁ daśa (4)*  
*tair mādhuryādibhiḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**They are artha-vyakti, udaratva, slesa, samata, kanti, praudhi, and samadhi. Those seven with the three make ten gunas.**

**Комментарий:**

The rhetoricians defined Bharata Muni’s ten gunas in various ways. Vamana subdivided each one into sabda-guna (quality of the sound) and artha-guna (quality of the meaning).

As regards the above list, Vamana’s sabda-guna artha-vyakti is the same as our prasada, whereas Vamana’s artha-guna prasada is simply the absence of the fault called adhika-pada (superfluous word), according to Mammata. Therefore the saukumarya-guna (softness), seen in every list of ten gunas, needs to be added to make a total of ten. In text 9.4, Kavi Karnapura mentions this guna, under the name su-kumarata, but he follows Visvanatha Kaviraja’s interpretation that Vamana’s saukumarya is simply the absence of harsh sounds: gramya-duhsravata-tyagat kantis ca sukumarata (Sahitya-darpana 8.12).

In Bharata Muni’s list, praudhi is called ojas, but his artha-vyakti is not the same as our prasada (Natya-sastra 16.96-114). Our prasada has no equivalent in Bharata Muni’s system.

Moreover, slesa-guna (coalescence of words) is distinct from and is the ancient prototype of slesa alankara (literal double meaning).

### 6.10

*saptānāṁ lakṣanān āha,*

**Перевод:**

**He defines the seven gunas:**

*prasāda evaujo-miśra-śaithilyātmā bhaved yadi*  
*tadārtha-vyaktir iṣyeta vikaṭatvam udāratā (5)*  
*padānām eka-rūpatvaṁ sandhy-ādāv asphuṭe sati*  
*śleṣo mārgābheda eva samataujjvalyam eva hi (6)*  
*kāntiḥ sābhiprāyatayā samāsa-vyāsayoḥ satoḥ*  
*vākyārthe pada-vinyāsaḥ padārthe vākya-nirmitiḥ*  
*prauḍhir ārohāvaroha-kramaḥ samādhir iṣyate (7)*

**Перевод:**

**If prasada is defined as a mix of saithilya (the words in Devanagari script are spaced out, and short compounds are allowed) and ojas (harsh phonetic combinations, and long compounds) (this is Vamana’s sabda-guna prasada), then artha- vyakti \[is the same as our prasada (clarity of the meaning)\].**

**Udarata means sprightliness (a construction of ojas suitably occurs in the context of madhurya).**

**When the words look like one block (in Devanagari script), that is the separation between the words is unclear, that is slesa (coalescence of words).**

**Samata (sameness of style) means there is no divergence from the chosen style of compounding.**

**Kanti (elegance) is the form of a resplendence (the absence of the fault of vulgarity).**

**Praudhi (Vamana’s artha-guna ojas) has subvarieties: (1) A word is highly purposeful, (2) Several short sentences are tightly grammatically constructed into one sentence, (3) The exact same purport is repeatedly stated in many ways, (4) One word means a whole sentence, and (5) The meaning of a clause is the same as the meaning of one word.**

**Samadhi (crescendo and decrescendo) is a sequence of a heightening effect and a lowering effect.**

**Комментарий:**

Pandita-raja Jagannatha explains that both prasada and samadhi involve a dense structure of words and a relaxed structure of words; the difference is that in prasada, those two are used out of sequence, whereas in samadhi they are sequential. Moreover, he says only their aspect of dense structure applies to our ojas therefore their aspect of relaxed structure is classed either in our madhurya (sweetness) or in our prasada (clarity).

### 6.11

*tad-antarbhāve yuktim vakti,*

**Перевод:**

**He details the logical reasoning in including the seven in the three:**

*teṣv evāntarbhavanty eka eke vaicitrya-bodhakāḥ*  
*eke doṣa-parityāgād gatārthā iti no daśa*  
*artha-vyaktiḥ prasādāntaḥ prauḍhir vaicitrya-bodhikā (8)*  
*na tu guṇa ity arthaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Some of them are included in the three. Some are simply forms of poetic expression. And some others are simply the absence of a fault. Thus the gunas are not ten. Artha-vyakti is included in our prasada. Praudhi is a form of poetic expression.**

### 6.12

*samatā tu kvacid doṣaḥ (9a)*  
*samatā tu kvacid doṣo ’pi bhavati.*

**Перевод:**

**Sometimes samata-guna (not deviating from the chosen style of compounding) is a fault.**

### 6.13

*kuta ity ata āha,*

**Перевод:**

**Why? Therefore he says:**

*vaiṣamyaṁ yatra vāñchyate*  
*sajātīya-vijātīya-yugapad varṇane sati (9bcd)*

*yatra paraspara-visadṛśayor yugapad varṇane sati vaiṣamyam*  
*abhīṣṭam, tatra samatā tu doṣa eva, yatra na tathā tatra guṇaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**In a simultaneous description of two mutually different things, samata is a fault when a dissimilarity is intended to be expressed. But when there is no dissimilarity, samata is a quality.**

### 6.14

*yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**This illustrates how disregarding samata-guna makes a quality:**

*ūrdhvordhva-spardhi-govardhana-śikhari-varoddhāra-sāroddhuro ’haṁ*  
*śaṅke paṅkeja-netre tava kuca-mukulālokane jāta-kampaḥ*  
*uddaṇḍe kāliyasya sphuṭa-vikaṭa-phaṇā-maṇḍale tāṇḍavāḍhyaḥ*  
*so ’haṁ rādhe ’bhibhūtas tava taralitayā hanta veṇī-bhujaṅgyā*

**Пословный перевод:**

urdhvordhva— \[clouds situated\] higher and higher; spardhi—which rivals; govardhana—called Govardhana; sikhari—of mountains; vara—the best; uddhara—in lifting; sara-uddhurah—one whose load is the best; aham—I; sanke—I fear; pankeja-netre—O lotus­eyed woman; tava—Your; kuca—\[in the form of\] breasts; mukula— the buds; alokane—when seeing; jata-kampah—one whose trembling has occurred; uddande—extraordinary; kaliyasya—of Kaliya; sphuta—clearly; vikata—formidable; phana—of hoods; mandale—on the multitude; tandava—with a wild dance; adhyah— richly endowed; sah aham—that well-known I; radhe—O Radha; abhibhutah—was overcome; tava—Your; taralitaya—restless; hanta—alas; veni—in the form of a braid; bhujangya—by the female snake.

**Перевод:**

**I am the foremost leader because I lifted Govardhana, the best mountain, which towers above the highest clouds. However, lotus-eyed girl, I’m afraid I can’t withhold a shiver when I gaze at the blown buds of Your breasts. I engaged in a frantic dance on Kaliya’s extraordinary and dreadful hoods, but alas, Radha, I’ve been overcome by the restless snake of Your braid.**

*ity-ādiṣv asamataiva guṇaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**In examples such as this, the absence of samata is a quality.**

**Комментарий:**

In the second and fourth lines, hard phonemes and long compounds were not used because the meanings do not relate to ojas guna (vigor). That is normal usage, but they were properly used in the first and third lines simply because of the significance of the expressed meanings, without regard for the contextual rasa (madhurya).

### 6.15

*grāmya-kaṣṭatvādi-hānād apāruṣyorarīkṛtau*  
*aujjvalya-rūpā yā kāntiḥ sā mādhuryāntara-sthitā*  
*anye tv ojasi vartante tena te na punar daśa (10)*

**Перевод:**

**The kanti (elegance) which is the form of a resplendence in the matter of acknowledging an absence of harshness by virtue of the avoidance of faults such as gramya (vulgarity) and kasta (the meaning is difficult to understand) is included in our madhurya. The others are in ojas. Thus the gunas are not ten.**

*anye śleśa-samādhy-udāratā ojasy evāntarbhavantīty arthaḥ. nanv evaṁ cet kliṣṭatva-doṣa-nirasanenaiva prasāda-guṇasyāpi mādhurya eva labdheḥ kiṁ prasāda-guṇasya pṛthaṅ-nirdeśaḥ? naivam, prasādasya svataḥ-siddhatvāt kvāntarbhāvaḥ? anyathā anavasthā-prasakteḥ. kiñca, matāntara-kathanam evaitat tena daśa-vidhatvaṁ na duṣṭam ity ubhayam evāsmākam abhīṣṭam.*

**Перевод:**

**The others are slesa, samadhi, and udarata. This means they are included in our ojas. Someone might wonder: “Why is prasada (clarity of meaning) accepted as a separate guna? It should be included in madhurya because prasada too is the absence of klista (hard to understand).” That reasoning is off. Prasada is a positive occurrence, so in which other guna might it fit? If this logic were not applied, nothing could be settled.**

**Moreover, the system of ten gunas is not faulty. We accept both methodologies.**

**Комментарий:**

Mammata rejected Vamana’s methodology. Kavi Karnapura, however, refers to the ten gunas, in the context of Vaidarbhi Riti (9.3).

### 6.16

*atha mādhuryādayaḥ ke ta ity āha,*

**Перевод:**

**Now he dilates upon the three gunas. This defines madhurya (sweetness):**

*rañjakatvaṁ hi mādhuryaṁ cetaso druti-kāraṇam*  
*sambhoge vipralambhe ca tad evātiśayocitam (11)*  
*ca-kārāt karuṇādau ca.*

**Пословный перевод:**

ranjakatvam—delightfulness; hi—only; madhuryam—sweetness; cetasah—of the heart; druti—of the melting; karanam—the cause; sambhoge—in meeting; vipralambhe—in separation; ca—and; tat eva—that same one (madhurya); atisaya-ucitam—highly suitable.

**Перевод:**

**Madhurya means delightfulness. It is the cause of the melting of the heart. Madhurya is highly suitable in sambhoga-srngara, in vipralambha-srngara, in karuna, and so on.**

**Комментарий:**

In karuna (lamentation), in santa (peacefulness), and in vipralambha (separation), madhurya means “melting” rather than “sweetness”.

### 6.17

**Перевод:**

**\[This defines ojas (vigor):\]**

*ceto-vistāra-rūpasya dīptatvasya hi kāraṇam*  
*ojaḥ syād vīra-bībhatsa-raudreṣu krama-puṣṭi-kṛt (12)*

**Пословный перевод:**

cetah—of the mind; vistara—of the expanse; rupasya—which is the form; diptatvasya—of blazingness; hi—only; karanam—the cause; ojah—the guna called ojas; syat—is; vira-bibhatsa-raudresu— in vira-rasa, in bibhatsa-rasa, and in raudra-rasa; krama—in sequence; pusti—the enhancement; krt—makes.

**Перевод:**

**Ojas is the cause of blazingness that is the expansion of the mind. Ojas makes an enhancement in vira-rasa, in bibhatsa- rasa and in raudra-rasa.**

*dīptatvaṁ śaithilyābhāvo gāḍhatety arthaḥ. tac ca cetaso vistāra-*  
*hetur visphāra-kāraṇaṁ kramād vīrādiṣu puṣṭam arhatīty arthaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Blazingness is the absence of saithilya (no conjunct consonant): This means the phonetic construction is dense. Blazingness is the cause of the expansion of the mind and is sequentially more preponderant in vira-rasa, bibhatsa-rasa, and raudra-rasa.**

**Комментарий:**

The blazingness mentioned in the verse is a quality in the experience one of those three rasas, whereas the blazingness expounded in the elaboration relates both to sound and meaning and to the style of compounding (long compounds).

### 6.18

**Перевод:**

**\[This defines prasada (clarity of the meaning):\]**

*śruti-mātreṇa yatrārthaḥ sahasaiva prakāśate*  
*saurabhyād iva kastūrī prasādaḥ so ’bhidhīyate (13)*  
*sa sarveṣu raseṣv eva sarvāsv api ca rītiṣu*  
*upayuktaḥ (14abc)*  
*sa prasāda-nāmā guṇaḥ.*

**Пословный перевод:**

sruti-matrena—merely by hearing; yatra—in which \[guna\]; arthah—the meaning \[of the whole sentence\]; sahasa eva— immediately; prakasate—manifests; saurabhyat—because of the fragrance; iva—like; kasturi— musk; prasadah—the guna called prasada; sah—that \[guna\]; abhidhiyate—is called; sah—that; sarvesu—all; rasesu—in the rasas; eva—indeed; sarvasu—all; api—also; ca—and; ritisu—in the styles; upayuktah—applied.

**Перевод:**

**When the meaning of the words clearly comes out simply by hearing or by reading, like musk applied to the skin under the clothes comes out due to its fragrance, that isprasada. It applies to all the rasas and to all the intis.**

**Комментарий:**

The term prasada means “clarity of the meaning” in reference to a text that is easily understood. But it means “satisfaction” in reference to the type of quality in the relishment of a rasa.

### 6.19

*vyañjakāḥ syur varṇāś ca racanā api (14cd)*  
*teṣām ity arthāt.*

**Перевод:**

**The phonemes and the styles are suggestive of the gunas.**

*tatra varṇanāṁ vyañjakatvam idāniṁ darśyate. racanāyā rīti-nirūpaṇe darśayitavyam.*

**Перевод:**

**Henceforth the suggestiveness of the phonemes will be shown. The suggestiveness of the styles will be illustrated in the chapter on nti.**

**Комментарий:**

The phonemes themselves, the phonetic combinations, and the style of compounding take the form of either madhurya or ojas, depending on the rasa or on the meaning itself (if there is no rasa). The construction of either madhurya or ojas should give rise to the madhurya or ojas which is the quality of the rasa (aesthetic delight), when there is a rasa.

The ritis (styles) relate to the basic phonemes, the type of phonetic combination and the style of compounding. Mammata does not acknowledge the ritis because those three topics are already included in the discussion on the gunas. The main purpose of the various types of ritis is to account for constructions other than madhurya and ojas. Except for Vaidarbh! Riti (madhurya-guna) and Gaudi Riti (ojas guna), the rhetoricians do not agree on the definitions of ritis.

### 6.20

*sparśāḥ sva-pañcamādhaḥ-sthā aṭa-vargā laghu-raṇau*

**Пословный перевод:**

sparsah—the sparsas (the consonants from k to m); sva-pancama— their fifth consonant; adhah—below; sthah—situated; ata-vargah— which are not part of the ta group; laghu-ra-nau—short r and short n; madhurya-vyanjakah—suggestive of sweetness; varnah— the phonemes; na—not; eka-rupah—of one form; kramena— sequentially; cet—if.

**Перевод:**

**The phonemes suggestive of madhurya are the sparsas, except the ta group, with the corresponding nasal placed before, as well as a short r, and a short n. But if any such phoneme is used repeatedly one after another, sweetness is not evoked.**

*naikarūpā iti pṛthak pṛthag vargajā eva. aṭa-vargā iti ṭa-vargaḥ kevalo vā sva-paścamādhaḥ-stho vā ojasy eva.*

**Перевод:**

**The phonemes of the ta group (t, th, d, and dh), whether single or combined with the corresponding nasal, only belong to ojas.**

**Комментарий:**

The phonemes that evoke sweetness are: nk, nkh, ng, ngh, nc, nch, nj, njh, nt, nth, nd, ndh, mp, mph, mb, mbh, single short r, and single short n. Sometimes the anusvara (m) occurs instead of the sound n, and so on.

An example of a sound with the letter r both before and after a consonant is: durgraha. Moreover, the phoneme ks eminently evokes ojas. These are examples of phonetic combinations. The single phonemes of ojas are only: t, th, d, dh, s, s. In text 6.20 it was said that these phonemes evoke ojas: nt, nth, nd, ndh. Other prominent phonemes of ojas are: st and sth.

## Seventh Ray - Ornaments of Sound

### 7.1

*atha śabdālaṅkāra-nirṇayaḥ. atha “upamiti-mukho ’laṅkṛtigaṇaḥ” iti yad uktaṁ tatra mukha-śabdasya mukhyārthatvād amukhyasya prāptau prathamato ’mukhyaṁ śabdālaṅkāram evāha—*

**Перевод:**

**Earlier it was said: upamiti-mukho ’lankrti-ganah, “Simile and other literary devices are the ornaments of the Kavya-purusa” (1.7). In that regard, since the word mukha, in upamiti-mukha, has the sense of “foremost”, it follows that there is a secondary topic, thus at first he elaborates on the secondary ornaments, the ornaments of sound.**

**Vakrokti**

### 7.2

*ekenārthena yat proktam anyenārthena cānyathā*  
*kriyate śleṣa-kākubhyāṁ sā vakroktir bhaved dvidhā (1)*  
*śleṣo ’pi ca bhaved dvedhā sa-bhaṅgābhaṅga-bhedataḥ (2)*

**Пословный перевод:**

ekena arthena—with one meaning; yat—which word; proktam— is spoken; anyena arthena—with another meaning; ca—and; anyatha—in another way; kriyate —is made; slesa-kakubhyam— because of a double meaning, or due to the intonation; sa—that; vakra-uktih—called vakrokti (crooked speech); bhavet—is; dvidha—twofold; slesah—double meaning; api—also; ca—and; bhavet—is; dvedha—twofold; sa-bhanga—with a \[different\] division \[of the phonemes\]; abhanga—without a division \[of the phonemes\]; bhedatah—according to the varieties.

**Перевод:**

**When a word is said in one meaning but is construed in another by slesa (literal double meaning) or by kaku (modulation of the voice), that is called vakrokti (ambiguous speech). Slesa as well has two varieties: abhanga and sa-bhanga.**

*śleṣeṇa kākvā vā śleṣaś ca dvidhā—abhaṅgaḥ sa-bhaṅgaś ceti.*

**Перевод:**

**Vakrokti has two varieties, slesa (7.66) and kaku (4.12). The two categories of slesa are abhanga (the double meaning occurs without breaking up the syllables in a different way) and sa- bhanga (the double meaning is achieved by breaking up the syllables in a different way).**

**Комментарий:**

When the hearer construes the meaning of the speaker’s words differently, that is vakrokti. It only occurs in a dialogue. This vakrokti (ambiguous speech) is not the same as the vakrokti (crooked speech) mentioned in the description of ladyloves (5.128).

*mugdhe viddhi janārdano ’smi tad iyaṁ yogyā vane ’vasthitir*  
*bāle ’haṁ madhusūdano ’smi viditaṁ yogyo dvi-repho bhavān*

**Пословный перевод:**

kah tvam—who are you?; syama—O Syama; harih—Hari; babhuva—became; tat—because of that; idam—this; vrndavanam— Vmdavana; nirmrgam—(a place) from which the deers have gone; hamho—hmm; nagari—O lover; madhavah—Madhava; asmi—\[I\] am; asamaye—at the wrong time; vaisakha-masah— the month of Vaisakha (April-May); kutah—how?; mugdhe—O bewildered girl; viddhi—know; janardanah—Janardana; asmi— \[I\] am; tat—therefore; iyam—this; yogya—is proper; vane—in the forest; avasthitih—the abiding; bale—hey girl; aham —I; madhusudanah—Madhusudana; asmi—am; viditam—it is known; yogyah—it is proper; dvi-rephah—(one who has) two r’s; bhavan— You.

**Перевод:**

**Radha: Syama! Who are You?**

**Krsna: I am Hari (or I am a lion).**

**Radha: Ah! That’s why all the deer left Vrndavana.**

**Krsna: Hmm. In truth, smart girl, I am Madhava (or the month of Vaisakha).**

**Radha: Oh, how is it that the month of Vaisakha has come at the wrong time?**

**Krsna: Simple girl, know that I am Janardana (or one who gives pain to living entities).**

**Radha: In that case Your residing in the forest is fitting.**

**Krsna: Dear girl, I am Madhusudana (or I am a bee (bhramara)).**

**Radha: I know! That You have two r’s is proper.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti: The word barbara (barbarian) is implied since it has two r’s. She means to say: “You’re also a barbarian,” since it is well-known that a cow herder is a barbarian. The derivation of Janardana is: janan ardayati (He kills people). A double meaning is: jana-pidaka (He gives pain to people).

*sa-bhaṅgo yathā*

**Перевод:**

*kānte kīrtir akīrtir eva vada me kiñcij jaḍebhyaḥ paraṁ*  
*dhīrā kāpi bhavaty aho katham aho buddhir bhavet pūrṇimā*  
*kā medhā tava bhūyasī na madane tvayy eva me dhāraṇaṁ*  
*tan mām āspṛśa na spṛśeyam iti sa śrīmān jito rādhayā*

**Пословный перевод:**

kante—O lover; kirtih—fame; akirtih—infamy; eva—only; vada me—tell me; kincit—something; jadebhyah—than inert things; param—other; dhira—an intelligent woman; ka—what; api— also; bhavati—is; aho—how amazing; katham—why; aho—Oh; buddhih—intelligence; bhavet—is; purnima—the full moon; ka—what; medha—intelligence; tava—your; bhuyasi—is; na— not; madane—on Cupid; tvayi—on you; eva—only; me—my; dharanam—mental focus; tat—therefore; mam—me; asprsa— touch softly; na sprseyam—I shall not touch; iti—thus; sah—that famous one; sriman—beautiful and glorious; jitah—is defeated; radhaya—by Radha.

**Перевод:**

**Or, as a double meaning (following Visvanatha Cakravarti’s commentary): kante—ka ante (meaning ka ante nase sati tisthati?): what remains at the end of life?; kincid—kim cid (meaning kim cid-vastu?): what is a transcendental object?; dhih—intelligence; rakapi—raka api: the full moon also; kame—on Cupid; dha— fixing the mind (dha means dharanam and is made with the suffix kvip); ma—Me; ma sprsa—don’t touch.**

**Krsna: Sweetheart ...**

**Radha (thinking He said: ka ante, What remains in the end?):**

**Only fame and infamy remain.**

**Krsna: Tell Me something about it!**

**Radha (thinking He said: kim cid, What is spirit?): It’s different than inert things.**

**Krsna: Oh! Someone here is intelligent!**

**Radha (thinking He said: dhih raka api, Intelligence too is a full moon):**

**“How is intelligence a full moon?”**

**Krsna: What wits do You have?!**

**Radha (thinking He said: kame dha, Your attention is on Cupid): My attention is only on You, not on Cupid.**

**Krsna: In that case You can touch Me.**

**Radha (thinking He said: ma ma sprsa, Don’t touch Me): I won’t touch You.**

**In this way Radha soundly defeated Krsna.**

**Anuprāsa**

### 7.6

*anuprāsyata ity arthe ’nuprāso varṇa-sāmyataḥ (3)*

**Пословный перевод:**

anuprasyate iti arthe—in the sense of anuprasyate; anuprasah— the ornament called anuprasa; varna-samyatah—on account of sameness.

**Перевод:**

**Anuprasa (alliteration) occurs on account of a repetition of a phoneme. The derivation of anuprasa is anuprasyate.**

*sa-jātīyaṁ varṇam anu sajātīya-varṇāntaraṁ prakarṣeṇāsyata iti vyutpattiḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Etymologically, anuprasa means: “preeminently (pra) placing (asyate) a phoneme after (anu) another phoneme of the same kind.”**

### 7.7

*sa ca dvedhā cheka-vṛtti-bhedāt (4ab)*

**Перевод:**

**It has two varieties: cheka and vrtti.**

*chekānuprāso vṛtty-anuprāsaś ceti sa dvedhā.*

**Перевод:**

**The two types of alliteration are cheka anuprasa and vrtti anuprasa.**

**Комментарий:**

There is a grand total of six types of alliteration (7.28 vrtti). In Sanskrit poetics, usually the alliteration of a vowel is not taken in consideration. Kavi Karnapura makes exceptions for alliteration of vowels and consonants together (7.18; 7.24). Thus for the most part anuprasa refers to the repetition of a consonant or of a conjunct consonant. An aspirate phoneme, such as kh, is one consonant.

Only Bharata Muni, Dandi and Bhoja valued the alliteration of a vowel (assonance). Kavi Karnapura and others consider this faulty on certain occasions (10.74).

The poetical theorists differ in their interpretations of alliteration. Mammata and Visvanatha Kaviraja expound cheka anuprasa, but Kavi KamapUra defines it somewhat differently.

Mammata and Visvanatha Kaviraja say cheka is so called because it is used by experts: cheko vidagdhas tat-prayojyatvad esa chekanuprasah (Sahitya-darpana 2.3). Kavi KamapUra used the word cheka in that sense (3.59). Moreover, in the context of alliteration the term vrtti means avrtt (repetition).

### 7.8

*chekaḥ sakṛttayā (4b)*

**Перевод:**

**Cheka involves an immediate repetition.**

*eka-vārānunyāsena chekaḥ syāt.*

**Перевод:**

**When a phoneme is placed one-time immediately after the same phoneme, that is cheka.**

*jagato ’viratodayam*

*dṛśoḥ prema-yaśo-mayam*

**Пословный перевод:**

**Перевод:**

**That renowned dark blue body should be meditated upon and extolled. It is eternal and beautifies the world. It is the embodiment of fame and is the abode of love for everyone’s eyes.**

*atra ma-kārādīnāṁ sakṛd anu nyāsaś ca.*

**Перевод:**

**In this example, the letters m are placed one after the other (in syamam), and so are the letters y (in dhyeyam).**

**Перевод:**

*sa eva varṇa-vinyāsaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**It too involves repeating only one kind of phoneme one-time.**

*yathā,*

*sambhedaḥ sveda-kampayoḥ*  
*śaṅke paṅke-ruha-dṛśo*  
*na rasyānanda-mattatā*

**Пословный перевод:**

ananga—(of the pastimes) of the god of love; mangala-arambhe— in the happy beginning; sambhedah—a combination; sveda- kampayoh—of perspiring and trembling; sanke—I fear; panke- ruha—are like a lotus (i.e. “growing in the mud”); drsah—of one whose eyes; na—not; rasya—delightful; ananda-mattata—the state of being exhilarated due to bliss.

**Перевод:**

**\[Looking through the branches and seeing her yuthesvari taking pleasure with Krsna, one sakhi tells another:\]**

**This lotus-eyed girl is already experiencing perspiration and trembling right at the beginning of union. I think she will not become fully enraptured by passion.**

**Комментарий:**

Here sweetness is produced from the immediate repetition of the sound ng, of the sound mbh, and of the sound nk. The sweetness is appropriate since it heightens madhura-rasa, the theme of the verse.

**Пословный перевод:**

ekasya—of one; api—even; athava—or; anekasya—of more than one; amreditataya—by the repetition; yadi—if; nyasah—placing; syat—there is; vrtti—\[called\] vrtti; anuprasah—the alliteration.

### 7.13

*yathā,*

**Перевод:**

*dhāma śyāmalam uddāma*  
*kāma-koṭi-manoharam*  
*dhyeyaṁ geyaṁ samāstheyaṁ*  
*samāneyaṁ ca mānase*

**Пословный перевод:**

dhama—body; syamalam—dark blue; uddama—unlimited, or very powerful; kama-koti-manoharam—which is more attractive than millions of Cupids; ; dhyeyam—should be meditated upon; geyam—should be glorified; samastheyam—should be taken shelter of; samaneyam—it should be brought; ca—and; manase— in the mind.

**Перевод:**

**Krsna’s body is dark blue and very powerful. It is more attractive than millions of Cupids. It must be meditated upon, glorified, completely resorted to, and brought within one’s mind.**

**Комментарий:**

In the first half of the verse, there is a vrtti anuprasa of m. In the second half, there is a vrtti anuprasa of y and another of s. The repetition of y in dhyeya is a cheka anuprasa, but in “dhyeyam gey am ” the repetition ofy turns into a vrtti anuprasa. The repetition of k in kama-koti is a cheka anuprasa (7.9).

### 7.14

*anekasya yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of a multiple repetition of more than one phoneme:**

*vividha-vadhū-vadha-sādho*  
*virama ramā-nātha nāthyatāṁ nātha*  
*kaitava-vijña samajñāṁ*  
*tava vijñātuṁ na vijñāham*

**Пословный перевод:**

vividha—many; vadhu—young women (or wives); vadha—at killing; sadhu—O expert; virama—please stop; rama-natha—O Lord of Rama,; nathyatam—asking should be done; na— not; atha—then; kaitava—of deceitfulness; vijna—O knower; samajnam—fame; tava—your; vijnatum—to understand; na—not; vijna—intelligent; aham—I am.

**Перевод:**

**Expert at killing young women: Stop. Do not ask me for anything later, god of Rama. O great deceiver, I am not intelligent enough to understand the extent of Your glories.**

**Комментарий:**

In the first line, there is a vrtti anuprasa of v and dh (in vidha- vadhu-vadha). In the second line, there is a vrtti anuprasa of r and m (rama rama), and a vrtti anuprasa of n and th (natha nathyatam natha). In the second half, there is a vrtti anuprasa ofjn.

There is no rule that a repetition should occur within a certain number of syllables, but the rule of thumb is that the repetition should not be distant. Dandi wrote: ity anuprasam icchanti natidurantara-srutim, “In this way, scholars say that in alliteration the repeated sound should not be too far away” (Kavyadarsa 1.58). In the second line of Dandi’s illustrative verse: bimbam pasyaitad ambare, the sound mb in ambare is in the fifth syllable after the previous sound mb. However, this alliteration does not fit in the moderns’ methodologies of alliteration.

### 7.23

*krameṇodāharaṇāni,*

**Перевод:**

**\[This illustrates a repetition of a word:\]**

*manojaneḥ punar iyad*  
*vaidagdhī-vaiduṣī kutaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

krsnatvena—as Krsna; sakhi—O lady friend; pradurbhavah— manifesting; manye—I think; manojaneh—Cupid (“He whose origin is the mind”); manojaneh—of Cupid; punah—moreover; iyat—such; vaidagdhi—in cleverness; vaidusi—skill; kutah—how.

**Перевод:**

**Sakhi, I think that Cupid has taken birth as Krsna. Then again, how is Cupid capable of such ingenuity?**

**Комментарий:**

Here the word manojaneh is repeated without a difference in meaning, yet the repeated word is positioned differently in the syntactical connection of the verse. This differentiates lata anuprasa from repetitions based on abhiksnya (frequent repetition) or vipsa (pervasion, i.e. a distributive sense). An example of abhiksnya is: bhajati bhajati, “He serves again and again.” An instance of vipsa is: gopi gopi ramaniya, “Every gopi is beautiful.”

**Перевод:**

**Your face is like a full moon. Therefore, when You and this girl whose friend is swoon when she feels the pang of separation from You are away from each other, this full-moon night, sweet on account of moonrays, burns only her.**

**Комментарий:**

In kirana-kirana, the nominal base is repeated in the same compound. In raka raka, the nominal base is repeated, but one nominal base is in a compound whereas the other is not. The words virahe virahe are an example of two nominal bases which are not in a compound, but they also illustrate the repetition of a declined word like the repetition of manojaneh in 7.23. There is no overlap in Mammata’s methodology because he lists a category where the word bases are in separate compounds: vrttav anyatra tatra va, namnah sa vrtty-avrttyos ca (Kavya-prakasa 9.82).

**Перевод:**

**Now we summarize. There are six kinds of alliteration:**

**1. cheka,**

**2. vrtti,**

**3. lata that is a repetition of a word,**

**5. lata that is a repetition of many words, and**

**6. lata that is a repetition of a nominal base.**

**Yamaka**

### 7.29

*yamakaṁ tv artha-bhinnānāṁ*

*kvacin nirarthakānāṁ ca*  
*sārthānarthavatāṁ kvacit (9)*

**Пословный перевод:**

yamakam—the ornament called yamaka; tu—but; artha—in meaning; bhinnanam—which are different; pada-admam—of the words and other elements; samakrtih—the same form (i.e. the repetition); kvacit—sometimes; nirarthakanam—which are meaningless; ca—and; sa-artha-anarthavatam—which have a meaning and are meaningless; kvacit—sometimes.

**Перевод:**

**A yamaka (word rhyme) is the repetition of a word, and so on, where the repeated sound has a different meaning. Sometimes the sound and the repeated sound are meaningful, sometimes both are meaningless, and sometimes one is meaningful while the other is not.**

*parasparam artha-gata-bhedavatāṁ padādīnāṁ nāma-padapadāvayava-vākyānāṁ samā ākṛtiḥ sārūpyam yamakam.*

**Перевод:**

**This means: The repetition of either a nominal base, a declined word, a part of a declined word, or a sentence that has a different meaning when repeated is called yamaka.**

prathamasya—of the first \[line\]; tu—only; dvitiyena—with the second; trtiyena—with the third; caturthena—with the fourth; iti—in that way; tat—it (yamaka); tridha—threefold; dvitiyah—the second \[line\]; tu—only; trtiyena—with the third; caturthena—with the fourth; iti—in that way; ca—and; dvidha—twofold; trtiyah—the third \[line\]; tu—only; caturthena—with the fourth; iti—in that way; ekah—one; eva—only; iti—in that way; sad bhidah—six varieties; prathamah—the first \[line\]; trisu—in three \[lines\]; api—also; anyah—another; iti—in that way; sapta—seven; dvayam—a pair; punah—again; prathamah—the first \[line\]; tu—only; caturthena— with the fourth; dvitiyah —the second \[line\]; tat-parena—with the third (“what is other than them”); ca—and; prathamah—the first \[line\]; tu—only; dvitiyena—with the second; trtiyah—the third \[line\]; tat-parena—with the fourth (“what is other than them”); ca—and.

*yaśo yaśodā-bhuvi vidyate ’dya te*

**Пословный перевод:**

na—do not; manam—loving anger; adhehi—place; manasi—in the heart; adah—that; syadah—impulse; subham—the good fortune; subhamyoh—who possesses fame; syati—destroys; devi—O goddess; te—of you; avite—O you who are protected; aho— what a wonder; ahan-ratra—day and night; krta—is produced; arusa— \[anger,\] because of which mental pain; rusa—by anger; ayasah—infamy; yasoda-bhuvi—toward Krsna (“who takes birth from Yasoda”); vidyate—is; adya—now; te—your.

**Перевод:**

**Beautiful girl, you have a good reputation. Don’t let mana stay in your heart: The pique will destroy your good fortune. How amazing, even now you remain shielded by your anger, which causes you pain day and night. By now the news of your bad temper must have reached Yasoda’s son; your reputation will suffer.**

**Комментарий:**

In verse 7.24, Kavi Karnapura gave the example “yaso yaso” in yaso yasoda as an instance of lata anuprasa, a repetition that does not involve a change in meaning. In the above yamaka, however, the etymological aspect of the second yaso is not intended to be expressed. In verse 24 the etymological derivation of Yasoda-suta (the son of she who gives fame) is meant to be expressed: Both words yaso are taken in the meaning of fame. The idea is that Yasoda gave Devaki the fame of being Krsna’s mother (Sarartha-darsim 10.3.53). Therefore, with regard to that sentence, it is fitting that fame occurs by serving the son of she who gives fame.

*sā sādhu dhutatarārā*  
*mama vavale lehi-hita-tanu nu*

**Пословный перевод:**

vi—with birds; vitata—is filled; nana—variegated; ma—whose beauty; ama—is incomparable; vividha—is manifold; dhana— whose opulence; nau—by us two; avasya—certainly; asya— should be pervaded (from the verbal root as\[un\] vyaptau); sa—that \[meeting place in the forest\]; sadhu—nicely; dhuta-tara—is very broken; ara—the path of which; mama—for me; vavale—was concealed; lehi—relishes; hita—and auspicious; tanu—you whose body; nu—(vocative particle).

**Перевод:**

*ity-ādi. evaṁ sapta-viṁśatir bhedāḥ. dvi-khaṇḍa-tri-khaṇḍādikaṁ ca uktodāharaṇeṣv antar-bhavatīti pṛthag na darśitam, tathāpi “aho aho-rātra-kṛtāruṣā ruṣā” ity-ādau dvi-khaṇḍam, “māso māso marīcyaḥ sa-madhura-madhura-preyasī” ity-ādau tri-khaṇḍam, “vi-vitata-nānā-māmā” ity-ādau catuḥ-khaṇḍam. evam anyāny apy ūhyāni. gadyeṣu tu nāyaṁ kramaḥ. tatra yayā sadāmoda-re dāmodare guṇa-sārādhikā sā rādhikānurajyati smeti.*

**Перевод:**

**Twenty-seven kinds of yamakas were thus illustrated. Examples of special varieties of yamaka where there are two, three or more repetitions in each line have not been shown separately since they are included in previous examples. For instance, in the verse which begins: na mānam ādhehi manasy adaḥ syadaḥ (7.62), there are two repetitions in each line; in the verse which begins: māso māso marīcyaḥ sa-madhura-madhura-preyasīpreya-sīmā (7.61), there are three repetitions in each line; and in the verse that begins: vi-vitata-nānā-māmā (7.65), there are four repetitions in each line. Thus other categories (five or more repetitions in each line) should be inferred.**

**This method of counting varieties of yamakas according to various combinations of lines is not used in prose. For example: yaya sadamoda-re damodare guna-saradhika sa radhikanurajyati smeti, “Radhika loved Damodara. She had many exalted qualities. And He was always delightful.”**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti glosses sadamoda-re as: sada modam rati dadatiti tasmin, “toward He who always gives pleasure” (Subodhini). The word sadamoda-re can also be separated as: sad- amoda-re, “toward He who gives bliss to devotees.”

As regards the pratyaksara-yamaka mentioned above, Kavi Karnapura refers to Vamana. In Kavyalankara-sutra (4.1.2), Vamana shows this verse, which he says is from a book called Hari-prabodha, and calls this kind of repetition a varna-yamaka- mala:

*vividha-dhavavana nagagarddharddhanana, vivitata-gagananam amajjaj-janana, rurusasa-lalana navavandhundhunana, mama hi hita-tanananana-svasvanana.*

**Śleṣa**

### 7.66

*bhinnā apy artha-bhedena yugapad bhāṣaṇa-kṣamāḥ*  
*tyajanti bhinna-rūpatvaṁ śabdā yac chleṣa eva saḥ (16)*

**Пословный перевод:**

bhinnah—separate; api—although; artha—in meaning; bhedena— on account of a difference; yugapad—the simultaneous; bhasana— expression; ksamah—tolerate; tyajanti—give up; bhinna- rupatvam—the state of being different; sabdah—words; yat—if; slesah—double meaning; eva—only; sah—that.

**Перевод:**

**If words that are different on account of a difference in meaning can tolerate the expression of another meaning, they abandon their dissimilarity. That is called a slesa (literal double meaning).**

*artha-bhedena śabda-bheda iti nyāyāt. svara-bhedena bhedo nārtha-bhedenety āśaṅkyāha—kāvye svarasyānupayogena svaragata-bhedābhāvāc ca, kevalārtha-bhedena bhinnā api śabdā yugapad ekadā yad yady arthāntara- bhāṣaṇa-kṣamāḥ santo ’pi bhinna-rūpatvaṁ tyajanti. artha-dvaya-śleṣaṇāt śleṣaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**This is based on the principle that separate words occur on account of a difference in meaning. If, however, someone were to argue that words (even the words which sound the same) differ because of a difference in svara (Vedic accent) rather than because of a difference in meaning, he (the author) replies with the verse above, which means:**

**“If (yat = yadi) the words, although different purely on account of a difference in meaning, not on account of a difference in svara, since svaras are not even used in poetry, can simultaneously tolerate the expression of another meaning, they abandon their being different. This is called a slesa, owing to a junction (slesa = slesana) of two meanings.”**

**Комментарий:**

For example, in Vedic Sanskrit a compound is classed as a tatpurusa or as a bahuvrihi based on both the kind of svara and the position of the svara (Astadhyayi 6.1.223; 6.2.1; and so on). An instance of such a word is indra-satro (Bhagavatam [6.9.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-6/9.11)): For the details, consult Visvanatha Cakravarti’s commentary thereon. The passage ofBhagavatam is in reference to: indra-satrur vadhasva (Satapatha Brahmana 1.6.3.1, Yajur-Veda).

Above, Kavi Karnapura, following Mammata, alludes to Udbhata, who said that slesa can be based on Vedic accents: svaritadi-gunair bhinnair bandhah slistam ihocyate, “Here the literary construction is called slista (a synonym of slesa) by virtue of distinct qualities such as the svarita accent” (Kavyalankara-sara-sangraha 4.9).

A slesa is two or more words that have united. For practical purposes, we use the term “paronomastic word”, but in truth there are two words, because by rule abhidha-vrtti can only be applied one-time for each word (2.31). Thus a paronomastic word like vama (beautiful; crooked) is the union of the word vama which means “beautiful” with the word vama which means “crooked”.

**♦   the word base (prakrti),**

**♦   the gender (linga),**

**♦   the phoneme (varna),**

**♦   the suffix (pratyaya),**

**♦   the type of language (bhasa),**

**♦   the inflection (vibhakti),**

**♦   the declined word (pada), and**

**♦   the number (singular, dual, or plural) (vacana).**

**The ninth variety of slesa is called nirapeksa, where both literal meanings are similar.**

*nirapekṣaḥ prakaraṇādi-vyatirekeṇāpi tulya-vācya-dvayaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Nirapeksa is a slesa where the two literal meanings are similar in spite of differences of context and so on (2.40).**

**Комментарий:**

Mammata lists a ninth variety of slesa: bhedabhavat prakrty- ader bhedo ’pi navamo matah (Kavya-prakasa 9.85). It consists of a double meaning of a verse. Kavi Kamapura’s definition of nirapeksa-slesa is such that it includes Mammata’s ninth variety of slesa and this additional variety: In the tulya-yogita ornament based on slesa, sometimes the paronomastic word is aprastuta (noncontextual): When that happens, each word that makes the paronomastic term is aprastuta.

Usually, in slesa both words are prastuta (contextual). If one meaning is contextual and the other noncontextual, that is in the scope of dhvani.

*atra īkṣaṇa-deti dāp lavane, kṣaṇa-deti ḍudāṣ dāne iti prakṛtibhedaḥ. iṣṭā iti puṁ-liṅgam iṣṭeti strī-liṅgam iti liṅga-bhedaḥ. punar iṣṭā iti bahu-vacanam, iṣṭety eka-vacanam. tena ca vacanabhedaḥ. vidhāv itī-kārokāra-sārūpye varṇa-bhedaḥ. tudantīti śatṛpratyayaḥ, tudanti ity ākhyāta-pratyayaḥ, tena pratyaya-bhedaḥ. harita iti pañcamī, harita iti, jas tena vibhakti-bhedaḥ. anenaikena ṣaḍ-bhedāḥ pradarśitāḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**There are six varieties of slesa in this verse:**

**1.   A prakrti-slesa: iksana-dah (cutting the eyes) is made from the verbal root da\[p\] lavane, whereas ksana-da (the night, “that which provides a festival”) is made from the verbal root \[du\]da\[n\] dane,**

**2.   A linga-slesa: istah is masculine, and ista is feminine,**

**3.   A vacana-slesa: istah is plural, and ista is singular,**

**4.   A varna-slesa: the word vidhau is the locative case singular either of vidhi (the creator) or of vidhu (the moon),**

**5.   Apratyaya-slesa: tudanti is made with the present participle suffix \[s\]at\[r\], and tudanti is made with a verbal suffix, and**

**6.   A vibhakti-slesa: haritah is the ablative case singular of hari and the feminine nominative case plural of harit (direction).**

### 7.72

*kṛṣṇa-pakṣe balavatī doṣākara-parāṅ-mukhī*  
*same dve tāmasī rātriḥ sāttvikī ca satāṁ matiḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

krsna-pakse—during the waning phase (or in regard to Krsna’s side); balavati—strong; dosa-kara—to the moon (“night maker”) (or dosa-akara—to a mine of faults); parak-mukhi—averse; same—are the same; dve—both; tamasi—dark; ratrih—the night; sattviki—in the mode of goodness; ca—and; satam—of the devotees; matih—mind.

**Перевод:**

**The dark night and the devotees’ pure minds are similar: The dark night is strong during the waning half of the month (krsna- pakse) and is thus averse to the moon (dosa-kara-paran-mukhi), whereas the devotees’ pure minds are strong on Krsna’s side (krsna-pakse) and are averse to a mine of faults (dosa-akara- paran-mukhi).**

*vākya-gatatvenāyaṁ samobhaya-vācyodāharaṇeṣu draṣṭavyaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**The slesa that relates to sentences can be looked into in examples where both literal meanings are equal (nirapeksa- slesa, 7.67 vrtti).**

**Комментарий:**

There are two kinds of pada-slesa: sa-bhanga and abhanga. The word krsna-pakse is a pada-slesa of the abhanga variety: One meaning is “in the dark fortnight of the month,” where krsna-pakse is a karma-dharaya compound (krsnah ca asau paksah ca tasmin), and the other meaning is “on Krsna’s side,” where krsna- pakse is a sasthi-tatpurusa compound (krsnasya paksah tasmin). The word pakse itself is a prakrti-slesa, because the nominal base is the same and because the case endings of both words paksa are the same. Although the word krsna is a prakrti-slesa at first, the whole compound is called a pada-slesa because each word krsna has a different case ending, even though the case endings are not apparent in the compound. In a prakrti-slesa (pun on the word base), there is no difference between the case endings of the words which make the double meaning.

### 7.73

*śabdārtha-śleṣayor ayaṁ bhedaḥ—yatra śabda-parivartanenāpi na śleṣatva-bhaṅgaḥ, so ’rtha-śleṣaḥ. anyas tu sabhaṅgābhaṅgatvābhyām eva śabda-śleṣaḥ. sa coktodāharaṇeṣu śabda-parivṛtty-abhāvāt.*

**Перевод:**

**The difference between sabda-slesa (literal double meaning) and artha-slesa (one word applies to two nouns in the text) is this: An artha-slesa occurs when the play on words would not be lost by using a synonym. A sabda-slesa is the opposite, and it occurs either by breaking up the words differently (sa- bhanga) or by not breaking up the words differently (abhanga). Sabda-slesa was seen in all the previous examples since in those instances the double meanings of a word would have been lost by using a synonym.**

### 7.74

*artha-śleṣo yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of artha-slesa:**

*vilola-samphulla-kadamba-mālaḥ*  
*samullasan-mañjula-barhi-barhaḥ*  
*aśeṣa-santāpa-haro janānāṁ*  
*kṛṣṇaś ca meghaś ca sahojjihīte*

**Пословный перевод:**

vilola—moving to and fro; samphulla—fully expanded; kadamba— of kadamba flowers; malah—whose garland (or because of which \[cloud\] there is a multitude); samullasat—brilliant (or appear); manjula—lovely; barhi-barhah—who has a peacock feather (or because of which \[cloud\] the peacock feathers); asesa—unlimited; santapa—affliction; harah—takes away; jananam—of people; krsnah—Krsna; ca—and; meghah—a cloud; ca—and; saha— simultaneously; ujjihite—arise (appear).

**Перевод:**

**Krsna has a garland of fully expanded kadamba flowers that swings to and fro; a cloud causes kadamba flowers to grow and to move with the wind. Krsna has a brilliant and lovely peacock feather; a cloud cause the lovely tail feathers of peacocks to be resplendent. As soon as they come into view, Krsna and a cloud soothe the pain of living entities.**

*atra kadambādi-śabdānāṁ parivṛttyāpi na śleṣatva-hānir ity arthaśleṣa eva.*

**Перевод:**

**In this verse, the pun would not be lost even by replacing the words, such as kadamba, by different words (any other name of a kadamba flower, etc.). Therefore this is called an artha-slesa.**

**Комментарий:**

The way this verse works as an artha-slesa is: “Krsna, as well as a cloud, is vilola-samphulla-kadamba-mala. Krsna, as well as a cloud, is samullasan-manjula-barhi-barha. Upon becoming visible, Krsna, as well as a cloud, soothes the pain of living entities.”

Kavi Karnapura expounds artha-slesa in the next chapter also (8.88). The difference is that there is sabda-slesa in this example. The word that is an artha-slesa has only one meaning, yet that meaning applies to two things. By definition, that word could be replaced with a synonym without affecting the pun. Here the two subjects of description, Krsna and a cloud, are clearly mentioned, therefore slesa can take place. In the second half of the verse, the word asesa-santapa-harah (one that soothes the pain of living entities) and the verb ujjihite (appears) are instances of artha-slesa because each word has only one meaning and literally applies both to Krsna and to a cloud.

An artha-slesa can also occur in a compound where a word can be replaced with a synonym. Here the word kadamba is an artha-slesa because it could be replaced with any synonym: nlpa-priyaka- kadambas tu haripriyah, “The words nlpa, priyaka, kadamba, and haripriya are synonymous” (Amara-kosa 2.4.42).

Any substitution needs to conform to the meter. In the two bahuvrlhi compounds vilola-samphulla-kadamba-malah and samullasan- manjula-barhi-barhah, each word is an artha-slesa—except mala, which is a sabda-slesa—because each applies to Krsna and to a cloud and could be replaced with a synonym.

In addition, the verse features another ornament of sound: punar- uktavad-abhasa (seeming redundancy) (7.103), in kadamba-malah, since although both kadamba and mala can mean a multitude they are not used in that sense at the same time here. In that way there is only a semblance of a repetition.

*garbhākṣaro yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of garbhaksara (syllables contained within):**

*kāma-trapālī-lāsya-rādhikā*  
*sādhvani śāte nāsya rājate*

**Пословный перевод:**

kama—on account of love; trapa—of shyness; all—of an abundance; lasya—the dance (a flurry); radhika—She experiences; sa—She; adhvani—on the path; sate—\[which is the form of\] happiness (or which is sharp, i.e. thorny); na—not; asya—related to Him; rajate—shines.

**Перевод:**

**She experiences a flurry of intense shyness due to feelings of love. She does not reflect light on the happy path that leads to Him.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti explains how garbhaksara is a kind of citra- kavya: garbhaksara iti, etany evaksarani krama-nairapeksyena garbhe nidhaya kavina nana-chandobhih slokah kriyantam ity etad apy ekam citram, “Let poets make verses in different meters, keeping these same syllables (aksara) inside (garbha). This one also is amazing” (Subodhinl). If we follow Visvanatha Cakravarti’s interpretation of garbhaksara, this verse might be a suitable example:

*kasyā nu kā makara-ketana-mantra-gopā*  
*līlāsya moda-surabher vara-rādhikā sā*  
*hṛd-bhū-raṇa-dhvani-dhiyā ca niśākareṇa*  
*tenāsya-rā śam ajate ’dhvani rāsa-keliḥ*

**kasyah—whom? (or belongs to which lady?); nu—indeed; ka— which?; makara-ketana-mantra—is He whose mantra relates to Cupid (“his banner is the makara”); gopa—\[the pastime,\] in which there is a cowherd; lila—pastime; asya—of this (spring) (or of His); moda—endowed with fragrance; surabheh—of spring (or moda—is delightful; surabheh—of He whose fragrance); vara— in the best way; radhika—fulfils (or vara-ra—one that gives the best; adhika—superior); sa— She (Radhika); hrd-bhu—of Cupid (“he is born from the heart”); rana—in the battle; dhvani—about the sounds (or hrd-bhu-rana-dhvani—about the implied meanings in the sounds originating from the heart); dhiya—by thinking; ca—and; nisa-karena—by the moon (“it makes the night”); tena— by that (the well-known moon); asya-ra—gives a face; sam—in such a way that there is happiness; ajate—to Him, who is going; adhvani—on the path; rasa-kelih—the pastime of the Rasa dance.**

“Which girl is best fulfilled by which pastime of fragrant spring? She is Radhika, and that pastime is the Rasa dance, a pastime connected to the cowherd whose mantra relates to Cupid. The pastime puts a smile on His face when He returns on the path while recalling the sounds of lovemaking and the renowned full moon of spring.”

The letters in bold type are in the text given by Kavi Karnapura. His garbhaksara corresponds to the thirty-third art among the sixty-four arts, called kavya-samasya-purana (completing a verse submitted partially by someone). In poetical theory, this can also be classed as a poetical game (kavya-krida). Rudrata enumerates some of them: matra-bindu-cyutake prahelika karaka-kriya-gudhe, prasnottaradi canyat krida-matropayogam idam. (Kavyalankara 5.24)
