**Saṅkara**

### 8.300

*saṅkaras tv aṅgāṅgi-bhāvaḥ (77a)*

**Пословный перевод:**

sankarah—a mix; tu—but; angangi—between anga (secondary thing) and angi (main thing); bhavah—the existence.

**Перевод:**

**Sankara, however, involves an anga and an angi.**

*eṣām alaṅkārāṇām aṅgāṅgi-bhāvaḥ saṅkaraḥ. sa cānugrāhyānugrāhaka-bhāvena.*

**Перевод:**

**Sankara (mix) is the relation of anga and angi between orna­ments. It takes place by the relation of facilitated (anugrahya) and facilitator (anugrahaka).**

**Комментарий:**

This sankara is called angangi-bhava sankara. Altogether there are three varieties of sankaras. The two others are stated in texts 8.303 and 8.308.

### 8.301

*yathā,*  
*kapolayoḥ kuṇḍala-padma-rāga-*  
*mayūkha-bimbaṁ vraja-rāja-sūnoḥ*  
*sva-cumba-lagnādhara-rāga-buddhyā*  
*sva-vāsasā lumpati kāpi mugdhā*

**Пословный перевод:**

kapolayoh—on the two cheeks; kundala—of the earrings; padma- raga—of the rubies; mayukha—of the luster; bimbam—the reflection; vraja-raja—of the king of Vraja; sunoh—of the son; sva-cumba—due to her kissing; lagna—adhering; adhara—of \[her\] lips; raga—redness; buddhya—on account of perceiving; sva-vasasa—with her cloth; lumpati—removes; ka api—some girl; mugdha—simpleminded.

**Перевод:**

**Mistaking the reflection of the luster of the rubies of the prince of Vraja’s earrings on His cheeks for her kiss marks, a simple- minded gopi began wiping off the redness of His cheeks with her cloth.**

*atra tad-guṇo ’ṅgī bhrāntimān aṅgam ubhayor*  
*anugrāhakānugrāhya-bhāvenasaṅkaraḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the angi is the tad-guna ornament, the anga is the bhrantiman ornament, and there is a sankara of those two by the mode of facilitator and facilitated.**

**Комментарий:**

The tad-guna consists of the cheeks’ relinquishing their natural luster and assuming the rubies’ luster. It facilitates the girl’s mistaken perception. The tad-guna begins as the anga because it facilitates bhrantiman, but ends up as the angi given that it conveys the most literary beauty: esu yo mukhyah so ’ngi, anye ’ngani (8.302). An exception is slesopama (simile based on paronomasia) and the like, where slesa remains classed as the anga. The difference between the three varieties of alankara-sankara and those of dhvani-sankara (3.65) is that ornaments do not facilitate one another (although some say slesopama, for instance, consists in a mutual facilitation).

**Пословный перевод:**

nirasya—after removing; kara—of the rays (or of the hand); lilaya—by the play; timira—in the form of darkness; nila-cela—of the blue cloth; ancalim—the edge; rathanga—of cakravaka birds; mithuna—in the form of a pair; stanau—the two breasts; api— even; nipidya—after squeezing; jata—occurred; smitah—whose smile; hriya—due to bashfulness; iva—as if; nimisat—closing; kuse-saya—lotuses (“lying on water”); drsam—who sees (or whose eyes); sa-ragam—red (or passionate); priyah—the boyfriend; priyam—\[kisses\] the girlfriend; iva—like; sudha-akarah—the moon (“a storehouse of nectar”); hari—of Indra; harit—in the form of the direction; vadhum—the young girl; cumbati—he kisses.

**Перевод:**

**Behaving like a lover does with his beloved, the moon lifts, with its playful rays (kara) (or hands), the dark blue veil that is the darkness, squeezes, with a smile, his beloved’s breasts which are a pair of cakravaka birds, and kisses her, the eastern direction. She becomes reddish (sa-raga) at dawn. Then the night lotuses of her eyes close as if out of bashfulness (they shy away from the sun).**

*atra rūpakam utprekṣā śleṣa upamā samuccayaś ceti parasparam aṅgāṅgitayaiva pañcālaṅkārāḥ. tathā hi timirasya nīla-celatvāropād rūpakam, “hriyeva” ity utprekṣā, “kara-līlayā” iti śleṣaḥ, “priyaḥ priyām iva” ity upamā, “nirasya” “nipīḍya” iti samuccayaḥ. eṣu yo mukhyaḥ, so ’ṅgī, anye ’ṅgāni. evaṁ śabdālaṅkāra-pakṣe ’pi, yathā—“sasāra sā” ity-ādau yamakānuprāsa-dvy-akṣara-murajabandha-go-mūtrikā-bandha-kavāṭa-mukta-kavāṭa-śṛṅkhalādayaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Here five ornaments—rupaka, utpreksa, slesa, upama, and samuccaya—are in a relation of angi and anga. For instance:**

**♦   An utpreksa is hriya iva (as if out of bashfulness);**

**♦   A slesa is kara-lilaya (with the playful rays, or with the playful hands);**

**♦   An upama is priyah priyam iva (like a lover does to his beloved);**

**♦   A samuccaya is nirasya (removing) and nipidya (squeezing) (this is a conjunction of actions).**

**Of these five ornaments, the one that is judged principal is the angi, whereas the others are the angas.**

**Sankara also occurs between ornaments of sound. This example was shown earlier:**

*sasāra sā sa-sārasāsa-sāra-sāsa-sāra-sā*

**Перевод:**

**Radha and Krsna stroll together in a forest. Her movements put to shame the bewildering power of sleep. Radhika holds a lotus flower and belittles the pose of the cakravakas. Upon seeing Her, these cakravakas cry, become stunned, and look resplendent. (7.64)**

**The verse illustrates yamaka, anuprasa, and dvy-aksara (using only two consonants in one verse). In addition, the verse fits in many diagrams, such as: (1) muraja drum, (2) go-mutrika (zig­zag), (3) baddha-kavata (closed door), (4) mukta-kavata (open door), and (5) srnkhala (chain).**

**Пословный перевод:**

bahunam—of many; va—either; dvayoh—of two; ca va—or; saha— together; avasthana—in the matter of being situated; badhena— due to the contradiction; bhavet—is; no—not; va—or; iti—thus; aniscaye—when there is uncertainty; sankarah—mix; aniscaya- akhyah—known as aniscaya; syat—is; yatha-sthanam—properly; pradarsyate—is shown.

### 8.304

*yathā,*  
*yathānanda-syandī dṛśi dṛśi yathāyaṁ bahu-kalo*  
*yathā nakṣatrāṇāṁ patir api yathā tāpa-haraṇaḥ*  
*yathāyaṁ bhānor apy upari parisartā katham atho*  
*tathā nāyaṁ dhātrā vidhur aniśa-pūrṇo viracitaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

yatha—just as; ananda—bliss; syandi—effuses; drsi drsi—in every eye; yatha—just as; ayam—this (the moon); bahu-kalah— which has many digits (kala); yatha—just as; naksatranam—of the constellations; patih—the husband; api—also; yatha—just as; tapa—heat (or affliction); haranah—takes away; yatha—just as; ayam—this; bhanoh—the sun; api—even; upari—above; parisarta—orbits; katham—why; atho—then; tatha—so; na—not; ayam—this (the moon); dhatra—by the creator; vidhuh—moon; anisa—is constant; purnah—one whose fullness; viracitah—was made.

**Перевод:**

**The moon effuses bliss in every eye, has many phases, is the constellations’ husband, orbits above the sun, and is cooling, so why did the creator not make the moon constantly full?**

*atra viśeṣyasya candrasya prastutasya śliṣṭair eva viśeṣaṇair aprastutasya kasyacid dharmasya pratīti-rūpā kiṁ samāsoktiḥ, kiṁ vā tasyaiva candrasyāprastutasya śaṁsana-mukhena kasyacit sādhos tathā-vidhasya kasyacit kṣīṇatādi-dharmasya prastutatvapratyāyiny aprastuta-praśaṁseti niścayābhāvād aniścayasaṅkaraḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**A doubt arises in the verse: (1) Is this samasokti? It could be, since the double-meaning modifiers belonging to the moon, which is the substantive and the subject of description, causes the perception of similar attributes in a certain person who is not the subject of description, (2) Or is it aprastuta-prasamsa ? That is also possible, since by talking about the moon and by considering that it is not the subject of description, similar qualities of a certain sadhu, such as thinness, are implied.**

**On account of the absence of certainty (niscaya) in that way, there is aniscaya-sankara (a doubt about which ornament is taking place).**

**Комментарий:**

The doubt mainly regards what is the subject of discussion (prastuta). If the moon is deemed prastuta, that is samasokti, but if the sadhu is deemed prastuta and the moon aprastuta, that is aprastuta-prasamsa, specifically the sadrsya variety (8.104). Neither ornament can be definitely rejected here, thus no decision about the classification can be reached.

From the perspective of samasokti, the adjectives carry other meanings:

(A)  ananda-syandl drsi drsi (it effuses bliss in every eye)—Krsna causes bliss to flow in every eye,

(B)  bahu-kalah (it has many fractions)—He has much expertise, (C) naksatranampatih (it is the constellations’ husband)—He is the Lord of Radha, Visakha, Anuradha, Citra, and Dhanistha, (these gopis are named after certain constellations),

(D)  tapa-haranah (it is cooling)—He removes distress, and

(E)  bhanor apy upari parisarta (it orbits above the sun)—He wanders beyond the purview of Vrsabhanu (unbeknownst to Her father, He enjoys pastimes with Radha). Thus the devotees reprimandingly ask the creator why he did not make Krsna fully visible to them at all times.

From the perspective of aprastuta-prasamsa, the scenario is that a very prominent and beloved sadhu became sick, and so his body became thin, therefore his followers reprimandingly ask the creator why he did not allow their master to always be plump. In this understanding, the double-meaning modifiers are interpreted as follows:

(1)  ananda-syandldrsi drsi—The sadhu gives joy to every eye,

(2)  bahu-kalah—he has much expertise,

(3)  tapa-haranah—he removes distress,

(4)  naksatranam patih—he is a leader of stars (his disciples), and (5) bhanor apy upari parisarta—he goes beyond the sun (after death he takes the solar path and never comes back).

**Перевод:**

*idaṁ te radana-dyotair etair upacitaṁ smitam*  
*jyotsneva mukha-candrasya kāmam āmodakaṁ dṛśoḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

idam—this; te—of yours; radana—of the teeth; dyotaih—due to the rays; etaih—due to these; upacitam—increased \[in beauty\]; smitam—smile; jyotsna—the moonlight; iva—like; mukha- candrasya—of the moon-like face; kamam—freely; amodakam— gives bliss; drsoh—to the eyes.

**Перевод:**

**This smile of your moon-like face is even more beautiful due to the radiance of your teeth. It profusely delights the eyes like moonlight does.**

*atra pradhānatayā smitaṁ mukha evānukūlam, na tu candre. tenopamāyāḥ sādhakaṁ na rūpakasya, ato mukha-candrasyeti rūpakaṁ na bhavati. tena na sandehaḥ, tad-abhāvāt saṅkaro ’pi na.*

**Перевод:**

**Usually a smile is in conformity with a face, not with the moon. Thus here the compound mukha-candra must be interpreted as a simile (moon-like face), not as a metaphor (moon face). Hence there is no doubt, and so there is no sankara.**

### 8.306

*aho bata mahaty asya dhṛṣṭatābhīrutāpi ca*  
*mukha-candre saty ayaṁ te yad anyaś candra udgataḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

aho—how amazing; bata—how astonishing; mahati—great; asya—of this \[moon\]; dhrstata—boldness; abhiruta—fearlessness; api—also; ca—and; mukha-candre sati—when there is a moon in the form of a face; ayam—this; te—your; yat—because; anyah— other; candrah—moon; udgatah—has arisen.

**Перевод:**

**How astonishing is its fearlessness! And how amazing is its great boldness because, although your moon face already exists, this other moon has arisen.**

*atrānyatvaṁ candrasyānukūlam, na tu mukhasya, tasya pratikūlam eva. tena rūpakasya sādhakam, na tūpamāyāḥ, tasyās tu bādhakam. “śāstrajña-bhāskaraṁ saṁjñā tvām āliṅgati sarvadā” ity atrāliṅganam upamā-bādhakam. nahi satī strī patisadṛśe ’nurajyati. ato rūpakasyaiva sādhakam.*

**Перевод:**

**The moon rises whereas a face does not. Therefore here mukha- candra must be interpreted as a metaphor.**

**This is another example: sastrajna-bhaskaram samjna tvam alingati sarvada, “Samjna, the lady that is perfect knowledge, always embraces you, a sun that is a knower of scriptures.” Here the action of embracing debars the word sastrajna- bhaskara from being a simile (a knower of scriptures who is like a sun) because a virtuous lady never loves someone who is like her husband (much less others). Therefore this only effects a metaphor.**

**Комментарий:**

Samjna is a wife of the sun, along with Chaya. Visvanatha Cakravarti analyzes the name Samjna as: samyag-jnana-rupa stri, “a lady in the form of complete knowledge.” The idea is that perfect knowledge embraces someone who knows the scriptures. Visvanatha Cakravarti’s analysis of Samjna as a metaphor referring to a lady is analogous to the words vidya-vadhu (the lady in the form of knowledge; Sarasvati) in Siksastakam.

### 8.309

*yathā,*

*magnaś ciraṁ hari-harit-sarasī-rasebhyaḥ*  
*ratyunmamajja śanakair amṛtāṁśu-haṁsaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

saivala—in the form of algae; laksana—a characteristic; vilaksana—crude; laksma—mark; laksmih—the splendor of whose; uddanda—extraordinary; rasmi—in the form of rays; visa—of lotus stems; mandala—with a multitude; mandyamanah—being adorned; magnah—being immersed; ciram—for a long time; hari-harit—in the form of the direction of Indra (Hari), i.e. the eastern direction; sarasi—of the lake; rasebhyah—from the waters; pratyunmamajja—emerged; sanakaih—gradually; amrta-amsu— in the form of the moon (“whose rays are nectar”); hamsah—a swan.

*atra rūpakānuprāsāv eka-pada-viṣayau, na tu saṁsṛṣṭi-vat pṛthagviṣayāv iti tri-vidhaḥ saṅkaraḥ.*

**Комментарий:**

In this verse there are four sankaras between rupaka and anuprasa, and each one is located in one word:

\- saivala-laksana-vilaksana-laksma-laksmlh: The rupaka is saivala-laksana (a characteristic in the form of algae): the anuprasa consists of a vrtti anuprasa of l, another of laksan (which is a portion of a word, 7.18), and another of laksm,

\- uddanda-rasmi-visa-mandala-mandyamanah: The rupaka is uddanda-rasmi-visa-mandala (lotus stems in the form of marvelous rays): the anuprasa is a vrtti anuprasa of m and an ojo vrtti anuprasa of nd,

\- hari-harii-sarasl-rasebhyah: The rupaka is hari-harit-sarasi (the lake in the form of the eastern direction): there is a yamaka of hari and a vrtti anuprasa of s (this is a sankara of one ornament of meaning and two ornaments of sound), and

\- amrtamsu-hamsah: The rupaka is the whole word (the swan in the form of the moon) and there is a cheka anuprasa of the anusvara (m).

artha-alankrtayah—ornaments of meaning; suddhah—pure; dvi-sastih—sixty-two; tat—of those \[ornaments of meaning\]; prabhedatah—according to the subdivisions; asva—seven \[horses of the sun\]; naga—eight \[elephants of the directions\]; sasa-ankah— one \[moon\]; syuh—are; tavata—by the same amount; gunanena— by multiplying; te—they.

### 8.314

*itaretara-saṁsṛṣṭyā graha-rtu-graha-sindhubhiḥ*  
*yuto ’gnir ete ca punaḥ saṅkareṇa tri-rūpiṇā*  
*aśva-bindu-grahāmbhodhi-bindu-candrāḥ prakīrtitāḥ (83)*

**Пословный перевод:**

itara-itara-samsrstya—by mutual combinations; graha—nine \[planets\]; rtu—six \[seasons\]; graha—nine \[planets\]; sindhubhih— with four \[oceans\]; yutah—joined; agnih—three \[fires\]; ete—these; ca—and; punah—again; sankarena—\[multiplied\] by the sankaras; tri-rupina—which has three forms; asva—seven \[horses of the sun\]; bindu—zero (the shape of a drop); graha—nine; ambhodhi— four \[oceans\]; bindu—zero; candrah—one \[moon\]; prakirtitah— announced.

**Перевод:**

**By mutual combinations made by multiplying them by the same amount (187 x 187), the total is 34,969 samsrstis of ornaments of meaning. Again, after multiplying by three, which is the number of sankaras, there is a grand total of 104,907 ornaments of meaning.**

### 8.315

*śabdālaṅkāra-saṁsṛṣṭyā vāji-sindhu-mataṅgajaiḥ*  
*bindu-vājībha-ṣaḍ-bāṇā ubhayālaṅkṛti-grahāḥ (84)*

**Пословный перевод:**

sabda-alankara—with the ornaments of meaning; samsrstya—by combining; vaji—seven \[horses of the sun\]; sindhu—four \[oceans\]; matangajaih—with eight \[elephants of the directions\]; bindu— two zeros (the shapes of two drops); vaji—seven \[horses of the sun\]; ibha—eight \[elephants of the directions\]; sad—six; banah— five \[arrows of Cupid\]; ubhaya-alankrti—of ubhaya alankaras (ornament of sound and ornament of meaning); grahah—covers the amount.

**Перевод:**

**By combining the total number of ornaments of meaning (104,907) with the total number of ornaments of sound (5,421), there is a grand total of 568,700,847 ubhaya alankaras.**

**Комментарий:**

This section about the count of combinations of ornaments is not found in other treatises on poetics. An ubhaya alankara is one ornament which is both an ornament of sound and an ornament of meaning. An example is punar-uktavad-abhasa. The above theory stated by Kavi Karnapura was implied by Mammata: tad ayam anugrahyanugrahakataya sandehena, eka-pada-pratipadyataya ca vyavasthitatvat tri-prakara eva samkaro vyakrtah. prakarantarena tu na sakyo vyakartum anantyat tat-prabhedanam iti pratipaditah sabdarthobhaya-gatatvena traividhya-juso ’lamkarah. (Kavya- prakasa 10.141)

**Rasavat, and so on**

### 8.316

*rasavat-preya-ūrjasvi-samāhita-samākhyayā*  
*rasālaṅkṛtayo ’py anyāś catasro rasa-poṣikāḥ (85)*

**Пословный перевод:**

rasavat-preyah-urjasvi-samahita—rasavat, preyas, urjasvi, and samahita; samakhyaya—by the name of; rasa—of rasa; alankrtayah—ornaments;       api—although; anyah—others; catasrah—four; rasa—of rasa; posikah—nourishers.

**Перевод:**

**Although rasavat, preyas, urjasvi, and samahita are ornaments in the form of rasa, they enhance the rasa.**

*yatra rase sphuṭatayā śabdālaṅkāro ’rthālaṅkāro vā nirṇītuṁ na śakyate, kevalaṁ rasa-sāmagrī sphurati, tatra rasālaṅkārā eva boddhavyāḥ. te ca yathā-yogyam eva sambhavanti. śṛṅgāre preya ūrjasvī vīra-bībhatsa-raudreṣu anyāv anyeṣu. te ’pi sati sambhave śabdārthālaṅkārābhyāṁ saṁsṛṣṭau bhavantīty api jñeyam.*

**Перевод:**

**When neither an ornament of sound nor an ornament of meaning can be clearly pointed out in a rasa, that is to say only the ingredients of the rasa are apparent, then rasavat, preyas, urjasvi, and samahita are only to be understood as ornaments in the form of a rasa. They occur in accordance with the suitability. Preyas occurs in srngara-rasa; urjasvi in vira- rasa, bibhatsa-rasa and raudra-rasa; and rasavat and samahita occur in the other rasas. When they are in combination with ornaments of sound and with ornaments of meaning, they too become manifold.**

**Комментарий:**

Kavi Karnapura does not provide examples. His interpretations of rasavat and so on are quite different from those of other poetical theorists. This topic ends here.

**Alankara-dosa**

### 8.317

*athaiṣāṁ kathyate doṣaḥ (86a)*  
*eṣāṁ śabdārthālaṅkārāṇām.*

**Перевод:**

**Now the faults related to ornaments of sound and to ornaments of meaning will be expounded.**

### 8.318

*vaiphalyaṁ vṛtty-ayogyatā*  
*prasiddheś ca viruddhatvam*  
*anuprāse mala-trayam (86bcd)*  
*malo doṣaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**In anuprasa (alliteration), there are three faults:**

**♦   vaiphalya (uselessness),**

**♦   vrtti ayogyata (also called vrtti-virodha, placing adverse phonemes), and**

**♦   prasiddhi-viruddha (contrary to what is well-known).**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti glosses vaiphalyam (uselessness) as apustarthatvam (not nourishing the sense). The literary faults are mentioned in chapter ten. Mammata says the faults in alliteration are included in those faults. According to him, vaiphalya is similar to apustartha (irrelevant, “not nourishing the sense”) (10.110), vrtti ayogyata is the same as pratilomaksara (adverse phonemes) (10.73), and prasiddhi-viruddha is the same as prasiddhi-virodha (contrary to what is well-known) (10.115) (Kavya-prakasa 10.142). This topic is mostly of interest to Sanskrit writers.

### 8.319

*krameṇodāharaṇāni,*

**Перевод:**

**Examples are shown.**  
**\[This is an instance of vaiphalya (uselessness):\]**

*dvandvaṁ dvandvaṁ vādayad-dundubhīnāṁ*  
*nandad-vṛndaṁ vyomni vṛndārakāṇām*  
*harṣotkarṣān nāka-mākanda-varṣaiḥ*  
*sāndrānandaṁ nanda-sūnuṁ vavande*

**Пословный перевод:**

dvandvam dvandvam—two by two; vadayat—are resounding; dundubhinam—by whom kettledrums; nandat—ajoyful; vrndam— multitude; vyomni—in the sky; vrndarakanam—of demigods; harsa—of joy; utkarsat—due to an upsurge; naka—celestial; makanda—of mango buds; varsaih—with showers; sandra— condensed; anandam—who has bliss; nanda-sunum—the son of Nanda; vavande—praised.

**Перевод:**

**A joyful legion of gods assembled in the sky and resounded pairs of kettledrums in unison. Due to an upsurge of joy, they extolled Nanda’s blissful son by showering celestial mango buds on Him.**

*atra mākanda-śabdo niṣphalaḥ. atraiva “harṣotkarṣād indu-kundadyutīnāṁ” iti pāṭhe sarveṣāṁ devānāṁ śuklatvam aprasiddham. tena “śīdhu-syandāmanda-mandāra-varṣaiḥ” iti nyāyyaḥ pāṭhaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the word makanda (mango buds) is fruitless. If the compound naka-makanda-varsaih (with showers of celestial mango buds) were replaced by: indu-kunda-dyutmam (\[gods\] whose effulgence is bright like the moon or jasmine), the inconvenience would be that the brightness of the gods is not well-known (this is an instance of the third fault, prasiddhi- viruddha). Therefore the preferred option is to change the whole third line to: sidhu-syandamanda-mandara-varsaih (with showers of abundant parijatas that exude nectar). The reading is proper that way.**

**Комментарий:**

The gods’ throwing mango buds is nothing special because mango buds are easily available on earth.

*vṛtti-virodho yathā,*

prakanda—excellent; bhuja—arms; dandah—like poles; ayam— this well-known \[Krsna\]; pundarika—are like lotuses; iksanah— whose eyes; ksani—who has an opportunity; kundala—on the earrings; udbhasi—shines; ganda—of whose cheeks; srih—the effulgence; stri—of ladies; mandalam—a multitude; amandayat— adorned.

**Перевод:**

**Here the vrtti anuprasa is not suited to madhura-rasa.**

**Комментарий:**

The vrtti anuprasa in this verse is conducive to ojas (vigor), not to madhurya (sweetness), the underlying topic. Here the ojas is mostly in reference to the sounds nd and ks, but they do not refer to any meaning in the scope of ojas.

*upamāyāṁ tu hīnatā ādhikyaṁ ca bhavej jāti-*

*idhy-āder api bhede cāsāmyāsambhāvyayor api (88)*

**Пословный перевод:**

ca-karad dharma-gatapi hmatadhikata ceti trayodasopama-dosah. upamayam—in regard to simile; tu—but; hinata—inadequacy; adhikyam—excessiveness; ca—and; bhavet—is; jati- pramanabhyam—in terms of category and size; tada—then; api—also; sah—that \[fault\]; lingasya—of gender; vacanasya—of the number; api—and; kalasya—of the time; purusasya—of the person; ca—and; vidhi-adeh—of the enjoinment and so on; api— and; bhede—in regard to a difference; ca—and; asamya—and dissimilarity; asambhavyayoh—in regard to an impossibility; api— also.

**5.   Difference in number (singular, dual, or plural),**

**8.   Difference in the person (first, second, or third person),**

### 8.324

*krameṇodāharaṇāni,*

**Перевод:**

**Examples are in order:**

*devo ’yaṁ puṣpa-kodaṇḍaś caṇḍāla iva dāruṇaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

devah—demigod; ayam—this; puspa-kodandah—Cupid (“he has a flower bow”); candalah—an outcaste; iva—like; darunah—harsh.

**Перевод:**

**This god, Cupid, is harsh like an outcaste.**

*atra jātyā hīnatā. “caṇḍāṁśur iva tāpa-kṛt” iti yuktam.*

**Перевод:**

**There is inadequacy in terms of category. A proper replacement is: candamsur iva tapa-krt, “\[This god, Cupid,\] scorches like the sun.”**

**Комментарий:**

Someone might wonder whether a poet would actually compare Cupid to an outcaste. Here Kavi Karnapura refers to Dandi, who wrote: kamam kandarpa-candalo mayi vamaksi nirdayah, tvayi nirmatsaro distyety agramyo ’rtho rasavahah, ““Girl with beautiful eyes, toward me the outcaste called Cupid is merciless at will. Due to fate, he has no malice toward you.” In this way a meaning that is not vulgar conveys relishment” (Kavyadarsa 1.64). Bhoja reiterated Dandi’s verse (Sarasvati-kanthabharana 5.6).

*vrajaṁ viśan nanda-sutaḥ pradoṣe*

Visvanatha Cakravarti comments that the verb atanoti, “\[like the moon\] expands \[bliss\]” should be added (Subodhini). The fault is that atatana, in the verse, is in the past tense. That type of fault is specifically illustrated below.

### 8.333

*bhāsi tvaṁ kalpa-vallīva sarva-kāma-phala-pradā*

**Пословный перевод:**

bhasi tvam—you shine; kalpa-valli—a desire creeper; iva—like; sarva-kama—of all desires; phala—the result; prada—gives.

**Перевод:**

*atra puruṣa-bhedas tenāśuddham. “kalpa-vallīva bhavatī bhāti sarva-phala-pradā” iti śuddham.*

**Перевод:**

**There is a difference in terms of person (the second person and the third person are used, but the verb only matches the second person). A proper substitution is: kalpa-valliva bhavati bhati sarva-phala-prada. (The mening is the same.)**

**Комментарий:**

The pronoun tvam (you) is replaced by the pronoun bhavati (you), since a verb connected with the pronoun bhavat\[r\] is conjugated in the third person. Or else, in the original wording the verb bhati would have to be added.

### 8.334

*kṛṣṇe pravahatu prītis tava gaṅgeva santatam*

**Пословный перевод:**

krsne—toward Krsna; pravahatu—may it flow; pritih—love; tava— your; ganga—the Ganga river; iva—like; santatam—continuously.

**Перевод:**

**May your love always flow toward Krsna like the Ganges flows.**

*ity atra vidhy-ādi-bhedaḥ, tenāśuddham. “gaṅgeva pravahadrūpā tava kṛṣṇe sadā ratiḥ” iti śuddham. ādi-śabdād anumatir api. asāmye, yathā—“grathnāmi kāvya-śaśinaṁ vitatārtha-raśmim” ity atra kāvya-śaśinoḥ kenāpy aṁśena sāmyaṁ nāsti. evam artharaśmyoś ca.*

**Перевод:**

**There is a discrepancy in the enjoinment. Thus it is faulty. An appropriate replacement is: gangeva pravahad-rupa tava krsne sada ratih, “Your constant love for Krsna is like the ever flowing Ganges.”**

**The word adi (and so on) (in this vrtti and in text 8.323) refers to anumati (giving permission).**

**This is an example of asamya (dissimilarity): grathnami kavya- sasinam vitatartha-rasmim, “I string together a kavya book that is like the moon, whose rays are like expanded meanings” (Kavyalankara-sutra-vrtti 4.2.16). Here there is no fraction of a similarity between kavya and the moon, nor between a meaning and a ray.**

### 8.335

*asambhāvyaṁ yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of asambhavya (impossibility):**

*tavānanād idaṁ rādhe nirgataṁ madhuraṁ vacaḥ*  
*ānandayati me karṇau candrād iva madhu kṣarat*

**Пословный перевод:**

tava—of Yours; ananat—from the mouth; idam—this; radhe—O Radha; nirgatam—gone away; madhuram—sweet; vacah—speech; anandayati—delights; me—my; karnau—two ears; candrat—from the moon; iva—like; madhu—honey; ksarat—flowing.

**Перевод:**

**Radha, these sweet words emanating from Your mouth delight my ears like honey flowing from the moon.**

*candrān madhu-kṣaraṇam asambhāvyam. karṇayor api madhuna ānandakatvam asambhāvyam. “āsvādyatvam atīvaiti padmād iva madhu kṣarat” iti śuddham.*

**Перевод:**

**Honey cannot flow from the moon nor can honey delight the ears, so the second half of the verse should be changed to: asvadyatvam atTvaiti padmad iva madhu ksarat. In that way the verse means: “Radha, these sweet words emanating from Your mouth are extremely relishable, like honey exuding from a lotus.”**

### 8.336

*dharma-hīnatā yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**This illustrates the inadequacy of a common element:**

*sa pīta-vāsāḥ śikhi-piccha-maulir viloka-hāro harir uccakāśe*  
*taḍil-latā-śakra-śarāsanābhyāṁ vibhūṣito navya ivāmbuvāhaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

sah—He; pita—is yellow; vasah—whose cloth; sikhi—of a peacock; piccha—is the tail feather; maulih—whose crest; viloka—glances; harah—who takes away; harih—Hari; uccakase—shone (appeared resplendent); tadit-lata—forked lighning; sakra-sarasanabhyam— with Indra’s bow; vibhusitah—adorned; navyah—new; iva—like; ambu-vahah—a cloud (“it carries water”).

**Перевод:**

**Hari is resplendent. Like a new raincloud adorned with lightning and a rainbow, He wears a yellow cloth, His crest is a peacock’s tail feather, and He catches the eye.**

*atra “viloka-hāraḥ” ity asya balākā-rūpa-dharma-hīnatā. tena “vibhūṣyamāṇaḥ kṣaṇa-rocir-indra-dhanur-balākābhir ivāmbuvāhaḥ.”*

**Перевод:**

**Here a crane, the element that would match “He catches the eye”, is missing. This is the replacement: vibhusyamanah ksana-rocir-indra-dhanur-balakabhir ivambuvahah, “like a raincloud adorned with a lightning flash, a rainbow, and a crane.”**

### 8.337

*dharmādhikyaṁ yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of the excessiveness of a common element:**

*cāmīkarābhaṁ vasanaṁ vasānaḥ*  
*śikhaṇḍa-cūḍo harir ābabhāse*  
*vibhūṣyamāṇaḥ kṣaṇa-rocir-indra-*  
*dhanur-balākābhir ivāmbuvāhaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

camikara—like gold; abham—which shines; vasanam—a cloth; vasanah—wearing; sikhanda—is a peacock’s tail; cudah—whose crest; harih—Hari; ababhase—shone (i.e. appeared resplendent); vibhusyamanah—being adorned; ksana-rocih—lightning (instant flash); indra-dhanuh—a rainbow; balakabhih—with cranes; iva— like; ambu-vahah—a rain cloud.

**Перевод:**

**Wearing a golden garment, Hari, who has a peacock feather crest, shone like a raincloud adorned with a lightning flash, a rainbow, and a crane.**

*atra balākā-rūpa-dharmādhikyam.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the excessiveness of a common element is that a crane is mentioned.**

### 8.338

*sārūpye liṅga-bhedas tu na doṣo na ca vā guṇaḥ (89)*

**Пословный перевод:**

sarupye—when there is sameness of form; linga—in regard to the gender; bhedah—difference; tu—nut; na—not; dosah—a fault; na—not; ca—and; va—either; gunah—a quality.

**Перевод:**

**However, when there is sameness of form, the difference in gender is neither a fault nor a quality.**

*sārūpyaṁ bhinna-liṅgatve ’py ekākāratvam.*

**Перевод:**

**Sameness of form means having the same grammatical form even when the genders are different.**

### 8.339

*yathā,*  
*mahā-ratnair iva guṇaiḥ kṛṣṇa-ratnākaro bhavān*  
*tavāmṛtam iva svāduṁ vyāhāraṁ vedmi rādhike*

**Пословный перевод:**

maha-ratnaih—large jewels; iva—like; gunaih—with qualities; krsna-ratna-akarah—Krsna’s jewel mine; bhavan—You; tava—Your; amrtam—nectar; iva—like; svadum—is delectable; vyaharam—speech; vedmi—I know; radhike—O Radhika.

**Перевод:**

**Radhika, I know Your speech is delectable like nectar. Since Your qualities are like large jewels, You are a jewel mine for Krsna.**

**Комментарий:**

Speech (vyahara) is compared to nectar (amrtam): Vyahara is masculine whereas amrta is neuter, but in the second case singular the case ending is the same. Similarly, the qualities (guna) are compared to jewels (ratnam): Guna is masculine whereas ratna is neuter, but in the third case plural the ending is the same.

### 8.340

*utprekṣāyāṁ yathā-śabdaḥ (90a)*

**Перевод:**

**In utpreksa (fanciful assumption), the usage of the word yatha (as) is faulty.**

*duṣṭa ity arthaḥ. yathā-śabdasya kevalaṁ sādharmya-mātraparyavasāyitvād avācakatvam utprekṣāyāḥ. tasyās tu nūnam, manye, dhruvam ity-ādayo vācakāḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**The word yatha does not express utpreksa, since yatha only amounts to a mere similarity. However, the following terms convey utpreksa: nunam (indeed), manye (I think), dhruvam (certainly), and so on.**

### 8.341

*udāharaṇam,*  
*citte dravati toyena pūryate nayana-dvayam*  
*priyayoś citta-nayane saṁvāda-cature yathā*

**Пословный перевод:**

citte—when the heart; dravati—melts; toyena—with water; puryate—are filled; nayana—of eyes; dvayam—the pair; priyayoh—of the two lovers; citta—the heart; nayane—and the eyes; samvada—at conversing; cature—expert; yatha—as.

**Перевод:**

**When the heart melts, the eyes become filled with tears, as (as though) the heart and the eyes of the two lovers were expert at conversing with each other.**

*atra yathā-śabda utprekṣāyā avācakaḥ. tena “saṁvāda-cature iva” “saṁvāda-cature dhruvam” iti vā śuddham*

**Перевод:**

**The word yatha is not expressive of an utpreksa. Therefore, the words samvada-cature yatha should be modified to either samvada-cature iva or samvada-cature dhruvam.**

### 8.342

*evam anye ’pi sūkṣmataḥ (90b)*  
*evam anye sūkṣmatamā alaṅkāra-doṣāḥ santi, teṣāṁ kecid agre doṣa-vivaraṇe darśayiṣyante.*

**Пословный перевод:**

evam—similarly; anye—other \[faults\]; api—also; suksmatah—on account of being subtle.

**Перевод:**

**Similarly, there are other, subtler faults in ornaments. Some of them will be shown later, in the treatment of literary faults.**

*ity alaṅkāra-kaustubhe ’rthālaṅkāra-nirūpaṇo nāma aṣṭamaḥ kiraṇaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Thus ends the eighth ray in Alankara-kaustubha, entitled “a disquisition on ornaments of meaning.”**

## Ninth Ray - The Styles

### 9.1

*atha rīti-nirṇayaḥ. atha “su-saṁsthānaṁ rītiḥ” iti yad uktaṁ sā hi lakṣaṇā kiyat-prakārā veti tām eva darśayati—*

**Перевод:**

**In the description of the Kavya-purusa, it was said that the style is the pose (1.7). “But what is the definition? And does it have subvarieties?” Therefore he shows the definition:**

*rītiḥ syād varṇa-vinyāsa-viśeṣo guṇa-hetukaḥ (1)*

**Перевод:**

**A style is a distinct placement of phonemes which is caused by a guna.**

*guṇās tūktāḥ. varṇa-vinyāsa-viśeṣa iti varṇānāṁ rasānuguṇaguṇānurodhopādhika-racanā-viśeṣa ity arthaḥ. yadyapi guṇavivekenaiva sa labhyate, tathāpi tad-viśeṣa-bodhārthaṁ rīti-kiraṇa ārabhyate.*

**Перевод:**

**The gunas were mentioned. The sense of “a distinct placement of phonemes” is: “a distinct construction whose essential characteristics are in conformity with the guna which is suitable to the rasa.” Although the understanding of the constructions was already obtained by a discussion on the gunas, the chapter on the styles is begun to give details on specific types of constructions.**

### 9.2

*vaidarbhy-ādi-viśeṣeṇa caturdhā sā nigadyate (2)*

**Перевод:**

**There are four kinds of style, because of special varieties such as Vaidarbhi.**

*sā rītiḥ, vaidarbhī pāñcālī gauḍī lāṭīti catur-vidhā. tāsāṁ lakṣaṇam āha—*

**Перевод:**

**The four styles are Vaidarbhi, Pancali, Gaudi and Lati. He defines them:**

### 9.3

*avṛttir alpa-vṛttir vā samasta-guṇa-bhūṣitā*  
*vaidarbhī sā tu śṛṅgāre karuṇe ca praśasyate (3)*

**Пословный перевод:**

avrttih—one in which there is no compound; alpa-vrttih—one in which there are short compounds; va—or; samasta-guna-bhusita— adorned with all the gunas; vaidarbhi—riti named Vaidarbhi (“existing in Vidarbha”); sa—that; tu—only; srngare—in srngara- rasa; karune—in karuna-rasa; ca—and; prasasyate—is highly approved.

**Перевод:**

**The Vaidarbhi has all the gunas. Either there is no compound or the compounds are short. Only the Vaidarbhi is very appropriate in srngara-rasa and in karuna-rasa.**

*samasta-guṇeti guṇās trayo vā daśa vā*

**Перевод:**

**“All the gunas” means either the three or the ten.**

**Комментарий:**

Kavi Kamapura’s methodology of riti is unique. Vamana says the Vaidarbhi has all the gunas. Most rhetoricians agree that the Vaidarbhi is simply the construction of the well-known madhurya- guna (sweet phonemes, and either no compound or short compounds) and the Gaudi is the construction of ojas guna.

### 9.4

*yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of Vaidarbhi in srngara-rasa:**

*ālokanaṅ kuṭilitena vilocanena*  
*sambhāṣaṇañ ca vacasā manasārdham ardham*  
*līlā-mayasya vapuṣaḥ prakṛtis taveyaṁ*  
*rādhe kramo na madanasya na vā madasya*

**Пословный перевод:**

alokanam—looking; kutilitena—made crooked; vilocanena—by a glance; sambhasanam—conversation; ca—and; vacasa—by speech; manasa—by the mind; ardham—half; ardham—half; lila-mayasya—consisting of pastimes; vapusah—of the body; prakrtih—nature; tava—of Yours; iyam—this; radhe—O Radha; kramah—the sequence; na—not; madanasya—of Cupid; na va— nor; madasya—of excessive delight.

**Перевод:**

**Radha, You habitually cast a look with a crooked glance, and Your expressions are half vocal and half psychological. Such is the nature of Your flirtatious body. This is neither the normal procedure of Cupid nor the usual sequence of a state of intoxication.**

*atrāvṛttir alpa-vṛttiś ca. ṅku-mbhāñceti mādhurya-vyañjakā varṇāḥ. ardham ardham ity ojo-vyañjakau dvau, artha-vaiśadyaṁ prasādaḥ, aniṣṭhuratvaṁ su-kumāratā, ity-ādi-samasta-guṇāḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Here for the most part there is no compound. The only compound is short. The phonemes nk, mbh, and nc suggest sweetness. Only two phonemes suggest ojas, in: ardham ardham. Prasada occurs since the overall meaning from the structure of the words is clear. There is sukumarata (softness) because there is no harsh sound. The list goes on. Thus all the gunas are present.**

### 9.5

*na kevalam iyaṁ tathā-vidha-varṇa-vinyāsād vṛtty-abhāvāc ca vaidarbhī, api tv artha-gataudāryeṇāpi. anyathā,*

**Перевод:**

**However, the Vaidarbhi does not take place merely because of such a placement of phonemes and because of the absence of compounding. Rather, the meaning must be noble. This is a counterexample:**

*madanena madena cālaso*  
*vanitābhir janitātilālasaḥ*  
*atimañjuni kuñja-mandire*  
*ramate ’sau sakhi nanda-nandanaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

madanena—because of Cupid; madena—because of rapture; ca— and; alasah—lazy; vanitabhih—by women; janita-atilalasah— He whose intense longing was generated; atimanjuni—very lovely; kunja-mandire—in the place which is a pleasure grove; ramate—takes pleasure; asau—He; sakhi—O confidante; nanda- nandanah—Nanda’s son.

**Перевод:**

**Sakhi, Krsna is lazy because of love and rapture, and His intense eagerness was caused by the women. Now He takes pleasure in the exquisite pleasure grove.**

*ity atrālpa-vṛttitvāt tathā-vidha-varṇa-vinyāsopādhi-guṇa-trayavattvāc ca vaidarbhī yadyapi, tathāpi tathā-vidhārthaudāryābhāvān na tathā śobhate.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the Vaidarbhi is not resplendent because although it takes place since there is no long compound and since the composition includes three gunas whose characteristics are such a placement of phonemes, the meaning is not noble.**

### 9.6

*pāko ’py asyāḥ sahāyaḥ syād āmra-vārttāku-pāka-vat (4)*

**Перевод:**

**The Vaidarbhi has an assistant: The type of development. It is either like a mango or like an eggplant.**

*asyā vaidarbhyāḥ pāko nirvāhaḥ. sa ca dvi-vidhaḥ—rasāla-pāko vārttāku-pākaś ceti. rasāla-pāka eva sahāyaḥ syāt śobhā-karatvāt, netaraḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**The term development means the way the style is carried out. There are two kinds: development like a mango and development like an eggplant. Only the first one is an assistant because it creates splendor. The second one is not like that.**

### 9.7

*pūrva-pūrva-daśāyāś ced uttarottara-ramyatā*  
*tadā rasāla-pākaḥ syād viparīte tad-anyakaḥ (5)*

**Перевод:**

**If delightfulness keeps increasing from beginning to end, that is development like a mango. The opposite is development like an eggplant.**

*krameṇodāharaṇāni—“ālokanaṅ kuṭilitena” ity-ādau caturthacaraṇe rasāla-pākaḥ. tatraiva yadi “līlā-mayasya vapuṣas tava rādhike yaḥ, kopa-kramo nu sahajaḥ kim u kṛtrimo vā.” atra satyām api vaidarbhyāṁ pākena vārttāku-pākatā, tenāsyā virasatvam. evaṁ chando ’py asyāḥ sahāyatāṁ vyanakti, tac ca vasanta-tilakopendra-vajrādi. yathā “etāni tāni nalinī vipināni vāpyām” ity-ādi, yathā “ālokanaṅ kuṭilitena” ity-ādi ca.*

**Перевод:**

**Examples are shown in order. The development like a mango occurs in the last sentence of text 9.4. But if it were changed to: “Is this the way You get angry or are You just faking it?”, the Vaidarbhi would be tasteless because the development like an eggplant would take place.**

**The type of meter too assists the Vaidarbhi. Such meters are vasanta-tilaka, upendra-vajra, and so on. Instances of Vaidarbhi in the vasanta-tilaka meter are texts 5.168 and 9.4.**

### 9.8

*yathā ca,*  
*na vāg-minaḥ santi katīha bhū-tale*  
*bhavanti sarve na hita-priyoktayaḥ*  
*mayūra-mukhyāḥ kati bhānti patriṇaḥ*  
*paraṁ pikā eva ruvanti pañcamam*

**Пословный перевод:**

na—not; vak-minah—those who have speech (in an eminent way); santi—are; kati—how many; iha—here; bhu-tale—on the face of the earth; bhavanti—are; sarve—everyone; na—not; hita-priya- uktayah—those whose words are beneficial and pleasing; mayura- mukhyah—the foremost of which are the peacocks; kati—a few; bhanti—are resplendent; patrinah—birds; param—but; pikah—the cuckoos; eva—only; ruvanti—make the sound; pancamam—the fifth.

**Перевод:**

**Aren’t there quite a few eloquent speakers here on earth? And isn’t everyone a sympathizer or a sweet talker every now and then? Moreover, a few birds, the best ones being the peacocks, are resplendent. But only the cuckoos sing the fifth note.**

*atrāpi “ruvanti pañcamam” ity anusvāras tathā-vidhaṁ naujo badhnāti, gurur apy ayaṁ klība-vad bhāsate. tena “na bhānti kiṁ keki-mukhyāḥ khagāḥ pikāḥ, parañ ca te pañcama-gānacañcavaḥ” ity eva śobhate.*

**Перевод:**

**Although there is an anusvara in the fourth line: ruvanti pancamam, it is unable to nullify those instances of ojas (in sarve, priyokta, patrinah). That single anusvara acts like a great man who is a eunuch. The reading would be better as: paran ca te pancama-gana-cancavah, “But only the cuckoos are known to sing the fifth note.”**

### 9.9

*ādi-śabdāt rathoddhatādi ca. yathā*

**Перевод:**

**Other meters that assist the Vaidarbhi are rathoddhata and so on. For example:**

*gāhate gahanam īhatetarām*  
*ardham ardham abhirāmam īhitam*  
*bhāsate vacanam unmadākulaṁ*  
*ko’yam indu-mukhi megha-meduraḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

gahate—enters deeply; gahanam—the deep part; ihate- taram—often endeavors; ardham—halfway; ardham—halfway; abhiramam—agreeably; ihitam—what is desired; bhasate—speaks; vacanam—words; unmada—extravagance; akulam—abounding in; kah—who?; ayam—this; indu-mukhi—O moon-faced woman; megha— \[like\] a cloud; medurah—smooth.

**Перевод:**

**Moon-faced girl, who is this youth, smooth like a cloud, that penetrates the deep part of the woodland? Often, He agreeably endeavors to do things halfway. And He speaks very extravagant words.**

### 9.10

*yathā vā,*

**Перевод:**

**Another example of Vaidarbhi in the rathoddhata meter:**

*indu-nindi-vadanaṁ mṛdu-smitaṁ*  
*kañja-gañji-nayanaṁ su-nāsikam*  
*snigdha-mugdha-vacanaṁ navaṁ navaṁ*  
*megha-meduram upāsmahe mahaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

indu—the moon; nindi—rebukes; vadanam—its mouth; mrdu— is gentle; smitam—its smile; kanja—lotuses; ganji—belittle; nayanam—its eyes; su-nasikam—it has a beautiful nose; snigdha— are affectionate; mugdha—and innocently charming; vacanam— its words; navam navam—ever fresh; megha—like a cloud; meduram—smooth; upasmahe—we revere; mahah—an effulgence.

**Перевод:**

**We revere an ever-fresh effulgent entity: Its face rebukes the moon, it has a gentle smile, its eyes belittle lotuses, it has a beautiful nose, its words are affectionate and charming, and it has a cloud-like sheen.**

*anyatra chandasi tathā-vidha-racanāyām api vaidarbhī na tathā camatkaroti. yathā “vaidarbhī garbhiṇīva sphurati rasa-mayī kāma-sū rukmiṇīva” iti chando-doṣān na tathā su-raseti. etac chandas tu gauḍy-anukūlam. yathā—“gauḍī gāḍhopagūḍhaprakaṭa-haṭha-ghaṭā-garva-garbheva gaurī.”*

**Перевод:**

**However, the Vaidarbhi is not so astonishing when the meter is other than those mentioned above, even when the construction is the same. For instance: vaidarbhi garbhiniva sphurati rasa- mayi kama-su rukminiva, “The Vaidarbhi is lovely like a pregnant woman, and a heart-ravishing woman is sexy like Rukmini.” Here the Vaidarbhi is not relishable because the meter is off. Rather, this meter (srag-dhara) is favorable to Gaudi. This is another example in that meter, in the Gaudi: gaudi gadhopagudha-prakata-hatha-ghata-garva-garbheva gaurT, “The Gaudi is like Gauri whose inner pride is the form of much obstinacy which is both deeply hidden and manifest.”**

### 9.11

*kathā-prāyo hi yatrārtho mādhurya-prāyako guṇaḥ*  
*na gāḍhatā na śaithilyaṁ sā pāñcālī nigadyate (6)*

**Пословный перевод:**

katha-prayah—which mostly involves a conversation (or a narrative); hi—only; yatra—in which \[style\]; arthah—the meaning; madhurya-prayakah—sweet for the most part; gunah—is a quality; na—no; gadhata—dense construction; na—no; saithilyam— relaxed structure; sa—that; pancall Pancali; nigadyate—is called.

**Перевод:**

**When most of the meanings are sweet and the contruction is neither pompous nor slack, that style is the Pancali. Usually it involves a conversation.**

**Комментарий:**

Vamana (c. 800 CE) introduced the Pancali in poetical theory. In his system, there are only three styles. His Pancali is the construction of softness: madhurya-saukumaryopapanna pancall (Kavyalankara-sutra 1.2.13). Subsequent poetical rhetoricians added a fourth style, Lati. Some of them redefined the Pancali. Kavi Karnapura, for example, says the Lati is the construction of softness. Moreover, Kavi Karnapura could have said that his intermediary ojas (6.27) is a subvariety of Pancali. For instance, Visvanatha Kaviraja cites Bhoja’s opinion that the Pancali is between the Vaidarbhi and the Gaudi: samasta-pancasa-padam ojah-kanti-gunanvitam, madhuram sukumaram ca pancallm kavayo viduh.

“Poets know that the Pancali is sweet and soft, has compounds of five or six words, and has ojas guna and kanti-guna (elegance).” (Sarasvail-kanihabharana 2.30) (Sahitya-darpana 9.4)

### 9.12

*yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An exa**

### 9.16

*yathā vā,*  
*dākṣiṇyotsukayā guṇair adhikayā premṇā gatālīkayā*  
*līlā-keli-patākayā kṛtakayā cit-kaumudī-rākayā*  
*dṛk-karpūra-śalākayā navakayā lāvaṇya-vāpīkayā*  
*kṛṣṇo rādhikayānvarañji na kayā jātaṁ nirātaṅkayā*

**Пословный перевод:**

daksinya—for straightforwardness (as opposed to vama, contrariness); utsukaya— \[by Radhika,\] who was eager; gunaih— due to qualities; adhikaya—much; premna—because of love; gata—was gone; alikaya—whose falsehood; lila-keli—of playful games; patakaya—who is the flag; krta-kaya—whose happiness (ka) was made; cit—of awareness; kaumudi—for the moonlight; rakaya—whose is the night of the full moon; drk—for the eyes; karpura—of camphor; salakaya—who is a pencil; navakaya—who is youthful; lavanya—of loveliness; vapikaya—who has a pond; krsnah—Krsna; radhikaya—by Radhika; anvaranji—was loved; na—did not occur; kaya—by which girl? jatam—the becoming; niratankaya—who was nonapprehensive.

**Перевод:**

**Radha loved Krsna again. She became intent on straight­forwardness because of its qualities. Her vanity vanished due to Her great love. She is Cupid’s victory flag and thus became joyful. She is the full moon for the moonlight of awareness. She is a cosmetic pencil of camphor for the eyes. She is youthful, and has a pond of loveliness. So which sakhi did not lose her uneasiness?**

**Комментарий:**

Kavi Karnapura implies that the verse should be classed as the Vaidarbhi. This is valid in a system where there are only two styles: Gaudi and Vaidarbhi. But here only the meanings are sweet: No series of sweet phoneme stands out. In this verse, the profuse alliteration of the sound kaya does not serve any purpose from the perspective of rasa. In Kavi Kamapura’s methodology, the alliteration cannot be classed in the subvariety of Gaudi because it is not in the scope of any guna (9.13).

Alternatively, because the meanings are sweet and because the phonemes of sweetness are not prominent, the verse can be classed as the Pancali: Bhoja says the Pancali is a mix of madhurya, ojas, and softness. But the real question is: The phoneme ‘k’ belongs to which style? Kavi Karnapura used it to some degree in his example of Pancali (9.12) and in his example of Lati (9.18). Only he says the Pancali involves a conversation.

Visvanatha Kaviraja defines the Pancali in this way: varnaih sesaih punar dvayoh, samasta-pancasa-pado bandhah pancalika mata. dvayor vaidarbhi-gaudyoh, “‘Pancali is a construction made with the rest of the phonemes. It has compounds of five or six words.’ The rest of the phonemes are those which are neither in the Vaidarbhi nor in the Gaudi” (Sahitya-darpana 9.4).

Visvanatha Kaviraja says the Lati is a style between the Vaidarbhi and the Pancali: lati tu ritir vaidarbhi-pancalyor antare sthita (Sahitya-darpana 9.5). His example of Lati abounds in the letter k: ayam udayati mudra-bhanjanah padmininam, udaya-giri- vanali-bala-mandara-puspam, viraha-vidhura-koka-dvandva- bandhur vibhindan, kupita-kapi-kapola-kroda-tamras tamamsi. (Sahitya-darpana 9.5). His example of Pancali abounds in the letter m: madhuraya madhu-bodhita-madhavi-madhu-samrddhi- samedhita-medhaya, madhukaranganaya muhur unmada-dhvani- bhrta nibhrtaksaram ujjage. (Sahitya-darpana 9.4)

**Пословный перевод:**

samantatah—everywhere; saithilyam—relaxed structure; yatra— in which \[style\]; mrdulaih—soft; varnaih—with phonemes; la- adibhih—among which the foremost is the letter l ; utkatam—to a high degree; sa—that style; lati—Lati; syat—is; lata-jana—to the people of Lata; priya—dear; anuprasa—with alliteration; nirbhara—filled.

**Перевод:**

**When there is a pervasive series of soft phonemes which mostly consists of the letter l and when there is no conjunct consonant, that style is Lati, so called because it is dear to the people of Lata. It abounds in alliteration.**

*lāṭo vidagdhaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**The term lata means expert (7.21).**

**Комментарий:**

In his commentary on text 9.19, Visvanatha Cakravarti points out that the term lata means komala (soft). Kavi Karnapura had mentioned it (7.20). Lata was the name of a country in southern Gujarat: “lata anuprasa, so called because it is dear to the people or poets of Lata, the country about Surat”.

*lāṭānuprāsa-bāhulye ’pi tathā. udāharaṇam,*

**Перевод:**

**Lati also takes place when there is an abundance of lata anuprasa (alliteration of soft phonemes) (7.20). For example:**

*smerāravinda-vadanā-vadanāravinda-*  
*saundarya-kāma iva śārada-śīta-raśmiḥ*  
*ākāśa-vāsa-tapasā saha saṁvidhatte*  
*dhūmasya pānam iva lakṣaṇa-lakṣaṇasya*

**Пословный перевод:**

smera—slightly opened (“smiling”); aravinda—\[is like\] a lotus; vadana— \[of Radha,\] whose face; vadana-aravinda—of the lotus face; saundarya—for the beauty; kamah—it has the desire; iva— as if; sarada-slta-rasmih—the autumnal moon; akasa—in the sky; vasa—\[in the form\] of residing; tapasa saha—along with the austerity; samvidhatte—does; dhumasya—of smoke; panam—the imbibing; iva—as if; laksana—is a mark (the rabbit on the moon); laksanasya—\[smoke,\] whose characteristic.

**Перевод:**

*eṣa lāṭānuprāsaḥ, eṣāpi lāṭī rītiḥ.*

The phonemes s and ks belong to ojas guna, and the phonemes r, nd, and n to madhurya-guna. The hard phonemes are used to evoke the harshness of performing austerity.

The poetical rhetoricians’ mention of the “style of compounding” in the construction of the gunas is arbitrary. Here, for instance, the first word of the verse is a compound of seven words in the scope of a sweet meaning. Conversely, Kavi Kamapura’s example of Gaudi involves a series of single words (9.13). Anandavardhana said that long compounds also suitably occur in srngara-rasa, and single words are also appropriate in raudra-rasa and the like: madhurya- prasadau rasa-bhava-tad-abhasa-visayav eveti visaya-niyamo vyavasthitah, sanghatanayas tu sa vighatate. tatha hi srngare ’pi dlrgha-samasa drsyate raudradisv asamasa ceti. (Dhvany-aloka 3.6)

*ity alankara-kaustubhe nti-nirupano nama navamah kiranah.*

**Перевод:**

**Here ends the ninth ray in Alankara-kaustubha, entitled “a discussion on the styles.”**

## Tenth Ray - Literary Faults

### 10.1

*atha doṣa-nirṇayaḥ. atha “yad asmin doṣaḥ syāc chravaṇakaṭutādiḥ sa na paraḥ” ity uddiṣṭasya doṣasya lakṣaṇa-parīkṣe darśayituṁ doṣa-kiraṇam ārabhate. ko ’sau doṣaḥ? ity āha—*

**Перевод:**

**Now, he begins the chapter on the faults to illustrate both the definition of a fault, simply mentioned by name in: “If there are faults in the Kavya-purusa, they are the well-known ones, such as harshness to the ears, not the minor ones” (1.7), and the examination of it. What is a fault? He defines it:**

*rasāpakarṣako doṣaḥ (1a)*

**Перевод:**

**A fault is that which diminishes the rasa.**

*apakarṣakaḥ sthagana-kārī. nanu rasasyātmanaḥ sthaganam ity āśaṅkyāha—*

**Перевод:**

**“It diminishes” means “It obstructs”. Someone might wonder: “Does this mean that it obstructs the rasa which is the soul of poetry?” With that in mind, he says:**

### 10.2

*raso ’trāsvāda ucyate (1b)*

**Перевод:**

**In this regard, rasa means relishment.**

*atra doṣa-lakṣaṇe rasa-śabdenāsvāda evocyate. rasyata iti rasaḥ, na tu śṛṅgārādika ātma-bhūtā rasaḥ. yathā na kāṇatva-khañjatvādikam ātmanaḥ kaurūpya-kāraṇam api tu dehasyaiva, tathātra śabdārthayor eva doṣaḥ, nātma-bhūtasya rasasya. tarhi “śabdārthāpakarṣako doṣaḥ” ity evāstu lakṣaṇam ity āśaṅkyāha—*

**Перевод:**

**In the definition of a literary fault, the word rasa only means relishment. Rasa is the relishing. It is not the srngara-rasa, for instance, that is the soul of a poem. Just as one-eyedness and lameness are bodily faults rather than faults of the soul, so a fault only relates to sabda (sound, word) or to artha (meaning), not to the rasa, the soul.**

**Someone might object, “Then the definition should only be: “A literary fault is that which diminishes the sound or the meaning.”” Expecting this, he specifies:**

### 10.3

*apakarṣas tat-sthaganam (2a)*

**Перевод:**

**The diminution of the rasa means the relishment is hampered.**

*tasyāsvādasya sthaganaṁ saṅkocaḥ. na hi śabdārthasya vā tena saṅkocaḥ kriyate, api tu tat-tad-āśrayeṇa satā āsvādasyaiva. ataḥ samyag-uktaṁ “rasāpakarṣako doṣaḥ” iti. āsvādaś ca sahṛdayāntar-gata eva, yena śabdāśrayeṇārthāśrayeṇa vā apakarṣakeṇa teṣāṁ jāyamāna āsvādaḥ saṅkucyate, sa eva doṣaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**It is not that the literary fault constricts the sound or the meaning. Rather, being based on the sound or the meaning, it only hampers the relishment. Thus the above definition “A fault is that which diminishes the rasa” is accurate.**

**Moreover, the relishment occurs in the connoisseurs’ hearts (1.9). Therefore, only that which diminishes the connoisseurs’ relishment, whether the diminution relates to the sound or to the meaning, is a fault.**

### 10.4

*sa ca dvedhā nirūpyate (2b)*

**Перевод:**

**There are two kinds of literary faults.**

*yāvad āsvādāpakarṣako yat kiñcid āsvādāpakarṣakaś ca. yatra sahṛdayānām asahiṣṇutā bhavati, sa tv ādyaḥ, yatra sahiṣṇutā syāt, so ’ntyaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**The two types of faults are: (1) It totally diminishes the relishment, and (2) It slightly diminishes the relishment. If the connoisseurs cannot tolerate the fault, it is classed in the first category, but if they can tolerate it, it is classed in the second one.**

**Комментарий:**

In text 1.7, Kavi Karnapura mentioned the possible occurrence of minor faults, but even in this chapter he does not say which ones they are. Arguably, among the five faults that Caitanya Mahaprabhu pointed out in Kesava Kasmiri’s verse, the instance of avimrsta- vidheyamsa in a compound (Caitanya-caritamrta, Adi [16.59](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/16.59)) and the redundancy (punar-atta) (CC, Adi [16.66](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/16.66)) are minor faults. But according to Lord Caitanya, one mere fault nullifies all the literary beauty created by the ornaments: dasa alankare yadi eka sloka haya, eka dose saba alankara haya ksaya (CC, Adi [16.69](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/16.69)).

### 10.5

*śruti-kaṭv-ādayas tatrādāv ucyante samāsataḥ*  
*pade vākye padāṁśe ’mī arthe ceti catur-vidhāḥ (3)*  
*amī śruti-kaṭv-ādayaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

sruti—on the ears; katu—harsh; adayah—beginning with; tatra—in that regard; adau—at first; ucyante—are mentioned; samasatah— in brief; pade—in a word; vakye—in a sentence; pada-amse—in a part of a word; ami—those \[faults\]; arthe—in a meaning; ca—and; iti—thus; catur-vidhah—fourfold.

**Перевод:**

**Below, at first the literary faults beginning from sruti-katu are mentioned. There are four broad kinds: A fault occurs either in a word, in a part of a word, in a sentence or in a meaning.**

### 10.6

*śravaṇa-kaṭhoram asaṁskṛtam asarthaṁ cāprayukta-nihatārthe*  
*vyartham avācakam api cānucitārthaṁ grāmyam apratītaṁ ca (4)*  
*aślīlaṁ sandigdhaṁ neyārtham atho samāsa-gaṁ kliṣṭam*  
*avimṛṣṭa-vidheyāṁśaṁ viruddha-mati-kṛc ca ṣoḍaśaitāni (5)*

**Пословный перевод:**

sravana—on the ears; kathoram—harsh; asamskrtam—not Sanskrit; asartham—incapable (asamartha, 10.9); ca—and; aprayukta—not in use; nihata-arthe—whose meaning is obstructed; vyartham— meaningless; avacakam—not expressive; api—also; ca—and; anucita-artham—the use of which is improper; gramyam—vulgar; apratitam—not understood; ca—and; aslilam—unpleasant; sandigdham—ambiguous; neya-artham—whose meaning can only be guessed; atho—then; samasa-gam—occurs in compounds; klistam—abstruse (i.e. not easily intelligible); avimrsta—has not been sufficiently considered; vidheya—of a predicate; amsam— where a part; viruddha—inappropriate; mati—thought; krt—it causes; ca—and; sodasa—sixteen; etani—these.

**Перевод:**

**These are sixteen literary faults: (1) sravana-kathora (sruti- katu ) (harsh to the ear),(2) asamskrta (grammatical mistake), (3) asamartha (not the intended meaning), (4) aprayukta (not in use), (5) nihatartha (obstructed meaning), (6) vyartha (meaningless), (7) avacaka (not expressive), (8) anucitartha (unsuitable meaning), (9) gramya (vulgar: rustic or obscene), (10) apratTta (not understood), (11) aslila (unpleasant), (12) sandigdha (ambiguous), (13) neyartha (the meaning can only be guessed), (14) klista (not easily understandable), (15) avimrsta-vidheyamsa (not giving sufficient importance to the predicate), and (16) viruddha-mati-krt (it causes a contradictory thought).**

*etāni ṣoḍaśa padāni duṣṭānīty arthaḥ. “atho” ity ārabhya kliṣṭādi-tritayaṁ samāsa-gam eva. asamastasya kliṣṭatvādyasambhavāt. śravaṇa-kaṭhoraṁ śruti-kaṭu, asaṁskṛtaṁ cyuta-saṁskṛti, vyarthaṁ nirarthakam. aślīlaṁ tu tri-vidham—vrīḍājugupsāmaṅgala-dāyitvāt.*

**Перевод:**

**Due to the word atho (then), these three faults: klista, avimrsta- vidheyamsa, and viruddha-mati-krt, only occur in a compound, since uncompounded words are not hard to understand and so on.**

**Sravana-kathora is a synonym of sruti-katu (hard on the ears). Asamskrta is the same as cyuta-samskrti \[a term used by Mammata\]. Moreover, there are three kinds of aslila (unpleasant): vrida-dayi (shameful), jugupsa-dayi (disgusting) and amangala-dayi (inauspicious).**

**Комментарий:**

Kavi Karnapura will give more details as he proceeds. Not every fault occurs in each of the four categories (pada-dosa, vakya-dosa, padamsa-dosa, artha-dosa) (10.5). Many more faults that take place in one or more of these categories are listed ahead, not to mention the rasa-dosas (10.127). Next, Kavi Karnapura begins to expound those sixteen faults in the scope of pada-dosa (fault in a word).

In the elaboration, Kavi Karnapura only means to say that those three faults (klista, avimrsta-vidheyamsa, and viruddha-mati-krt) do not belong to the category of padamsa-dosa (part of a word). Thus he will state that there are only thirteen padamsa-dosas (10.125). He will also illustrate how klista occurs in a sentence, even if there is no compound (10.48). Similarly, he will show that avimrsta-vidheyamsa also occurs in a compound (10.49-50) and in a sentence, regardless of compounds (10.51-52). As an artha-dosa, klista is called kasta (10.108).

### 10.7

*krameṇodāharanāni,*

**Перевод:**

**Examples are shown in order.**

**\[This illustrates sruti-katu (harsh to the ear):\]**

*śirīṣa-puṣpād api komalāni*  
*rādhe tavāṅgāni kuraṅga-netre*  
*stana-dvayaṁ te hṛdayasya śiṣyaṁ*  
*kaṭhoryam uccair yad idaṁ bibharti*

**Пословный перевод:**

sirisa-puspat—than a sirisa flower; api—even; komalani—softer; radhe—O Radhe; tava—Your; angani—limbs; kuranga—are like a doe’s; netre—O You whose eyes; stana-dvayam—pair of breasts; te hrdayasya—of Your heart; sisyam—are the disciples; kathoryam— hardness; uccaih—to a high degree; yat—because; idam—this; bibharti—have.

**Перевод:**

**Radha, O doe-eyed girl, Your limbs are even softer than a sinsa flower. But since Your breasts are Your heart’s disciples, they are very hard.**

*atra kaṭhoryam iti śruti-kaṭu, tena kāṭhinyam iti pāṭhyam.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the word kathorya is hard on the ears (sruti-katu). It should be replaced by kathinya.**

### 10.8

**Перевод:**

**\[This is asamskrta (grammatical mistake):\]**

*brūmaḥ kim anyair vraja-sundarī-janaiḥ*  
*samaṁ samatvaṁ tava devi rādhike*  
*vaidagdhyam adhyāpayate vayo ’parāṁ*  
*vayas tvam adhyāpayase vidagdhatām*

**Пословный перевод:**

brumah—\[can\] we say; kim—how; anyaih—other; vraja-sundari- janaih—beautiful girls of Vraja; samam—with; samatvam— equality; tava—Your; devi—O goddess; radhike—O Radhika; vaidagdhyam—craftiness; adhyapayate—teaches; vayah—youth; aparam—other girls; vayah—youth; tvam—You; adhyapayase— teach; vidagdhatam—craftiness.

**Перевод:**

**O Radhika, beautiful lady, how can we say that You are like the other lovely girls of Vraja? Youthfulness teaches them craftiness, but You give youthfulness lessons on craftiness!**

*atrādhyāpayata ity ātmanepadaṁ cyuta-saṁskṛti. tena “vaidagdhyam adhyāpayatītarāṁ vayas tad etad adhyāpayasi tvam agrataḥ” iti pāṭhyam.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the atmanepada verb adhyapayate is the fault called cyuta-samskrti (grammatical mistake). The proper form is adhyapayasi. In consideration of the meter, the second half of the verse should read: vaidagdhyam adhyapayatitaram vayas tad etad adhyapayasi tvam agratah, “Youthfulness teaches the other girls craftiness, but You give youthfulness even better lessons on craftiness.”**

### 10.9

**Перевод:**

**\[This is asamartha (not the intended meaning):\]**

*haṁsīva haṁsi mada-medura-manda-mandam*  
*ālokase sa-cakitaṁ hariṇāṅganeva*  
*ābhāṣase mṛdu-kalaṁ lalite pikīva*  
*lakṣmīṁ bibharṣi sarasaś ca vanasya ca tvam*

**Пословный перевод:**

hamsi—a female swan; iva—like; hamsi—you move; mada—on account of rapture; medura—smoothly; manda-mandam—slowly; alokase—you look; sa-cakitam—afraid; harina—deer; angana— female; iva—like; abhasase—you speak; mrdu—softly; kalam— sweetly; lalite—O Lalita; piki—a female cuckoo; iva—like; laksmim—the beauty; bibharsi—possess; sarasah—of the lake; ca—and; vanasya—of the forest; ca—and; tvam—you.

**Перевод:**

**Lalita, owing to rapture you move slowly and smoothly like a female swan, you look apprehensive like a doe, and you speak softly and sweetly like a cuckoo, thus you are endowed with the beauty of the lakes and of the forests.**

*atra yadyapi haṁsīti “han hiṁsā-gatyoḥ” iti hantir gaty-arthe ’pi vartate, tathāpi śleṣādikaṁ vinānyatra gamanārthe ’samartham idam. tena “haṁsīva yāsi” iti paṭhanīyam.*

**Перевод:**

**Although the verb hamsi is made from the verbal root han\[a\] himsa-gatyoh (2P, to kill, to move) in its sense of gati (moving), nonetheless when there is no desire to express the double meaning of the verbal root, the verb hamsi is incapable of conveying its sense of “moving.” This is the fault called asamartha (incapable, i.e. it does not express the intended meaning). The words hamsTva hamsi should be replaced by: hamsTva yasi.**

### 10.10

**Перевод:**

**\[This is aprayukta (not in use):\]**

*rādhe tavāṅghri-padmo ’yaṁ*  
*satyaṁ dohada-daivataḥ*  
*akāle ’pi padāghātād*  
*aśokaḥ puṣpito ’bhavat*

**Пословный перевод:**

radhe—O Radha; tava—of Yours; anghri-padmah—lotus feet; ayam—these; satyam—truly; dohada—of the desires \[of plants\]; daivatah—are the deities; akale—out of season; api—even; pada- aghatad—on account of the striking of the foot; asokah—the asoka tree; puspitah—filled with flowers; abhavat—became.

**Перевод:**

**Radha, truly these lotus feet of Yours are the plants’ wish­fulfilling deities: Even out of season, asoka trees bloom when You strike them with Your feet.**

*atra “vā puṁsi padmaṁ nalinam” “daivatāni puṁsi vā” iti yadyapy anuśāsanaṁ vartate, tathāpi kavibhir aprayujyamānatvād aprayuktam. tena “rādhe tava padāmbhojaṁ satyaṁ dohadadaivatam” iti paṭhyam.*

**Перевод:**

**The words padma and daivata can be declined in the masculine gender, by these definitions: (1) va pumsi padmam nalinam (Amara-kosa 1.10.39) and (2) daivatani pumsi va (Amara-kosa 1.1.9). However, such a usage is an instance of the fault called aprayukta (not in use) since these rules are not used by poets. Therefore the first half of the verse should read: radhe tava padambhojam satyam dohada-daivatam, “Radha, Your lotus feet are truly the plants’ wish-fulfilling deities.”**

### 10.11

**Перевод:**

**\[This is nihatartha (obstructed meaning):\]**

*lākṣā-rasena tava śoṇitam adya vakṣas*  
*tasyāḥ padāmburuhato galitena kṛṣṇa*  
*ābhāti phulla-nava-kokanadāvalīkaḥ*  
*śāntormiko hrada iva dyumaṇeḥ sutāyāḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

laksa-rasena—because of the lac juice; tava—Your; sonitam—red; adya—now; vaksah—chest; tasyah—her; pada-amburuhatah— from the lotus foot; galitena—rubbed off; krsna—O Krsna; abhati—is beautiful; phulla—expanded; nava—fresh; kokanada— of red lotuses; avalikah—\[a lake\] in which there is a multitude; santa—are calm; urmikah—whose waves; hradah—a lake; iva— like; dyu-maneh—of the sun (“the jewel of the sky”); sutayah—of the daughter.

**Перевод:**

**Now Your chest looks beautiful, Krsna! It is red because of the lac from that girl’s feet. It resembles a still lake abounding in red lotuses and connected to the Yamuna.**

*atra yadyapy aruṇitādi-padaṁ samānārthakaṁ śoṇita-padam, tathāpi prasiddhena kṣatajārthatvatāprasiddhārtho vyāhanyata iti nihatārthaḥ. tena lohitam iti pāṭhyam.*

**Перевод:**

**Although the word sonita is synonymous with words like arunita (red), nevertheless its meaning of red, which is not well- known, is obstructed by its familiar meaning of blood (Amara- kosa 2.6.64). This is the fault called nihatartha (obstructed meaning), so sonitam should be replaced by lohitam (red).**

### 10.12

**Перевод:**

**\[This is vyartha (meaningless):\]**

*guṇās tv anenaiva tavohitā hare*  
*prāṇeśvarī-jīvita-vallabho ’si yat*  
*doṣo ’py ayaṁ kintu kulāṅganā-tater*  
*mano-maṇi-steya-karatvam eva ca*

**Пословный перевод:**

gunah—qualities; tu—but; anena—because of this; eva—only tava—Your; uhitah—are considered; hare—O Hari; prana—of the life airs; isvan—of the controller; jlvita—of the life; vallabhah— the beloved; asi—You are; yat—that; dosah—the fault; api—also; ayam—this; kintu—however; kula-angana—of respectable ladies; tateh—of a multitude; manah—in the form of the heart; mani— of the jewel; steya-karatvam—the theft; eva—only; ca—(a verse filler).

**Перевод:**

**Hari, we think You have good qualities only because You are the beloved of our Pranesvan. But You do have a fault: You steal the jewels hearts of respectable girls.**

*atra ca-kāraḥ kevalaṁ pāda-pūraṇārthatvād vyartha-padam. tena “mano-maṇi-steya-karatvam eva te” iti pāṭhyam.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the word ca is a meaningless word since it is used merely to fill a line of verse. The last line should read: mano-mani- steya-karatvam eva te (Your being a stealer of jewel hearts).**

### 10.13

**Перевод:**

**\[This is avacaka (not expressive):\]**

*yasyām īkṣaṇa-kaumudīyam uditā hā hanta sābhūn niśā*  
*yo ’yaṁ tad-virahāndhakāra-gahanaḥ so ’bhūd aho vāsaraḥ*  
*tad-rūpa-smaraṇe ya indriya-layaḥ so ’bhūd aho mūrchanaṁ*  
*kiṁ brūyām avivekatāṁ tava vidhe vāmāya tubhyaṁ namaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

yasyam—\[the time\] in which; iksana—for the eyes; kaumudi—is moonlight; iyam—She (Radhika); udita—arose; ha—alas; hanta— alas; sa—that \[time\]; abhut—became; nisa—the night; yah—which; ayam—this; tat-viraha—of separation from Her; andhakara—with the darkness; gahanah—thick; sah—that; abhut—has occured; aho—how amazing; vasarah—brightness (has come); tat-rupa— Her form; smarane—while remembering; yah—which; indriya— of the senses; layah—inertness; sah—that; abhut—has become; aho—how amazing; murchanam—a swoon; kim—what; bruyam— can I say?; avivekatam—lack of judgment; tava—your; vidhe—O creator; vamaya—crooked; tubhyam—to you; namah—obeisances.

**Перевод:**

**\[Agitated due to separation from Radhika, Krsna, in Mathura, thinks to Himself:\]**

**Alas, alas, the time during which She was like rising moonlight for My eyes has become night, and the time which is thick with the darkness of separation from Her has become day. How amazing it is that the inertness of my senses upon remembering Her form has turned into a swoon. Obeisances to you, O crooked creator. What can I say about your lack of judgment?**

*atra pūrvārdhe “niśā” padaṁ kevalāndhakāre ’vācakam. evaṁ “vāsaraḥ” śabdo ’pi kevala-prakāśe ’vācakaḥ. tenedam avācakam. ato “hā hanta sā tāmasī, yeyaṁ tad-virahāndhakāra-gahanā jyotsnāvatī sābhavat.”*

**Перевод:**

**In the first half of the verse, the word nisa (night) is not expressive of the sense of “completely dark.” Similarly, the word vasara (day) is not expressive of the sense of “completely bright.” This is the fault called avacaka (not expressive). The proper version is: ha hanta sa tamasi, yeyam tad-virahandhakara-gahana jyotsnavati sabhavat, “Alas, alas, \[the time during which She was like rising moonlight for My eyes\] has turned dark, and the time that is thick with the darkness of separation from Her has become bright.”**

**Комментарий:**

The word tamasi (a dark night), in the new version, inherently expresses darkness (tamas), and the word jyotsnavatl (a moonlit night) inherently expresses light (jyotsna).

### 10.14

**Перевод:**

**\[This is anucitartha (unsuitable meaning):\]**

*bibharṣi nīlaṁ vasanaṁ yad etad*  
*dhalaṁ ca pāṇau na kathaṁ karoṣi*  
*jānātu lokas tava kṛṣṇa veṣād*  
*varṣīyasi bhrātari bhaktimattvam*

**Пословный перевод:**

bibharsi—You wear; nilam—blue; vasanam—dress; yat—because; etat—this; halam—plow; ca—and; panau—in the hand; na—don’t; katham—why?; karosi—You do (i.e. You take); janatu—should know; lokah—people; tava—Your; krsna—O Krsna; vesat— because of the attire; varsiyasi—elder; bhratari—for the brother; bhaktimattvam—devotion.

**Перевод:**

**\[A gopi in mana sees Krsna arriving. He had come to break her mana, but had acidentally dressed Himself with the blue dress of a rival girl after His enjoyment.\]**

**Krsna, since You’re wearing blue clothes, why don’t You take a plow in Your hand? People should know about Your devotion to Your elder brother.**

*atra “hala”padaṁ kṛṣṇaṁ prati sākūtatvenocitam api kṛṣakatvavyañjanayākṣepeṇa tad eva baladevaṁ praty anucitam ity anucitārtham. tena prakṛta-bhaṅgyaiva “kathaṁ na pāṇau muṣalaṁ karoṣi” iti prakṛtārthaṁ praty ucitam eva. atrāpi dhvanyantara-sad-bhāvaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Here, even though it is proper to use the word hala (plow) with a hidden intention toward Krsna, since as a hint the name Krsna, made from the verbal root krs\[a\] (to plow), suggests the idea of being a farmer, still, such a usage of the word hala is unsuitable in relation to Baladeva (because there is no intention to deride Baladeva, the respectable elder brother, with the derogatory suggestion of being a farmer). This is the fault called anucitartha (unsuitable meaning). Therefore, simply by a roundabout mode of expressing the subject matter, the replacement is: katham na panau musalam karosi, “Why don’t You take a cudgel in Your hand?” This is suitable for the subject matter under discussion, and it contains another implied sense.**

**Комментарий:**

According to Visvanatha Cakravarti, that suggestion is: “I could tolerate Your beating me with a cudgel, but I cannot tolerate Your wearing the clothes of a rival girl!”

### 10.15

**Перевод:**

**\[This is gramya (vulgar):\]**

*vakṣo-ruhau kāñcana-padma-korakau*  
*muṣṭi-prameyaṁ tava su-bhru madhyamam*  
*kaṭiś ca te hema-śilā-vilāsinī*  
*śaśī mukhaṁ padma-jam aṅghri-yugmakam*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaksah-ruhau—two breasts (“rising out from the chest”); kancana— golden; padma—of a lotus; korakau—two buds; musti—by a closed hand; prameyam—is measurable; tava—your; su-bhru—O beautiful-browed girl; madhyamam—the waist; katih—buttocks; ca—and; te—your; hema—golden; sila—like rocks; vilasini—move to and fro; sasi—is the moon; mukham—mouth; padma-jam—arise from a lotus; anghri-yugmakam—pair of feet.

**Перевод:**

**Girl with beautiful brows, Your breasts are golden lotus buds, your waist is so thin that it can be held in the hand, your buttocks sway like two golden rocks, your face is a moon, and your feet are lotuses.**

*atra “kaṭi” śabdo grāmyaḥ. evam uttama-nāyake nāgarādi-śabdo ’pi nāgarika-nāgarayor ekārthatvāt. tena “śroṇiś ca te hema-śilāvilāsinī” iti pāṭhyam.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the word kati (buttocks) is a vulgar word. This is the fault called gramya, thus kati should be replaced by sroni. Similarly, words such as nagara are considered vulgar when the sense is “a foremost male lover.” This is because nagara has the same meaning as nagarika (one who lives in a small town).**

### 10.16

**Перевод:**

**\[This is aprattta (not understood):\]**

*nāme na pacyamāne vā*  
*na pakve ’py ayam āśaye*  
*yāti prema-rasaḥ kintu*  
*durjaro ’ṅga-vimardakaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

na—does not; ame—is in a condition where there is undigested food; na—does not; pacyamane—is in a condition when \[food\] is being digested; va—or; na—does not; pakve—is in a condition when \[food\] is digested; api—also; ayam—this \[prema-rasa\]; asaye—when the stomach; yati—go away; prema-rasah—loving bliss; kintu—but; durjarah—difficult to dilute; anga—the body; vimardakah—hurts.

**Перевод:**

**\[Usually digestive rasa (gastric juice) occurs when the food in the stomach is undigested, but it becomes diluted as the food is being digested or is digested\]. However, this rasa, prema-rasa, doesn’t become diluted whether the food in the stomach is undigested, is being digested, or is digested. Rather it remains, and gives pain to the body.**

*atrāśaya-śabdas tasya traividhyaś ca vaidyaka-śāstre eva pratītam. anyatra apratītam iti tathā. tena “nāmo ’sau pacyamānaś ca na pakvaś ca bhavaty asau, ekāvasthaḥ prema-raso durjaraḥ prāṇapīḍakaḥ” iti pāṭhyam.*

**Перевод:**

**The word asaya, used in the sense of “stomach,” and the three conditions of the stomach are understood only in the context of textbooks on Ayurvedic medicine. In other instances, however, this knowledge is difficult to grasp (asaya usually means “mind” or “place”). Thus this verse is an illustration of the fault called aprattta (not understood). The proper version of the verse is:**

*nāmo ’sau pacyamānaś ca*  
*na pakvaś ca bhavaty asau*  
*ekāvasthaḥ prema-raso*  
*durjaraḥ prāṇa-pīḍakaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**“Prema-rasa does not become diluted, and pains the life force. This is because prema-rasa exists only in one state: It is not undigested, it is not being digested, and it does not become digested.”**

### 10.17

*aślīlaṁ tu tri-vidham iti yad uktaṁ tasya bhedam āha. vrīḍā-dāyī yathā—*

**Перевод:**

**As mentioned previously (10.6), aslila (unpleasant) has three varieties. Now he describes the varieties. First, an example of vrida-dayt asltla (shamefully unpleasant):**

*lāvaṇyam anyādṛśam anyathaiva*  
*mādhuryam anyādṛg idaṁ vapuś ca*  
*yoge viyoge ca bhavanti yasya*  
*sa te ’nuvartī kim ato bhagaṁ te*

**Пословный перевод:**

lavanyam—beauty; anyadrsam—is like another; anyatha—is another way; eva—only; madhuryam—sweetness; anyadrk—is like another; idam—this; vapuh—body; ca—and; yoge—in union; viyoge—in separation; ca—and; bhavanti—are; yasya—of whom; sah—He (Krsna); te—your; anuvarti—follower; kim—what; atah—therefore; bhagam—good fortune; te—your.

**Перевод:**

**Your body, beauty, and sweetness are not the same in union and in separation from Krsna. He always follows you, so what can be said about your good fortune?**

*atra “bhagaṁ śrī-kāma-māhātmya” ity-ādiṣu yadyapy anekeṣv artheṣu vartate, tathāpy atra vrīḍā-karam, kintu subhagādurbhagā-bhaginī-bhagavatīty-ādiṣu na tathā, śabdasya tathaiva maryādā. tena “sa eṣa kṛṣṇas tava pārśva-vartī” iti pāṭhyam. evaṁ liṅga-padam api kvacid vrīḍā-karam, na tu sarvatra. uktaṁ ca “śiva-liṅgasya saṁsthāne kasyāsabhyatva-bhāvanā” evaṁ yony-ādi-śabdo ’pi kvacin nāpi yathātma-yoni-prabhṛtiḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Although the word bhaga (good fortune) has many meanings, for example: bhagam sn-kama-mahatmya-virya-yatnarka- kirtisu, “Bhaga means good fortune, lust, glory, strength, endeavor, the sun, and fame” (Amara-kosa 3.3.26), nonetheless it is shameful in this context (because of the possibility of its referring to the female genitalia: bhagam yonir dvayoh, Amara-kosa 2.6.76).**

**However, by convention that is not the case for similar words, such as subhaga (fortunate, beautiful), durbhaga (unfortunate), bhagini (sister), and bhagavati (the Lord’s counterpart; or beautiful). Therefore the words sa te ’nuvarti kim ato bhagam te should be replaced by: sa esa krsnas tava parsva-varti, “He, Krsna, is always by your side.”**

**Sometimes the use of the word linga (phallus) is shameful. But this is not always the case. For example, the use of the word linga is not shameful in: siva-lingasya samsthane kasyasabhyatva- bhavana, “Who would think vulgar thoughts in a Siva-linga temple?” Similarly, words such as yoni (which can also refer to the female genitalia) are not always disgraceful.**

**For instance: atma-yoni (self-born) (a name of Brahma, Visnu, Siva, and Cupid).**

*jugupsā-karaṁ yathā,*

*śūdro vā nija-dharmataḥ*  
*na nistarati saṁsāraṁ*  
*vinā kṛṣṇāṅghri-sevanāt*

**Пословный перевод:**

brahmanah—a Brahmana; ksatriyah—a Ksatriya; vit—a Vaisya; va—or; sudrah—a Sudra; va—or; nija-dharmatah—by means of one’s duty; na nistarati—does not cross; samsaram—material existence; vina—without; krsna-anghri—Krsna’s feet; sevanat— serving.

**Перевод:**

**Although he executes his own duty, a Brahmana, a Ksatriya, a Vaisya or a Sudra cannot cross material existence unless he serves Krsna’s lotus feet.**

**Although vis (Vaisya) and vis (stool) have respectively different nominal bases, both of them have the form vit in the first case singular. Consequently here the word vit is disgusting. The words vid va should be replaced by vaisyah.**

### 10.19

*evaṁ vāyu-prabhṛti-padam api, yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**In like manner, even words like vayu (wind) can constitute the fault called jugupsa-kara aslila (disgustingly unpleasant). For example:**

*rajaḥ-prasūnasya mamākṣi-lagnam*  
*iti vyathāṁ kāpi tathābhyanaiṣīt*  
*mukhasya vāyuṁ dadatā mukunde-*  
*nodasya tat tatra ca sā cucumbe*

**Пословный перевод:**

rajah-prasunasya—with flower pollen; mama—my; aksi—in the eye; lagnam—is stuck; iti—thus; vyatham—pain; ka api—a girl; tatha—in that way; abhyanaisit—acted (i.e. faked); mukhasya—of the mouth; vayum—air; dadata—who was giving; mukundena—by Mukunda; udasya—having cast away; tat—that \[flower pollen\]; tatra—there \[on the mouth\]; ca—and; sa—she; cucumbe—was kissed.

**Перевод:**

**“Flower pollen is stuck in my eye,” Saying this, a gopi faked pain. After removing that flower pollen by blowing air from His mouth into her eyes, Mukunda kissed her.**

*atra vāyu-prabhṛti-śabdo jugupsā-janakaḥ śabda-maryādayā, tena “mukhānilenaiva nirasyatā tat, kṛṣṇena sā tatra ciraṁ cucumbe” iti pāṭhyam.*

### 10.20

*amaṅgala-dāyi yathā,*

**An example of amangala-dayi asltla (inauspiciously unpleasant):**

*ahaha hṛdaya-bandhoḥ ko ’pi śokaḥ kukūlo*  
*jvalati kim api mandaṁ mandam evāpi tīkṣṇaḥ*
