*dhag iti bhavati dīptas taj-janasyāvaloke*

**Пословный перевод:**

ahaha—alas; hrdaya-bandhoh—of Krsna (“the heart’s friend”); kah api—a certain indescribable; sokah—sorrow; kukulah—chaff fire; jvalati—burns; kim api—to a considerable extent; mandam— slowly; mandam—slowly; eva—only; api—although; tiksnah— harsh; api tu—but yet; dahati—burns; sarvani—all; eva—only; marmani—sensitive parts (of the body); gadham—excessively; dhak—a crackling sound; iti—thus; bhavati—becomes; diptah— blazing; tat-janasya—of His people (of those dear to Him); avaloke—when there is the sight.

**Перевод:**

**Alas, Krsna’s indescribable sorrow is a chaff fire burning slowly. It is harsh nonetheless: It scorches all His vital organs. When He, the heart’s friend, sees His devotees, that fire crackles and turns into a blaze.**

*atra śoka iti karuṇa-rasa-sthāyitvād amaṅgalaṁ maraṇa-rūpaṁ pratyāyayati, ato ’maṅgala-smaraṇād aślīlam. tena “priya-virahakukūlaḥ ko ’pi noccaiḥ-śikho ’pi” iti vācyam. evaṁ nāśādi- śabdo ’py adarśana-vācy api tathā.*

**Перевод:**

**Because it is the sthayi-bhava of karuna-rasa (lamentation), here the sorrow (soka) causes the perception of inauspiciousness in the form of impending death. It is classed as asttla (unpleasant) since it causes the remembrance of something inauspicious. The first line should be changed to: priya-viraha-kukulah ko ’pi noccaih-sikho ’pi, “The indescribable chaff fire of separation from His dear ones, though its flames are not high...”**

**Similarly, words such as nasa (destruction) (vinasa, mrtyu) are also inauspicious, even when they refer to someone’s disappearance.**

### 10.21

**Перевод:**

**\[This is sandigdha (ambiguous):\]**

*kālindyāḥ pulināplāvi*  
*kāñcanaṁ sa-taraṅgakam*  
*dyotate surata-srastā*  
*veṇiḥ śroṇi-gateva te*

**Пословный перевод:**

kalindyah—of the Yamuna River; pulina—the shore; aplavi— which splashes; ka-ancanam—the movement of the water, i.e. the flow; sa-tarangakam—which has waves; dyotate—is resplendent; surata—on account of conjugal enjoyment; srasta—fallen; venih— braid; sroni—the hips; gata—which reaches; iva—like; te—your.

**Перевод:**

**The wavy water of the Yamuna that splashes upon its shore is beautiful like your braid, which is loose because of erotic enjoyment and reaches your hips.**

*atra kasya jalasya añcanaṁ gatiḥ kiṁ vā kāñcanaṁ kanakam iti sandehāt sandigdham. tena “pulināplāvinī dhārā ghana-vīcir yama-svasuḥ” iti pāṭhe doṣāntaraṁ ca naśyati.*

**Перевод:**

**In this verse there is a doubt as to what the word kancanam actually means: does it refer to the movement (ancanam) of the water (ka), or does it mean gold (kancanam)? This is an example of the fault called sandigdha (ambiguous). The first half of the verse should read: pulinaplavini dhara ghana-vicir yama-svasuh, “The flow of the Yamuna River is replete with strong waves and splashes the shore...” In this new version, the other fault is also removed.**

**Комментарий:**

Regarding the verse, the wavy water of the Yamuna is compared to her open braid because her hair is black and because it is wavy when not braided. Visvanatha Cakravarti comments that her hair reaches her hips, which are adorned with a white cloth. Thus the shore of the Yamuna, which is full of white sand, is likened to Her hips.

Visvanatha Cakravarti adds: The explanation of the words “the other fault is also removed” is as follows: The word kancanam (the flow of water) is neuter while the word veni (braid) is feminine. This is the fault of using a different gender in a simile (upama) (8.331) (Subodhim). Actually, Kavi Karnapura, not satisfied with the current example of sandigdha (ambiguous), gives another illustration of sandigdha in the next verse. This is because the meaning of the verse does not make sense if kancana is taken to mean gold. In other words, there is no real ambiguity in this verse.

### 10.22

*yathā vā,*

**Перевод:**

**Another example of sandigdha (ambiguous):**

*kṛṣṇo ’syā vaśa-vartīti*  
*vadanād vadanaṁ gatā*  
*candrāc candre padaṁ kṛtvā*  
*stutyā kīrtiḥ prayāti te*

**Пословный перевод:**

krsnah—Krsna; asyah—Her; vasa-varti— is under control; iti— thus; vadanat—from mouth; vadanam—to mouth; gata—went; candrat—from a moon; candre—in the moon (to a moonlike face); padam—its abode; krtva—having made; stutya—by means of praising (or praiseworthy); kirtih—fame; prayati—roams; te— Your.

**Перевод:**

**The words “Krsna is under Her control” are spreading from one moonlike mouth to another. Your fame is expanding by such praise (or Your praiseworthy fame is expanding).**

*atra stutyeti tṛtīyayā kiṁ stavena kiṁ stavārheti sandehaḥ. tena “kīrtir bhramati te bhuvi” iti vācyam.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the doubt is: Does stutya mean “by such praise” or “praiseworthy”? Therefore the fourth line should read: kirtir bhramati te bhuvi, “Your fame is spreading on the earth.”**

### 10.23

**Перевод:**

**\[This is neyartha (the meaning can only be guessed):\]**

*tava nayana-cakorī-puccha-kacchābhighāta-*  
*vyathita-hṛdaya-vṛttīnīva nīlotpalāni*  
*kamala-mukhi janebhyo lajjayā na prakāśaṁ*  
*dadhati divasa-madhye mudritāny eva santi*

**Пословный перевод:**

tava—of yours; nayana—\[in the form\] of the eyes; cakori—of the cakora bird; puccha—of a tail; kaccha—of the end; abhighata—by the striking; vyathita—are afflicted; hrdaya—of the heart; vrttini— whose functions; iva—as if; nila-utpalani—blue lotuses; kamala- mukhi—O girl with a lotus face; janebhyah—toward people; lajjaya—out of shyness; na prakasam dadhati—do not expand; divasa—the day; madhye—during; mudritani—closed; eva—only; santi—are.

**Перевод:**

**Girl with a lotus face, out of shyness toward people blue lotuses do not open during the day: They remain contracted. It’s as if their heart functions are troubled by the strikes of the tails of the cakora birds of your eyes.**

*atra puccha-kacchābhighātety-ādinā nirjitatvam eva lakṣyate. sā ca lakṣaṇā duṣṭaiva. uktaṁ ca “lakṣaṇā sā na kartavyā kaṣṭenārthāgamo yataḥ. na yatra śakya-sambandho na rūḍhir na prayojanam” tena neyārtham idam. tena “tava nayana-yuga-śrī sāhacaryaṁ na labdhā” iti pāṭhyam.*

**Перевод:**

**In this verse, the idea that blue lotuses have been defeated by the beloved gopi’s eyes is figuratively expressed by “puccha- kacchabhighata” and so on (by the strikes of the tail ends of cakora birds). That type of metaphorical usage is faulty. This is the fault called neyartha (the meaning can only be guessed).**

**It has been said: laksana sana kartavya kastenarthagamoyatah, na yatra sakya-sambandho na rudhir naprayojanam, “Laksana- vrtti should not be used when the meaning derived from it is understood with difficulty, when there is no connection with the literal meaning, when there is no conventional meaning (rudhi), or when there is no purpose (prayojana) (an implied sense).”**

**The first line should read: tava nayana-yuga-sri sahacaryam na labdha, “The beauty of your eyes is unmatched.”**

### 10.24

*atha kliṣṭādīni samāsa-gatāny eva,*

**Перевод:**

**Now examples of klista and other faults which only occur in compounds will be shown. This verse illustrates klista (not easily intelligible):**

*yamunā-janaka-jyotir-*  
*udaya-smita-śālibhiḥ*  
*tvan-mukhasya tulām āptum*  
*udavāsa-tapo dadhe*

**Пословный перевод:**

yamuna—of the Yamuna; janaka—of the father; jyotih—of the luminosity; udaya—because of the rising; smita—for smiling; salibhih—by those which are distinguished; tvat-mukhasya—with your face; tulam—equality; aptum—in order to attain; uda—in water; vasa—of staying; tapah—the austerity; dadhe—was done.

**Перевод:**

**Those things distinguished for smiling when the sun’s lumi­nosity first appears performed the austerity of staying in water to attain equality with your face.**

*atra yamunā-janakaḥ sūryas tasya jyotiṣa udayena smita-śālīni padmāni tair iti kleśata evārthāvagatir iti kliṣṭam*

**Перевод:**

**Here it is said that the austerity is done by the things distinguished for smiling when the sun’s luminosity first appears; this refers to lotuses. That is the fault called klista (not easily intelligible), since the meaning is difficult to understand.**

### 10.25

**Перевод:**

**\[This is avimrsta-vidheyamsa (not giving sufficient importance to the predicate) in a compound:\]**

*nāyaṁ pauṣpaḥ khalu na dhanuṣo nāpi maurvyāś ca nighno*  
*mugdhe digdhaḥ kim amṛta-rasenaiva kiṁ vā viṣeṇa*  
*nirmukto ’pi prakaṭam asakṛd vīkṣyate mucyamāno*  
*rādhe ko ’yaṁ tava rati-pateḥ ṣaṣṭha-bāṇaḥ kaṭākṣaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

na—not; ayam—this \[crooked glance\]; pauspah—made of flowers; khalu—indeed; na—not; dhanusah—of a bow; na api—nor even; maurvyah—of a bow string; ca—and; nighnah—under the control; mugdhe—O innocent girl (or lovely girl); digdhah—anointed; kim—is it?; amrta-rasena—essence of nectar; eva—only; kim va—or is it?; visena—with poison; nirmuktah—released; api— although prakatam—manifest; asakrt—repeatedly; viksyate—it is seen; mucyamanah—being released; radhe—O Radha; kah—is it?: ayam—this; tava—of Yours; rati-pateh—of Cupid (“Rati’s husband”); sastha-banah—the sixth arrow; kata-aksah—sidelong glance.

**Перевод:**

**Radha, O beautiful girl, this sidelong glance of Yours is certainly not made of flowers, nor is it used with a bow or a bowstring. Is it Cupid’s sixth arrow? Is it anointed with nectar or with poison? Although it is shot only once, it seems to be shot many times.**

*atra ṣaṣṭhatvaṁ vidheyaṁ, tat tu samāsena guṇī-bhūtam ity avimṛṣṭa-vidheyāṁśaḥ. tena mugdhe ity atra rādhe iti kṛtvā “ṣaṣṭhaḥ ko ’yaṁ nayanam ayi te pañca-bāṇasya bāṇaḥ” iti pāṭhe sādhu.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the predicate is the word sastha (sixth), in sastha-banah (sixth arrow), but its meaning has become secondary since the word is compounded. This is the fault called avimrsta- vidheyamsa (not giving sufficient importance to the predicate).**

**The proper version is: sasthah ko ’yam nayanam ayi te panca- banasya banah, “O Radha, is this glance of Yours Cupid’s sixth arrow?”**

**Комментарий:**

The word sastha-bana (sixth arrow) is a karma-dharaya compound. By rule, in a karma-dharaya the last word has more importance than the first word. The word sastha (sixth) is the predicate of bana (arrow). As a predicate, sastha should have the same status as its substantive, but in the compound it is secondary by being the first word. Therefore compounding should not be done.

Incidentally, in Manirariha-dipika Visvanatha Cakravarti quotes Sanat-kumara-samhita and mentions Cupid’s five flower arrows: asoka, amra-manjari (mango bud), mallika (jasmine), madhavi, and bakula. Jayadeva compares Radha to a different set of Cupid’s five flower arrows:

*bandhūka-dyuti-bāndhavo ’yam adharaḥ snigdho madhūka-cchavir*  
*gaṇḍaś caṇḍi cakāsti nīla-nalina-śrī-mocanaṁ locanam*  
*nāsābhyeti tila-prasūna-padavīṁ kundābha-danti priye*  
*prāyas tvan-mukha-sevayā vijayate viśvaṁ sa puṣpāyudhaḥ*

**“Hot-tempered girl, Your glossy lips are the friends of the splendor of a bandhuka flower. Your resplendent cheeks are the color of a madhuka flower. Your eyes emanate the beauty of a blue lotus, and Your nose has the status of a sesame blossom. O beloved with jasmine-like teeth, by serving Your face, Cupid, the flower archer, has conquered the world.” (Gita-govinda 10.14)**

Prabodhananda Sarasvati comments: *tvan-mukhe bandhūkamadhūka-nīlotpala-tila-kunda-puṣpāṇi santīti tvan-mukhād eva prāptāyudhaḥ kāmo viśvaṁ vijayata iti bhāvaḥ. tathā ca, raktapīta-nīla-kaṣāyojjvaleti ākarṣaṇa-vaśī-karaṇonmādana-drāvaṇaśoṣaṇeti kāmasya śarā kathitāḥ,* “The sense is: “Cupid has conquered the world after obtaining his weapons from Your face”: That is to say the bandhuka, madhuka, blue lotus, sesame, and jasmine flowers are in Radha’s face, and thus Cupid’s arrows are described as red, yellow, blue, yellowish red, and blazing white, which further correspond to the actions of attracting, bringing into submission, maddening, causing to melt, and parching.”

### 10.26

*yathā vā,*

**Перевод:**

**Another example of avimrsta- vidheyamsa in a compound:**

*akṛtaṁ sukṛtaṁ kiñcid*  
*ataptaṁ ca tathā tapaḥ*  
*bhaveyaṁ yena te nātha*  
*karuṇā-lava-bhājanam*

**Пословный перевод:**

akrtam—was not done; sukrtam—virtuous deed; kincit—some; ataptam—was not performed; ca—and; tatha—similarly; tapah— austerity; bhaveyam—I may become; yena—by which; te—Your; natha—O Lord; karuna—of compassion; lava—of a fraction; bhajanam—a recipient.

**Перевод:**

**O Lord, I did not perform virtuous deeds nor did I practice penance by means of which I could become a recipient of a fraction of Your mercy.**

*atra naṣaḥ prādhānyam, tasya samāsena guṇī-bhāvaḥ. evaṁ lavasya vidheyatvena samāsena guṇī-bhāvaḥ. tena “na kṛtaṁ sukṛtaṁ kiñcin na taptaṁ ca tathā tapaḥ, mayi yena bhaven nātha karuṇāyā lavo ’pi te” iti sādhu. tathā “udayati śaśī śrī-rādhāyā na tan mukha-maṇḍalam” ity atra na-kārasya prādhānyād guṇaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the negative particle, na\[n\], should be primary (since it is an important part of the predicate), but it has become secondary since it is compounded (in akrtam and in ataptam). Additionally, the word lava (fraction), a predicate, has become secondary due to being compounded. The proper version is: na krtam sukrtam kincin na taptam ca tatha tapah, mayi yena bhaven natha karunaya lavo ’pi te. (The meaning is the same, but compounding is not done.)**

**Similarly, earlier it was said: udayati sasi sri-radhaya na tan mukha-mandalam, “This is the rising moon, not the orb of Sri Radha’s face (5.64).” This makes a literary quality since na\[n\] has primary importance (because it is not compounded insofar as the negation is central in the text).**

### 10.27

*yatra tu viśeṣābhidhānaṁ tatra naṣaḥ samāso ’pi na duṣyati. yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**It should be understood, however, that even a compound with na\[n\] is not faulty when the purpose is to express a speciality of the word compounded with na\[n\]. For example:**

*amārjita-sucikkaṇair anabhiṣikta-dhautojjvalair*  
*abhūṣita-manoharair ananulipta-sat-saurabhaiḥ*  
*tamāla-dala-komalair nayana-kaumudī-kandalair*  
*aho kim idam aṅgakaiḥ sphurati nīlam ādyaṁ mahaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

amarjita—without being rubbed; su-cikkanaih—very glossy; anabhisikta—without being sprinkled (i.e. without being given an abhiseka); dhauta—clean; ujjvalaih—effulgent; abhusita—without being adorned; manoharaih—charming; ananulipta—without being anointed; sat—is eminent; saurabhaih—whose fragrance; tamala-dala—like a tamala leaf; komalaih—soft; nayana—for the eyes; kaumudi— of moonlight; kandalaih—a sprout; aho—what a wonder; kim idam—what is this?; angakaih—by means of limbs; sphurati—shines; nilam—dark blue; adyam—foremost; mahah— effulgence.

**Перевод:**

**What is this unparalleled dark blue effulgence that emanates from these limbs? How amazing! They are very glossy even without being massaged. They are pure and bright even without being consecrated by abhiseka. They are charming even without being adorned, and they are fragrant even without being anointed. They are as soft as a tamala leaf and are shoots of moonlight for the eyes.**

*atra sucikkaṇādi-viśeṣābhidhāne ’mārjitādiṣu naṣaḥ samāso guṇa eva, tad-rūpatvam eva vidheyaṁ na tena vidheyāvimarṣaḥ, yathā “apīta-kṣīva-kādambam” iti daṇḍinaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the use of na\[n\] in compounds such as amarjita is a literary quality since the purpose is to express the special features of the limbs such as glossiness. Thus the idea of having such a form is actually the predicate, and so there is no lack of consideration of the predicate (avimrsta-vidheya = vidheyavimarsa).**

**The poet Dandi gives a similar example: apita-ksiva-kadambam, “The grey-winged goose is drunk without drinking” (Kavyadarsa 2.200).**

**Комментарий:**

The substantive is kadambam (grey-winged goose). Here, ksiva (drunk) is the positive expression of a distinctive feature. Thus the idea of being drunk without drinking is the predicate; the mere absence of drinking is not the predicate.

In the elaboration, Kavi Karnapura shows that the term avimrsta in the name avimrsta-vidheyamsa (not giving sufficient importance to an aspect of the predicate) literally means “ill-considered”, from the verbal root mrs (to consider), and not “impure”, as derived from the root mrj (to purify).

### 10.28

*yathā vā,*

**Перевод:**

**Another example of a nonfaulty usage of na\[n\] in a compound:**

*anāsaktaḥ karma kurvann*  
*asakto viṣayāṣ juṣan*  
*apramatto bhajan kṛṣṇaṁ*  
*na sa tais tair nibadhyate*

**Пословный перевод:**

anasaktah—not attached; karma—activities; kurvan—while doing; asaktah—not attached; visayan—sense objects; jusan— while experiencing; apramattah—not being inattentive; bhajan— worshiping; krsnam—Krsna; na—not; sah—he; taih taih—by suchactivities and sense objects; nibadhyate—is bound.

**Перевод:**

**Detached while doing activities and while experiencing sense objects, a person who attentively worships Krsna is not bound by activities nor by sense objects.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Cakravarti explains that the mere absence of attachment is not the predicate here, rather the idea of being a doer of the activities with the special characteristic of being without attachment is the predicate (Subodhim). In other words, anasaktah karma kurvan is one predicate (detached while doing activities), thus the compounds with na\[n\] are not faulty.

### 10.29

*yathā vā,*

**Перевод:**

**Yet another example of a nonfaulty usage of na\[n\] in a compound:**

*apūtaḥ pūtanaṁ gacched*  
*avijño vijñatāṁ vrajet*  
*aguṇī guṇitām eti*  
*kṛṣṇe bhakto bhaved yadi*

**Пословный перевод:**

aputah—one who is impure; putanam—purity; gacchet—may attain; avijnah—an ignorant person; vijnatam—wisdom; vrajet— attains; agunl one without qualities; gunitam—the state of having qualities; eti—attains; krsne—of Krsna; bhaktah—a devotee; bhavet—he is; yadi—if.

**Перевод:**

**If a person who is impure, ignorant, and without quality becomes a devotee of Krsna, he becomes pure, wise, and full of qualities.**

*yathā “agṛdhnur ādade so ’rthān” ity-ādi kālidāsaḥ. yatra naṣaḥ prādhānyena doṣāntaram āpatati, tatra doṣa eva. yathā “giro na hari-tatparā dṛg api no harīkṣottarā” ity-ādau “kiṁ giro na hari-tatparāḥ, kiṁ hari-tatparā giro na, kiṁ giro na yato haritatparāś cet” iti sandehaḥ syāt. tena “giras tv ahari-tatparā dṛg api cāharīkṣottarā” iti sādhu.*

**Перевод:**

**Another such example is in this passage by Kalidasa: agrdhnur adade so ’rthan, “He accepted sensory objects without being greedy” (Raghu-vamsa 1.21).**

**Moreover, there may be a fault even when na\[n\], as a predicate, is primary. For example, giro na hari-tatpara drg api no hariksottara, “Words do not have Hari as their highest aim, nor does sight have the vision of Hari as its highest aim.” Here there is a doubt. Does this sentence mean: (1) “Words do not have Hari as their highest aim,” or (2) “Things which have Hari as their highest aim are not words,” or (3) “These are not words if they have Hari as their highest aim.” This is the fault called sandigdha (ambiguous). The sentence should read: giras tv ahari-tatpara drg api cahariksa-para. (The meaning is the same, but na\[n\] was compounded.)**

### 10.30

**Перевод:**

**\[This is viruddha-mati-krt (it causes a contradictory thought) in a compound:\]**

*vinā śapatham ālīnāṁ*  
*vinā kṛṣṇasya namratām*  
*na sammukhīnāsīty eṣa*  
*rādhe kas tava durgrahaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

vina—without; sapatham—the oath; alinam—of lady friends; vina—without; krsnasya—Krsna’s; namratam—being bowed down; na—not; sammukhina—facing; asi—you are; iti—therefore; esah—this; radhe—O Radha; kah—what is?; tava—of Yours; durgrahah—obstinacy, or illness.

**Перевод:**

**Radha, without Your friends’ promises and without Krsna’s bowing to You, You do not turn your face toward Him. What is this obstinacy of Yours?**

*atra “durgrahaḥ” iti durāgrahārtha-vācī ca, graha-vaiguṇyapratipādakatvena viruddha-mati-kṛt. “vinā śapatham” ity atrāpi vināśa-śabdo ’pi viruddhatā. tena “ṛte śapatham ālīnām” iti paṭhitvā “rādhe ko ’yaṁ durāgrahaḥ” iti pāṭhyam.*

**Перевод:**

**The word durgraha here conveys the meaning of obstinacy, but since it is also the name of an illness, a seizure, it causes a contradictory thought. The words vina sapatham cause a contradictory thought also, by separating them as vinasa- patham (path of destruction). The proper version is: rte sapatham alinam (without Your friends’ promises) and radhe ko ’yam duragrahah (Radha, what is this obstinacy?).**

### 10.31

*yathā vā,*

**Перевод:**

**Another example of viruddha-mati-krt in a compound:**

*samāṁ-samīnāvali cārayadbhir*  
*gavāṁ kulaṁ vallava-bāla-vṛndaiḥ*  
*vṛndāvane kautuka-keli-lolaḥ*  
*punātu vaḥ śrī-vraja-rāja-sūnuḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

samam-samina—cows who give birth every year; avali—in which \[herd\] there are many; carayadbhih—who are causing to go (i.e. who tend); gavam—of cows; kulam—a herd; vallava- bala—cowherd boys; vrndaih—along with many; vrndavane—in Vmdavana; kautuka—of festivity; keli—pastimes; lolah—who longs for; punatu—may He purify; vah—you all; sri— beautiful; vraja—of Vraja; raja—of the king; sunuh—the son.

**Перевод:**

**May the beautiful prince of Vraja purify all of you. He longs for pastimes of festivity in Vrndavana with the cowherd boys, who tend herds of cows that bear calves every year.**

*atra māṁsa-mīnāvali-sahitam iti viruddha-mati-kṛt. evam “akārya-mitraṁ bhavānī-patir ambikā-ramaṇaḥ” ity-ādayo ’pi viruddha-mati-kṛtaḥ. kiṁ bahunā? priyatama-vallabhatamā ityādayo ’pi priyāntaraṁ vallabhāntaraṁ ca pratipādayanti, tena te ’pi tathā. priyatamā-prabhṛtayas tu na tathā, aucityād iti kecid āhuḥ. vṛṣaṇa-vāntādi-śabdās tu na tathā, kavi-prayuktāt.*

**Перевод:**

**Here samam-saminavali (many of which bear calves every year) causes a contradictory thought. It could be interpreted to mean mamsa-minavali-sahitam (accompanied with much meat and fish). Similarly, words like akarya-mitram (true friend, lit. “a friend that wasn’t made,” but the unwanted double meaning is “partner in crime”), bhavani-pati (Siva, lit. “the master of Siva’s wife,” which suggests that Durga has a paramour), and ambika-ramana (Siva, lit. “Durga’s lover,” which hints at the possibility of more than one lover) also cause contradictory thoughts. Someone might wonder, “Does the fault of viruddha- mati-krt also occur on account of many lovers?” The answer is: Yes, words like priyatama, “most dear \[out of many\],” and vallabhatama, “most beloved \[out of many\],” convey the idea of other lovers, thus they also create contradictory thoughts. However, some say priyatama, “dearest girlfriend \[out of many\],” is suitable so it is not an instance of viruddha-mati-krt.**

**Moreover, vrsana (“strong,” or “scrotum,” or “sprinkling”), vanta (“ending with va,” or “vomited”), and other terms are not instances of viruddha-mati-krt because they are used by poets.**

### 10.32

*eṣāṁ samāsa-gatatvena diṅ-mātram udāharaṇaṁ kriyate. samāsagata-śruti-kaṭu yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**Now a few examples where the faults such as sruti-katu occur in compounds will be shown to illustrate the concept. The following verse is an instance of sruti-katu (harsh on the ears) in a compound:**

*pracakrame vikrama-vikrayaṁ bhruvā*  
*su-vakrayāsau rati-cakram akramāt*  
*suniṣṭhura-ṣṭhyūta-kaṭākṣa-sauṣṭhavā*  
*goṣṭhādhirājasya sute visaṁṣṭhule*

**Пословный перевод:**

pracakrame—began; vikrama—of masculine power; vikrayam— in which there is a sale (i.e. a loss); bhruva—with the brow; su- vakraya—very crooked; asau—She (Radha); rati—of love games; cakram—a multitude; akramat—after taking an opposite position (i.e. after mounting in the male position); su-nisthura—in such a way that there is harshness; sthyuta—is ejected (i.e. sent); kata-aksa—of the sidelong glance; sausthava— \[Radha\] whose excellence; gostha—of the cowherd village; adhirajasya—of the king; sute—toward the son (Krsna); visamsthule—who is unsteady (i.e. in a different position, the female position).

**Перевод:**

**After mounting in the male position, Radha began her many love games, which involve a loss of male domination. Krsna, the son of the king of the cowherds, laid down in the female position. With Her crooked brows, She showed Him Her expertise in throwing harsh sidelong glances.**

*atra parārdhe samāsa-gataṁ śruti-kaṭu-samudāyena pratikūlavarṇatvāt prakṛta-rasānanuguṇaḥ, visaṁṣṭhula iti samāpta-punarāttaṁ ceti parivṛttau mūla-nāśaḥ. evam anye ’pi yathā-sthalam anumeyāḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**In the second half of the verse there is no literary quality that corresponds to madhura-rasa, inasmuch as the phonemes are adverse. This is due to the many instances of sruti-katu, which occur in compounds here.**

**Moreover, visamsthule is an example of samapta-punar-atta (continuing with a modifier when the sentence is already complete: 10.84, meaning it was already said that Radha had assumed the male position, so it is redundant to say that Krsna assumed the female position). For these reasons, if corrections were made the whole verse would be changed.**

**Examples of the other faults in a compound can be inferred according to the context in this manner.**

### 10.33

*evam anye yathā-sthalaṁ jñeyā vākye tathaiva ca (6)*

**Пословный перевод:**

evam—in this way; anye—others (other faults); yatha-sthalam— according to the circumstance; jneyah—should be understood; vakye—in a sentence; tatha—in that way; eva—only; ca—and.

**Перевод:**

**Similarly, the other faults should be understood to also occur in a sentence, depending on the situation.**

*cyuta-saṁskṛty asamarthaṁ nirarthakaṁ varjayitvevaite śrutikaṭv-ādayo doṣā anumeyāḥ. krameṇodaharaṇāni—“pracakrame vikrama-vikrayam” ity-ādi vākyam eva śruti-kaṭu*

**Перевод:**

**This sutra means: The faults beginning from sruti-katu, but excluding cyuta-samskrti (grammatical mistake), asamartha (not the intended meaning) and nirarthaka (vyartha, meaningless), should be inferred to occur in a sentence.**

**Now examples will be shown according to the sequence (10.6). In the previous verse, there is an instance of sruti-katu in the first half: pracakrame vikrama-vikrayam bhruva su-vakrayasau rati-cakram akramat.**

### 10.34

*yathā vā,*

**Перевод:**

**Another instance of sruti-katu in a sentence:**

*kaṣṭam aṣṭāpadasyedaṁ*  
*dauṣṭhvaṁ ca sudhā-ṣṭhyuraḥ*  
*varṣmaṇo hy anayā ghṛṇyā*  
*tuṇḍena ca tava priye*

**Пословный перевод:**

kastam—difficulty (i.e. gold shall not remain being so highly regarded); astapadasya—of gold; idam—this; dausthvam— faultiness; ca—and; sudha-sthyurah—of the moon (“it throws nectar”); varsmanah—of the body; hi—only; anaya—due to this; ghrnya—on account of a ray; tundena—on account of the face; ca—and; tava—of yours; priye—O dear girl.

**Перевод:**

**Darling, gold is in trouble because of your bodily rays, and the moon is faulty due to your face.**

*sudhā-ṣṭhyuraś candrasya ghṛṇyā kiraṇena, atra vākyam eva tathā.*

**Перевод:**

**This is the fault of sruti-katu in a sentence. Sudha-sthyurah means “of the moon,” and ghrnya means “because of a ray.” (The cerebral phonemes are not conducive to madhura-rasa.)**

### 10.35

**Перевод:**

**\[This is aprayukta (not in use) in a sentence:\]**

*lekhair duścyavana-praṣṭhaiḥ*  
*sura-jyeṣṭhādikair api*  
*vandyamāno vidhū rātu*  
*śātaṁ śyatu ca duṣkṛtam*

**Пословный перевод:**

lekhaih—by demigods; duscyavana—Indra (“who is difficult to make fall”); prasthaih—whose leader; sura-jyesthadikaih— headed by Brahma; api—even; vandyamanah—who is glorified (or offered obeisances); vidhuh—Krsna; ratu—may he give; satam— happiness; syatu—may he destroy; ca—and; duskrtam—evil-doers.

**Перевод:**

**The gods led by Indra and headed by Brahma offer obeisances to Krsna. May He give joy to you all and make evil-doers insignificant.**

*lekhair devair, duścyavana indraḥ, sura-jyeṣṭho brahmā, vidhuḥ śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ, rātu dadātu, śyatu kṛśaṁ karotu. atra lekhādi-śabdāḥ surādi-vācakā api śleṣādikaṁ vinānyatra kavibhir aprayuktatvād aprayuktās tena vākyam evedam aprayuktam.*

**Перевод:**

**In this verse, lekhaih refers to the gods, duscyavana denotes Indra, sura-jyestha is Brahma, vidhu is Sri Krsna, ratu means “may he give,” and syatu means “may he make insignificant.” Here, the words lekhaih, duscyavana, and sura-jyestha, though they signify the gods, Indra and Brahma respectively, are not in use simply because poets do not use these terms unless they intend to make a pun. Thus, this is an instance of the fault called aprayukta (not in use) occurring in a sentence.**

### 10.36

**Перевод:**

**\[This is nihatartha (obstructed meaning) in a sentence:\]**

*kṣamā-kṣamā-dharānanta-*  
*makara-dhvaja-laṅghinaḥ*  
*plavante śaibya-sugrīva-*  
*meghapuṣpa-balāhakāḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

ksama—the earth; ksama-dhara—mountain (“which preserves the earth”); ananta—the sky (“who has no end”); makara-dhvaja— the ocean; langhinah—they cross over; plavante—they go; saibya— Saibya; sugriva—Sugnva; meghapuspa—Meghapuspa; balahaka—Balahaka.

**Перевод:**

**Saibya, Sugnva, Meghapuspa and Balahaka gallop and go beyond the earth, mountains, sky, and oceans.**

*atra kṣamādayo balāhakāntāḥ śabdāḥ kṣānty-ādibhiḥ prasiddhair nihatārthāḥ. tathā hi—kṣamā kṣāntiḥ, kṣamā-dhara kṣamī, anantaḥ parameśvaraḥ, makara-dhvajaḥ kāmaḥ, śaibyaḥ śibiputraḥ, sugrīvo vānara-rājaḥ, megha-puṣpaṁ jalaṁ, balāhako meghaḥ. etaiḥ prasiddhaiḥ pṛthvī-parvata-vyoma-samudrā bhagavato hayāś catvāraś cāprasiddhā vyāhanyante.*

**Перевод:**

**All the nouns in this verse, from ksama to balahaka, are instances of the fault called nihatartha (obstructed meaning). This is because these nouns carry well-known meanings: ksama means “patience,” ksama-dhara means “one who is tolerant (peaceful),” ananta refers to the Lord, makara-dhvaja is a name of Cupid (Amara-kosa 1.1.27), saibya means “Sibi’s son,” sugnva is the name of the king of monkeys, megha-puspa is water (“flower in the form of a cloud”) and balahaka is a cloud. Therefore the lesser known meanings of these nouns, specifically: ksama as “earth,” ksama-dhara as “mountain,” ananta as “sky,” makara-dhvaja as “ocean,” and saibya, sugnva, meghapuspa and balahaka as the Lord’s four horses are obstructed by these well-known definitions.**

**Комментарий:**

Sibi was a king who saved Agni. Agni, in the form of a dove, was attacked by Indra in the form of a hawk, but Sibi offered his own flesh, equal in weight to the dove, to Indra (Mahabharata).

The Padma Purana describes Krsna’s horses: saibyas tu suka- patrabhah sugrivo hema-pingalah, meghapuspas tu meghabhah panduro hi balahakah, “Saibya is green like a parrot’s wings, Sugnva is yellow-gold, Meghapuspa is the color of a cloud, and Balahaka is whitish” (cited in Sarartha-darsini 10.53.5).

### 10.37

*yathā vā,*

**Перевод:**

**Another example of nihatartha (obstructed meaning) in a sentence:**

*sāmudraṁ nava-nītaṁ ca*  
*mahā-riṣṭiś ca nandakaḥ*  
*hari-vatsa-śayāsannau*  
*vātāṁ śātaṁ sadaiva vaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

samudram—the Kaustubha jewel (“born from the ocean”); nava- nitam—is newly brought; ca—and; maha-ristih—which is a great sword; ca—and; nandakah—Nandaka (name of the Lord’s sword); hari—of Hari; vatsa—and the chest; saya—the hand; asannau— are near; vatam—may they two bestow; satam—happiness; sada— always; eva—only; vah—to all of you.

**Перевод:**

**The Kaustubha jewel, newly brought from the ocean, and Nandaka, the great sword, are always near Hari’s chest and hand respectively. May those two bestow happiness to you all.**

*atra sāmudraṁ nava-nītaṁ kaustubhaḥ, mahā-riṣṭir nandakaḥ khaḍgaḥ, vatsaṁ vakṣaḥ, śayaḥ pāṇiḥ. ete sāmudra-lavaṇanavanīta-mahotpāta-samṛddhi-janaka-tarṇaka-śayanaiḥ prasiddhaiḥ nihatā iti vākyam eva nihatārtham.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the words samudram nava-nttam denote the Kaustubha jewel, the words maha-ristih nandakah denote the Lord’s sword, whereas vatsa means “chest” and saya means “hand”. Yet these meanings are obstructed by these well-known meanings: samudra means “sea salt”, navamta means “butter”, maha-risti means “great misfortune”, nandaka means “making happy”, vatsa means “calf”, and saya means “resting”. This verse is an instance of nihatartha in a sentence.**

**Комментарий:**

The word samudra used in this verse (“born from the ocean”) is made from the word samudra, in the sense of “born there” (tatra jatah, HNV 1145). Moreover, in Visnu-lila, the Kaustubha jewel appears from the churning of the Milk Ocean (Bhagavatam [8.8.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-8/8.6)). In Krsna-lila, however, it is a gift from the serpent Kaliya. Srimad- Bhagavatam states that Kaliya offered j ewels to Krsna (Bhagavatam [10.16.65](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/16.65)). Snla Rupa Gosvami writes: kaustubhakhyo manir yena pravisya hradam auragam, kaliya-preyasi-vrnda-hastair atmopaharitah, “The Lord had made His Kaustubha gem enter the serpent’s lake. Then He arranged for it to be presented to Him through the hands of Kaliya’s wives” (Radha-krsna-ganoddesa-dipika 2.129).

### 10.38

**Перевод:**

**\[This is avacaka (inexpressive) in a sentence:\]**

*viṣṇu-syandana-parṇānāṁ*  
*pṛṣad-aśvena dhāvitāḥ*  
*nipetuḥ kāśyapī-kāntāḥ*  
*kauṇḍinyāḥ kara-pīḍane*

**Пословный перевод:**

visnu-syandana—of Garuda (“Visnu’s vehicle”); parnanam—of the wings; prsat-asvena—because of the wind; dhavitah— trembling; nipetuh—fell; kasyapi—of Kasyapa’s daughter; kantah—the lovers; kaundinyah—of Rukmini; kara-pidane—on the occasion of pressing the hand.

**Перевод:**

**When Rukmini was taken away, the kings trembled and fell to the ground on account of the wind generated by Garuda’s wings.**

*atra viṣṇu-syandanādayaḥ śabdā viṣṇu-rathādaya iva garuḍādyarthaṁ na bodhayanti, tenāmī avācakā iti vākyam evāvācakam. parṇaṁ pakṣaḥ, dhāvitāḥ kampitāḥ, kāśyapī-kāntā mahīśvarāḥ, kauṇḍinyāḥ rukmiṇyāḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Here parna means “wing” (usually it means leaf), dhavitah means “trembled” (usually it means either ran or purified), kasyapi-kantah means “lords of the earth” (kings), and kaundim means “Rukmini”. In this verse the terms used are not as expressive of the intended meaning as their synonyms. For example, the word visnu-syandana does not quickly reveal the meaning it expresses in this verse as well as visnu-ratha does: both signify Garuda. Therefore these words are not expressive \[because they carry many meanings\]. This is the fault called avacaka occurring in a sentence.**

**Комментарий:**

Visnu-syandana can also mean “Visnu’s perspiration,” or “Visnu’s movement.” In regard to Garuda, Snmad-Bhagavatam explains that Garuda’s wings are the forms of hymns of praise (stotra-vajin, Bhagavatam [4.7.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/7.19)). Visvanatha specifies that one wing represents brhat, and the other rathantara (Sarartha-darsirii 4.7.19). Brhat and rathantara are names of groups of hymns from the Sama-Veda, which comprises metrical, beautiful hymns of praise of the Lord. In other words. Garuda manifests these hymns by flapping his wings. The episode of Krsna’s kidnapping Rukmini is narrated in the fifty­fourth chapter of the Tenth Canto, but Garuda is not mentioned there. Perhaps other Puranas describe Krsna’s arriving on the back of Garuda in another kalpa.

### 10.39

**Перевод:**

**\[This is anucitartha (unsuitable meaning) in a sentence:\]**

*balakṣe pakṣe ’yaṁ divasa-pariṇāme śaśa-dharo*  
*divi-ṣṭhaṁ ku-ṣṭhaṁ vā na kiraṇa-kalāpaṁ vikirati*  
*tathāpi draṣṭèṇāṁ nayana-kusumaṁ vyoma-saraso*  
*mahā-proṣṭhī-valkākṛtir api ku-loka-priyatamaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

balakse—bright; pakse—during the phase \[of the moon\]; ayam— this; divasa-pariname—in the afternoon (“a transformation of the day”); sasa-dharah—the moon (“who bears \[a the mark of\] a hare”); divi-stham—situated in heaven; ku-stham—situated on the earth; va—or; na—not; kirana—of rays; kalapam—a bundle (multitude); vikirati—scatters; tatha api—nevertheless; drastenam—of onlookers; nayana—for the eyes; kusumam—\[which moon\] is like a flower; vyoma—\[in the form of\] the sky; sarasah—of a lake; maha—big; prosthl—of a fish (Amara-kosa 1.10.18); valka—of scales; akrtih—\[the moon\] has an appearance; api—also; ku—of the earth; loka—to people; priyatamah—is very dear.

**Перевод:**

**During its bright phase, in the late afternoon the moon does not reflect much light on earth nor in the heavens. Still, to the onlookers the moon appears to be like a flower in the lake of the sky, or like one scale of a big white fish. In this way the moon is very dear to people on earth.**

*atra pṛthivī-sthādi-vācino ’pi ku-ṣṭhādayaḥ śabdāḥ kuṣṭhaṁ vyādhiḥ, nayana-kusumaṁ nayana-vyādhiḥ, kulokaḥ kujanaḥ ity anucitārtha-pratipādakāḥ, tenedaṁ vākyam anucitārtham.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the words ku-stha and so on, used in the sense of prthivi- stha (situated on earth) and so on, express an unsuitable meaning as well. For example, kustha is the name of a certain disease, nayana-kusuma (a flower for the eyes) can also mean “an eye disease,” and ku-loka (people on earth) can also mean “bad people.” This is the fault called anucitartha (unsuitable meaning) occurring in a sentence.**

### 10.40

**Перевод:**

**\[This is gramya (vulgar) in a sentence:\]**

*khāna-pānādi-sāmagrī*  
*nādyāpi bata sādhitā*  
*kṛṣṇo ’yam āgata-prāyo*  
*bhallaṁ te galla-carvaṇam*

**Пословный перевод:**

khana—of food; pana-adi—drink and so on; samagri—totality; na—not; adya—now; api—even; bata—alas; sadhita—has been effected; krsnah—Krsna; ayam—He; agata-prayah—has almost arrived; bhallam—talk; te—your; galla—on the cheek; carvanam— chewing.

**Перевод:**

**\[Nanda says to Yasoda:\]**

**Krsna has almost come back from the forest. Gee, the food preparations aren’t even under way. You always brag that only you prepare Krsna’s food and drink. Your talk is as useless as chewing on the cheek.**

*atra khāna-pānādayaḥ śabdā grāmyāḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the words khana (food), pana (drink), and so on are vulgar (rustic).**

**Комментарий:**

Khana could be replaced by bhaksya or bhojya, and pana could be replaced by peya, panlya. and panaka. Visvanatha Cakravarti says that bhallam te galla-carvanam (Your talk is as useless as chewing on the cheek) as well is vulgar usage; the acarya glosses it as tava vag-vyayo vrtha (your expending energy in speaking is useless) (Subodhini). Bhalla does not have that sense in Apte nor in Monier-Williams, yet it could be made from the verbal root bhall\[a\] paribhasane, which means “to talk.” At any rate, all these words are village words; khana and pana are still used in Prakrit languages today (khana and pana in Hindi, and pana in Bengali, for example).

### 10.41

**Перевод:**

**\[This is aprattta (not understood) in a sentence:\]**

*koṣebhyo ’nna-mayādibhyo*  
*viśvādibhyaś ca yaḥ paraḥ*  
*sa te prāṇa-patiḥ kṛṣṇaḥ*  
*saubhāgyaṁ kim ataḥ param*

**Пословный перевод:**

kosebhyah—than the layers; anna-maya-adibhyah—to anna-maya and so on; visva-adibhyah—to visva and so on; ca—and; yah—who is; parah—superior; sah—He; te—of yours; prana—of the life airs; patih—the master; krsnah—Krsna; saubhagyam—auspiciousness; kim—is there?; atah—than Him; param—greater.

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, the master of your life force, is beyond the five layers beginning from anna-maya. He is also superior to the three states of consciousness beginning from visva. Can there be anything more auspicious than Him?**

*atra anna-mayādayaḥ pañca-koṣāḥ, viśva-taijasa-prājñāś ca traya ātmānaḥ, kevala-vedānta-śāstra-mātra-prayuktatvād pratītāḥ, tenedam apratītaṁ vākyam.*

**Перевод:**

**Here, anna-maya and other terms refer to the five layers (panca- kosa), whereas visva, taijasa, and prajna are the three bodies.**

**This is understood only in the context of scriptures on monistic Vedanta. Therefore this verse is an instance of the fault called aprattta (not understood) occurring in a sentence.**

**Комментарий:**

The term panca-kosa, also written panca-kosa, is well-known. It originates from Paingala Upanisad (2): In this interpretation, the five sheaths covering a soul are the body, the life force, the mind, the intelligence, and the ego. This last covering is also called karana-sarira (causal sheath) and ananda-maya-sarira (the body imbued with bliss) (Paingala Upanisad 2). This is because ego is described as cit (spiritual) and acit (inert): karanam cid-acin- mayah (Bhagavatam [11.24.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/24.7)). However, in Taittiriya Upanisad 2.3-5, there is a different interpretation: The concept of panca- purusa (five humanlike shapes), not panca-kosa, is used: (1) the physical body (anna-maya), (2) the life force (prana-maya), (3) mind, intelligence and ego (mano-maya), (4) the soul (vijnana- maya), and (5) Paramatma (ananda-maya).

Similarly, there are two different explanations of the terms visva, taijasa and prajna. Firstly, visva is the gross body, taijasa is the subtle body, and prajna is the causal body composed of ego. This is also explained in Paingala Upanisad (2). For the details, consult Bhagavatam [7.15.54](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-7/15.54).

Secondly, there are five states of consciousness: visva is the normal state of being awake (jagrat), taijasa is the state of dreaming (svapna), prajna is deep sleep (susupti), turya is transcendence (saksi-jiva), and turyatita is the state beyond the fourth (suddha- jiva, and Paramatma). The source is Mandala-brahmana Upanisad (2). For more details, consult Sarartha-darsini 2.2.16.

Sometimes there is no mention of a fifth state, and the fourth state denotes transcendence as a whole: (1) mayi turye, “in Me, the fourth” (Bhagavatam [11.13.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/13.28)) (2) narayane turiyakhye, “in Narayana, known as the fourth” (Bhagavatam [11.15.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/15.16)). Regarding a soul’s designation as the fourth state, consult Bhagavatam [11.13.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/13.27) and Sarartha-darsini 11.13.32.

### 10.42

**Перевод:**

**\[This is vrida-dayi aslila (shamefully unpleasant) in a sentence:\]**

*apānenābhojanenā-*  
*mehanenāpi khidyase*  
*kiṁ te tapasvin kaṣṭena*  
*bhaja kṛṣṇaṁ sukhī bhava*

**Пословный перевод:**

apanena—because of not drinking; abhojanena—because of not eating; amehanena—because of a lack of oil; api—even; khidyase—you are afflicted; kim—what is the use; te—of yours; tapasvin—O ascetic; kastena—of this hardhip; bhaja—worship; krsnam—Krsna; sukhl—happy; bhava—be.

**Here the words apana and so on, although expressing the absence of drinking and so on, make one perceive the meaning of “farting” and so on. Thus they are unpleasant (aslila) on account of generating shame (vrida). In this verse, amehana means “absence of oil”.**

The unintended meaning of mehana is “copulation”, by the definition: mehanam mutra-sisnayoh, “Mehana means urine, and the male organ” (Medim-kosa). Similarly, apana means both “absence of drinking” and “the downward vital air,” and abhojana means “absence of eating” as well as “bad food.”

**However, the usage of the word vanta is not faulty when there is a desire to express an arthantara-sankramita-vacya dhvani (implied meaning regarding which the literal meaning changed to another meaning) and so on.**

**For example, the poet Murari writes: vantair aksara-murtibhih su-kavina mukta-phalair gumphita, “This poem is a garland strung by an expert poet and endowed with pearls that are the embodiment of sounds ending with va” \[as in the title Anargha- raghava \] (Anargha-raghava).**

**The same applies to a different usage of the verbal root vam. For example:**

*iti kandarpa-mañjarī. “mā vama saṁvṛṇu viṣam idam” iti sātaṅkaṁ pitāmahenoktam,” “prātar jayati sa-lajjaḥ kajjala-malinādharaḥ śambhuḥ” iti govardhanaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**This verse is from Kandarpa-manjari. Moreover, the poet Govardhana writes: “Grandsire Bhisma apprehensively tells Siva: ma vama samvrnu visam idam, “Don’t vomit the poison; hold it back.” Later, the author expounds: pratarjayati sa-lajjah kajjala-malinadharah sambhuh, “In the morning, Sambhu is glorious since he is shy because his lips are stained with eyeliner \[from ParvatT’s eyes\]” (Arya-saptasati).**

**Комментарий:**

Bhisma met Siva many millenniums after the churning of the Milk Ocean, when Siva swallowed the black kala-kuta poison and consequently became known as kala-kantha (he whose throat is dark). The poet Govardhana was a colleague of Jayadeva in the court of Maharaja Laksmana Sena (13th century CE). Jayadeva glorifies “Acarya Govardhana” in Gita-govinda (1.4).

**Пословный перевод:**

hari-carana—of the sky; ratna—of the jewel; kirana—on account of the rays; ujjagaram—excited (bloomed); ambhoda-kusuma— from water; janmanam—\[of lotuses,\] which take birth; gahanam— the forest (“an impervious place”); anuharati—resembles; prasava-asu-ga—of Cupid (“he has arrows (asu-ga, “they go fast”) of flowers”); kurdana—\[produced\] on account of the games; nidra—from sleep; uttha—who has arisen; yuvati—of a young girl; mukha—of the face; susamam—the beauty.

### 10.49

**Перевод:**

**\[This is avimrsta-vidheyamsa (not giving sufficient importance to the predicate) occurring in compounds:\]**

*navaṁ vayas te ’dhika-saukumāryatā*  
*priyānurāgāmṛta-sindhu-ratnatā*  
*yathottaraṁ vṛddhimatī guṇāvaliḥ*  
*kā te samānā bhavatīha rādhike*

**Пословный перевод:**

navam—fresh; vayah—youth; te—Your; adhika—abundantly; saukumaryata—the state of being very delicate; priya—of the beloved (for You); anuraga—in the form of love; amrta—of nectar; sindhu—in an ocean; ratnata—the state of being a jewel; yatha- uttaram—according to the subsequent one; vrddhimatt—which increase; guna—of qualities; avalih—multitude; ka—who; te—to You; samana—equal; bhavati—is; iha—in this world; radhike—O Radhika.

**Перевод:**

**Radhika, Your fresh youth is Your abundance of delicateness. It is a jewel in the nectar ocean of Your beloved’s love for You. Each quality of Yours seems better than the next and simply keeps increasing. Who in this world is equal to You?**

*atrādhika-saukumāryatā priyānurāgety-ādi ca vidheyaṁ, tac ca samāsa-gatatvenāvimṛṣṭam. tena “navaṁ vayas te sukumāratādhikaṁ, priyasya ca prema navaṁ navaṁ tvayi” iti sādhu*

**Перевод:**

**Here the predicate of vayas is adhika-saukumaryata and priyanuragamrta-sindhu-ratnata. However, the fault of avimrsta- vidheyamsa occurs because they are in compounds. The first half of the verse should read: navam vayas te su-kumaratadhikam, priyasya ca prema navam navam tvayi, “Your fresh youth is excellent on account of Your delicateness, and Your beloved’s love for You is ever fresh.”**

**Комментарий:**

They are two bahuvrlhi compounds. In such a compound, the meaning of the other word outside the compound is predominant, because that other word is the noun which the bahuvrlhi adjective modifies. In addition, the taddhita suffix ta\[p\], which indicates a state of being, further contributes to the secondariness of the words adhika and saukumarya in adhika-saukumaryata. The same understanding applies to the compound priyanuragamrta-sindhu- ratnata (being a jewel in the ocean of nectar in the form of the sweetheart’s love). Previously, the example sastha-bana (sixth arrow) was shown (10.25).

### 10.50

*yathā vā,*

**Перевод:**

**Another example of avimrsta-vidheyamsa in a compound:**

*sevante jaladāgame mṛga-dṛśāṁ keśān raver dvādaśa*  
*grīṣme yatra bhajanti deha-latikāś cāndrāḥ kalāḥ ṣoḍaśa*  
*pratyūṣeṣu niśā-mukheṣu śiśire veṣoṣma-sampādikā*  
*jyotiḥ-pallavam udgiranti śanakair mūrtāḥ kṛśānor daśa*

**Пословный перевод:**

sevante—serve; jala-da—of the clouds; agame—at the arrival; mrga-drsam—of the doe-eyed girls; kesan—the hair; raveh—in relation to the sun; dvadasa—twelve; grlsme—in the summer; yatra—at which time; bhajanti—worship; deha-latikah—the creepers in the form of bodies (i.e. creeperlike bodies); candrah— of the moon; kalah—digits; sodasa—sixteen; prati-usesu—at every dawn; nisa-mukhesu—which begins with night; sisire—in the winter; vesa—for the clothes; usma—heat; sampadikah—they produce; jyotih—of light; pallavam—a shoot; udgiranti—emit; sanakaih—slowly; murtah—embodied forms; krsanoh—of fire; dasa—ten.

**Перевод:**

**In the monsoon season, the twelve aspects of the sun serve the doe-eyed girls’ hair. In the summer, the sixteen aspects of the moon worship their creeper-like bodies. And in the winter, at every dawn, which begins with the end of night, the tens aspects of fire gently emit shoots of light that warm their clothes.**

*atra veṣoṣma-sampādanaṁ nānuvādyam api tu vidheyam. tenātra samāsa-gatam avimṛṣṭa-vidheyāṁśatvam. tena “veṣoṣmaṇaḥ kṣiptayaḥ” iti vācyam.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the idea of producing heat for their clothes (vesosma- sampadikah) is not the subject, rather it is the predicate. As such, it illustrates the fault of avimrsta-vidheyamsa (not giving sufficient importance to an aspect of the predicate) in a compound. The modification should be: vesosmanah ksiptayah, “They cast warmth on the clothes.”**

**Комментарий:**

The compound vesosma-sampadikah means: “They produce heat for the clothes.” Both vesosman and sampadika, as one unit, are the predicate, because by definition a predicate (vidheya) is anything that is stated in reference to the subject (uddesya). To correct the fault, the two words must be stated separately so that each has predominance, as in: vesosmanah sadhikah. Kavi Karnapura reworded this as vesosmanah ksiptayah to fit the meter.

### 10.51

*asamāsa-gatatve ’pi vākyāvimṛṣṭa-vidheyāṁśatvaṁ draṣṭavyam. yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**The fault called avimrsta-vidheyamsa can occur in a sentence even when the fault is not related to a compound. For example:**

*saubhāgyaṁ mama punar etad eva kṛṣṇa*  
*yat kāntā-gaṇa-gaṇane mamāpi lekhaḥ*  
*atrāyaṁ yad adhika ādaras tad etan*  
*māhātmyaṁ tava param uttamaṁ kṛpāyāḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

saubhagyam—good fortune; mama—my; punah—moreover; etat—this; eva—only; krsna—O Krsna; yat—that; kanta-gana— female lovers; ganane—when counting; mama—of me; api— even; lekhah—mentioning; atra—in it; ayam—this; yat—which; adhikah—great; adarah—honor; tat—that is; etat—this very; mahatmyam—glory; tava—of Yours; param—superior; uttamam— excellent; krpayah—of mercy.

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, my good fortune is this—that I am also counted among Your lovers. That you have shown me such great honor—this is the superexcellent glory of Your mercy.**

*atra etad eveti vidheyaṁ na tv anuvādyaṁ tat tu paścān nirdeśenāpy anuvādyam eva jātam. tena “asmākaṁ punar idam eva saubhagaṁ yat kṛṣṇa tvaj-jana-gaṇane mamāpi lekhaḥ” iti pāṭhyam. atrāsmākam iti bahu-vacanaṁ sthāne vidheyatāṁ yāti, mamāpīti eka-vacanam api sthāne vidheyatāṁ yāti.*

**Перевод:**

**The word etad (this) in the first sentence has the position of a predicate, not that of a subject. Nonetheless, etat is the actual subject even though it is mentioned after \[the words saubhagyam mama punar, which are the true predicate\]. This is the fault called avimrsta-vidheyamsa (improperly placed predicate). The first half of the verse should read: asmakam punar idam eva saubhagam yat krsna tvaj-jana-ganane mamapi lekhah.**

**Комментарий:**

Such an inversion between the subject as a pronoun and its predicate are often seen, but in this verse the real problem is in the first sentence, because in addition to the inversion the word yat is used in the sense of “that”. In philosophy, the rule is: anuvadam anuktvaiva na vidheyam udirayet, “A predicate should not be mentioned without first stating the subject” (Caitanya-caritamrta, Adi [16.58](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/16.58)). But in poetics that rule is not used.

In the case of pronouns such as etad and idam (this), which denote something about to be stated, the corresponding clause is a predicate. The examples of avimrsta-vidheyamsa in a sentence almost always involve a form of etad or idam (this). For example, in Kesava Kasmin’s verse beginning mahattvam gangayah satatam idam abhati nitaram yat (Caitanya-caritamrta, Adi [16.41](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/16.41)), idam (this) is the subject, mahattvam gangayah (is the glory of the Ganga) is the predicate, which is used in conjunction with the yat clause, but the fault of avimrsta-vidheyamsa occurs because the predicate is stated before the subject. However, in sentences where the subject is not a form of etad or idam and yat (that) is not used, the principle of avimrsta-vidheyamsa is not applied.

*yathā vā,*

*apāṅga-bhaṅgena dhṛtiṁ dhunīte*  
*kalena veṇoś ca hriyaṁ lunīte*  
*kulaṁ ca śīlaṁ ca punaḥ punīte*  
*sparśena yo ’sau purataḥ priyas te*

**Пословный перевод:**

apa-anga—of the corner of the eye; bhangena—by the crooked glances; dhrtim—the patience; dhunite—destroys; kalena—with the sweet sound; venoh—of the flute; ca—and; hriyam—shyness; lunite—destroys; kulam—aristocratic birth; ca—and; sllam— good behavior; ca—and; punah—moreover; punite—purifies; sparsena—by the touch; yah—who; asau—he; puratah—in front; priya—beloved; te—your.

**Перевод:**

**Your beloved, who destroys your patience with His crooked sidelong glances, who shatters your shyness with the sweet melodious sound of His flute, and who purifies your aristocratic birth and good behavior with His touch, is in front of you. \[Do something!\]**

*atra yo ’sāv ity etayoḥ padayoḥ pūrvam anuvādyaṁ dvitīyaṁ tu vidheyam, sannikṛṣṭatamatvena dvitīyam evānuvādya-vat pratibhāsate. tena “sparśena yas te sakhi so ’bhyupaiti” iti vācyam. evaṁ prastāvato yat-tadoḥ sambandho ’pi vicāryate. tathā hi—yatra hi prakrānta-prasiddhānubhūtārtha-viṣayas tacchabdaḥ, tatra hi yac-chabdo nāpekṣitaḥ syāt.*

**Перевод:**

**Here yah, in the fourth line, is the subject and asau is the predicate. However, since they are right next to each other, the predicate, asau, almost seems to be part of the subject. The fourth line should be changed to: sparsena yas te sakhi so ’bhyupaiti.**

**In this connection, the relationship between yad and tad should be considered. Although yad and tad often act as correlatives, in some cases tad (that) is used without yad (which). These particular instances refer to three specific applications of tad. There is no usage of yad when tad has the sense of either:**

**1.   prakranta (introducing),**

**2.   prasiddha (well-known), or**

**3.   anubhuta artha (something experienced before).**

*sa candrikāyāṁ niśi sundarībhiḥ*

*atra sa iti prakrāntaṁ śrī-kṛṣṇam eva prastauti. “sa rāsa-lāsyaṁ vitatāna kṛṣṇaḥ” iti pāṭhe sa iti prasiddha-mātra-dyotakam.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the words sah (He) in the second and fourth lines serve to introduce Sri Krsna. This is an instance of tad used in the sense of prakranta (introducing). If the fourth line were replaced by: sa rasa-lasyam vitatana krsnah, “That well-known Krsna began the Rasa dance,” the pronoun sah in this wording would merely have the sense of prasiddha (well-known).**

### 10.56

*evaṁ cottara-vākya-stho yac-chabdaḥ pūrva-vākyasya tac-chabdaṁ prati na sākāṅkṣaḥ. yathā—*

**Перевод:**

**The word yad can be used in the second sentence without its correlative tad, provided the first sentence does not require tad. For instance:**

*yena svakīyaṁ padam ādareṇa*  
*pradīyate mukty-adhikaṁ bhajadbhyaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

trailokya—of the three worlds; laksmi—in the form of the beauty; mukuta—on the crown; eka-ratnam—who is the chief jewel; sri- krsnah—Sri Krsna; eva—only; pranayena—with love; sevyah— should be served; yena—by whom; svakiyam—His own; padam— abode; adarena—with high regard; pradiyate—is bestowed; mukti—to liberation; adhikam—which is superior; bhajatbhyah— unto those who worship.

**Перевод:**

**Only Sri Krsna should be served with love. He is the chief jewel on the crown that is the beauty of the three worlds. With high regard for those who worship Him, He grants them residence in His abode, a position superior to liberation.**

*atrottara-vākya-stho yac-chabdaḥ svācchandyenaiva śobhate. pūrva-vākya-stho yac-chabda uttara-vākya-sthaṁ tac-chabdaṁ prati sāpekṣaḥ. yathā—“yena svakīyaṁ param ādareṇa” ityādy uttaram ardhaṁ pūrvārdhaṁ yadi bhavati, tadaiva tacchabdākāṅkṣā, tena “śrī-kṛṣṇa eva praṇayāt sa sevyaḥ” iti caturtha-caraṇaṁ pāṭhyam.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the word yena (a form of yad) in the second sentence shines independently of tad. However, a yad in the first clause requires a correlative tad in the next. For instance, if the halves of this verse were switched, yena would be placed in a sentence prior to tad, therefore a form of tad would have to be used. Then the fourth line of this new verse should read: sn-krsna eva pranayat sa sevyah, “Only He, Sri Krsna, should be served with love.”**

### 10.57

*dvayor anupādāne ’pi dvayor arthaḥ kvacid avagamyate. yathāsmad-guravaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Even when yad and tad are not used, sometimes their sense is understood. This verse composed by my guru (Snnatha Pandita) is an example:**

*na vādi-nigrahaḥ sādhyo*  
*na śiṣyānugraho ’pi naḥ*  
*ubhayāyita-rūpasya*  
*manaso hy ubhayaṁ matam*

**Пословный перевод:**

na—has not; vadi—the disputant; nigrahah—defeating; sadhyah— been effected (brought about); na—has not; sisya—to a disciple; anugrahah—showing favor; api—even; nah—by us (me); ubhayayita—which acts like both (i.e. a disputant and a disciple); rupasya—which is the embodiment; manasah—for the mind; hi— only; ubhayam—both (i.e. defeating and showing favor); matam— intended.

**Перевод:**

**I will neither defeat a disputant nor show favor to a disciple, but I intend to do both to my mind, which has assumed both roles.**

*atra yo vādī bhavati tasya jigīṣā me nāsti, yaḥ śiṣyo bhavati tasminn apy anugraho nāsti, kintu mana eva ubhayāyitam. tena tasyaivobhayaṁ nigrahānugrahau iti vākya-dvaye pūrva-vākye yat-tador abhāve ’pi yat-tad-artha-pratyāyakatvam.*

**Перевод:**

**This verse contains two sentences, one in each half of the verse. Even though yad and tad are absent in the first sentence, their sense is perceived. The first sentence contains two clauses, one in each line. The implied understanding of yad and tad in the first line is: “Which (yah) disputant there is, I have no desire to defeat him (tasya) in debate.”**

**The implied understanding of yad and tad in the second line is: “Which (yah) disciple there is, no favor has been shown to him (tasmin) either.”**

**The sense of the second sentence is that the mind behaves like both as a disputant and as a disciple. The word ubhayam (both) signifies both defeating the disputant in the form of the mind and showing favor to the disciple in the form of the mind.**

### 10.58

*tathāsāv iti śabdaḥ sa ity asyārthaṁ nābhidhatte. yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**Now we will discuss how asau does not convey the sense of sah:**

*asau guṇānāṁ nikaṣo guṇānām*  
*utpatti-bhūmir bhavatī ca rādhe*  
*janas tṛtīyaḥ katham atra yogyo*  
*yena dvayor dautyam urī-kriyeta*

**Пословный перевод:**

asau—He (Krsna); gunanam—of qualities; nikasah—is a testing stone; gunanam—of good qualities; utpatti—of origin; bhumih—a place; bhavati—You; ca—and; radhe—O Radha; janah—\[this\] person; trtiyah—third; katham—how; atra—in this regard; yogyah—fit; yena—because of which; dvayoh—of You two; dautyam—the state of being a messenger; uri-kriyeta—may be accepted.

**Перевод:**

**Radha, He is the testing stone for qualities and You are the qualities’ place of origin. I, however, am a third person (without any quality). How can I become qualified to accept the role of Your Lordships’ messenger?**

*atra sa ity arthe nāsau-śabdaḥ, api tu prakrānta evārthe. yadyapi “yas te priyo ’sau na jahāti pārśvam” iti yac-chabdānantaraṁ vyavahito ’py asau-śabdas tac-chabda-pratītau samartha-vad bhāsate, tathāpi vinā tac-chabdāntaraṁ na vākyārtha-paripoṣaḥ, tac-chabdopādānenaiva sa syāt. yathā—“yas te priyo ’sau sa tavaiva pārśve” iti.*

**Перевод:**

**In this verse, asau does not have the correlative sense of sah, rather it is used in the sense of prakranta (introducing). Even though in a sentence such as: yas tepriyo ’sauna jahatiparsvam, “Your lover never leaves you,” the word asau seems to be able to convey the correlative sense of tad, since it is used after yah and is separated by some distance, still, without tad the sense of the sentence is not fully nourished, so a form of tad must be used, in this case sah. The corrected sentence is: yas te priyo ’sau sa tavaivaparsve, “He, Your lover, is at your side.”**

### 10.59

**Перевод:**

*rākendu-nindā-kara-vaktra-bimbo*  
*mayāyam āloki vanaṁ prayāntyā*

**Пословный перевод:**

yah—who; te—of yours; manah-ratna—the jewel in the form of the heart; harah—who steals; su-netre—O girl with beautiful eyes; navina—new; nila-ambuda—dark rainclouds; vrnda—than many; kantah—who is \[more\] beautiful; raka—on a full moon day; indu— the moon; ninda-kara—belittles; vaktra-bimbah—the orb of whose face; maya—by me; ayam—He; aloki—was seen; vanam—to the forest; prayantya—who was going.

**Перевод:**

**Girl with charming eyes, while I was going to the forest I saw that thief who steals the jewel of your heart, who is more beautiful than newly formed rainclouds, and whose face belittles the full moon.**

*kvacid idaṁ-śabda-vad adaḥ-śabdo ’pi tac-chabdārtham abhidhatta iti yat tat tu naika-vākya-stham uttara-vākya-stham eva tathā, na tu yo ’yaṁ yo ’sāv iti yac-chabda-nikaṭatve tathā sati prasiddhārtha-bodhakam eva, yathā yac-chabda-nikaṭa-sthas tacchabdaḥ prasiddhārtham evābhidhatte.*

**Перевод:**

**Just like the usage of the word idam here (i.e. ayam, He), the pronoun adas (that) sometimes conveys the sense of tad if yad is in the first sentence and adas is in the next.**

**However, adas cannot be used with yad like idam is in constructions like yo ’yam. When adas is close to yad in such type of construction, as in yo ’sau for instance, adas merely denotes the sense of prasiddha (well-known), in the same way that tad denotes the sense of prasiddha when it is juxtaposed to yad (as in yat tat).**

*tad yathā,*

*prema kṣema-karaṁ mahat*  
*tat kiṁ varṇayituṁ śakyaṁ*  
*girā devyāpi karhicit*

**Пословный перевод:**

radha-madhavayoh—of Radha and Madhava; yat—which; tat— well-known; prema—love; ksema-karam—which gives security (happiness); mahat—great; tat—that \[love\]; kim—is?; varnayitum— to be described; sakyam—capable; gira—by Sarasvati (speech personified); devya—the goddess; api—even; karhicit—at any time.

**The well-known love of Radha and Madhava conveys a sense of well-being. Can that great love possibly be described, even by SarasvatT?**

*atra tat kim iti punas tac-chabdenaiva nirākāṅkṣam. evaṁ prāg-upāttasya yac-chabdasya vīpsāyām uttara-vākya-stha-tacchabdasyāpi vīpsā kartavyaiveti na niyamaḥ, tad-akaraṇe ’pi doṣābhāvāt. yato vīpsā-pratipādyaṁ yat kiñcic chabdārtha-rūpaṁ tad evottara-vākya-sthaika-tac-chabdenaiva samarthyate, uttaravākya-sthiti-sāmarthyād eva.*

**Here the sense of yad is complete by its connection with the second tad, which occurs in the third line. Therefore the tad in the first line only has the sense of prasiddha.**

**Moreover, there is no rule that there should be the same number of tad words expressing vlpsa (pervasion) as there are yad words expressing vipsa in a previous clause, because there is no fault if the word tad in the correlative clause does not express vipsa (i.e. if tad itself is not immediately repeated). In other words, only one tad in the correlative clause can express the meaning of any number of yad words denoting the sense of vipsa in the first clause, simply on the strength of being in the correlative clause. For example:**

### 10.61

*yathā,*  
*guṇā api kvāpi bhavanti doṣā*  
*doṣā api kvāpi guṇā bhavanti*  
*yo yo guṇas te sa sa tādṛg eva*  
*doṣas tu yo yo na ca tasya leśaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

gunah—qualities; api—even; kva api—sometimes; bhavanti— become; dosah—faults; dosah—faults; api—even; kva api—in some places; gunah—qualities; bhavanti—become; yah yah— whatever; gunah—qualities; te—of yours; sah sah—all those; tadrk—like that; eva—only; dosah—faults; tu—and; yah yah— whatever; na—is not; ca—and; tasya—of those various \[faults\]; lesah—slight trace.

**Перевод:**

**Qualites may sometimes be faults and faults may sometimes be qualities, but whatever qualities you have are indeed only qualities. There is no trace of a fault in you.**

*atra tṛtīya-caraṇe dvayor api vīpsā, caturtha-caraṇe yacchabdasyaiva. uktodāharaṇa-dvaye prāmāṇyam. “yaṁ yaṁ vyatīyāya patiṁvarā sā, vivarṇa-bhāvaṁ sa sa bhūmi-pālaḥ” iti kālidāsaḥ. “yad yat pāpaṁ pratijahi jagan-nātha namrasya tan me” ity-ādi bhavabhūtiḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**In the third line here, both yah and sah are reduplicated, but in the fourth line only yah is reduplicated (but not tasya, which denotes the sense of vipsa regardless, although tasya tasya might be expected). Authoritative evidence of those two possibilities (the optional reduplication of tad) is now shown. The poet Kalidasa wrote: yam yam vyatiyaya patimvara sa, vivarna-bhavam sa sa bhumi-palah, “Each king that the lady who was free to choose her husband passed by became pale” (Raghu-vamsa 6.69).**

**On the other hand, the poet Bhavabhuti stated: yad yat papam pratijahi jagan-natha namrasya tan me, “O Lord of the universe, kindly destroy whatever sinful reaction I might have, for I am Your devotee” (Malati-madhava).**

**Instead of using the suffix \[k\]ta and saying vijitah (was defeated), the krtya suffix ya\[t\] was used here to make the word vijeyah (being defeated). However, this word is not clearly expressive of the past tense. This is an instance of the fault called avacaka (not expressive) in a part of a word (a suffix). The first line should be changed to: jito ’pi smara-sangrame, “although defeated in the battle of Cupid.”**

### 10.69

*hariṇā hariṇā iva*

**Hundreds of evil beings who distress the gods were killed by Hari, like deer slaughtered by a lion.**

**Here, vistha in divisthanam creates inauspiciousness because it sounds like the word vistha, which means \[...\]. This is an instance of amangala-dayi aslila (inauspiciously unpleasant) in a part of a word. Therefore divi-sthanam (of those who reside in heaven) should be replaced by devatanam (of gods).**

**Similarly, other words such as puyate (purified) and abhipreta (intended) are also instances of amangala-dayi aslila occurring in a part of a word: puyate contains the sound puya (pus), and abhipreta contains the sound preta (ghost, dead).**

*sa dakṣiṇo jagat-prāṇaḥ*  
*praṇayī samapadyata*

mrga-akslnam—of the doe-eyed girls; kama-rane—in the battle of Cupid; niscestanam—who were motionless; vapuh—the body; sprsan—touching; sah—that \[well-known\]; daksinah— coming from the south; jagat-pranah—wind; pranayi—a lover; samapadyata—became.

**Here, the word kama-rane (in the battle of love) contains the sound marane (in death). This is an instance of amangala-dayi aslila in a part of a word. ### 10.71

**Перевод:**

**\[This is neyartha (the meaning can only be guessed) in a part of a word:\]**

*nīlāśma-hāro hariṇī-*  
*dṛśāṁ vatsa-ruhopari*  
*saroja-koraka-gato*  
*bhṛṅga-saṁgha ivābabhau*

**Пословный перевод:**

nila-asma—of blue gems; harah—the necklace; harim-drsam—of the doe-eyed girls; vatsa-ruha—the breasts (“which grow on the chest”); upari—above; saroja-koraka—lotus buds; gatah—which have attained; bhrnga—of bees; samghah—a multitude; iva—like; ababhau—shone (appeared beautiful).

**Перевод:**

**Like bees on lotus buds, the sapphire necklace was resplendent on the doe-eyed girls’ breasts.**

*atra vatsa-śabdena vakṣo lakṣyate, tac ca neyārthaṁ padāṁśagatam eva. tena “vakṣo-ruhopari” iti vācyam. yadyapi pūrvapada-parivṛtti-saham uttara-pada-parivṛtti-saham ubhayapada-parivṛtti-sahaṁ ceti prāg evoktam, tathāpi teṣāṁ yathāprasiddhi-parivṛttiḥ kāryā, sā tu mahā-kavi-prayogataḥ sahṛdaya-hṛdayādūṣaṇāc ca samucitā bhavati, na hi sarvāṇy eka-paryāyoktāni parivṛtti-kṣamāṇi. yadyapy ayam aprayukta eva doṣas tathāpi pūrvair neyārthatayāyaṁ bhedo likhita iti likhitam.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the word vatsa is supposed to mean vaksa (chest). This an instance of neyartha (the meaning can only be guessed) in a part of a word. Therefore vatsa-ruhopari should be changed to vaksa-ruhopari.**

**Moreover, in the second chapter it was said that yaugika words (words that have a derived meaning) are of three varieties: (1) Those where the first word can be changed, (2) Those where the second word cannot be changed, and (3) Those where both words can be changed (2.13). Still the change should be made according to what is well-known, and is considered proper if it conforms to the great poets’ usage and if it does not disturb the connoisseurs’ hearts. Still, not all the words which are said to have only one synonym can be changed.**

**Although this fault (vatsa meaning chest) is technically an example of aprayukta (a meaning that is not in use), the previous teachers listed it in the category of neyartha (the meaning can only be guessed).**

**There are twenty-one additional faults in a sentence:**

**(1) pratilomaksara (adverse consonant), (2) ahata-visarga (the change of a visarga to the letter o), (3) nasta-visarga (deleted visarga), (4) samhita-hma (devoid of sandhi or degradation because of the sandhi), (5) hata-vrtta (defect in the meter), (6) hma-pada (missing word), (7) adhika-pada (redundant word), (8) kathita-pada (repeated word), (9) praskhalat-prakarsa (declining eminence), (10) samapta-punar-atta (continuing with a participle when the sentence is already complete), (11) nasyan-mata- yoga (the presumed syntactical connection is non-existent), (12) sankirna (mixed), (13) ardhantara eka-vacaka (one word placed in the wrong half of the verse), (14) anabhihita-vacya (omission of what must be said), (15) prasiddhi-dhuta (disregard of usage), (16) apada-stha-pada (a wrongly placed word), (17) apada-stha- samasa (a compound out of place), (18) garbhita (a parenthesis), (19) bhagna-krama (breaking the parallelism), (20) akrama (bad word order), and (21) amata-parartha (the adverse sense of another rasa).**

### 10.73

*pratilomākṣaram ukta-rasānuguṇa-varṇa-pratikūla-varṇatvaṁ*  
*yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**When phonemes are adverse to those expressive of the contextual rasa, that is the fault called pratilomaksara. For example:**

*puṣpa-kodaṇḍa-kaṇḍūla-*  
*prakāṇḍa-bhuja-maṇḍalam*  
*kambu-kaṇṭhi samutkaṇṭhaṁ*  
*kaṇṭhe ’kuṇṭhā hariṁ kuru*

**Пословный перевод:**

puspa-kodanda—for Cupid (“who has a flower bow”); kandula—are itching; prakanda—branch-like (or excellent); bhuja-mandalam— whose arms; kambu-kanthi—O girl with a conchshell-like neck; samutkantham—who is longing; kanthe—on the neck; akuntha— being unrestricted; harim—Hari; kuru—make (i.e. put).

**Girl with a conchshell-like neck, Hari longs for love. His superb arms are itching for a battle of Cupid. Be unreserved and go embrace Him.**

*atrādy-antyayor luptā visargāḥ.*
