### 10.76

*saṁhitā sandhis tayā hīnaṁ visandhir ity arthaḥ. vivakṣitaś ca sa sandhir bhavatīti vākya-balāt kṛto visandhiḥ, sa sakṛd api doṣāvahaḥ, pragṛhyādi-hetukaś ced asakṛd eva. saṁhitāyāṁ hīnam ity arthe saṁhitāyāṁ duḥśravyam aślīlaṁ ceti tri-vidho ’yaṁ doṣaḥ. krameṇodāharaṇāni.*

**Перевод:**

**Samhita means sandhi (phonetic combination), thus samhita- hina means “devoid of sandhi” or in other words visandhi (improper sandhi or non-sandhi). Visandhi is done on the strength of the statement: “Sandhi depends on the wish of the speaker.” (The writer can do sandhi even without the usual requirements or not do sandhi at all because of the meter.) Such improper sandhi or non-sandhi, even when done only once, constitutes a fault (in written language). However, if the non­sandhi occurs on the basis of something like thepragrhya sutra, then it is not faulty, unless it is repeatedly done.**

**Alternatively, the compound samhita-hma can be analyzed as: samhitayam hmam, “degradation when there is sandhi,” which could mean either that the sandhi is difficult to hear or is unpleasant. Thus the fault called samhita-hma has three varieties: (1) visandhi (improper sandhi or non-sandhi), (2) duhsravya (difficult to hear), and (3) aslila (unpleasant). Examples are shown in order.**

### 10.77

**Перевод:**

**\[This verse illustrates the visandhi variety:\]**

*tavaitad vadanaṁ indu-*  
*nindakam paṅkajekṣaṇe*  
*sa kalaṅkī niṣkalaṅke*  
*katham asmin na lajjatām*

**Пословный перевод:**

tava—of yours; etat—this; vadanam—face; indu—the moon; nindakam—which belittles; pankaja-iksane—O girl with lotus eyes; sah—that well-known; kalanki—moon (“which has marks”); niskalanke—when the face (“which has no mark”); katham—why; asmin—in regard to this; na lajjatam—should it not be embarrassed.

**Перевод:**

**Lotus-eyed girl, Your face belittles the moon. When you show your face, how can that spotted moon not become embarrassed?**

*atra “candra-nindakam” iti pāṭhyam.*

**Перевод:**

**Here indu-nindakam should be changed to candra-nindakam.**

**Комментарий:**

The anustubh meter, in which this verse was composed, requires the sixth syllable in every line to be guru (heavy). That is why the m in vadanam indu was changed to anusvara (m). But when the word indu follows, this sandhi change is unjustified and is thus improper. When the word candra follows, however, the sandhi change of m to m is justified by the usual sandhi rules and is thus proper. In this way Kavi Kamapura’s verse is an example of improper sandhi done to fit the meter.

Visvanatha Kaviraja gives an example of non-sandhi done to fit the meter: vasavasa-mukhe bhati indus candana-bindu-vat, “The moon shines on the face of Indra’s quarter (the east) like a dot of sandalwood-paste” (Sahitya-darpana 7.8). Here bhati and indus don’t join to become bhatindus because the extra syllable is needed to fill out the meter. Visvanatha also gives an example where the repeated non- sandhi of the pragrhyas becomes a fault: dalite utpale ete aksini amalangi te, “O you of spotless form, these eyes of yours are expanded blue lotuses” (Sahitya-darpana 7.8).

### 10.78

**Перевод:**

**\[This verse illustrates duhsravya samhita-hma (degradation because the sandhi is difficult to hear):\]**

*kalaṅkinaś candramasaḥ*  
*su-bhrv ānanam idaṁ tava*  
*ruciṁ bibhrad api prāyo*  
*niṣkalaṅkam itīryate*

**Пословный перевод:**

kalankinah—which has marks; candramasah—of the moon; su- bhru—O girl with beautiful eyebrows; ananam—face; idam—this; tava—of Yours; rucim—the effulgence; bibhrat—having; api— even though; prayah—generally; niskalankam—without any mark; iti—therefore; Iryate—is said.

**Перевод:**

**Girl with charming eyebrows, even though Your face has the effulgence of the spotted moon it is generally said to be spotless.**

*atra su-bhrvā iti duḥśravyam. tena “rādhe mukham” iti pāṭhyam.*

**Перевод:**

**The sound su-bhrva in su-bhrv ananam is difficult to hear. Instead, the second line should read: su-bhru radhe mukham tava.**

### 10.79

**Перевод:**

**\[This is aslila samhita-hma (degradation because the sandhi is unpleasant):\]**

*alaṁ ḍamaru-ḍāmbaryaṁ*  
*tava madhye virājini*  
*sa harasya kara-grāhyaḥ*  
*kara-grāhyam idaṁ hareḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

alam—in vain; damaru—the damaru drum; dambaryam— the loud noise; tava—when your; madhye—waist; virajini—is resplendent; sah—that \[damaru drum\]; harasya—by Siva (“the destroyer”); kara—with the hand; grahyah—is held; kara—with the hand; grahyam—is held; idam—this \[waist\]; hareh—by Hari.

**Перевод:**

**In the presence of your waist the damaru’s loud boasts of “I have the thinnest midsection” are in vain. The damaru is held by Hara, but your waist is held by Hari.**

*atra laṇḍa-śabdo ’ślīlaḥ. tena “vṛthā ḍamaru-ḍāmbaryam” iti pāṭhyam.*

**Перевод:**

**The words alam damaru contain the sound landa (...). This is an instance of unpleasant sandhi. The first line should read: vrtha damaru-dambaryam (“the damaru’s loud boasts are in vain”).**

**Комментарий:**

Here lam da is optionally taken as landa, by the rule that an anusvara can become the nasal corresponding to the next consonant.

### 10.80

*hata-vṛttaṁ chando-gata-vairūpyaṁ gurau laghutvam. yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**The fault called hata-vrtta (defect in the meter) signifies a dis­tortion of the meter. This occurs when a short syllable is used instead of a long one. For instance:**

*śaśi-mukhi sakhi rādhike ’dhikāsi*  
*guṇa-vibhavena samasta-sundarībhyaḥ*  
*tvayi nihata-manā manāg api śrī-*  
*vraja-pati-sūnur upaiti nānya-pārśvam*

**Пословный перевод:**

sasi-mukhi—O girl with a moonlike face; sakhi—O friend; radhike—O Radhika; adhika—are superior; asi—You; guna— of qualities; vibhavena—on account of the greatness; samasta- sundaribhyah—than all beautiful girls; tvayi—to You; nihata—is attached (i.e. devoted); manah—whose mind; manak—a little; api—even; sri—divine; vraja-pati—of the king of Vraja; pati- sunuh—the son; upaiti na—does not attain; anya—of another; parsvam—the side.

**Перевод:**

**Sakhi Radhika, You are superior to all beautiful girls owing to the greatness of Your qualities. O moon-faced girl, the divine prince of Vraja is so devoted to You that He does not go near any other girl, not even for a minute.**

*atra pādānte laghur gurur veti vākya-balāt kṛto laghu-varṇavinyāso hata-vṛttatāṁ vyanakti. tat tu dvitīya-pādānte śobhate, na tu caturtha-pādānte, bandha-śaithilyāt. prathama-tṛtīya-pādānte tu naiva.*

**Перевод:**

**In this verse, the usage of a short syllable \[at the end of the first and fourth lines\] on the strength of the rule “A short syllable at the end of a line can optionally be considered long” leads to a distortion of the meter, since that rule is true only for the second line, not for the fourth line, because using a short syllable at the end of the fourth line would be sloppy composition. The rule never applies to the first and third lines.**

**Комментарий:**

The meter of this verse is puspitagra. According to Visvanatha Kaviraja, the rule that a short syllable at the end of a line can optionally be considered long applies to any aksara-vrtta meter (qualitative meter), except for the first and third lines of a half-even meter like puspitagra.

### 10.81

*evam āryāsu ca gaṇa-kṛtā viruddhatā. yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**Similarly, a fault occurs in an arya meter if the ganas are direct opposites. For example:**

*gokula-lalanā-maṇḍala-*  
*rati-raṇa-pāṇḍitya-mugdha-madhura-śrīḥ śrī-*  
*vraja-rāja-kumāro*  
*rāsa-vilāse kumārayati*

**Пословный перевод:**

gokula—of Gokula; lalana—of ladies; mandala—with the multitude; rati—of love; rana—in the battle; panditya—on account of expertise; mugdha—charming; madhura—and sweet; srih—whose beauty; sri-vraja—of divine Vraja; raja-kumarah— the prince; rasa—of the rasa dance; vilase—in the pastimes; kumarayati—plays.

**Перевод:**

**The divine prince of Vraja plays in the Rasa pastimes. His beauty is sweet and charming because of His expertise in the battle of love with the young ladies of Gokula.**

*atra dvitīya-tṛtīya-gaṇau sa-kāra-bha-kārau viruddhau. tena “vraja-lalanā-maṇi-mālā-rati” ity-ādi pāṭhyam.*

**Перевод:**

**At the beginning of this verse, the ganas called sa and bha are the second and third ganas used. These two ganas are opposites: That is the fault. Consequently the verse should begin: vraja- lalana-mani-mala-rati-rana-panditya.**

**Комментарий:**

The arya meter belongs to the category of matra-vrtta (quantitative meter). Moreover, prosody in general is based on a system of eight ganas (groups), each consisting of three measures. The ganas are distinguished from one another by the different orders of short and long syllables within the three syllable unit. The gana called sa is two short syllables followed by a long one. This corresponds to the second gana used in this verse (the word lalana). The gana called bha is exactly the opposite: it consists of one long syllable followed by two short ones. This corresponds to the third gana used in the verse (the word mandala). The gana bha is also the first gana used in the verse (the word gokula).

### 10.82

*evaṁ rasānanuguṇaṁ vṛttaṁ ca hata-vṛttam, pajjhaṭikādi śṛṅgārakaruṇādau viruddham, hāsya-śāntādau na. śṛṅgāre yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**A meter that is not conducive to the contextual rasa is also an instance of the fault called hata-vrtta (defect in the meter). For instance, the matra-vrtta meter called pajjhatika (small bell) is adverse to madhura-rasa, karuna-rasa, and so on, but it evokes hasya-rasa, santa-rasa, and so on.**

**The following verse is faulty in the sense that the context is madhura-rasa and the meter is pajjhatika.**

*he sakhi mā kuru mānam akharvaṁ*  
*mānaḥ saukhyaṁ grasati hi sarvam*  
*kuru sānandaṁ hṛdayam amandaṁ*  
*rasa-bhara-kandaṁ bhaja govindam*

**Пословный перевод:**

he sakhi—O confidante; ma kuru—don’t perform; manam—pique; akharvam—very deep; manah—pique; saukhyam—happiness; grasati—devours; hi—because; sarvam—all; kuru—make; sa- anandam—blissful; hrdayam—the heart; amandam—fervently; rasa—bliss; bhara—of much; kandam—who is the root cause; bhaja—worship; govindam—Govinda.

**Перевод:**

**Sakhi, don’t let your mana become lofty because it will devour your happiness. Make your heart joyful by fervently worshiping Govinda, the root cause of bliss.**

### 10.83

*hīnaṁ padaṁ yathā—kamala-mukhi vicitrasyāvadhiḥ ko ’pi dṛṣṭas taraṇi-duhitṛ-tīropāntam adya prayāntyā. atra mayeti hīnapadam. tena “taraṇi-duhitṛ-tīraṁ hanta yāntyā mayādya” iti pāṭhyam. adhika-padaṁ yathā—nava-jaladhara-dhāmā śyāmalo ’yaṁ kiśoraḥ. ity atra nava-dhara-dhāmā ity anenaiva siddhiḥ śyāmala ity adhikam. tena “nava-kuvalaya-dāmā śyāmalo ’yam” iti pāṭhyam. kathita-padaṁ yathā—kalayati jala-keliṁ mattamātaṅga-keliḥ. atra keli kelir iti kathita-padam. tena “mattamātaṅga-līlaḥ” iti śuddham.*

**Перевод:**

**An example of the fault called hina-pada (missing word) is as follows: kamala-mukhi vicitrasyavadhih ko ’pi drstas, tarani- duhitr-tiropantam adya prayantya, “Lotus-faced girl, today while going to the bank of the Yamuna a certain person, who was most wonderful, was seen.” Here, the word maya (by me) is missing. This is the fault called hina-pada. The second line should be replaced with: tarani-duhitr-tiram hanta yantya mayadya.**

### 10.84

**Перевод:**

**This illustrates the fault called adhika-pada (redundant word): nava-jaladhara-dhama syamalo ’yam kisorah, “This dark blue youth, who has the effulgence of a new raincloud...” Here the fault is that the sense of syamala (dark blue) is already expressed by the compound nava-jaladhara-dhama (He has the effulgence of a new raincloud). The sentence should be changed to: nava- kuvalaya-dama syamalo ’yam kisorah, “This dark blue youth, who has a garland of fresh blue lotuses...”**

### 10.85

**Перевод:**

**This illustrates the fault called kathita-pada (repetition of a word): kalayati jala-kelim matta-matanga-kelih, “He whose pastimes are like those of a mad elephant performs water pastimes.” Here the word keli is repeated: That is the fault. Consequently, matta-matanga-kelih should be replaced with a synonym: matta-matanga-lilah.**

### 10.86

*praskhalat-prakarṣaṁ pūrvārdhe utkarṣa uttarārdhe ’pakarṣaś cet tadā praskhalat-prakarṣa-vākyam, patat-prakarṣam ity arthaḥ. yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**When there is eminence in the first half of a verse but no eminence in the second half, that is the fault called praskhalat- prakarsa in a sentence. Praskhalat-prakarsa means patat- prakarsa (declining eminence). For example:**

*hari hari hariṇākṣī-lakṣa-vakṣoja-hāra-*  
*truṭana-paṭima-śāṭī-pāṭana-prauḍha-darpaḥ*  
*ayam adayam udāro ’līka-ghaṭṭādhipatyaṁ*  
*kalayati pathi gavye dāna-līlāṁ dadhānaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

hari hari—alas, alas; harina-aksi—of doe-eyed girls; laksa—of hundreds of thousands; vaksah-ja—on the breasts; hara—the necklaces; trutana—in breaking; patima—on account of the dexterity; sati—the blouses; patana—on account of tearing up; praudha—heightened; darpah—whose pride; ayam—this well-known (Sri Krsna); adayam—mercilessly; udarah—who is lofty; alika—false; ghatta—at a toll station; adhipatyam—the role of an official; kalayati—plays; pathi—on the path; gavye—which is in relation to dairy products; dana-Ulam—the toll pastime; dadhanah—who is performing.

**Перевод:**

**Alas, alas, this arrogant boy, who dexterously breaks open the necklaces and blouses of thousands of doe-eyed girls, is mercilessly playing the role of a lofty proud official at a mock toll station on the path used for carrying dairy products, while performing the toll pastime.**

*atra pūrvārdhād uttarārdhe patann eva prakarṣaḥ. atra samāptapunar-āttatvaṁ ca “kalayati pathi gavye” ity anenaivākāṅkṣāsamāpter “dāna-līlāṁ dadhānaḥ” iti punar upāttam.*  
*tenottarārdhaṁ pūrvārdhī-kṛtya pāṭhyaṁ tathā sati doṣa-dvayahāniḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the eminence in the second half of the verse declined compared to the excellence shown in the first half. This is the fault called patat-prakarsa (declining eminence).**

**There is another fault in this verse, called samapta-punar- atta (continuing with a participle when the sentence is already complete). The participle clause dana-lilam dadhanah (performing the toll pastime) is a superfluous continuation, since the expected information was completed with the clause kalayati pathi gavye (He amused Himself on the path used for carrying dairy products).**

**These two faults, patat-prakarsa and samapta-punar-atta, are removed by switching the halves of the verse.**

### 10.87

*naśyan-mata-yogo ’sammato yogo yatra, abhavan-mata-yoga ity arthaḥ. yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**The fault called nasyan-mata-yoga (the presumed syntactical connection is non-existent) occurs when the syntactical connection between the words is unauthorized. It corresponds to abhavan-mata-yoga \[in Kavya-prakasa\]. For instance:**

*yasyājñā vidhi-mauli-mālya-madhupī yaṁ sevate śaṅkaro*  
*yasmin sarvam idaṁ carācara-gurau kṛṣṇe tri-lokī yataḥ*  
*yenākāri samasta-dānava-vadhū-vaidhavyam urvī-bharaṁ*  
*yo jahre balim arpayanti vibudhā yasmai sa pāyāj jagat*

**Пословный перевод:**

yasya—whose; ajna—order; vidhi—of Brahma; mauli—on the crowns; malya—on the garlands; madhupi—is a bee; yam—whom; sevate—serves; sankarah— Siva; yasmin—in whom; sarvam idam—this world \[abides\]; cara-acara—ofmoving and non-moving living entities; gurau—who is the spiritual master; krsne—in Krsna (i.e. in whom); tri-loki—the three worlds \[manifested\]; yatah— from whom; yena—by whom; akari—was caused; samasta—all; danava—of the demons; vadhU—of the wives; vaidhavyam— widowhood; urvi—of the earth; bharam—the burden; yah—who; jahre—took away; balim—tribute; arpayanti—offer; vibudhah— the demigods; yasmai—unto whom; sah—He; payat—may he protect; jagat—the world.

**Перевод:**

**May Krsna protect the world, which manifested from Him and abides in Him. He is the spiritual master of all living entities. He dispelled the earth’s burden by turning all the demons’ wives into widows. The gods offer Him tribute, Siva serves Him, and Brahma carries His orders on his own heads. It’s as if these orders take the shape of bees hovering over the garlands on Brahma’s crowns.**

*atra “kṛṣṇe” iti padaṁ viśeṣyaṁ prathamāntaṁ yadi syāt tadā bhavan-mata-yogo bhavati, yac-chabdair nirdiṣṭasya tacchabdārthasya kṛṣṇa-padasya yac-chabdārthe eva praveśe ’bhavan-mata-yogaḥ. tena—yasyājñā vidhi-mauli-mālya-madhupī yaṁ sevate śaṅkaro, yenākāri samasta-dānava-vadhū-vaidhavyam urvī-bharam, yo jahre balim arpayanti vibudhā yasmai tri-lokī yato, yasmin sarvam idaṁ carācaram asau kṛṣṇaḥ sa pāyāj jagad iti śuddham.*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna is the substantive here, so if the word krsne, in the second line, were in the first case singular \[so that it would match sah in the fourth line\], then the presumed syntactical connection between the words would be factual.**

**In this verse however, the word krsna, which should have been connected with the word tad (sah) but is expressed by correlative forms of the word yad, has instead been connected with the word yad (yasmin). This is the fault called abhavan- mata-yoga (the presumed syntactical connection is non­existent). Therefore the verse should be rewritten in this way (the meaning is the same):**

*yasyājñā vidhi-mauli-mālya-madhupī yaṁ sevate śaṅkaro*  
*yenākāri samasta-dānava-vadhū-vaidhavyam urvī-bharam*  
*yo jahre balim arpayanti vibudhā yasmai tri-lokī yato*  
*yasmin sarvam idaṁ carācaram asau kṛṣṇaḥ sa pāyāj jagat*

### 10.88

*tathāpi vibhakty-akrama-doṣaḥ. tena,*

**Перевод:**

**Nevertheless, there is a discrepancy in the revised version of the verse: The sequence of case endings of the forms of yat is off. This is the fault called vibhakti akrama (lack of sequence of case endings). Hence the verse is rewritten again:**

*yo bhaktyaiva vaśī-bhavet paśu-patir yaṁ sevate yena bhūr*  
*nirbhārā balim arpayanti vibudhā yasmai tri-lokī yataḥ*  
*yasyājñā vidhi-mauli-mālya-madhupī yasmin samastaṁ jagat*  
*so ’yaṁ gopa-vadhū-vilāsa-rasikaḥ kṛṣṇo ’stu vaḥ śreyase*

**Пословный перевод:**

yah—who; bhaktya—by devotional service; eva—alone; vasi- bhavet—who may become controlled; pasu-patih—Siva; yam— whom; sevate—serves; yena—because of whom; bhuh—the earth; nirbhara—\[became\] one from whom a burden has gone; balim— tribute; arpayanti—offer; vibudhah—the demigods; yasmai—unto whom; tri-loki—the three worlds; yatah—from whom; yasya— whose; ajha—order; vidhi—of Brahma; mauli—on the crowns; malya—on the garlands; madhupi—is a bee; yasmin—in whom; samastam—the entire; jagat—world \[abides\]; sah—that; ayam— well-known; gopa-vadhu—with the wives of the cowherds; vilasa—of pastimes; rasikah—expert enjoyer; krsnah—Krsna; astu—may he be; vah—of you all; sreyase—for the highest benefit.

**Перевод:**

**May Krsna continue relishing pastimes with the gopis for the sake of your happiness. He becomes controlled by devotional service. Siva serves Him, the earth’s burden was dispelled by Him, the gods offer Him tribute, the worlds emanate from Him yet remain in Him, and His orders are like bees hovering over the garlands on Brahma’s crowns.**

*iti śuddham.*

**Перевод:**

**This is proper.**

**Комментарий:**

In this verse, the successive forms of yat are used: yah (who), yam (whom), yena (by whom), yasmai (unto whom), yatah (from whom), yasya (whose), and yasmin (in whom). The sequence of the forms of yat in the previous verse was not in order: yasya, yam, yena, yah, yasmai, and yasmin.

### 10.89

*yathā vā,*

**Перевод:**

**Another example of nasyan-mata-yoga (the presumed syntactical connection is non-existent):**

*muñcati tvayi dṛśoḥ padavīṁ me*  
*yena yena śṛṇu yad yad avāptam*  
*jīvanena kaṭutā maraṇena*  
*prārthyatā priyatayā parivādaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

muncati tvayi—when You left; drsoh—of the eyes; padavim—the path; me—My; yena yena—by which various \[conditions\]; srnu— please listen; yat yat—which various \[qualities\]; avaptam—were attained; jivanena—by life; katuta—causticity \[was attained\]; maranena—by death; prarthyata—desirability \[was attained\]; priyataya—by love; parivadah—condemnation \[was attained\].

**Перевод:**

**Hear about what happened when You left the path of My eyes. My life became caustic, My death became desirable, and My love became a farce.**

*atra śṛṇv iti kriyāyāḥ karmāpekṣitve jīvanādeḥ sarvasya karmatve dvitīyāntatvaṁ matam. vākyārtha- karmatve jīvanādeḥ prathamāntatvam eva, tad ubhayābhāve ’bhavan-mata-yoga iti kecit. vastutas tu vākyārtha-karmatve yena yena yad yad avāptaṁ tac chṛṇv ity anenaiva vākyārthaś caritārthaḥ. paścāt jīvanena kaṭutāvāptety-ādinā liṅga-vyatyayenānvayena nokta-doṣaḥ. avāptam ity atra avāpīti cet kriyate, tadā sutarāṁ na doṣaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**The words jivana, marana, and priyata are expected to take a second case ending, since the verb srnu (hear) requires an object, and they are the objects. On the other hand, if the sense of the sentence as a whole is taken to be the object of the verb, then the nouns in the second half of the verse should take a first case ending.**

**If neither option is taken, some scholars say it is an instance of abhavan-mata-yoga (the presumed connection of the words is non-existent).**

**In reality, however, the sense of the sentence is just fine if the sense of the sentence itself is taken as the object of the verb; the syntactical connection is, yena yena yadyad avaptam tac chrnu, “Hear about what was attained by what.” In that way the fault under discussion, abhavan-mata-yoga, technically does not occur even though the syntactical connection later involves a change of gender, as in jivanena katuta avapta (i.e. avaptam in the second line becomes feminine (avapta) when connected to katuta and to prarthyata, and masculine (avaptah) when connected to parivadah). Still, a better solution is to replace avaptam by avapi (was attained). In that case there is no fault at all.**

**Комментарий:**

Since avapi is a verb and not a participle, it has no gender, so there can be no mismatch of gender when avapi is carried forward instead of the participle avaptam. In the alternative with avapi, the main syntactical connection is: yenayenayadyad avapi tac chrnu, “Hear about what was attained by what.”

### 10.90

*yathā vā,*

**Перевод:**

**Another example of nasyan-mata-yoga:**

*svābhirūpya-kamalākara-jāte*  
*paṅkaje iva saha bhramarābhyām*  
*niḥsarottara-kṛpā-makarande*  
*mādhavasya nayaṇe rurucāte*

**Пословный перевод:**

sva-abhirupya—of His beauty; kamala-akara—in a lake (“the place of origin of lotuses”); jate—which are manifest; pankaje— two lotuses; iva—like; saha bhramarabhyam—with two bees; nihsara—is oozing; uttara-krpa—of eminent mercy; makarande—from which \[two lotuses\] the thick honey; madhavasya—of Madhava; nayane—the two eyes; rurucate—shone (appeared beautiful).

**Перевод:**

**Madhava’s eyes are resplendent. They resemble two lotuses in a lake of beauty with a bee on each one, and emanate the thick honey of His eminent mercy.**

*atra sva-śabdo mādhave vivakṣitaḥ. sa tu vākya-maryādayā kartṛgatatvena pratibhāsamāno nayana-bhramara-gata eva jātaḥ. tenābhirūpyety eva śuddham.*

**Перевод:**

**Here, the word sva in svabhirupya is expressed with the intention of referring to Madhava. However, according to the rules governing sentences, the reflexive pronoun sva should only be used to refer to the subject, in this case nayane (the two eyes). It is better to delete sva and only say abhirupya.**

### 10.91

*saṅkīrṇaṁ yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of sankirna (mixed):**

*mā kuru mānini kṛṣṇaṁ*  
*pada-gatam utthāpya viṣama-viṣa-tīkṣṇam*  
*āliṅga bhuvana-maṅgala-*  
*maṅgalam antar-malaṁ mānam*

**Пословный перевод:**

ma kuru—don’t perform; manini—O proud girl; krsnam—Krsna; pada-gatam—who has fallen at your feet; utthapya—after lifting up; visama—dangerous; visa—like poison; tiksnam—which is harsh; alinga—please embrace; bhuvana—on earth; mangala—of auspicious things; mangalam—who is the auspiciousness; antar— of the heart; malam—which is an impurity; manam—pique.

**Перевод:**

**Proud girl, don’t be in mana. It is an impropriety of the heart and is harsh like a deadly poison. Therefore lift up Krsna, who has fallen at your feet, and embrace Him. He is the cause of all auspicious things on earth.**

*atra vākya-dvayasya padāni vyatyayena vākya-dvayāntar-gatāni. eka-vākya-gata-padānām anyonya-saṅkulatvena tu kliṣṭam iti bhedaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**In this verse, the words belonging to the two sentences are mixed up: Some of the words syntactically connected with one sentence have been wrongly placed in the other sentence. The difference with the fault called klista is that in klista the words, which are also mixed up, belong to only one sentence (10.48).**

**Комментарий:**

The two syntactical connections are: (1) manini, antar-malam visama-visa-tiksnam manam ma kuru, and (2) bhuvana-mangala- mangalam pada-gatam krsnam utthapyalinga.

### 10.92

*ardhāntaraika-vācakaṁ yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of the fault called ardhantara eka-vacaka (one word placed in the wrong half of the verse):**

*kim induḥ kiṁ sarasi-jaṁ*  
*kim āsyaṁ lalitāṅgi kim*  
*khañjanau kiṁ smara-śarau*  
*rādhe kiṁ locane tava*

**Пословный перевод:**

kim—is it?; induh—the moon; kim—is it?; sarasi-jam—a lotus; kim—is it?; asyam—a face; lalita—is voluptuous; angi—O You whose body; kim—are these?; khanjanau—two khanjana birds; kim—are these?; smara—of Cupid; sarau—two arrows; radhe—O Radha; kim—are these?; locane—the two eyes; tava—of Yours.

**Перевод:**

**Radha, girl with a voluptuous body, is this the moon, is it a lotus, or is it Your face? Are these two khanjana birds? Are these two arrows of Cupid? Or are these Your eyes?**

*atrottarārdhasyaikaṁ kim iti vācakaṁ pūrvārdhānte*

**Перевод:**

**Here the word kim, at the end of the first half of the verse, belongs to the second half of the verse, where it should have been placed.**

**Комментарий:**

The word kim at the end of the first half is syntactically connected to khanjanau (two khanjana birds). There is no fault if two or more words that belong to the syntactical connection of one half are in the other half.

### 10.93

**Перевод:**

**\[Another instance of ardhantara eka-vacaka:\]**

*padānta-patitaṁ rādhe*  
*paśya kṛṣṇaṁ ruṣaṁ tyaja*  
*tan mama śrūyatāṁ vāṇī*  
*gāḍho mānaḥ paraṁ viṣam*

**Пословный перевод:**

pada—the feet; anta—near; patitam—who has fallen; radhe—O Radha; pasya—see; krsnam—Krsna; rusam—anger; tyaja— abandon; tat—therefore; mama—my; sruyatam—should be heard; van!—speech; gadhah—excessive; manah—pique; param—is the supreme; visam—poison.

**Перевод:**

**Radha, look, Krsna has fallen at Your feet. Listen to my words: Excessive mana is a severe poison, therefore stop Your anger.**

*atra tac-chabdaḥ pūrvārdha-vākya-sthaḥ, tat tasmād ruṣaṁ tyajety arthaḥ. sa tūttarārdhādi-stha iti tathā.*

**Перевод:**

**In this example, the word tat belongs to the sentence in the first half of the verse, yet it is placed in the second half. Here, tat means tasmat (therefore). The syntactical connection is: tasmad rusam tyaja, “Therefore stop Your anger.”**

### 10.94

*anabhihitaṁ vācyaṁ yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An instance of anabhihita-vacya (omission of what must be said):**

*kvāsau harir mama manoratha-dūravartī*  
*kvāhaṁ na me guṇa-lavo na kalāṇukaś ca*  
*kiṁ dūti dūnayasi māṁ tvam alīkayaiva*  
*vācā vicāraya kathaṁ sa vaśo mama syāt*

**Пословный перевод:**

kva—where; asau—is He?; harih—Hari; mama—of mine; manoratha—from the heart’s fanciful desire; dura—far; varti— remains; kva—where; aham—am I; na—is not; me—my; guna— of a quality; lavah—a fraction; na—is not; kala—of expertise; anukah—a minute particle; ca—nor; kim—why?; duti—O messenger; dunayasi—you cause pain; mam—me; tvam—you; alikaya—false; eva—only; vaca—by speech; vicaraya—please consider; katham—how; sah—he; vasah—controlled; mama—by me; syat—may become.

**Перевод:**

**Where is Hari? He remains far from my heart’s innermost desire. And where am I? I do not even have a trace of a quality nor a bit of expertise. O messenger, why do you torment me with false words? You should devise a means whereby I can bring Him under my control.**

*atra manorathasyāpi dūravartī guṇasyāpi lavaḥ kalāyā apy aṇuka ity avaśya-vācyam anabhihitam.*

**Перевод:**

**In this verse, there is an omission of what must be said in these three compounds: manoratha-duravarti, guna-lavah, and kalanukah. The sense of manoratha-duravarti should actually be expressed with the words manorathasyapi duravarti (He remains far even from my heart’s innermost desire).**

**Similarly, the sense of guna-lavah should be conveyed with the words gunasyapi lavah (even a trace of a quality), and the sense of kalanukah should be stated as kalaya apy anukah (even a bit of expertise). Since the word api, which has to directly stated, was omitted here, this is an example of the fault called anabhihita-vacya (omission of what must be said).**

**Комментарий:**

In the last two examples in the vrtti the placement of the word api in the middle is doubtful as Visvanatha Cakravarti inserts api in the above three compounds as follows: manorathasyapi duravarfi, mama gunasya lavo pii nasti, tatha mama kalaya anur api nasti. Similarly, in this context Visvanatha Kaviraja gives the example: vyatikrama-lavam kam me viksya vamaksi kupyasi, “Pretty-eyed girl, what trace of impropriety do you see in me due to which you become so angry?”, where he says vyatikrama-lavam api (even a trace of impropriety) should have been stated instead of vyatikrama-lavam (Sahitya-darpana 7.8).

Visvanatha Kaviraja provides another illustration of anabhihita- vacya: The omission of the verb asi (are): carananata-kantayas tanvi kopas tathapi te, “Slender girl, nonetheless you, whose lover has fallen at your feet, are angry” (Sahitya-darpana 7.8). He specifies that carananata-kantasi (you are one whose lover has fallen at the feet) should have been said instead of carananata- kantayah. This is because the latter is merely an adjective of the word te (you), whereas the replacement carananata-kantasi, with an implied yadyapi (although), forms the correlative of the tatha clause (nonetheless you are angry). The statement should have been: “Slender girl! Although your lover has fallen at your feet, nonetheless you are angry.”

### 10.95

*raṇitādi nūpurādiṣu vihagādiṣu kūjitādīni*  
*stanitādi ca jaladādau bhery-ādiṣu bhāṁ-kṛtādīni (10)*  
*maṇitādīni ca surate ravādi bhekādiṣu prasiddhir iyam*  
*asyā viparyaye syāt prasiddhi-dhūta-dūṣaṇaṁ vākye (11)*

**Пословный перевод:**

ranita-adi—the word ranita (sound) and so on; nupura-adisu— in the context of anklets and so on; vihaga-adisu—in the context of birds; kujitadini—the word kUjita (cooing, warbling) and so on; stanita-adi—the word stanita (rumbling, thundering) and so on; jalada-adau—in regard to clouds and so on; bheri-adisu—in regard to kettledrums and so on; bhan-krtadini—the word bhan- krta (“made the sound bham”) and so on; manita-adini—the word manita (murmur of a woman during intercourse) and so on; ca— and; surate—in regard to lovemaking; rava-adi—the word rava (sound) and so on; bheka-adisu—in regard to frogs and so on; prasiddhih—is what is well-known; iyam—this; asyah—than this; viparyaye syat—if there is a modification; prasiddhi-dhuta—called prasiddhi-dhuta (“disregard of usage”); dusanam—it causes the fault; vakye—in a sentence.

**Перевод:**

**The following attribution of terms are the convention. Anything that differs from this constitutes the fault called prasiddhi-dhuta (disregard of usage), which occurs in the context of a sentence:**

**♦   ranita (sound) and similar words are to be used in the context of anklets and so on,**

**♦   kujita (cooing, warbling) and equivalent words refer to birds,**

**♦   stanita (rumbling, thundering) and similar words pertain to clouds,**

**♦   bham-krta (“made the sound bham”) and such terms are used to refer to kettledrums and so on,**

**♦   manita (murmur made during intercourse) and analogous words refer to lovemaking,**

**♦   rava (sound) and such words refer to frogs and to other living beings.**

*yathā,*

### 10.97

*apada-stham asthāna-sthaṁ padaṁ yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**The fault called apada-stha-pada signifies asthana-stha-pada (wrongly placed word). For instance:**

*vivāha-veṣeṇa tadā murārer*  
*babhūva yā śrīḥ kavayantu ke tām*  
*sapatna-bhāvād iva sābhyasūyā*  
*sarasvatī kvāpi na tāṁ vyanakti*

**Пословный перевод:**

vivaha-vesena—on account of the wedding attire; tada—then; murareh—of Murari; babhuva—occurred; ya—which; srlh— beauty; kavayantu—can describe; ke—who; tam—that \[beauty\]; sapatna—of enmity; bhavat—on account of a mood; iva—as if; sa-abhyasuya—envious; sarasvati—Sarasvati; kva api na—never; tam—that \[beauty\]; vyanakti—expresses.

**Перевод:**

**Murari looked resplendent in His wedding attire. Who can describe His charm at that time? Even SarasvatT never expresses that beauty, as if she were jealous on account of rivalry.**

*atra tāṁ na vyanaktīti sthāna-sthitatvaṁ, tad-abhāve tathā. tena “vāṇy eva tāṁ kvāpi ca na vyanakti” ity vācyam.*

**Перевод:**

**The proper order of the last words of this verse is: tam na vyanakti (she does not express that beauty). Due to the absence of this sequence, there is the fault of apada-stha-pada (wrongly placed word). Therefore, \[in consideration of the meter,\] the last line should be, vany eva tam kvapi ca na vyanakti, “SarasvatT never expresses that beauty.”**

**Комментарий:**

The replacement “vany eva tam kvapi ca na vyanakti” can also mean: “SarasvatT does not reveal it anywhere.” In addition, the word ca (and) is meaningless (vyartha).

### 10.98

*yadi sannikarṣa eva sthāne vaijātyaṁ tadaiva doṣaḥ na tu viprakarṣe. yathā—“vāṇī na kutrāpi ca tāṁ vyanakti” iti ca vācyam. yathā ca—na me vāṇī vṛndāvana-ramaṇa-līlāmṛta-hrade, nimagnāpy utthātuṁ prabhavati kathaṁ yātu parita ity-ādi. yat tu “srajaṁ na kācit” iti, tatra “na kācij jahau, api tu sarvaiva jahau” iti viruddhārtha-jananam.*

**Перевод:**

**The fault of apada-stha-pada (wrongly placed word ) only occurs if the words are positioned in the wrong order right beside each other, not if the words are positioned wrongly from afar. Consequently, it is also okay to say: vani na kutrapi ca tam vyanakti, “SarasvatT never expresses that beauty.”**

**\[This is another example of apada-stha-pada, because the words are wrongly positioned:\]**

*na me vāṇī vṛndāvana-ramaṇa-līlāmṛta-hrade*  
*nimagnāpy utthātuṁ prabhavati kathaṁ yātu paritaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**“Being immersed in the nectar lake of the pastimes of the lover residing in Vrndavana, my speech is not able to rise. How could it possibly go everywhere?”**

**However, what the poet Bharavi wrote is faulty: srajam na kacij jahau (Kiratarjuniya 8.37). This is because it produces an opposite sense, such that srajam na kacij jahau (no girl took off her garland) means: api tu sarvaiva srajam jahau (all the girls took off their garlands).**

**Комментарий:**

Bharavi’s full verse is quoted in Caitanya-caritamrta (Antya [10.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/10.21)):

*priyeṇa saṅgrathya vipakṣa-sannidhāv*  
*upāhitāṁ vakṣasi pīvara-stanī*  
*srajaṁ na kācid vijahau jalāvilāṁ*  
*vasanti hi premṇi guṇā na vastuni*

**“The lover strung a garland and placed it on the chest of his beloved in the presence of her rivals. She had raised breasts and was very beautiful, yet although the garland was withered by the water, she did not remove it, for its value lay not in material things but in love.”**

Here the intended meaning of the words srajam na kacid vijahau is: “the girl did not remove the garland,” but this meaning would have been better expressed by saying kacit srajam na vijahau, “the girl did not remove the garland.”

**In this verse, there is no long compound in the statement of the angry Lord, but there is a long compound in the statement of the other speaker (the poet), who is not angry. To avoid this discrepancy, the first half of the verse (which expresses the Lord’s statement) should be written with long compounds, so that the verse turns out as follows:**

*kiṁ lāṅgūla-vighaṭṭana-kṣata-ghana-vyūhaṁ khura-kṣodana-*

### 10.100

*garbhitaṁ prakṛta-vākye ’prakṛta-vākyasya garbha-sthitiḥ. yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**The fault called garbhita (parenthesis) occurs when an incidental sentence is located within the principal sentence (the principal subject matter). For instance:**

*jhañjhānilam iva lavalī*  
*praṇaya-latā na sahate dīrghām*  
*pratighāṁ priya-sakhi tattvaṁ*  
*vadāmi tava mātikopinī bhūyāḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

jhanjha-anilam—the wind of a hurricane; iva—like; lavali—the lavali creeper; pranaya—in the form of love; lata—the creeper; na sahate—does not tolerate; dirgham—prolonged; pratigham—anger (Amara-kosa 1.7.26); priya-sakhi—O dear confidante; tattvam— the truth; vadami—I speak; tava—to You; ma—not; ati-kopini— very angry; bhuyah—may You become.

**Перевод:**

**Just as a lavali creeper cannot withstand a hurricane, the creeper of love cannot tolerate prolonged anger, dear sakhi, I am telling You the truth, so please don’t be enraged.**

*atra “tattvaṁ vadāmi tava” iti vākyāntaraṁ garbhitam. ataḥ*  
*“pratighāṁ mānini rādhe tena tvaṁ mātikopinī bhūyāḥ” iti sādhuḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Here, the sentence “I am telling You the truth” is contained within another sentence. Therefore, \[to get rid of this paren­thesis\] the second half of the verse should be changed to pratigham manini radhe tena tvam matikopim bhuyah, “Sulky Radha, so please don’t be enraged.”**

### 10.101

*bhagna-kramo bhagna-prakrama ity arthaḥ. sa ca kāraka-vacana-*  
*paryāyādi-krama-bhagnāditvena bahudhā bhavati. yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**The fault called bhagna-krama signifies bhagna-prakrama (breaking the parallelism). It is of many kinds on account of the breaking the parallelism of the karaka (case ending, etc.), the vacana (number), the paryaya (synonym), and so on. This verse shows examples of the karaka and vacana varieties:**

*kācid vīṇāṁ murajam aparā kāpi vaṁśīṁ dadhānā*  
*kāścit tālaṁ kara-kiśalaye tāla-dhāritvam āptāḥ*  
*cakruḥ saṅgīta-kavi-racanāṁ rāsa-madhye kayācid*  
*gānaṁ nānā-svara-parimalāmodam uccair vitene*

**Пословный перевод:**

kacit—a certain girl; vinam—a lute; murajam—a drum; apara— another girl; kapi—a certain girl; vamsim—a flute; dadhana— holding (playing); kascit—some girls; talam—cymbals; kara— of the hands; kisalaye—in the bud; tala-dharitvam—the state of maintaining a beat; aptah—attained; cakruh—they did; sangita— musical; kavi—of a composer; racanam—the composition; rasa- madhye—in the rasa dance; kayacit—by a certain girl; ganam— singing; nana-svara—on account of the different notes; parimala— which was like that of sexual intercourse; amodam—because of which there was bliss; uccaih—loudly; vitene—was done.

**Перевод:**

**In the Rasa dance, one gopi played a lute, another a flute, and yet another a muraja drum. Others kept the beat by playing hand cymbals and thus played the part of the maestro. Because of the various notes, the singing by some gopi was eminent to the point that the bliss was reminiscent of lovemaking.**

*atra kayācid iti kāraka-krama-bhaṅgaḥ. kāścid iti vacana-kramabhaṅgaḥ. tena kāścid iti sthāne kācid ity eva pāṭhyam. āptā ity atra visargābhāvaś ca, cakrur ity atra cakra iti ca. kayācid ity atra “rāsam āsādya kācid, gānaṁ nānā-svara-parimalāmodam āviścakāra” iti pāṭhyam. paryāya-krama-bhaṅgo yathā—hareḥ kṛpā kāpi samujjihīte, mukunda-bhakteṣu na cāpareṣu. atra paryāya-krama-bhaṅgaḥ. tena “hari-priyeṣv eva na cāpareṣu” iti vācyam. idaṁ ye prācīnā devatādi-viṣaye rasaṁ na manyante, teṣāṁ matānurodhena likhitam. te tu satyaṁ vyāharanti, śrī-bhagavantam vinā anyeṣāṁ nāmāntarābhāvād bheda-pratītiḥ syād eva, tattan-nāmnā prasiddhasya śrī-bhagavatas tu nāmāntarākhyāne na paryāya-krama-bhaṅga-doṣaḥ—tasya nāmnām anantatvāt. atra tu sutarāṁ na doṣaḥ, hari-mukundayor bheda-pratīter abhāvāt. atra kathita-padāśaṅkāpi na kāryā.*

**Перевод:**

**The word kayacid (by some girl) at the end of the third line is an instance of karaka-krama-bhanga. The sentence should be changed to the active voice: “Having entered the Rasa dance, one gopi performed a song that was blissful like lovemaking on account of its different notes.”**

**The pronoun kascit (some girls), in the second line, is an instance of vacana-krama-bhanga (broken parallelism of the number). Kascit (some girls) should be replaced by kacit (some girl), aptah (they attained), at the end of the second line, should be changed to the singular, and cakruh (they did) should be changed to cakre (she did).**

**This is an example of paryaya-krama-bhanga (broken paral­lelism due to the usage of a synonym): hareh krpa kapi samujjihite mukunda-bhaktesu na caparesu, “A particular mercy of Hari arises toward Mukunda’s devotees, not toward anyone else.” The parallelism is broken due to the usage of a synonym. The sentence should read: hari-priyesv eva na caparesu, “A particular mercy of Hari arises toward Hari’s devotees and not toward anyone else.”**

**This example was written in accordance with the opinion of earlier poets who do not think that the sthayi-bhava can turn into rasa when the object is a devata. They speak the truth on this topic; usually a difference would be perceived because persons other than the Supreme Lord do not have other names. Still, the fault of broken parallelism due to the usage of a synonym does not occur when another name of the Supreme Lord is used, since He has unlimited well-known names.**

**However, in the aforesaid replacement: hari-priyesv eva na caparesu, there is obviously no fault at all because one cannot possibly make the mistake that Hari and Mukunda are different persons. There is no need to worry about a repeated word here: The repetition of the word Hari is not faulty.**

### 10.102

*yathā ca,*

**Перевод:**

**The reason that such a repetition is not faulty is:**

*viṣāde vismaye harṣe kope dainye ’vadhāraṇe*

*anukampādike cāpi paunaruktyaṁ na duṣyati (12)*

**Пословный перевод:**

visade—in the sense of despondency; vismaye—in the sense of amazement; harse—in the sense of joy; kope—in the sense of anger; dainye—in the sense of wretchedness; avadharane—in the sense of restriction; uddesya—of the substantive (the subject); pratinirdesya—the reiteration; visaye—in a situation that requires; ca—and; prasadane—in the sense of making clear; anukampa- adike—in the sense of compassion and so on; ca—and; api—also; paunaruktyam—repetition; na dusyati—is not faulty.

**Перевод:**

**The repetition of a word is not faulty if the sense is:**

**♦   visada (despondency),**

**♦   vismaya (amazement),**

**♦   harsa (joy),**

**♦   kopa (anger),**

**♦   dainya (wretchedness),**

**♦   avadharana (restriction),**

**♦   uddesya-pratinirdesya-visaya (a situation that requires the reiteration of the noun),**

**♦   prasadana (making clear),**

**♦   anukampa (compassion), and so on.**

*atra uddeśya-pratinirdeśya-viṣayataiva.*

**Перевод:**

**The previous corrected example “hareh krpa kapi samujjihtte hari-priyesv eva na caparesu” was a instance that required the reiteration of the noun (10.101).**

### 10.103

*yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**Another example of a situation that requires the reiteration of the noun:**

*na bhajati tapasā klamaḥ klamatvaṁ*  
*viṣaya-bhavaṁ na sukhaṁ sukhatvam eti*  
*viṣam api ca viṣasya nāśakaṁ syān*  
*na hi sadṛśe sadṛśatvam eva nityam*

**Пословный перевод:**

na bhajati—does not attain (does not share the nature of); tapasa— caused by austerity; klamah—fatigue; klamatvam—\[worldly\] fatigue; visaya—is worldy objects of the senses; bhavam—whose origin; na—does not; sukham—happiness; sukhatvam—the state of \[transcendental\] happiness; eti—attains; visam—poison; api—even; ca—and; visasya—of poison; nasakam—is a destroyer; syat—is; na—there is not; hi—because; sadrse—in regard to similar things; sadrsatvam—similarity; eva—only; nityam—always.

**Перевод:**

**Fatigue engendered due to practicing austerity is not like fatigue caused by worldly exertion. Material happiness cannot become transcendental happiness. Even poison can counteract poison. There isn’t always a similarity between similar things.**

*ity-ādau paunaruktyaṁ tac-chabdena nirdeśo vā guṇaḥ. ādiśabdād arthāntara-saṅkramite ’pi, yathā—phalam api phalaṁ mākandānām ity-ādi.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the repetitions are a quality. Indicating a word again by the use of the pronoun tat would be a quality too.**

**Due to the word adi (and so on) (10.102), the repetition of a word is not faulty if the sense is arthantara-sankramita (or any type of lata anuprasa). The verse beginningphalam apiphalam (3.5) is an example.**

**Комментарий:**

The example in Kavya-prakasa is also very illustrative: udeti savita tamras tamra evastam eti ca, “Red rises the sun, and red it sets.” Here if the same meaning of ‘red’ were to be expressed with another word (there are many synonyms of ‘red’ in Sanskrit), then that other word would seem to convey a different sense and would obstruct the quickness of the reader’s understanding of the sense of the sentence, especially because of the rest of the verse: sampattau ca vipattau ca mahatam eka-rupata, “In affluence and in adversity, the greats have the same uniform outlook” (KP verse 244).

### 10.104

*yatra tu ārambha eva kramo nāsti tatra bhagna-krama-doṣo nāsti. yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**But when there is no series in the beginning, naturally the fault of bhagna-krama (broken parallelism) does not occur. For example:**

*āliṅgan bāhudāyās tanum anuramayan narmadāṁ tuṅgabhadrāṁ*  
*cumban bhadrāṁ vikarṣan niravadhi-suraso devikāyā rasena*
