*kāverī-vāri-khelāṁ kalayati ramaṇī-maṇḍale kṛṣṇa-sindhuḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

alingan—embracing; bahudayas—of Bahuda (“she gives arms”); tanum—the body; anuramayan—continually delighting; narmadam—Narmada (“who provides jokes”); tungabhadram— Tungabhadra (“who is prominently beautiful”); cumban—kissing; bhadram—Bhadra; vikarsan—attracting; niravadhi—endlessly (i.e. always); su-rasah—rich in water (or Krsna, who is charming); devikayah—of Devika; rasena—because of the water (or because of the conjugal love); van-matyah—of Vanmati (“who possesses elegant speech”); keli—to sport; lubdhah—who is greedy; mukha—the mouth; nikata—near; milat—is meeting; candra- bhagah—the ocean (“with whom the Candrabhaga river”), (or Krsna, with whom Candrabhaga gopl is meeting near the face); ayam—this well-known; uccaih—intensely; kaveri—in the Kaveri (or with turmeric); vari—in water; khelam—pastimes; kalayati— performs; ramani-mandale—among the female lovers; krsna- sindhuh—Krsna in the form of the ocean.

**Перевод:**

**In the company of his lovers, the Krsna ocean embraces Bahuda’s body, delights Narmada, kisses Tungabhadra, attracts Bhadra, and is always charming on account of Devika’s love \[or the ocean is always full due to the waters of the Devika river\]. He longs to sport with VanmatT, He meets Candrabhaga face to face, and He intensely performs water pastimes with KaverT \[or Krsna plays water games in a yellowish lake\].**

*evam anyad apy ūhyam.*

**Перевод:**

**Other cases should be inferred in this way.**

**Комментарий:**

No order is established at the outset because the first river is in the sixth case (bahudayah) (of Bahuda) and the second one is in the second case (narmadam). Any gopl can have those names, except Kaveri, with regard to the play on words.

As for the pun on Kaven, according to tradition there is a pastime of Vraja-lila in which the water of a lake turned yellow. That place is called Pili-pokhara (the yellowish pond). It is located in Varsana, across from Brahma-parvata, near the road going to Uncagaon. Once, Radhika and Her sakhls went to Nandagrama to see Mother Yasoda. The queen of Vraja was so charmed by Radhika’s beauty that she decided to marry Her to Krsna. As a token of auspiciousness, she painted Radhika’s hands yellow. On the way back to Varsana, Radha became embarrassed and washed Her hands in that pond. It is also called Piyala-kunda because piyala trees surround it.

### 10.105

*na vidyate kramo yatra tad akramam. yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**The fault of akrama (bad word order) occurs when the proper order of words is not followed. For instance:**

*iha mayi sukhaṁ nidrām āpte kayā mama coritā*  
*maṇi-muralikā hāraḥ kaṇṭhāt sa cādhika-durlabhaḥ*  
*nigaditam iti śrutvā patyur vihasya vihasya sā*  
*nibhṛta-nibhṛtaṁ celāñcalyā mukhendum apāvṛṇot*

**Пословный перевод:**

iha—here (in the kunja); mayi—when I; sukham—happily; nidram—sleep; apte—attained; kaya—by whom; mama—My; corita—was stolen; mani—endowed with jewels; muralika—flute; harah—a necklace; kanthat—from the neck; sah—that well-known \[necklace\]; ca—and; adhika—exceedingly; durlabhah—difficult to attain (expensive); nigaditam—what was said; iti—thus; srutva— having heard; patyuh—by the husband; vihasya vihasya—laughing again and again; sa—she; nibhrta-nibhrtam—almost secretly; cela—of a garment; ancalya—with the border (the end); mukha- indum—the moon of her mouth; apavrnot—covered.

**Перевод:**

**“Who stole My gem-studded flute and the expensive necklace from My neck as I was happily sleeping in the kunja?” When a certain girl heard these words of the husband, she laughed continuously and secretly covered her moonlike mouth with the end of her sari.**

*atra “hāraś cāyaṁ maṇīndra kulojjvalaḥ” iti ca-kāra-sthitau kramas tad-anyathākramaḥ. evam “iti nigaditaṁ śrutvā” iti kramas tad-anyathākramaḥ. asthāna-stha-padād atrāyaṁ bhedaḥ. tat tu tathā-bhūtam apy anvaya-bodhaṁ jhaṭiti karoty eva, idaṁ tu na tathā.*

**Перевод:**

**In the second line, the words harah kanthat sa cadhika- durlabhah should be replaced with: haras cayam manmdra- kulojjvalah, “and My well-known necklace, which is splendid on account of many diamonds.” This way, the conjunction ca is properly placed, and the order is correct. Otherwise there is the fault of akrama (bad word order). Similarly, in the third line, nigaditam iti srutva should be replaced with: iti nigaditam srutva, “having heard this.” That is the proper order of the words. Otherwise there is the fault of akrama.**

**Since it involves a word wrongly placed, akrama is a variety of the fault called asthana-stha-pada (wrongly placed word) (10.97). The two corrections to this verse show the proper order of the words. The syntactical connection is immediately understood only in this way. The previous construction of the verse did not reveal the syntactical connection so clearly.**

### 10.106

*amato viruddhaḥ parārthaḥ parasya rasasyārtho yatra tad amataparārtham. yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**The fault called amata-parartha signifies “The adverse sense of another rasa.” For example:**

*hari-paricayān nīvī mokṣaṁ gatā gata-bandhanaś*  
*cikura-nikaro hāraś cāyaṁ guṇena viyojitaḥ*  
*daśana-vasanaṁ nirlepatvaṁ jagāma mṛgī-dṛśāṁ*  
*surata-rabhaso jñānābhyāsād atīva viśiṣyate*

**Пословный перевод:**

hari—with Hari; paricayat—because of intimate connection; nivi—a girdle (the ends of a cloth on a woman’s waist tied into a knot in front); moksam—loose; gata—became; gata—has gone; bandhanah—\[became\] one whose binding; cikura—of head hair; nikarah—the mass; harah—necklace; ca—and; ayam—this; gunena—from the the string; viyojitah—\[became\] disjoined; dasana-vasanam—the lips (“the place of residence of the teeth”); nirlepatvam—unsmeared; jagama—attained (became); mrgi- drsam—of the doe-eyed girls; surata—of eroticism; rabhasah— the fervor; jnana-abhyasat—from the practice of knowledge (continuous trance in Brahman); ativa—exceedingly; visisyate—is distinguished (is better than).

**Перевод:**

**As a result of union with Hari, the doe-eyed women’s girdles became free, their braids lost their ties, their necklaces gave up the gunas (strings), and their lips became clean. In this way the gopis’ erotic fervor excels the bliss of Brahman.**

*atra parārthaḥ śānta-rasaḥ śṛṅgāra-rase viruddha ity amataparārtham. tena “iha viharaṇe nīvī” ity-ādi paṭhitvā caturthacaraṇe “ghana-rasamayī-bhāvaḥ kāmotsavaś ca samo ’bhavat” iti pāṭhyam.*

**Перевод:**

**The context is madhura-rasa, but santa-rasa is also expressed. This is the fault called amata-parartha, since santa-rasa is adverse to madhura-rasa. The words “because of union with**

**Hari” should be changed to “during the games”, and the last sentence should read: ghana-rasamayi-bhavah kamotsavas ca samo ’bhavat, “The gopis’ emotions consisting of deep relishment and the festival of Cupid became the same.”**

**Комментарий:**

In Rupa Gosvami’s methodology, this verse is not rasabhasa (improper mixing of rasas) because the two rasas are compared (Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu 4.8.63), not to mention that the verse is based on a semblance of paronomasia (slesabhasa) (an ornament which Mammata does not acknowledge). In Kavi Kamapura’s opinion, here the mix of madhura-rasa and santa-rasa is improper because both appear to be in the same sphere (the gopis) (10.138).

### 10.107

*evaṁ vākya-doṣān uktvā artha-doṣān āha,*

**Перевод:**

**Having described the faults in a sentence, he expounds the faults in a meaning:**

*kaṣṭo ’puṣṭa-vyāhata-punar-ukta-grāmya-duṣkramā api ca*  
*saṁśayito hetu-hataḥ prasiddhi-vidyā-viruddhaś ca (13)*  
*anavī-kṛtaḥ sa-niyamo ’niyame ’niyamas tathā sa-niyame ca*  
*sāmānye sa-viśeṣaḥ sāmānya-yuto viśeṣe ca (14)*  
*sākāṅkṣo nirvāhe pūraṇa-kārī virūpa-sahacaritaḥ*  
*vyaṅgya-viruddho vidhy-anuvādāyuktas tathāślīlaḥ*  
*tyaktaḥ punaḥ svī-kṛta iti duṣṭā arthās tu viṁśatis tri-yutā (15)*  
*pratyekenodāharaṇāni vyastena.*

**Пословный перевод:**

kastah—difficult; apusta—irrelevant; vyahata—contradictory; punah—again; ukta—mentioned; gramya—vulgar; duskramah— bad sequence; api—also; ca—and; samsayitah—dubious; hetu— of a cause; hatah—deprived; prasiddhi—to convention; vidya— and to authoritative knowledge; viruddhah—contrary; ca—and; anavi-krtah—not made new; sa-niyamah—it has a restriction; aniyame—where no restriction is required; aniyamah—it has no restriction; tatha—in that way; sa-niyame—where a restriction is required; ca—and; samanye—where a generality is required; sa-visesah—specification; samanya—with a generality; yutah— endowed; visese—where a specification is required; ca—and; sa- akanksah—with a need to supply words; nirvahe—when there is completeness; purana-kan—filling up space; virupa—is irregular; sahacaritah—where what is associated; vyangya—in regard to the implied meaning; viruddhah—contrariety; vidhi—in regard to the application; anuvada—in regard to the subject; ayuktah—improper; tatha—and; aslilah—unpleasant; tyaktah—rejected; punah—then; svi-krtah—accepted; iti—thus; dustah—faulty; arthah—meanings; tu—(term used as an expletive); vimsatih—twenty; tri-yuta— endowed with three.

**Перевод:**

**There are twenty-three varieties of faults related to the meaning: (1) kasta (difficult to understand), (2) apusta (irrelevant), (3) vyahata (contradictory or inconsistent), (4) punar-ukta (repetition), (5) nirvahepurana-kan (filling up space when the idea is already complete), (6) samanye sa-visesa (specification where a generality is called for), (7) sa-niyame aniyama (lack of restriction where a restriction is required), (8) aniyame sa-niyama (restriction where a restriction is not required), (9) duskrama (bad sequence), (10) gramya (vulgar), (11) samsayita (dubious) (sandigdha), (12) hetu-hata (lacking an explanation), (13) vyangya-viruddha (contradictory implied meaning), (14) prasiddhi-viruddha (contrary to the convention of poets), (15) vidya-viruddha (contrary to authoritative knowledge), (16) anavi-krta (not made new), (17) visese samanya (generality where a specification is required), (18) sakanksa (missing words), (19) virupa-sahacarita (irregularity of associated ideas), (20) vidhy-ayukta (debased predicate), (21) anuvada ayukta (unsuitably described subject), (22) aslila (unpleasant), and (23) tyaktah punah svi-krta (resumption of the concluded).**

**Examples are not shown according to the sequence in the karikas.**

**Комментарий:**

For this reason and for the sake of clarity, we translated the three karikas in such a way that the sequence of the names of faults follows the order that Kavi Karnapura uses from now on.

### 10.108

*“na vaṁśī-karam āsādya” ity-ādi. atra yamānujanir yamunā,*  
*pakṣe niyamaḥ. yama-niyameti gaṇanā-kramād iti kaṣṭo ’rthaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**The fault called kasta (difficult to understand) can be seen in verses 7.55 and 7.56. The word yamanujani occurs in each verse. In verse 7.56, yamanujani (she whose birth occurred after Yama’s) signifies Yamuna. In verse 7.55, however, yamanujani (that which comes after yama) means niyama (rules). But this meaning is difficult (kasta) to understand, because it comes only by counting: “First comes yama. Then comes niyama” \[and because there is nothing in verse 7.55 that hints at the eightfold yoga system\].**

### 10.109

*kintv ayaṁ citra-kāvyādau na doṣo na ca vā guṇaḥ (16)*

**Перевод:**

**However, kasta is actually neither a fault nor a quality when the context is citra-kavya and so on.**

### 10.110

*apuṣṭo yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of apusta (irrelevant):**

*kaustubha-mahasā vakṣaḥ-*  
*sthalam idam ābhāti rādhikā-jāneḥ*  
*udyad-dinamaṇi-kiraṇair*  
*ativitatā gagana-saraṇīva*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaustubha—of the Kaustubha; mahasa—on account of the splendor; vaksah—of the chest; sthalam—place; idam—this; abhati—shines; radhika-janeh—of Krsna (“of He whose wife is Radhika”); udyat—rising; dina-mani—of the sun (“jewel of the day”); kiranaih—on account of the rays; ativitata—expansive; gagana—of the sky; saram— a path; iva—just like.

**Перевод:**

**Krsna’s chest is resplendent with the majestic Kaustubha, in the same way that the expansive path of the sky is lustrous on account of the rays of the rising sun.**

*atrātivitatatvam apuṣṭam.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the sky’s being expansive is irrelevant (apusta).**

**Комментарий:**

Apusta means the sense is “not nourishing.” The word is formed in the passive impersonal voice. Visvanatha Kaviraja explains apustatvam (irrelevancy) as mukhyanupakaritvam (being of no assistance in the principal subject matter). He gives the example vilokya vitate vyomni vidhum munca rusam priye, “Behold, my love, the moon in the expansive sky and give up your anger” (Sahitya-darpana 7.12): The sky’s being expansive does not in any way contribute toward the woman’s giving up her anger. This type of fault is common because sometimes a poet has to fill a line of a verse somehow or other. It is a minor fault.

### 10.111

*vyāhato yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of vyahata (contradictory or inconsistent):**

*yasyāś candana-candrikā-sarasija-prāleya-varṣopala-*  
*sparśād apy adhikaṁ tvacāṁ sukha-karaḥ sparśo nidāghāhani*  
*seyaṁ locana-kaumudī mama sakhe rādhā himasyāgame*  
*vakṣoja-dvitayoṣmaṇaiva harate śītasya bhītiṁ ca me*

**Пословный перевод:**

yasyah—whose; candana—sandalwood paste; candrika— moonlight; sarasija—lotus; praleya—snow; varsopala—of a hailstone; sparsat—than the touch; api—even; adhikam—more; tvacam—of the skin (the plural is used in the sense of high regard); sukha-karah—which gives happiness; sparsah—the touch; nidagha—in the summer; ahani—during the day; sa— She (Radha); iyam—this well-known; locana—for \[My\] eyes; kaumudi— who is moonlight; mama—My; sakhe—O friend; radha—Radha; himasya—of winter; agame—with the arrival; vaksah-ja—of breasts (“arising on the chest”); dvitaya—of the couple; usmana— by the warmth; eva—only; harate—takes away; sitasya—of cold; bhitim—fear; ca—and; me—My.

**Перевод:**

**My dear companion, in the summer, touching Her skin gives more joy than feeling the touch of sandalwood paste, moonlight, a lotus, or a ball of snow. She is moonlight for My eyes. In winter She dispels My fear of cold by the warmth of Her breasts.**

*atra “candrikāyā apy adhiko yasyāḥ sparśaḥ” iti tasyā apakarṣaḥ sūcitaḥ, punaḥ “seyaṁ locana-kaumudī” iti tasyā evotkarṣe vyāhato ’rthaḥ. tena “seyaṁ citta-rasāyanam” iti pāṭhyam.*

**Перевод:**

**Here, by saying that Radha’s touch is superior to moonlight, what is indicated is that moonlight is inferior. Yet this is contradicted in the third line when moonlight is presented as an excellent thing in the phrase: seyam locana-kaumudi (She is moonlight for the eyes). The latter should be replaced by: seyam citta-rasayanam, “She is a tonic for the heart.”**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Kaviraja defines vyahatatvam (contradiction or inconsistency) as kasyacit prag utkarsam apakarsam vabhidhaya pascat tad-anyatha-pratipadanam, “First stating the superiority or inferiority of something and then later describing it otherwise” (Sahitya-darpana 7.12).

### 10.112

*punar-ukto yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of punar-ukta (repetition):**

*preyasi rādhike kathaṁ mamorau sati bhūmāv upaviśyate. tathā hi:*  
*ūruḥ pīṭham uro vilāsa-śayanaṁ līlopadhānaṁ bhujau*  
*khelābjaṁ kara-pallavo maṇi-mayādarśaḥ kapola-sthalī*  
*ācamyaṁ vadanāmbujāsava-rasaḥ svecchopadaṁśo ’dharo*  
*man-mūrtis tava vallabhe madhumatī siddhiḥ svayaṁ-sādhitā*

**Пословный перевод:**

uruh—the thigh; pitham—is a seat; urah—the chest; vilasa—for games; sayanam—is a bed; lila—for pastimes; upadhanam— are a pillow; bhujau—two arms; khela-abjam—are a play lotus; kara—of the fingers; pallavah—the buds; mani-maya—composed of jewels; adarsah—is a mirror; kapola—of the cheeks; sthali— the place; acamyam—a beverage; vadana-ambuja—of the lotus mouth; asava—\[in the form of\] the nectar of the lips; rasah— the liquor; sva-iccha—according to one’s desire; upadamsah— are a snack; adharah—the lips; mad-murtih—My body; tava— Your; vallabhe—O beloved; madhumati—which contains liquor; siddhih—is a perfection; svayam—by itself; sadhita—is made perfect.

**Перевод:**

**Dear beloved Radhika, given that My thighs are here, why do You sit on the ground?**

**My thighs are Your seat, My chest Your play bed, My arms Your pastime pillows, My fingers Your play lotuses, and My cheeks Your jewel-studded mirrors. The nectar of My lips is Your intoxicating beverage and My lips themselves are Your snack of choice. O beloved, for You My body is a self-perfected perfection full of the liquor of love.**

*atra kandarpa-mañjarī nāṭikāyāṁ cūrṇikāyāṁ “preyasi rādhike” iti sambodhane sati punar api “vallabhe” iti sambodhanam artha-paunaruktyam. tena cūrṇikāyāṁ “ayi” iti sambodhane sati doṣa-hāniḥ. “madhumatī siddhiḥ” ity atraiva samāpyate cet tathāpi “svayaṁ-sādhitā” iti nirvāhe pūraṇa-kārī doṣaḥ. evaṁ “madhumatī” iti sāmānye sa-viśeṣaḥ. “man-mūrtir eva” iti vivakṣite sati sa-niyame ’niyamaḥ. tena “madhumatī kāpy eva siddhiḥ parā” iti cet kriyate tadā pūraṇa-kāri-doṣa-hāniḥ. kintv aniyame sati sa-niyamo doṣaḥ. tantreṇa catvāro doṣā darśitāḥ. tena “svecchopadaṁśo ’dharaḥ, prāyo ’yaṁ mama vigrahaḥ khalu tava krīḍopahāraḥ paraḥ” iti pāṭhe sarva-doṣa-hāniḥ. kiṁ cāsya tṛtīya-caraṇaṁ cec caturtha-caraṇaṁ bhavati, tadā duṣkramadoṣo ’pīti. kiṁ ca “prāyo ’yaṁ mama kāya eva hi mayā bhogāya te kalpitaḥ” iti grāmyo ’pi.*

**Перевод:**

**This verse and its preliminary are from a play called Kandarpa- manjari. In the preliminary, there is a vocative term: preyasi radhike (O Radhika, dear beloved). In the fourth line of the verse, there is another vocative term: vallabhe (O beloved). This is an instance of a repetition of the meaning (punar-ukta). The fault is removed by replacing the word preyasi, in the introduction, by ayi (dear girl).**

**Moreover, if we consider that the idea in the phrase madhumati siddhih (it is perfect and contains liquor) is already complete, then we must regard the compound svayam-sadhita (made perfect by itself) as a space-filler. This is the fault called nirvahe purana-kan (filling up space when the idea is already complete).**

**The word madhumati (it contains liquor) is an example of the fault called samanye sa-visesa (specification where a generality is called for). Moreover, if the real intent were to say: man- murtir eva (only My body), then the fact that it is only said man- murtir (My body) in the verse would be the fault of sa-niyame aniyama (lack of restriction where a restriction is required).**

**Therefore, if the words madhumati siddhih svayam-sadhita are replaced by: madhumati kapy eva siddhih para (it is only a particular supreme perfection, which contains liquor), then the fault of purana-kari (filling up space when the idea is already complete) is corrected. However, in this replacement there is the fault of aniyame sa-niyama (restriction where no restriction is required) (the word “only” should not have been used).**

**In this way, four faults have been shown by means of one model.**

**All these faults are corrected simply by changing the fourth line to: prayo ’yam mama vigrahah khalu tava kridopaharah parah, “For the most part, this body of Mine is indeed the best gift for Your games.”**

**Moreover, the fault of duskrama (bad sequence) would occur if the third and fourth lines were switched, since the sequence in the verse would be obstructed. Also, the fault called gramya (vulgar) would occur if the fourth line, man-murtis tava vallabhe madhumatisiddhih svayam-sadhita, were replaced by: prayo ’yam mama kaya eva hi maya bhogaya te kalpitah, “For the most part, this body of Mine has been fashioned for Your union with Me.”**

### 10.113

*saṁśayitaḥ sandigdho yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of samsayita, which means sandigdha (dubious):**

*nṛ-deham āsādya niṣevanīyaṁ*  
*kim atra tatropadiśantu bhavyāḥ*  
*govinda-pādāmburuhāsavaḥ kiṁ*  
*strī-ratna-vaktrāmburuhāsavaḥ kim*

**Пословный перевод:**

nr-deham—a human body; asadya—having obtained; nisevaniyam kim—what is to served?; atra tatra—regarding this and other subject matters; upadisantu—you all should instruct; bhavyah—O righteous persons; govinda—of Govinda; pada-amburuha—of the lotus feet; asavah—the nectar; kim—is it?; stri—of women; ratna—of the jewel (i.e. the best); vaktra-amburuha—of the lotus face; asavah—the nectar; kim—is it?

**Перевод:**

**O saintly persons, having obtained a human body, to what shall I dedicate myself? You should instruct me on this topic. Shall I serve the nectar of Govinda’s lotus feet or the nectar of the lotus face of the best woman?**

*atra śānta-śṛṅgārayoḥ śāntasyaivopadeśyatvād asandigdhatve praśno doṣaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Here, out of santa-rasa and madhura-rasa, only santa can be instructed. Thus the question is faulty because there is actually no doubt about the answer. In this way the sense of the question is dubious.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Kaviraja gives a similar example with a different explanation of the fault: “acala abala va syuh sevya bruta mamsinah?” atra prakaranabhavac chanta-srngarinoh ko vakteti niscayabhavat sandigdhatvam. Due to the lack of a context in the question: “Tell me, O learned men, should the mountains be served or should women be served?” there is no certainty about whether the speaker is associated with santa-rasa or with madhura-rasa. Therefore there is ambiguity (sandigdha)” (Sahitya-darpana 7.12).

Matsya: We are talking about the persons in the rasas rather than the rasas themselves as is evident from Sahitya-darpana’s use of the word srngarin. Thus, “Out of santa-rasa and madhura-rasa, the person being instructed is associated only with santa-rasa.”

### 10.114

*hetu-hato yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of hetu-hata (lacking an explanation):**

*api deśaḥ sa kim āste*  
*śravaṇa-śalākeva kokilālaptiḥ*  
*dāvānala-kīlā iva*  
*na yatra sakhi candramasaḥ pādāḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

api—and; desah—place; sah—that; kim aste—is there?; sravana— for the ears; salaka—a sharp stick iva—is like; kokila—of the cuckoos; alaptih—the cooing; dava—forest; anala—of a fire; kilah—flames; iva—like; na—\[pain\] is not; yatra—in which \[place\]; sakhi—O friend; candramasah—of the moon; padah—rays.

**Перевод:**

**Sakhi, is there a place where there is no cooing of cuckoos, which is like a thorn in the ear, and where there are no moonrays, which are like the flames of a forest fire?**

*atra kokilālapty-ādeḥ śravaṇa-salākāditve hetur noktaḥ. tena “priya-viraheṇa sa deśaḥ śravaṇa-śalākeva yatra na pikoktiḥ, na ca dava-dahana-jvālā iva vā yatrendu-dīdhitayaḥ” iti pāṭhyam. “api deśaḥ sa kim āste śravaṇa-śalākeva kokilālaptiḥ, dāvānalakīlā iva dayita-viyoge na yatra śaśi-bhāsaḥ” iti cet tadā vyaṅgyo viruddho bhavati, tasmin deśe vallabhāntaraṁ labhyate iti vyaṅgye viruddham.*

**Перевод:**

**In this verse, the reason the cooing is like a sharp stick in the ear and the moonrays are like the flames of a forest fire is not mentioned. Thus the verse should be changed to:**

*priya-viraheṇa sa deśaḥ*  
*śravaṇa-śalākeva yatra na pikoktiḥ*  
*na ca dava-dahana-jvālā*  
*iva vā yatrendu-dīdhitayaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

priya—from the male lover; virahena—on account of separation; sah—that; desah—should be told; sravana—for the ears; salaka—a sharp stick; iva—like; yatra—in which \[place\]; na—is not; pika—of the cuckoos; uktih—the cooing; na ca—nor; dava— forest; dahana—of a fire; jvalah—flames; iva—like; va—or; yatra—in which; indu—of the moon; didhitayah—the rays.

**Перевод:**

**“Tell me about that place where there is neither the cooing of cuckoos nor moonrays, which, due to separation from my beloved, are like a sharp stick in the ear and like the flames of a forest fire respectively.”**

**However, if the verse were changed as follows, it would be an instance of vyangya-viruddha (contradictory implied meaning):**

*api deśaḥ sa kim āste*  
*śravaṇa-śalākeva kokilālaptiḥ*  
*dāvānala-kīlā iva*  
*dayita-viyoge na yatra śaśi-bhāsaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**“Is there a place where, in separation from my beloved, the cooing of cuckoos is not like a sharp stick in the ear and where the moonrays are not like the flames of a forest fire?”**

**Here, the implied meaning is contrary to what is taught in the textbooks on rasa, since what is suggested is that another male lover is to be found in that place where the heroine longs to go.**

**Комментарий:**

In the last verse, the heroine asks where she might go to meet another lover, thinking that in the course of union with that other lover the cooing and moonlight, though still there, will no longer give her pain. This type of implied meaning is contrary because it is improper for a lady to have more than one lover, not counting her husband (Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu 4.9.13-16).

Visvanatha Kaviraja covers the fault of vyangya-viruddha under the name of prakasita-viruddhata and gives this example: kumaras te naradhlsa sriyam samadhigacchatu, “O king, may your son obtain opulence.” The implied meaning is contrary here: “You should die \[so that he can inherit the throne\]” (Sahitya-darpana 7.12).

### 10.115

*prasiddhi-viruddho yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of prasiddhi-viruddha (contrary to the convention of poets):**

*tvam anākula-bakula-taro*  
*mattaḥ khalu su-bhaga evāsi*  
*rādhāyāḥ pada-kamalaja-*  
*ghātād yad akāle phullo ’si*

**Пословный перевод:**

tvam—you; anakula—not confused; bakula-taro—O bakula tree; mattah—than Me; khalu—indeed; su-bhagah—fortunate; eva— only; asi—are; radhayah—of Radha; pada-kamala-ja—produced from the lotus foot; ghatat—because of the striking; yat—because; akale—out of season; phullah—abounding in flowers; asi—you are.

**Перевод:**

**O carefree bakula tree, indeed, you are more fortunate than I, since you bloom out of season simply by the strike of Radha’s lotus foot.**

*atra padminyāś caraṇa-ghātena raktāśoka evākāle phullati, mukhamadirā-gaṇḍūṣeṇa hi bakula iti kavi-sampradāye prasiddhiḥ. tad anyathā cet prasiddhi-viruddho ’rthaḥ. tena “rādhāyā mukhamadirā-gaṇḍūṣa-balād akāla-phullo yat” iti vācyam. vidyāviruddhaḥ śāstra-viruddho yathā— “ayaṁ mahātmā paramatapasvī snāyī niśītheṣu niśītha-bhojī” ity-ādau grahoparāgādikam antareṇa rātri-snānaṁ dharma-śāstraṁ viruddham. niśītabhojanam api tathā, yady upahāsa-param idaṁ tadā na doṣaḥ. stuti-paratve doṣa eva.*

**Перевод:**

**According to the tradition of poets, the red asoka tree blooms out of season when struck by the foot of a padmini heroine, and the bakula tree blooms out of season when sprinkled by a padmini heroine with a mouthful of liquor. If anything different is indicated, it is a meaning that is contrary to convention (prasiddhi-viruddha). The second half of the verse should read: radhaya mukha-madira-gandusa-balad akala-phullo yat, “because you bloom out of season by being sprinkled with the sweet wine from Radha’s mouth.”**

**Now an example of the fault called vidya-viruddha is shown, where the meaning is contrary to scriptural knowledge: ayam mahatma parama-tapasvi snayi nisithesu nisitha-bhoji, “He is a great soul and an outstanding ascetic; he bathes and eats at night.” According to the scriptures on religious principles (dharma-sastras), bathing at night is forbidden unless there is an eclipse of the sun or of the moon. Eating at night is also prohibited. If the purpose of this sentence is to mock someone, there is no fault, but if the intention is to praise the person, then the ideas of bathing and eating at night are instances of the fault of vidya-viruddha (contrary to authoritative knowledge).**

### 10.116

*yathā vā,*

**Перевод:**

**Another example of vidya-viruddha (contrary to authoritative knowledge):**

*nakhāṅkitaṁ dos-taṭam aṅgadasyā-*  
*ropeṇa gopāyati kāpi gopī*  
*urojayoḥ kācana cumba-lagnaṁ*  
*tāmbūla-rāgaṁ ghusṛṇaiḥ pinaṣṭi*

**Пословный перевод:**

nakha—with nails; ankitam—which are marked; doh—of the arm; tatam—the side; angadasya—a bracelet \[worn on the upper arm\]; aropena—by fixing; gopayati—hides; kapi gopi—a certain gopi; urah-jayoh—on the two breasts (“arising on the chest”); kacana—a certain girl; cumba—because of a kiss; lagnam—which adhered; tambula—of the betel nut; ragam—the red color; ghusrnaih—with saffron; pinasti—grinds (i.e. rubs).

**Перевод:**

**A certain gopi hides nail scratches on the side of her upper arms by fixing bracelets there. Another gopi rubs saffron on the red-betel-juice kiss marks on her breasts.**

*ity-ādāv aṅgada-sthāne nakha-kṣataṁ stanayoś ca cumbanaṁ kāma-śāstra-viruddham. evaṁ yasya yac-chāstraṁ tasya tadviruddhatvaṁ doṣaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**In verses such as this the mention of nail scratching on the upper arms and kissing on the breasts is contrary to the ways of love mentioned in the textbooks on eroticism. Thus the fault of vidya-viruddha can occur with regard to any authoritative text.**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Kaviraja gives the following example of vidya- viruddha: adhare karaja-ksatam mrgaksyah, “the nail scratches on the lips of the doe-eyed girl” (Sahitya-darpana 7.12). Bite marks, not fingernail scratches, on the lips are mentioned in texts on eroticism.

### 10.117

*anavī-kṛto yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of anavi-krta**  
**(not made new) (monotonous):**

*jātaṁ kule dhanavatāṁ mahatāṁ tataḥ kiṁ*  
*śāstreṣu buddhir akhileṣu kṛtā tataḥ kim*  
*puṇyāny urūṇi vihitāni janais tataḥ kim*  
*vistāritaṁ ca bhuvaneṣu yaśas tataḥ kim*

**Пословный перевод:**

jatam—birth (being born); kule—in a family; dhanavatam—rich; mahatam—of great people; tatah kim—what comes from that? (i.e. what is the use?); sastresu—to the scriptures; buddhih— intelligence; akhilesu—in all; krta—applied; tatah kim—what comes from that? (i.e. what is the use?); punyani—pious deeds; uruni—many; vihitani—performed; janaih—by people; tatah kim—what comes from that? (i.e. what is the use?); vistaritam— expanded; ca—and; bhuvanesu—in the three worlds; yasah—fame; tatah kim—what comes from that? (i.e. what is the use?).

**Перевод:**

**What is the use of a birth in a rich aristocratic family? And what is the use of applying one’s intelligence to the scriptures? What is the use of people performing many pious deeds? And what is the use of being famous throughout the three worlds?**

*atra “tataḥ kim” ity etair artho ’navī-kṛtaḥ. tena “kṛṣṇe ratir hi paramaṁ padam ātanoti” iti navī-kṛtaḥ syāt. sa-niyamo hi doṣo “madhumatī kāpy eva siddhiḥ parā” ity atra darśitaḥ. aniyamaś ca “man-mūrtir eva” iti yan na kṛtaṁ tena tatraiva darśitaḥ. sāmānye viśeṣaś ca “madhumatī siddhiḥ” ity atraiva madhumatīti viśeṣa-nirdeśe darśitaḥ. vastutaḥ siddhi-sāmānyam eva nirdeṣṭuṁ yujyate*

**Перевод:**

**In this verse, the words tatah kim are repeated thrice. In this way the sense of the sentences is not kept fresh. The fourth line should read: krsne ratir hiparamam padam atanoti, “Only love for Krsna effects the highest position.” In this way the meaning is innovative.**

**In the vrtti of text 10.112, it was shown how the clause madhumati kapy eva siddhih para (it is only a particular supreme perfection, which contains liquor) is an instance of aniyame sa-niyama (restriction where no restriction is required). In the same vrtti it was also shown how saying man-murtir (My body) instead of man-murtir eva (only My body) is an instance of the fault of sa-niyame aniyama (lack of restriction where a restriction is required).**

**It was also shown that the use of the specification madhumati in madhumati siddhih (a perfection that contains liquor) is an example of samanye visesa (specification where a generality is called for). In reality it is proper to mention only the generality, siddhih (perfection).**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Kaviraja gives the following as an example of samanye visesa (specification where a generality is called for): hirakanam nidher asya sindhoh kim varnayamahe, “What can we say about the ocean, a reservoir of diamonds?” (Sahitya-darpana 7.12). Here instead of the specification hirakanam (of diamonds), it would be proper to state the generality ratnanam (of jewels).

### 10.118

*viśeṣe sāmānyaṁ yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of visese samanya (generality where a specification is required):**

*bhāgyādhikyataḥ uttarottara-samutkarṣāvadhibhyo guṇa-*  
*grāmebhyo ’pi balādhikas tanumatāṁ ko ’pi svabhāvodayaḥ*  
*janma kṣīra-nidhau śriyā saha-gataḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa-vakṣaḥ-sthale*  
*vāso hanta tathāpi tasya na maṇer aśmeti vādo hataḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

bhagya—of good fortune; adhikyatah—greater than an abundance; uttara-uttara—which is higher and higher; samutkarsa—of pre­eminence; avadhibhyah—which are the limit; guna—of qualities; gramebhyah—\[greater\] than a multitude; api—also; bala—of power; adhikah—an abundance; tanumatam—among those who are embodied; kah api—a certain; svabhava—due to their nature; udayah—whose appearance; janma—\[whose\] origin; ksira—of milk; nidhau— \[occurred\] in the ocean; sriya—with Sri (Laksmi); saha-gatah—goes along; sri-krsna—of Sri Krsna; vaksah-sthale— is on the chest; vasah—\[whose\] residence; hanta—alas; tatha api— nevertheless; tasya—its; na—not; maneh—the jewel; asma—a stone; iti—thus; vadah—calling; hatah—has ended.

**Перевод:**

**Embodied souls must have some great power of obstinacy arising from their nature that overrides their great good fortune and superexcellent qualities, because even though this jewel appeared from the Milk Ocean and rests on Sri Krsna’s chest along with Laksmi, alas, they say it is a stone!**

*atra viśeṣe kaustubhe sāmānyasya maṇer nirdeśaḥ. tena “vāso yasya tathāpi kaustubha-maṇes tasyāśmatā no gatā” iti pāṭhyam.*

**Перевод:**

**In the fourth line of this verse, a jewel in general is mentioned instead of the specific Kaustubha jewel. That is the fault of visese samanya (generality where a specification is required). The fourth line should read: vaso yasya tathapi kaustubha- manes tasyasmata no gata, “nevertheless, the talk that the Kaustubha jewel is a stone remains.”**

**Комментарий:**

Visvanatha Kaviraja gives the following example: yanti nila- nicolinyo rajanisv abhisarikah, “The girls going to meet their lovers move about in the night covered with blue wrappers” (Sahitya-darpana 7.12 vrtti). Here, instead of only saying rajanisu (in the nights), which is a generality, the specific kind of nights should be mentioned, as in tamisrasu rajamsu (in the dark nights, i.e. on amavasya nights).

### 10.119

*sākāṅkṣo yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of sakanksa (missing words):**

*vṛthākṛthā mānini mānam uccaiḥ*  
*kṛṣṇo ’yam etāś ca vayaṁ samastāḥ*  
*prasīda rādhe vinidhehi citte*  
*kṛpām apāro guṇa-vāridhis te*

**Пословный перевод:**

vrtha—uselessly; akrthah—You did (exhibited); manini—O proud girl; manam—anger; uccaih—lofty; krsnah—Krsna; ayam—this well-known; etah—these; ca—and; vayam—we; samastah—all; prasida—be pleased; radhe—O Radha; vinidhehi—please put; citte—in the heart; krpam—compassion (tenderness); aparah—is boundless; guna-varidhih—the ocean of qualities; te—Your.

**Перевод:**

**Radha, You exhibited lofty mana uselessly. Krsna \[should not be neglected\] and we \[do not deserve to be tormented\]. Be gracious, proud girl. Your qualities are a boundless ocean. Let Your heart flow with tenderness.**

*atrāyaṁ kṛṣṇo nopekṣituṁ yogyaḥ, nāpi vayaṁ kleṣayituṁ yogyā ity ākāṅkṣām apekṣata iti sākāṅkṣaḥ. nirvāhe pūraṇa-kārī tu madhumatī siddhiḥ svayaṁ-sādhitā” ity atra svayaṁ-sādhiteti pūraṇa-kārī madhumatī siddhir ity etāvat eva nirvāhaḥ syāt. imam eva doṣam apada-yukta iti pūrve paṭhanti.*

**Перевод:**

**The fault of sakanksa (missing words) occurs in this verse because extra words are required to complete the sense. For instance, the words krsno ’yam in the verse stand for: ayam krsno nopeksitum yogyah (He, Krsna, should not be neglected), and the words ca vayam stand for: napi vayam klesayitum yogyah (nor do we deserve to be tormented).**

**Moreover, the fault of nirvahe purana-kari (filling up space when the idea is already complete) was shown in verse 10.112 with the example, madhumati siddhih svayam-sadhita. The compound svayam-sadhita (made perfect by itself) is the space­filler and madhumati siddhih (it is perfect and it contains liquor) is the already complete idea. The previous teachers named this fault apada-yukta (applied in a wrong place).**

### 10.120

*virūpa-sahacaritaḥ sahacara-bhinna ity arthaḥ. sa yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**The fault called virupa-sahacaritah signifies sahacara-bhinna (irregularity of an associated idea). For example:**

*stavena lajjā draviṇair amattatā*  
*śrutena dhairyaṁ yaśasātinamratā*  
*doṣeṇa tāpaḥ praṇayena vaśyatā*  
*satām iyaṁ svārasikī hi rītiḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

The natural behavior of saintly persons is that they are shy when praised, unexcited by wealth, grave due to scriptural knowledge, meek due to fame, sorrowful on account of their deficiencies, and controlled by affection.

*atra stavādibhir utkṛṣṭaiḥ saha-carair doṣa-tāpayor nikṛṣtayor vairūpyam. tena “dānair atṛptiḥ” iti pāṭhyam. vyaṅgya-viruddhas tu “api deśaḥ sa kim āste śravaṇa-śalākā” ity-ādau prāg eva darśitaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**In this verse, there is a difference of pattern between the words dosena tapah (sorrow on account of faults), which express lowliness, and stavena lajja (shy due to praise) along with the other words in the first three lines, which express eminence. Therefore, dosena tapah should be replaced by: danair atrptih (not satisfied with gifts, i.e. not bought with gifts).**

**The fault of vyangya-viruddha (contrary implied meaning) was shown in the vrtti of text 10.114.**

### 10.121

*vidhy-ayukto vidheyasyānyathā-sthitimattā. yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**The fault called vidhy-ayukta (debased predicate) signifies that the predicate has a different rank than it should have. For example:**

*muhur lalitayā rādhe*  
*tvaṁ prayatnaiḥ prabodhitā*  
*tvayāsamīkṣya-kāriṇyā*  
*tathāpi kriyate haṭhaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

muhuh—repeatedly; lalitaya—by Lalita; radhe—O Radha; tvam—You; prayatnaih—through great efforts; prabodhita—are made enlightened; tvaya—by You; asamiksya-karinya—who are acting inconsiderately; tatha api—nevertheless; kriyate—is done; hathah—violence.

**Перевод:**

**Radha, You are repeatedly enlightened by Lalita with great efforts. Still, You are inconsiderate and act harshly.**

*atra tvaṁ prayatnaiḥ prabodhyase ity eva vidheyaṁ, tad-anyathāsthitau vidhy-ayuktaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Here it should have been said prabodhyase instead ofprabodhita. It was stated otherwise, and so that is the fault called vidhy- ayukta (debased predicate).**

**Комментарий:**

The speaker meant to express the present tense. Grammatically, the participle prabodhita can be used in the present tense—by the rule that the suffix\[k\]ta has the sense of the present when the meaning of the verbal root is buddhi (to know): mati-buddhi-pujarthebhyas ca (Astadhyayl 3.2.188)—, but the verbal form prabodhyase is clearer.

### 10.122

*anuvādāyukto yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of anuvada ayukta (unsuitably described subject):**

*ayi para-bhṛta tasyāḥ kaṇṭha-nādena tasyāṁ*  
*tava nipatitam akṣi prāyaśo vismayena*  
*virahi hṛdaya-kāla-vyāla mā vañcayetāḥ*  
*kathaya katham idānīṁ labhyate kutra rādhā*

**Пословный перевод:**

ayi—(vocative particle); para-bhrta—O cuckoo (“nourished by another”); tasyah—Her; kantha—of the voice; nadena—on account of the sound; tasyam—on Her; tava—your; nipatitam— fallen; aksi—eye; prayasah—for the most part (i.e. almost); vismayena—on account of amazement; virahi—O you who feels separation; hrdaya—of the heart; kala—black; vyala—snake; ma vancayetah—you should not deceive; kathaya—please tell; katham—how; idanim—now; labhyate—attained; kutra—where \[is\]; radha—Radha.

**Перевод:**

**O black cuckoo, bumbstruck by Radha’s sweet pitch, you stared at Her so intensely that your eyes almost fell. O black snake of the heart, who feels separation, don’t deceive Me. Tell Me where and how I may find Her at this time.**

*atra “virahi hṛdaya-kāla-vyāla” iti nānuvādyaṁ, kutaḥ kathayeti prārthanā-phalābhāvāt. tena “mama ruci-sadṛśatvān mitra” ity anuvādyam*

**Перевод:**

**Here, in the third line, the vocative words virahi hrdaya-kala- vyala (O black snake of the heart, who feels separation) is not a proper substantive. If it were, what is the point of saying “please tell Me” afterwards? One could not expect any positive reply this way. Consequently, virahi hrdaya-kala-vyala should be replaced by: mama ruci-sadrsatvan mitra (O friend on account of a similar luster): This is a proper substantive in this context.**

### 10.123

*aślīlo yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of aslila (unpleasant):**

*āditsayāṁśukānām*  
*unnata-bhuja-vīrudhāṁ kumārīṇām*  
*paśyati harau vireje*  
*gata-vasanānām adho-dṛṣṭiḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

aditsaya—on account of a desire to take; amsukanam—garments; unnata—sublime; bhuja—on account of their arms; virudham— who are creepers; kumarinam—of the young girls; pasyati harau— when Hari saw; vireje—He shone (i.e. appeared beautiful); gata- vasananam—of the gopis (“of those whose clothes have gone”); adhah—low; drstih—the glance.

**Перевод:**

**Hari was resplendent when He looked at the girls, whose creeperlike arms were elongated since the girls wanted to retrieve their clothes. The glance of those naked gopis was low.**

*atra “namrā dṛṣṭiḥ” iti vivakṣitam. tatrādho-dṛṣṭir iti yat pratīyate tad evāślīlam. tena “gata-vasanānāṁ natā dṛṣṭiḥ” ity eva śuddham.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the meaning intended by “low glance” is “submissive glance”. Thus “low glance” is unpleasant (aslila). The proper reading is nata drstih (bowed glance: eyes looking at the ground).**

### 10.124

*tyakta-punaḥ-svī-kṛto yathā,*

**Перевод:**

**An example of tyakta-punah-svi-krta (resumption of the concluded):**

*na candreṇāsyaṁ te tulayitum idaṁ sāhasam aho*  
*mamāste tenaiṣā stutir api na candrānana iti*  
*na candro lajjāvāṁs tad api yad udeti smita-mukho*  
*dhig enaṁ yaṁ śaśvad glapayati kuhū-rātrir asatī*

**Пословный перевод:**

na—is not; candrena—with the moon; asyam—face; te—of yours; tulayitum—to compare; idam—this; sahasam—boldness; aho— Ah; mama—of mine; aste—is; tena—therefore; esa—this; stutih— praise; api—even; na—not; candra-anane—O girl with a moonlike face; iti—thus; na—is not; candrah—the moon; lajjavan— ashamed; tat api—nevertheless; yat—because; udeti—rises; smita- mukhah—smiling face; dhik—fie on; enam—this \[moon\]; yam— which \[moon\]; sasvat—always (every month); glapayati—causes to wane; kuhuh—of the new moon; ratrih—the night; asati—bad.

**Перевод:**

**I am not overtly bold in comparing your face to the moon, therefore calling you “Moon-faced girl” is not a praise. Nevertheless the moon is not ashamed because with its crescent shape it looks like a smiling face. Fie on the moon, which the wicked new-moon night causes to wane every month.**

*atra “stutir api na candrānana” ity evopasaṁhāraḥ kṛtaḥ, tathāpi “na candro lajjāvān” iti yad aparam upakramyate, tena tyaktapunaḥ-svī-kṛtatā.*

**Перевод:**

**Here the conclusion was made: “calling you ‘moon-faced girl’ is not a praise.” The text after that is a meaning that is taken again (punah svi-krtah).**

### 10.125

*uktās trayo-viṁśatir doṣāḥ. yeṣu yeṣv ete doṣā darśitās teṣu teṣv anye ’pi doṣā boddhavyāḥ. tena doṣā api saṅkareṇa saṁsṛṣṭyā caika-rūpayā ukta-saṁkhyāḥ śabdādi-gatā doṣā bahavo bhavanti. tathā hi—śruti-kaṭv-ādayaḥ ṣoḍaśa-pada-doṣāḥ. ete samāsagatatve ’pi punaḥ ṣoḍaśa. tena punar dvātriṁśat. padāṁśe trayodaśa, vākye ṣoḍaśaiva, evam ūnatriṁśat. punar vākyam eva yad duṣṭaṁ tatra pratiloma-varṇāditvenaika-viṁśatiḥ. punar artha-doṣās trayoviṁśatiḥ. evaṁ catuścatvāriṁśat. sarvaikatve pañcottara-śataṁ doṣāḥ. ete yathā-sthiti-saṅkara-saṁsṛṣṭyā bahudhaiveti.*

**Перевод:**

**Thus the twenty-three faults relating to the meaning have been shown, but the other faults can be perceived in those examples, thus the total number of faults, with regard to sound and so on, is higher than that in consideration of combinations (samsrsti) and mixes (sankara) of faults. The explanation is this: The faults beginning from sruti-katu are sixteen faults in a word (pada-dosa). The same sixteen faults also occur in compounds. This makes a total of thirty-two. Out of those sixteen, thirteen of can also occur in a part of a word (padamsa-dosa) (the sixteen minus klista, avimrsta-vidheyamsa, and viruddha-mati-krt). The same sixteen also occur in a sentence (vakya-dosa). This makes twenty-nine categories. Another set of twenty-one faults occurs in a sentence (10.72). And there are twenty-three faults in a meaning (artha-dosa). This makes forty-four categories, for a total of one hundred and five faults. They become manifold by sankara (combinations of faults in the same sphere) and samsrsti (independent combinations).**

### 10.126

*karṇāvataṁsādiṣu yat karṇādiḥ śabda īkṣyate*  
*tat-sānnidhyādi-bodhārthaṁ taj jñeyaṁ na prayojayet (17)*

**Пословный перевод:**

karna-avatamsa-adisu—in karna-avatamsa and so on; yat—if (yat = yadi); karna-adih—beginning with karna (ear); sabdah—a word; iksyate—is seen; tat—to that; sannidhya-adi—closeness and so on; bodha—of making known; artham—for the sake; tat—that; jneyam—should be understood; na prayojayet—should not be used.

**Перевод:**

**If words such as karna is seen in karnavatamsa and so on, their purpose is to cause to perception of nearness and so on. They should not be used.**

*avataṁsādi-śabdaḥ karṇādy-ābharaṇārthaka eva, tathāpi teṣu karṇādi-śabdo yadīkṣyate, tat tad-ārūḍhatvādi-pratipatty-arthaṁ jñeyaṁ, na tad dūṣyam ity arthaḥ. na tu prayojayet svayaṁ kavināprayojyam, “prakṣālanād dhi paṅkasya dūrād sparśanaṁ varam” iti nyāyāt. yadi dṛśyate kvāpi tadā na dūṣayed iti yāvat, ādi-śabdāt śiraḥ-śekharaḥ śravaṇa-kuṇḍalaṁ dhanur-jyā eṣu sārūḍhādy-arthaḥ. muktā-hāraḥ puṣpa-mālā anayor anyaratnāmiśratvotkṛṣṭa-puṣpa-nirmitatve, kevala-hāraḥ-śabdena kevala-mālā-śabdenaiva tat-tat-pratīteḥ, na prayojayed ity asyāyam artho vā, evam-ādīnāṁ kavi-prayuktatvāt kadācit prayoktavyatvaṁ ca na tv ity-ādi-diśā pāda-nūpura-jaghana-kāñcyādi prayoktavyam iti vācaṁ jagādety-ādiṣu vāg-viśeṣaṇārtham eva vācam ity-ādi prayogaḥ, viśeṣaṇābhāve tu vācaṁ jagādeti doṣa eva, dhātv-arthenaiva tat pratīteḥ. tatrāpi kriyā-viśeṣaṇenaiva tad-avagater na dātavyaṁ vācam ity-ādi padam iti kecit. tan na, bahu-viśeṣaṇe kriyā-viśeṣaṇaṁ na camatkāri. evaṁ padbhyāṁ gacchatīty-ādiṣv api viśeṣaṇe sati na doṣaḥ. khyāte ’rthe nirhetutā na doṣaḥ, khyāter eva jhaṭiti prabuddhe ’rthe hetur nāpekṣate. śruti-kaṭv-ādīnāṁ doṣāṇāṁ para-kathitānukathane na doṣaḥ. kvacid vaktrādy-aucityenānukathanaṁ vināpi guṇo ’pi, kvacin na doṣo na guṇaś ca. vaiyākaraṇādau vaktari raudrādau rase ca guṇaḥ. nīrase na guṇo na doṣaś ca. atrāprayukta-nihatārthau śleṣādau na duṣṭau. aślīlaṁ tu śānte vaktari na duṣṭam. yat tu “dvyarthaiḥ padaiḥ piśunayec ca rahasya-vastu” iti muni-vacana-balāt “kari-hastena sambādhe” ity-ādau kecit paṭhanti. tad asat tasyāślīlatvād artha-doṣa eva. kintu rahasya-vastv iti yasya śabdavācyatāyāṁ doṣas tad eva na tv aślīlam. sandigdham api kvacid aprastuta-praśaṁsā-vyāja-stuty-ādi-pratipādakaṁ yadi bhavati tadā na doṣaḥ, pratyuta guṇa eva. pratipādya-pratipādakayor jñāpakatve saty apratīto guṇaḥ. adhama-prakṛtiṣu vidūṣakādau ca grāmyo guṇaḥ. nyūna-padaṁ harṣa-śoka-mattatādhikye sati guṇaḥ. kvacin na guṇo na doṣaḥ. adhika-padaṁ viṣādādau guṇaḥ. prāg uktam etat, mattatāyāṁ tu viśeṣata eva. kathita-padaṁ lāṭānuprāse ’rthāntara-saṅkramita-vācye vihitasyānuvāde ca guṇaḥ. patat-prakarṣaḥ krameṇa krodhādi-hrāse guṇaḥ, bhinnavākyatayā rasa-bhede ca. samāpta-punar-āttaṁ kvacin na doṣo na guṇaḥ. kvacid iti yatra jhaṭiti rasāpakarṣaṁ na syād iti viśeṣaṇadānārtham eva, yatra punar dīyate na vākyāntaratvena tatraiva dūṣaṇam. asthāna-samāsaṁ kvacid guṇaḥ, krodhādy-asthāne ’pi yatra krodhādy-anukaraṇaṁ tatrety arthaḥ. garbhitam avaśyaviśeṣatvena prakṛta-vākye paripoṣakatve sa sati guṇaḥ. anye sarve duṣṭā eva.*

**Перевод:**

**The word avatamsa already means an ornament for the ear. Still, if the word karna is seen with it, its purpose is to cause the understanding that the ornament is clinging to the ear. The purport is that there is no fault. But a poet should not use such words. This is in accordance with the logic, “After cleaning up, it is better to stay away from dirt.” If the usage of such terms is seen occasionally, it doesn’t spoil the composition.**

**There are other expressions of that sort, indicated by the term “and so on” in the above karika: sirah-sekhara (crest on the head), sravana-kundala (earring on the ear), and dhanur-jya (bowstring on a bow).**

**In the case of mukta-hara (necklace of pearls), the sense is that the necklace is intermingled with other jewels. In puspa-mala (garland of flowers), the idea is that the garland was strung with excellent flowers. This is because the words hara and mala already connote pearls and flowers respectively. In regard to those two expressions, the sense of “They should not be used” optionally applies. Expressions of that sort can be used on occasion because the poets used them, but expressions such as pada-nupura (anklet on the foot) and jaghana-kanci (a girdle on a woman’s zone) should never be used.**

**In vacam jagada (she spoke words) and the like, the term vacam (words) is used so that an adjective may accompany it. Without an adjective, stating vacam jagada is faulty because the sense of “words” is already included in the meaning of the verbal root. Some say there is no need of vacam at all because an adjective can be turned into an adverb, but that is wrong because many adjectives in the same sentence would have to be turned into adverbs, and using many adverbs does not convey astonishment. Similarly, the expression padbhyam gacchati (he goes with two feet) is not faulty when an adjective is used.**

**The fault called nirhetu (hetu-hata, lacking an explanation) (10.114) is not a fault when the meaning is well-known. No explanation is needed when the idea is immediately understood because of the renown.**

**Among the faults beginning from sruti-katu, there is no fault if the context is a citation. On account of the suitability of the speaker, and so on, sometimes even a fault is a quality, and sometimes a so-called fault is neither a fault nor a quality. For instance, if the speaker is a grammarian or if the context is raudra-rasa (anger) or vira-rasa (chivalry), the faults beginning from sruti-katu might not be faulty even in the absence of a citation. If there is no rasa, sometimes a fault is neither a quality nor a fault. In slesa and so on, aprayukta (not in use) (10.35 etc.) and nihatartha (obstructed meaning) (10.36 etc.) are not faulty. Aslila (unpleasant) is not faulty when the speaker is in santa- rasa.**

**A respected author stated, “One should hint at secret topics with words that have double meanings.” On the strength of this maxim, some writer (Visvanatha Kaviraja) gives the verse that begins kari-hastena sambadhe as an example of nonfaulty aslila (because the verse is spoken to persons who want to hear about srngara-rasa):**

***kari-hastena sambādhe praviśyāntar-viloḍite***  
***upasarpan dhvajaḥ puṁsaḥ sādhanāntar virājate***

**“Having entered in the midst of the agitated crowd of the enemy army with the help of the elephant’s trunk, the hero’s banner kept moving. It was resplendent in the midst of that army.” (Sahitya-darpana 7.17)**

**\[As a double meaning, kari-hastena sambadhe (in the crowd by means of an elephant’s trunk) also means “in the vagina with the membrane of an elephant.”\] That is bad: It is a fault related to the meaning (artha-dosa) because it is unpleasant (aslila).**

**If the said secret topic (such as srngara-rasa) is expressed with its own word, the fault is just that (sabda-vacyatva) (10.127), but it is not unpleasant (aslila).**

**Sometimes, even the fault called sandigdha (ambiguous) is a quality, for example when it conveys the aprastuta-prasamsa ornament (indirect expression) or the vyaja-stuti ornament (artful praise).**

**The fault called apratita (not understood) is actually a quality when there is just a slight indication of what meaning is conveyed and what conveys it (for example when both the speaker and the hearer are knowledgeable of the topic). The fault called gramya (vulgar is a quality in the words of a buffon or of a person who has a base nature.**

**Nyuna-pada (hma-pada, missing word) (10.83) is a quality when there is great joy, great sorrow, or much intoxication. Sometimes it is neither a quality nor a fault. Adhika-pada (redundant word) (10.83) is a quality when the sense is dejection (visada) and so on. This was said earlier (10.102), and it is especially true in intoxication.**

**Kathita-pada (repetition of a word) (10.83) is a quality in lata anuprasa, in arthantara-sankramita-vacya, and when there is a reiteration of the noun (Commentary 10.103).**

**Patat-prakarsa (declining eminence) (10.86) is actually a quality when there is a gradual decrease of anger, and so on, and when there is a different rasa in a different part of the text.**

**Samapta-punar-atta (10.32; 10.86) is neither a fault nor a quality when the addition of a modifier does not diminish the relishment or when what is added afterward makes a whole new sentence.**

**Asthana-stha-samasa (a compound in the wrong place) (10.99) is a quality when there is an imitation of anger, and so on, even in a circumstance that is unfit for real anger and so on. Garbhita (parenthesis) is a quality when, as a needed predicate clause, it enhances the contextual meaning. All other faults are faults.**

*jala-kaṇam iva yauvanaṁ viddhi*

**Пословный перевод:**

mugdhe—O inexperienced girl; ma kuru—don’t do; manam— pique; kalaya—please amuse; kata-aksena—by means of a sidelong glance; pundarika-aksam—Pundarikaksa (i.e. Krsna, “whose eyes resemble white lotuses”); anila—on account of the wind; tarala— which is fickle; nalini—of a lotus; dala—on a petal; jala—of water; kanam—a drop; iva—\[is fickle\] like; yauvanam—youthfulness; viddhi—please know.

**Перевод:**

**Simple girl, stop your mana and amuse Pundankaksa with a sidelong glance. You should know that youthfulness is fickle like a drop of water on a petal of a lotus swinging in the wind.**

*atra śṛṅgāre pratilomasya śāntasyānityatā-prakāśana-rūpo vibhāvas tat-prakāśitaś ca nirveda iti duṣṭam. evaṁ śṛṅgāre śāntānubhāvaś ca pratilomatayā duṣṭaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Reminding her about the nondurability of youth is a vibhava (uddipana) of santa, a rasa adverse to srngara, the contextual topic (this is pratiloma-vibhava-graha).**

**In addition, the vyabhicari-bhava called nirveda (indifference toward material life) becomes apparent because of that nondurability (this is pratiloma-vyabhicari-graha).**

**Similarly, in the context of srngara, an anubhava of santa is considered faulty due to being adverse (this is pratiloma anubhava-graha).**

**Комментарий:**

A similar verse is text 4.6.

### 10.135

*abhīkṣṇaśo dīptiḥ, punaḥ punar ekasyaiva rasasyaujjvalyaṁ, yathā kumāra-sambhave rati-vilāpe. vṛthā-vistāro ’kāṇḍe prathanaṁ veṇī-saṁhāre dvitīye ’ṅke aneka-saṅkṣaye pravṛtte bhānumatyā saha duryodhanasya śṛṅgāra-varṇanam. vṛthā-hrāso ’kāṇḍe chedo, yathā vīra-carite dvitīye ’ṅke rāghava-bhārgavayor vīra-rase “kaṅkaṇa-mocanāya gacchāmi” iti rāghavoktau. aṅgasyātivistṛtir, yathā hayagrīva-vadhe hayagrīvasya. aṅgino ’nabhisandhānaṁ ratnāvalyāṁ caturthe ’ṅke bābhravy-āgamane sāgarikā-vismṛtiḥ. prakṛtīnāṁ vyatikramas tu yathā—prakṛtayas tāvat divyā adivyā divyādivyāś ca, tathā dhīrodāttādīnāṁ prāg uktānāṁ caturṇām uttamā madhyamā adhamāś ca. atrottama-prakṛter madhyamādhama-prakṛtikatvena varṇanaṁ, madhyamādhama-prakṛtikayor uttama-prakṛtikatve varṇanam, adhamasya madhyamatvena madhyamasyādhamatvena ca varṇanaṁ duṣṭam.*

**Перевод:**

**The fault called abhiksnaso dipti signifies “heightening a rasa again and again.” An example is in Kumara-sambhava, in Rati’s lamentation.**

**The fault called vrtha-vistara means akande prathana (empha­sizing a rasa, out of place).An example is in Vem-samhara: In the second act, when much destruction is going on, there is a description of the romance between Duryodhana and Bhanumati.**

**The fault called vrtha-hrasa means akande cheda (interrupting the rasa on the wrong occasion). An example is in Vira-carita: When the vira-rasa between Rama and Parasurama is taking place, Rama says: “Sir, I am going to untie My nuptial bracelet.”**

**An example of angasya ativistrti (excessive elaboration on a secondary subject matter) is the description of HayagrTva in Hayagriva-vadha.**

**An intance of anginah anabhisandhana (not taking interest in the main aspect) is in the fourth act in Ratnavali: Sagarika does not pay attention to Babhravya when he arrives.**

**Regarding the fault called prakrti-viparyaya (discrepancy in the description of the nature): The natures are these three kinds: divya (divine), adivya (not divine) and divyadivya (both divine and nondivine). In addition, the three divisions of uttama (elevated), madhyama (ordinary) and adhama (lowly) apply to the aforementioned four types of heroes: dhirodatta, dhiroddhata, dhira-lalita and dhira-santa. Thus a fault occurs when the description of the nature of the person is contrary to their actual nature. For instance, the description of someone who has an elevated nature as someone who has either an ordinary nature or a lowly nature is faulty.**

### 10.136

*uttama-devatānāṁ pārvatī-parameśvarādīnāṁ śṛṅgāra-varṇanaṁ ca na kāryam, yat tu kṛtaṁ kālidāsādibhis tad duṣṭam. tad-varṇanaṁ hi sva-pitroḥ śṛṅgāra-varṇanam iva. śrī-keśavayor apīti kecit. kecit tu varṇayanti tayor īśvaratvād devatātvaṁ neti. varṇanaṁ yathā “viparī-a-ra-e lacchī” ity-ādi “andhatvam andha-samaye” ity-ādi ca. rādhā-mādhavayos tu varṇanīyam eva, sarveśvareśvaratvena devatātvābhāvāt. vidhi-vākyaṁ ca—vikrīḍitaṁ vraja-vadhūbhir idaṁ ca viṣṇoḥ, śraddhānvito ’nuśṛṇuyād atha varṇayed yaḥ” ityādi. kintu yatra yatrānaucityaṁ pratīyate tat tad eva na varṇanīyam iti bhāvaḥ. uktaṁ hi dhvani-kṛtā, “anaucityād ṛte nānyad rasabhaṅgasya kāraṇam, prasiddhaucitya-bandhas tu rasasyopaniṣat parā” iti.*

**Перевод:**

**A description of the intimate romance between topmost devatas such as Parvati and Siva should not be done. What Kalidasa did is wrong. He is not alone in this matter. Depicting the intimate romance between Parvati and Siva is like depicting the intimate romance between one’s parents. Some say the same applies to Laksmi and Narayana. Other scholars depict Their romance, but only because They are gods in the highest sense; they do not consider Them demigods. This is an example of such a description:**

*viparīarae lacchī bamhaṁ daṭṭhūṇa ṇāhi-kamala-ṭhṭhaṁ*  
*hariṇo dāhiṇa-ṇaaṇaṁ rasāulā jhatti ḍhakkei*  
*(Prakrit language)*

*viparīta-rate lakṣmīr brahmāṇaṁ dṛṣṭvā nābhi-kamala-stham*  
*harer dakṣiṇa-nayanaṁ rasākulā jhaṭiti ḍhaukate*  
*(Sanskrit rendering)*

**Перевод:**

**“During intercourse in reverse, Laksmi suddenly saw Brahma, who was seated on the lotus originating from Visnu’s navel. Overcome by sensual relishment, she at once covered His right eye.” (Kavya-prakasa, verse 137)**

**This is another such example:**

*andhatvam andha-samaye badhiratvaṁ badhira-kāla ālambya*  
*śrī-keśavayoḥ praṇayī prajāpatir nābhi-vāstavyaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**“Assuming blindness at a time appropriate for blindness and deafness at a time appropriate for deafness, Brahma, seated on the lotus, felt love for Laksmi and Narayana.” (Arya-saptasati, a-kara-vrajya 8)**

**But there is no question that descriptions of the intimate romance between Radha and Madhava should be made, because They are not devatas since They are the gods of gods. The authoritative statement is:**

*vikrīḍitaṁ vraja-vadhūbhir idaṁ ca viṣṇoḥ*  
*śraddhānvito ’nuśṛṇuyād atha varṇayed yaḥ*  
*bhaktiṁ parāṁ bhagavati pratilabhya kāmaṁ*  
*hṛd-rogam āśv apahinoty acireṇa dhīraḥ*

**Перевод:**

**“An intelligent person who has faith and who hears and then describes this romance between Krsna and the gopis will achieve the topmost devotion unto the Lord and quickly, without delay, deliver himself from lust, the disease of the heart.” (Bhagavatam** [**10.33.39**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/33.39)**)**

**However, no such description should occur whenever some sort of inappropriateness is apparent. That was stated by the Dhvanikara:**

*anaucityād ṛte nānyad*  
*rasa-bhaṅgasya kāraṇam*  
*prasiddhaucitya-bandhas tu*  
*rasasyopaniṣat parā*

**Перевод:**

**“Other than inappropriateness, there is no cause of the disruption of the relishment. A literary construction based on a well-known appropriateness is the highest secret teaching for the relishment of a rasa.” (Dhvany-aloka 3.14)**

### 10.137

*anaṅgasya rasānupakārakasya prakaṭanaṁ duṣṭam. ūhyam udāharaṇam.*

**Перевод:**

**The fault called anangasya prakatana (mentioning something that is not an aspect) means something that does not assist the rasa is emphasized. An example can be inferred.**

### 10.138

*ekāśrayatve rasayor na virodhaḥ pravartate*  
*bhinnāśrayatve virodhaḥ śānta-śṛṅgārayor yathā (21)*

**Пословный перевод:**

eka-asrayatve—when there is only one scope; rasayoh—of two rasas; na—not; virodhah—incompatibility; pravartate—is produced; bhinna-asrayatve—when the spheres of activity are different; virodhah—incompatibility; santa-srhgarayoh—of santa- rasa and srhgara-rasa; yatha—like.

**Перевод:**

**Just as in certain cases there is no incompatibility between two rasas in the same scope, so santa-rasa and srngara-rasa are not incompatible if they are located in separate scopes.**

*ekāśrayatve hāsya-śṛṅgārayoḥ, adbhuta-hāsyayoś ca, adbhutaśṛṅgārayor vīra-karuṇayor na virodha eva. śānta-śṛṅgārayoḥ śṛṅgāra-karuṇayoḥ, śṛṅgāra-bībhatsayoḥ kevalaṁ virodha eva. śṛṅgāra-karuṇayor aṅgāṅgi-bhāve na doṣaḥ. yathā—vana-vāsastha-sītāyā garbha-darśanāt prāk-śṛṅgāra-smṛtiḥ. atra karuṇo ’ṅgī śṛṅgāro ’ṅgam.*

**Перевод:**

**When the scope is one and the same, there is no incompatibility between hasya and srngara, adbhuta and hasya, adbhuta and srngara, and vira and karuna, but there is incompatibility between santa and srngara, srngara and karuna, and srngara and bibhatsa. However, there is no fault if srngara and karuna have the roles of anga and angi. For example: “Upon seeing the womb of Sita, who was residing in the forest, there occurred a remembrance of her previous amorous pastimes.” Here karuna is the angi and srngara is the anga.**

### 10.139

*śānta-śṛṅgārayoḥ kvacin na doṣaḥ, yathā—nirvāṇa-nimbarasam eva pibanti kecid bhavyā na te rasa-viśeṣa-vido vayaṁ tu, śyāmāmṛtaṁ madana-manthara-gopa-rāmā-netrāñjalī-culukitāvasitaṁ pibāmaḥ. atra pūrvārdhe śāntaḥ, parārdhe śṛṅgāraḥ, tathāpi śuddham, śāntasya nyak-kṛtatvāt śṛṅgāra eva puṣṭaḥ. prāg-ukta-lakṣaṇasya rasasyānanda-svarūpatvena pratipādite caikye rasasya rasena virodha iti yad iha pratipādyate tat tu sāmagrī-bhūtasya sthāyy-āder eva na tu rasasya.*

**Перевод:**

**Similarly, sometimes there is no fault in combining santa and srngara. For instance:**

*nirvāṇa-nimba-rasam eva pibanti kecid*  
*bhavyā na te rasa-viśeṣa-vido vayaṁ tu*  
*śyāmāmṛtaṁ madana-manthara-gopa-rāmā-*  
*netrāñjalī-culukitāvasitaṁ pibāmaḥ*

**Пословный перевод:**

nirvana—\[in the form\] of the bliss of Brahman; nimba—bitter like a nimba leaf; rasam—the juice; eva—only; pibanti—drink; kecit— some; bhavyah—righteous people; na—are not; te—they; rasa— of rasa; visesa—of the speciality; vidah—knowers; vayam—we; tu—but; syama—of Syama; amrtam—the nectar; madana—on account of Cupid; manthara—who are indolent; gopa-rama—of the gopis; netra-anjali—for the eyes \[in the form of\] cupped hands (open hands placed side by side and slightly hollowed in order to hold the nectar); culukita—made into a mouthful; avasitam—and ascertained; pibamah—we drink.

**Перевод:**

**Some righteous persons drink the bitter nim juice of the bliss of Brahman. They do not know about the excellence of Rasa. We, however, drink the nectar of Syama. The gopis who are indolent due to Cupid think it belongs to them. This nectar turns out as a mouthful relished in the cupped hands of their eyes.**

**In this verse, the first half features santa and the second srngara. Still, that is proper because srngara is valued by belittling santa.**

**The incompatibilities expounded here between one rasa and another only relate to a rasa which is a sthayi-bhava that has all its constituent parts, not to rasa which is rapture, because in the definition of rasa it was explained that its nature is bliss, therefore Rasa is one.**

*ity alaṅkāra-kaustubhe doṣa-pradarśano nāma daśamaḥ kiraṇaḥ. samāpto ’yaṁ granthaḥ.*

**Перевод:**

**Thus ends the tenth ray in Alankara-kaustubha, entitled “an analysis of faults.” The treatise ends here.**
